declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasDenseChowModification
declarations.doc: **Chow's lemma over a Noetherian base.**
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDenseChowModification {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    HasDenseChowModification f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_chowGraph
declarations.doc:
**The graph of a proper modification is a closed immersion.** It is proper, because the
projection `𝐏ⁿ_S ×_S X ⟶ X` is separated and the composite is `π`, and a monomorphism, because
the composite with the projection to `𝐏ⁿ_S` is the immersion `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_chowGraph (π : X' ⟶ X) (i : X' ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S) [IsProper π]
    [IsImmersion i] (hcomm : π ≫ f = i ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S)) :
    IsClosedImmersion (chowGraph π i hcomm)
declarations.comment: part (1): `X' ⟶ 𝐏ⁿ_S ×_S X = 𝐏ⁿ_X` is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveMorphism_chowModification
declarations.doc:
**The modification in Chow's lemma is H-projective.** Its graph is a closed immersion into
the projective space `𝐏ⁿ_X` over `X`, compatibly with the structure morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjectiveMorphism_chowModification (π : X' ⟶ X) (i : X' ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S)
    [IsProper π] [IsImmersion i] (hcomm : π ≫ f = i ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S)) :
    IsProjectiveMorphism π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_chowModification
declarations.doc: **The modification in Chow's lemma is projective**: an H-projective morphism is projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_chowModification (π : X' ⟶ X) (i : X' ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S) [IsProper π]
    [IsImmersion i] (hcomm : π ≫ f = i ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S)) :
    IsProjective π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_chowModification
declarations.doc:
**In Chow's lemma the inverse image of the dense open may be assumed scheme-theoretically
dense.** Replace `X'` by the scheme-theoretic closure of `π⁻¹(U)`; the dimension `n` of the
ambient projective space and the dense open `U` are unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_chowModification (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (π : X' ⟶ X)
    (i : X' ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S) (U : X.Opens) [IsProper π] [IsImmersion i]
    (hcomm : π ≫ f = i ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S)) (hU : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hiso : IsIso (π ∣_ U)) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (ρ : Y ⟶ X) (j : Y ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S),
      IsProper ρ ∧ Surjective ρ ∧ IsImmersion j ∧
        ρ ≫ f = j ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S) ∧ Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsIso (ρ ∣_ U) ∧
        Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (ρ ⁻¹ᵁ U)
declarations.comment: part (2): `π⁻¹(U)` may be assumed scheme-theoretically dense in `X'`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isReduced_chowModification
declarations.doc:
**In Chow's lemma over a reduced scheme the modification may be chosen reduced.** The
scheme-theoretic closure of `π⁻¹(U)` has reduced source, since `π⁻¹(U) ≅ U` is an open subscheme
of the reduced scheme `X`, and the scheme-theoretic image of a reduced scheme is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReduced_chowModification (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsReduced X] (π : X' ⟶ X)
    (i : X' ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S) (U : X.Opens) [IsProper π] [IsImmersion i]
    (hcomm : π ≫ f = i ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S)) (hU : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hiso : IsIso (π ∣_ U)) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (ρ : Y ⟶ X) (j : Y ⟶ ProjectiveSpace n S),
      IsProper ρ ∧ Surjective ρ ∧ IsImmersion j ∧
        ρ ≫ f = j ≫ (ProjectiveSpace n S ↘ S) ∧ Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsIso (ρ ∣_ U) ∧
        Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (ρ ⁻¹ᵁ U) ∧ IsReduced Y
declarations.comment: part (3): if `X` is reduced then `X'` may be chosen reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasChowModification_of_compactSpace_quasiSeparatedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Chow's lemma over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base.** A separated morphism of finite
type onto a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme admits a proper surjective modification immersed
in a projective space over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChowModification_of_compactSpace_quasiSeparatedSpace {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] : HasChowModification f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasDenseChowModification_of_finite_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0203]: the variant of Chow's lemma with a dense open.** Let `S` be
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated and of finite type, and suppose
`X` has only finitely many irreducible components. Then there are `n`, a scheme `X'`, a proper
surjective `π : X' ⟶ X` and an immersion `X' ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` making the triangle over `S` commute, such
that `π` is an isomorphism over a dense open subscheme of `X`.

The dense open does not survive base change, so unlike [Stacks, Tag 0202] this cannot be had by
descending `X` to a stage and pulling the modification back. Instead the whole inverse system
`Yⱼ = Sⱼ ×_{S_{i₁}} Y₁` is kept, Chow's lemma over a Noetherian base is applied to the
**scheme-theoretic image** of `X` in a stage chosen so that the finitely many generic points of
`X` have pairwise non-specializing images, and the dense open of that image then pulls back to a
dense open of `X` because it contains every generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDenseChowModification_of_finite_irreducibleComponents {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    HasDenseChowModification f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_tfae
declarations.doc:
A separated morphism of finite type is proper precisely when all of its base changes along
morphisms locally of finite type are closed, or equivalently when its base changes to all
finite-dimensional affine spaces are closed.

The second condition is the hypothesis that `X ×_S S' ⟶ S'` is a closed map for every `S' ⟶ S`
locally of finite type, and the third that `𝔸(n; X) ⟶ 𝔸(n; S)`, the base change of `f` along
`𝔸(n; S) ↘ S`, is a closed map for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsProper f,
       ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S),
         LocallyOfFiniteType g → IsClosedMap (pullback.snd f g),
       ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosedMap (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_tfae_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0207.** For a morphism locally of finite type over a locally
Noetherian scheme, separatedness is equivalent to uniqueness in the valuative criterion; it
suffices to use discrete valuation rings, and even the discrete valuation subrings of the
function fields of the irreducible components of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_tfae_of_locallyOfFiniteType {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsSeparated f,
        ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness f,
        ∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f),
          IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R → Subsingleton D.commSq.LiftStruct,
        ∀ (η : X), η ∈ genericPoints X →
          ∀ (A : Subring (X.residueField η)),
            IsDiscreteValuationRing A →
              IsFractionRing A (X.residueField η) →
                ∀ (i₂ : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
                  (sq : CommSq (X.fromSpecResidueField η)
                    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom A.subtype)) f i₂),
                  Subsingleton sq.LiftStruct ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_genericDiscreteValuativeCriterion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0208], condition (4) implies condition (1).** A morphism of finite type to a
locally Noetherian scheme is proper as soon as every valuative diagram whose valuation ring is a
discrete valuation subring of the residue field at a generic point of an irreducible component
of the source, with that residue field as its fraction field, and whose generic arrow is the
canonical one, has exactly one dotted arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_genericDiscreteValuativeCriterion (p : V ⟶ W)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian W] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    (h : GenericDiscreteValuativeCriterion p) : IsProper p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_tfae_genericDiscreteValuativeCriterion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0208].** Let `S` be locally Noetherian and `f : X ⟶ S` of finite type. The
following are equivalent:

1. `f` is proper;
2. every valuative diagram for `f` has exactly one dotted arrow;
3. every valuative diagram for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring has exactly
   one dotted arrow;
4. for every generic point `η` of an irreducible component of `X` and every discrete valuation
   subring `A` of `κ(η)` with fraction field `κ(η)`, every valuative diagram whose generic arrow
   is the canonical `Spec κ(η) ⟶ X` has exactly one dotted arrow, that is,
   `AlgebraicGeometry.GenericDiscreteValuativeCriterion f`.

Conditions (1) to (3) are `AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_tfae_of_isFiniteType`; (3) implies (4)
because such a diagram is a valuative diagram over a discrete valuation ring, and (4) implies (1)
is `AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_genericDiscreteValuativeCriterion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_tfae_genericDiscreteValuativeCriterion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsProper f,
        ValuativeCriterion f,
        ∀ D : ValuativeCommSq f,
          IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R → Nonempty (Unique D.commSq.LiftStruct),
        GenericDiscreteValuativeCriterion f ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_tfae_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0208, conditions (1), (2) and (3).** For a morphism of finite type to a
locally Noetherian scheme, properness, the existence of exactly one dotted arrow in every
valuative square, and the existence of exactly one dotted arrow in every valuative square over a
discrete valuation ring are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_tfae_of_isFiniteType {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsProper f,
        ValuativeCriterion f,
        ∀ D : ValuativeCommSq f,
          IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R → Nonempty (Unique D.commSq.LiftStruct) ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety
declarations.doc:
A scheme over a field is a variety when it is integral and its structure morphism is
separated and of finite type.
declarations.statement:
class IsVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop
    extends IsIntegral X, IsSeparated f, LocallyOfFiniteType f, QuasiCompact f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.InseparableHypersurface.nilpotentElement_pow_eq_zero
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 020F.** The displayed element is nilpotent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nilpotentElement_pow_eq_zero (K : Type*) [Field K]
    [Algebra (rationalFunctionField p) K] (a b : K)
    (ha : a ^ p = algebraMap (rationalFunctionField p) K (transcendentalGenerator p 0))
    (hb : b ^ p = algebraMap (rationalFunctionField p) K (transcendentalGenerator p 1)) :
    nilpotentElement p K a b ^ p = 0
declarations.comment: the displayed element has p-th power zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.InseparableHypersurface.hypersurface_isVariety
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 020F.** The hypersurface over `𝔽ₚ(s,t)` is a variety.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hypersurface_isVariety :
    IsVariety (rationalFunctionField p) (hypersurfaceToSpec p)
declarations.comment: the original scheme is a variety

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.InseparableHypersurface.nilpotentElement_ne_zero
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 020F.** The displayed element is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nilpotentElement_ne_zero (K : Type*) [Field K]
    [Algebra (rationalFunctionField p) K] (a b : K) :
    nilpotentElement p K a b ≠ 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.InseparableHypersurface.baseChange_not_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 020F.** The base change to a field containing both roots is
not reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChange_not_isReduced (K : Type) [Field K]
    [Algebra (rationalFunctionField p) K] (a b : K)
    (ha : a ^ p = algebraMap (rationalFunctionField p) K (transcendentalGenerator p 0))
    (hb : b ^ p = algebraMap (rationalFunctionField p) K (transcendentalGenerator p 1)) :
    ¬ IsReduced (pullback (hypersurfaceToSpec p)
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (rationalFunctionField p) K))))
declarations.comment: the base change is not reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gaussianRationals_isVariety
declarations.doc: `Spec ℚ(i)` is a variety over `ℚ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gaussianRationals_isVariety :
    IsVariety ℚ gaussianRationalsToRat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gaussianRationals_product_reducible
declarations.doc: The product `Spec ℚ(i) ×_{Spec ℚ} Spec ℚ(i)` is reducible.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gaussianRationals_product_not_isVariety
declarations.doc: The product of these two varieties is not a variety.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gaussianRationals_product_not_isVariety :
    ¬ IsVariety ℚ
      (pullback.fst gaussianRationalsToRat gaussianRationalsToRat ≫
        gaussianRationalsToRat)
declarations.comment: the product is not a variety

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gaussianRationals_product_iso_coprod
declarations.doc: The product is isomorphic to two disjoint copies of `Spec ℚ(i)`.
declarations.comment: the product is two copies of the factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyPointwiseIntegralAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is geometrically pointwise integral at `x : X` if, after every
base change from the spectrum of a field, every point above `x` has an integral local ring.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev GeometricallyPointwiseIntegralAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X) :
    Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyPointwiseIntegral
declarations.doc:
A morphism is geometrically pointwise integral if it is geometrically pointwise integral
at every point of its source.
declarations.statement: public abbrev GeometricallyPointwiseIntegral {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIntegral_iff_isIntegral_pullback
declarations.doc:
A scheme `X` over a field `k` is geometrically integral if and only if the base change
`X_{k'}` is integral for every field extension `k'/k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIntegral_iff_isIntegral_pullback {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    GeometricallyIntegral f ↔
      ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K],
        IsIntegral (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyReducedAt_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
A reduced local ring of a scheme over a perfect field is geometrically reduced at the
corresponding point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_of_isReduced
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) [_root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk x)] :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced
declarations.doc: A reduced scheme over a perfect field is geometrically reduced over that field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsReduced X] :
    GeometricallyReduced f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 020J.** An irreducible scheme over a separably closed field is
geometrically irreducible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isSepClosed
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IrreducibleSpace X] : GeometricallyIrreducible f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.exists_isStandardZariski_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 020Q.** Every Zariski covering of an affine scheme has a finite
refinement by standard opens, each contained in a member of the original covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem OpenCover.exists_isStandardZariski_refinement {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    (𝒰 : T.OpenCover.{v}) :
    ∃ (𝒱 : T.OpenCover.{v}) (_refinement : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒰),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardZariskiCovering 𝒱

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardZariskiCovering
declarations.doc:
A Zariski covering of an affine scheme `T` is standard if it has finitely many members and
every member identifies with a standard affine open `T.basicOpen f` of the target.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStandardZariskiCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    (𝒰 : T.Cover.{v} Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigZariskiSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 020S.** A big Zariski site consists of an initial set of schemes and initial
Zariski covering families, a sufficiently large cutoff category containing those schemes,
and a bounded set of Zariski covering families.

The last two fields say that the selected families satisfy the site axioms and that every
Zariski covering family has a combinatorially equivalent selected representative.
declarations.statement: public structure BigZariskiSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigZariskiOver
declarations.doc: The big Zariski category of `S` is the slice of the chosen big category.
declarations.statement: public abbrev BigZariskiOver

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigZariskiOver.IsCovering
declarations.doc: A family over `S` covers when its underlying family covers in the chosen big site.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (BigZariskiOver B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski
declarations.doc: The small Zariski category consists of schemes open in `S`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev SmallZariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.IsCovering
declarations.doc: Small-site coverings are precisely big-site coverings of small-site objects.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (SmallZariski B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineZariski
declarations.doc: The big affine Zariski category consists of affine schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev BigAffineZariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineZariski.IsCovering
declarations.doc: Big affine coverings are standard Zariski coverings.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (BigAffineZariski B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineZariski
declarations.doc: The small affine Zariski category consists of affine opens in `S`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev SmallAffineZariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineZariski.IsCovering
declarations.doc: Small affine coverings are the standard Zariski coverings inherited from the small site.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (SmallAffineZariski B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isSite
declarations.doc: Zariski coverings of schemes open in `S` satisfy the site axioms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSite (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) : IsSite (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.IsCovering B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineZariski.isSite
declarations.doc: Standard Zariski coverings of affine schemes over `S` satisfy the site axioms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSite (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) : IsSite (AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineZariski.IsCovering B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineZariski.isSite
declarations.doc: Standard Zariski coverings of affine opens of `S` satisfy the site axioms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSite (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) : IsSite (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineZariski.IsCovering B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasPullbacks_bigZariskiSite
declarations.doc: The underlying category of a big Zariski site has fibre products.
declarations.statement: public instance hasPullbacks_bigZariskiSite : HasPullbacks B.Schemes
declarations.comment: fibre products in the big Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasPullbacks_smallZariski
declarations.doc: The small Zariski category of `S` has fibre products.
declarations.statement: public instance hasPullbacks_smallZariski : HasPullbacks (SmallZariski B S hS)
declarations.comment: fibre products in the small Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasPullbacks_bigAffineZariski
declarations.doc: The category of affine objects in the big Zariski category over `S` has fibre products.
declarations.statement: public instance hasPullbacks_bigAffineZariski : HasPullbacks (BigAffineZariski B S hS)
declarations.comment: fibre products in the big affine Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasPullbacks_smallAffineZariski
declarations.doc: The affine small Zariski category of `S` has fibre products.
declarations.statement: public instance hasPullbacks_smallAffineZariski : HasPullbacks (SmallAffineZariski B S hS)
declarations.comment: fibre products in the small affine Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesPullbacks_bigZariskiSiteInclusion
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of a big Zariski site's underlying category into schemes preserves fibre
products.
declarations.statement:
public instance preservesPullbacks_bigZariskiSiteInclusion :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan B.inclusion
declarations.comment: preservation by the big Zariski site inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesPullbacks_smallZariskiToScheme
declarations.doc:
The canonical functor from the small Zariski category to schemes preserves fibre
products.
declarations.statement:
public instance preservesPullbacks_smallZariskiToScheme :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan (SmallZariski.toScheme B S hS)
declarations.comment: preservation by the small Zariski functor to schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesPullbacks_bigAffineZariskiToScheme
declarations.doc: The canonical functor from affine objects over `S` to schemes preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
public instance preservesPullbacks_bigAffineZariskiToScheme :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan (BigAffineZariski.toScheme B S hS)
declarations.comment: preservation by the big affine Zariski functor to schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesPullbacks_smallAffineZariskiToScheme
declarations.doc:
The canonical functor from affine open objects over `S` to schemes preserves fibre
products.
declarations.statement:
public instance preservesPullbacks_smallAffineZariskiToScheme :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan (SmallAffineZariski.toScheme B S hS)
declarations.comment: preservation by the small affine Zariski functor to schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.finalIsTerminal
declarations.doc: The object `S / S` is final in the small Zariski category of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def SmallZariski.finalIsTerminal :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smallZariskiBaseChange
declarations.doc:
There is a morphism of small Zariski sites from `T` to `S` whose underlying functor, after
including both small sites into schemes over `T` and `S`, is naturally isomorphic to base change
along `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_smallZariskiBaseChange :
    ∃ F : SmallZariski B S.1 S.property ⥤
        SmallZariski B T.1 T.property,
      _root_.IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1} F
        (SmallZariski.topology B S.1 S.property)
        (SmallZariski.topology B T.1 T.property) ∧
      Nonempty (F ⋙ smallSiteInSchemesOver B T ≅
        smallSiteInSchemesOver B S ⋙ Over.pullback (B.inclusion.map f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites_ringUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0211 at the universe of the structure rings.**  Small Zariski base change along

of the structure sheaves.

This is the input a morphism of ringed sites needs, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites` does not provide it: that one is
stated for sheaves of sets in `Type (u + 1)`, the universe of the objects of the site.
declarations.comment: f_small on small Zariski sites, at the universe of the structure rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
Under the small-site equivalences, inverse image is the usual inverse image
of sheaves on the underlying topological spaces.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallZariskiPullbackIso :
    (smallZariskiSheafEquiv B S.1 S.property).functor ⋙
      (Opens.map (B.inclusion.map f).base).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((B.inclusion.obj S).toPresheafedSpace : TopCat))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((B.inclusion.obj T).toPresheafedSpace : TopCat)) ≅
      (smallZariskiBaseChange B f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (SmallZariski.topology B S.1 S.property)
      (SmallZariski.topology B T.1 T.property) ⋙
      (smallZariskiSheafEquiv B T.1 T.property).functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
Under the small-site equivalences, direct image is the usual direct image
of sheaves on the underlying topological spaces.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallZariskiPushforwardIso :
    (smallZariskiSheafEquiv B T.1 T.property).functor ⋙
      (Opens.map (B.inclusion.map f).base).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((B.inclusion.obj S).toPresheafedSpace : TopCat))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((B.inclusion.obj T).toPresheafedSpace : TopCat)) ≅
      (smallZariskiBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      (Type (u + 1))
      (SmallZariski.topology B S.1 S.property)
      (SmallZariski.topology B T.1 T.property) ⋙
      (smallZariskiSheafEquiv B S.1 S.property).functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiBaseChange_comp_inclusionIso
declarations.doc:
The square of functors underlying the four morphisms of Zariski sites
commutes up to a natural isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallZariskiBaseChange_comp_inclusionIso :
    smallZariskiBaseChange B f ⋙
        SmallZariski.inclusion B T.1 T.property ≅
      SmallZariski.inclusion B S.1 S.property ⋙ Over.pullback f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiProjection_baseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
The geometric morphisms satisfy `f_small ∘ π_T ≅ π_S ∘ f_big`;

declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallZariskiProjection_baseChangeIso :

      (smallZariskiProjection B T)).inverseImage ≅
    ((smallZariskiProjection B S).comp
      (bigZariskiMorphism B T S f)).inverseImage

      ((bigZariskiMorphism B T S f).comp
        (smallZariskiToBigZariskiMorphism B T T (𝟙 T))).pushforward

declarations.doc: The inverse image of `i_f` agrees naturally with that of `f_big ∘ i_T`.

        (smallZariskiToBigZariskiMorphism B T T (𝟙 T))).inverseImage

        (smallZariskiToBigZariskiMorphism B T S f)).inverseImage

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0212.** The direct image of `g_big ∘ f_big` agrees naturally with that of

Both are read as restriction along slice base change, where the comparison is the canonical
isomorphism `(U ×_Z Y) ×_Y X ≅ U ×_Z X` of iterated fibre products.

declarations.doc:
Global sections of the canonical restriction at a scheme are the sections

public noncomputable def bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv

    (T : BigZariskiOver B S hS) :
    (((bigZariskiSheafRestriction.{u, v} B S hS).obj F).sheaf T).1.obj (op ⊤) ≃
      F.1.obj (op T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc: The identification of global sections is natural in the big-site sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv_naturality
    {F G : Sheaf (BigZariskiOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max u v))}
    (α : F ⟶ G) (T : BigZariskiOver B S hS)
    (s : (((bigZariskiSheafRestriction.{u, v} B S hS).obj F).sheaf T).1.obj (op ⊤)) :
  bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv B S hS G T
      (((((bigZariskiSheafRestriction.{u, v} B S hS).map α).app T).1.app (op ⊤)) s) =
    α.1.app (op T)
      (bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv B S hS F T s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigZariskiSheafRestriction_pullback_sections
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical identifications of global sections, the pullback
comparison is exactly the restriction map of the big-site sheaf. Applying this
to every object, including open subschemes, controls the comparison on opens.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bigZariskiSheafRestriction_pullback_sections
    (F : Sheaf (BigZariskiOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max u v)))
    {T T' : BigZariskiOver B S hS} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (s : F.1.obj (op T)) :
    let D := (bigZariskiSheafRestriction.{u, v} B S hS).obj F
    let ftop := (B.inclusion.map f.left).base
    let η := (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImagePushforwardAdjunction.{u, v} ftop).unit.app
      (D.sheaf T)
    bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv B S hS F T'
      ((D.pullback f).1.app (op ⊤)
        (η.1.app (op ⊤)
          ((bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sectionEquiv B S hS F T).symm s))) =
      F.1.map f.op s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sheaf
declarations.doc:
At each scheme over `S` the sheaf produced by canonical restriction is the inverse image
of the big-site sheaf along the small-to-big morphism of topoi, transported to the space of
that scheme.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sheaf
    (F : Sheaf (BigZariskiOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max u v)))
    (T : BigZariskiOver B S hS) :
    ((bigZariskiSheafRestriction.{u, v} B S hS).obj F).sheaf T ≅
      canonicalSmallSheaf B S hS F T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sheafNatIso
declarations.doc:
The componentwise identification is natural in the big-site sheaf; hence
its maps on every open subset are the canonical restriction maps.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigZariskiSheafRestriction_sheafNatIso
    (T : BigZariskiOver B S hS) :
    bigZariskiSheafRestriction.{u, v} B S hS ⋙ BigZariskiSheafData.eval B S hS T ≅
      canonicalSmallSheafFunctor.{u, v} B S hS T
declarations.comment: naturality on opens and in the sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_affine_etaleCovering_le_of_mem_etaleTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0218 for the étale subcollection of a big fppf site.** A covering sieve of the big
étale topology `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleTopology B` at an object `X` whose underlying scheme is
affine contains a selected étale covering family of `X` which is finite and whose members again
have affine underlying scheme.

This is the étale analogue of `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardFppf_refinement` (Stacks 021P) on
the same category, and it is proved by reading the étale subcollection as the big étale site
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.toBigEtaleSite` and applying
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSite.exists_finite_affine_refinement` there; see the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_affine_etaleCovering_le_of_mem_etaleTopology (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    {X : B.Schemes} (hX : IsAffine (B.inclusion.obj X))
    {R : Sieve X} (hR : R ∈ etaleTopology B X) :
    ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} X, etaleCovering B ⟨X, E⟩ ∧ Finite E.I₀ ∧
      (∀ i, IsAffine (B.inclusion.obj (E.X i))) ∧ E.presieve₀ ≤ R.arrows
declarations.comment: for the étale subcollection of a big fppf site, inside a covering sieve

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardEtaleCovering
declarations.doc:
A standard étale covering of an affine scheme `T`: a finite family of étale morphisms
`f i : U i ⟶ T` with affine sources whose images cover `T`, that is, the étale case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStandardEtaleCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] {I : Type v}
    (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StacksBigEtaleSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021A.** A big étale site: a site `Sch_étale` in the sense of Stacks 00VH constructed
as follows.

1. A set of schemes `S₀` and a set `Cov₀` of étale coverings among these schemes.
2. As underlying category a full subcategory `Sch` of schemes as in Stacks 000J starting with
   `S₀`: the fields of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsBigSchemeCategory`.
3. A set `Cov` of coverings as in Stacks 000X starting with `Sch`, the class of étale coverings
   of `Sch` and `Cov₀`: `Cov` consists of étale coverings, contains `Cov₀`, satisfies the axioms
   of a site (Stacks 00VH), and every étale covering of `Sch` is combinatorially equivalent
   (Stacks 00VU (1)) to a member of `Cov`.

Stacks takes the objects of `Sch` to be the schemes in a stage `V_α` of the von Neumann hierarchy
and `Cov` to be the étale coverings in a stage `V_β` with index set of cardinality at most `κ`.
Lean's type theory assigns no von Neumann rank to a scheme or to a family of morphisms; what the
stages provide is that the objects and the coverings form *sets*, which is recorded here as
`Small.{u}`, `u` being the universe of the sets underlying the schemes. A family of morphisms has
its index set in `Type u`.
declarations.statement: public structure StacksBigEtaleSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (1).** The underlying category of the big étale site of `S` is the
slice of the chosen big étale category over `S`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev BigEtaleOver

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleOver.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (1).** A family in the slice is covering precisely when its underlying
family is a covering in the chosen big étale site.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (BigEtaleOver B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (2).** The small étale category of `S` is the full subcategory of the
big étale category over `S` consisting of objects étale over `S`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev SmallEtale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (2).** A family in the small étale category is covering when its
image in the big étale category over `S` is covering.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (SmallEtale B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (3).** The big affine étale category over `S` is the full subcategory
of the big étale category over `S` consisting of affine source schemes.
declarations.statement: public abbrev BigAffineEtale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineEtale.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (3).** A family in the big affine étale category is covering when its
image in the big étale category over `S` is a standard étale covering.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (BigAffineEtale B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (4).** The small affine étale category of `S` is the full subcategory
of the small étale category consisting of affine schemes.
declarations.statement: public abbrev SmallAffineEtale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021B, part (4).** A family in the small affine étale category is covering when
its image in the small étale category is covering and it is finite (hence standard étale,
since its source objects are affine).
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (SmallAffineEtale B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021C, small étale site.** The étale covering families on the
small étale category of a scheme satisfy the axioms of a site.
declarations.statement:

`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleInclusion_isMorphismOfSites` is the same assertion for sheaves of

declarations.comment: the morphism of sites, at the universe of the structure rings

The geometric morphism `π_S` associated to the inclusion of the small
étale site into the big étale slice.

      (Sheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectionCompInclusionPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
The composite `π_S ∘ i_S` is naturally the identity of the small étale
topos, where `i_S` is the geometric morphism attached to `𝟙_S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def projectionCompInclusionPushforwardIso :
    (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B (B.obj S hS) (B.obj S hS)
        (𝟙 (B.obj S hS))).pushforward ⋙
      (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S hS).pushforward ≅
        𝟭 (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inclusionInverseImageIsoProjectionPushforward
declarations.doc:
Inverse image along `i_S` is naturally restriction to the small étale
site, equivalently direct image along `π_S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def inclusionInverseImageIsoProjectionPushforward :
    (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B (B.obj S hS) (B.obj S hS)
        (𝟙 (B.obj S hS))).inverseImage ≅
      (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S hS).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMap_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 021H.** Composition with `f` is cocontinuous for the big étale topologies.
declarations.statement:

      (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMap_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
Composition with `f` is also continuous.  This is the continuity used to identify inverse
image with restriction and to construct the lower shriek.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigEtaleMap_isContinuous :
    (Over.map f).IsContinuous
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtalePullback_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021H.** Pullback along `f`, sending `U / S` to the canonical fibre product
`U ×_S T / T`, is continuous for the big étale topologies.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigEtalePullback_isContinuous :
    (Over.pullback f).IsContinuous
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
declarations.comment: continuity of the base-change right adjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021H.** The morphism of big étale topoi induced by the cocontinuous functor
`Over.map f`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigEtaleMorphism (f : T ⟶ S) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMorphismInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021H.** Inverse image is restriction along composition with `f`.  On an object
`U / T`, this is the formula `f_big⁻¹(G)(U / T) ≅ G(U / S)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigEtaleMorphismInverseImageIso :
    (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage ≅
      (Over.map f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMorphismPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021H.** Direct image is restriction along base change.  On an object `U / S`,
this is the formula `f_big,*(F)(U / S) ≅ F(U ×_S T / T)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigEtaleMorphismPushforwardIso :
    (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward ≅
      (Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021H.** The inverse-image functor has the sheaf pullback along postcomposition
as a left adjoint; this is `f_big!`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigEtaleLowerShriekAdjunction :
    (Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
      (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property) ⊣
        (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc: **Stacks 021H.** The lower shriek commutes with fibre products.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan
      ((Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers
declarations.doc: **Stacks 021H.** The lower shriek commutes with equalizers.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair
      ((Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRestrictionProjectionPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**`i_f^{-1}π_S^{-1} = f_{small}^{-1}`.** Pulling a sheaf back from the small étale site of `S`
to the big étale site over `S` and then restricting it to the small étale site of `T` along `f`
is pulling it back along `f_{small}` directly.

This is the identity the clauses of Stacks 0DDH about `π_S^{-1}` reduce to: it converts the
comparison of big-site cohomology over `T` with small-site cohomology of `i_f^{-1}` into a
statement about `f_{small}^{-1}`.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleRestrictionProjectionPullbackIso :
    (SmallEtale.inclusion B S.obj S.property).sheafPullback A
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property) ⋙
      (smallEtaleToBigEtaleFunctor B T S f).sheafPushforwardContinuous A
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)
        (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property) ≅
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback A
      (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites_ringUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I at the universe of the structure rings.** Base change along `f : T ⟶ S` defines
a morphism of sites from the small étale site of `T` to that of `S`, for sheaves of sets valued in
the universe `u` of the sections of the structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public instance smallEtaleBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites_ringUniverse :
    IsMorphismOfSites.{u} (smallEtaleBaseChange B f)
      (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)
declarations.comment: small_etale_morphism at the universe of the structure rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, base-change continuity.** Base change along a morphism in a big étale
site is a continuous functor between the corresponding small étale sites.
declarations.statement:
public instance smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    Functor.IsContinuous (smallEtaleBaseChange B f)
      (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, small étale morphism.** Base change along `f : T ⟶ S` defines a
morphism of sites from the small étale site of `T` to that of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public instance smallEtaleBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1} (smallEtaleBaseChange B f)
      (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmallEtalePushforwardCommIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, commutative diagram.** The square formed by small étale base change, big
étale base change, and the two projections from big to small étale topoi commutes on direct
images.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmallEtalePushforwardCommIso :
    (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B T.obj T.property).pushforward ⋙
        (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
          (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property) ≅
      (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward ⋙
        (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, big-site factorization.** The inverse-image functor of `i_f` is naturally
isomorphic to the inverse image of `f_big ∘ i_T`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso :
    (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage ≅
      (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage ⋙
        (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B T T (𝟙 T)).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, big-site factorization.** The direct-image comparison for
`i_f = f_big ∘ i_T`, naturally in the small étale sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso :
    (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward ≅
      (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B T T (𝟙 T)).pushforward ⋙
        (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePushforwardIsoBigFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, small-site factorization.** The small étale direct image is canonically the
composite of inclusion into the big étale topos over `T`, big-site direct image along `f`, and
projection to the small étale topos of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtalePushforwardIsoBigFactorization :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property) ≅
      (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B T T (𝟙 T)).pushforward ⋙
        (bigEtaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward ⋙
          (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePushforwardIsoDirectFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021I, small-site factorization.** The small étale direct image is canonically the
composite of the direct morphism `i_f` to the big étale topos over `S` and its projection.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtalePushforwardIsoDirectFactorization :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property) ≅
      (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward ⋙
        (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_idIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** Small étale base change along an identity morphism is the identity
functor, since pullback along an identity is.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleBaseChange_idIso (X : B.Scheme) :
    smallEtaleBaseChange B (𝟙 X) ≅ 𝟭 (SmallEtale B X.obj X.property)
declarations.comment: small étale site functor at the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafPullbackIdIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** Inverse image along the identity morphism of a scheme is the identity on
sheaves on its small étale site, for any coefficient category.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleSheafPullbackIdIso (X : B.Scheme) (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} A]
    [((smallEtaleBaseChange B (𝟙 X)).sheafPushforwardContinuous A
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).IsRightAdjoint] :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B (𝟙 X)).sheafPullback A
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≅
      𝟭 (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) A)
declarations.comment: small étale inverse image at the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafPullbackCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** Inverse image along a composite of morphisms of a big étale site is the
composite of the inverse images, for any coefficient category.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleSheafPullbackCompIso (X Y Z : B.Scheme) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} A]
    [((smallEtaleBaseChange B g).sheafPushforwardContinuous A
      (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)).IsRightAdjoint]
    [((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous A
      (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).IsRightAdjoint]
    [((smallEtaleBaseChange B (f ≫ g)).sheafPushforwardContinuous A
      (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).IsRightAdjoint] :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B g).sheafPullback A
        (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property) ⋙
      (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback A
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≅
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B (f ≫ g)).sheafPullback A
      (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
declarations.comment: small étale inverse images, general coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_compIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** The canonical comparison of successive small étale base changes with
base change along the composite, characterized by its image under the inclusion of the small
étale category.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_compIso_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** The small-site comparison is the canonical comparison of pullbacks in
the ambient slice category, after forgetting the étale condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleBaseChange_compIso_app
    (U : SmallEtale B Z.obj Z.property) :
    (SmallEtale.inclusion B X.obj X.property).map
      ((smallEtaleBaseChange_compIso B X Y Z f g).val.hom.app U) =
    (Over.pullbackComp f g).inv.app U.obj
declarations.comment: canonicity of small étale site composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** The canonical big-site direct-image comparison, obtained from the
base-change formula and the composition comparison of pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigEtaleMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso :
    (bigEtaleMorphism B X Y f).pushforward ⋙
        (bigEtaleMorphism B Y Z g).pushforward ≅
      (bigEtaleMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** The inverse-image comparison is the mate of the big direct-image
comparison under the three geometric adjunctions.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigEtaleMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso :
    (bigEtaleMorphism B Y Z g).inverseImage ⋙
        (bigEtaleMorphism B X Y f).inverseImage ≅
      (bigEtaleMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** The direct-image comparison induced by the canonical composition
comparison of small-site base-change functors.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ⋙
      (smallEtaleBaseChange B g).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property) ≅
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B (f ≫ g)).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021J.** The inverse-image comparison is the mate of the small direct-image
comparison under the three sheaf adjunctions.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B g).sheafPullback
        (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property) ⋙
      (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback
        (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≅
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B (f ≫ g)).sheafPullback
      (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSheafData
declarations.doc:
A compatible system of sheaves on the small étale sites of the schemes over `S`: a sheaf on
the small étale site of every `T / S`, a comparison map from the inverse image of the sheaf at `T`
to the sheaf at `T'` along every morphism `T' ⟶ T` over `S`, subject to the cocycle condition for
a composite and to being an isomorphism whenever the morphism is étale.
declarations.statement: public structure BigEtaleSheafData

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.characterizeSheafBigEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 021K.** A sheaf on the big étale site over `S` is precisely a
compatible family of sheaves on the small étale sites of all the schemes over `S`: the
restriction functor is an equivalence of categories.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.characterizeSheafBigEtale_functor_comp_eval
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 021K.** Evaluating the equivalence at a scheme `T` over `S` is
restriction to the small étale site of `T`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.characterizeSheafBigEtale_pullback_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 021K.** Under the equivalence the adjoint of each comparison map is
restriction along the projection `U ×[T] T' ⟶ U`, for every small étale object `U` of `T`; so
the equivalence determines the comparison maps as well as the sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem characterizeSheafBigEtale_pullback_app
    (F : Sheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    {T T' : BigEtaleOver B S hS} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (U : SmallEtale B T.left.1 T.left.property) :
    ((B.smallPullbackAdjunction f.left (Type (max (u + 1) v))).homEquiv _ _
        (((characterizeSheafBigEtale.{u, v} B S hS).functor.obj F).pullback f)).hom.app
          (op U) =
      F.obj.map (bigEtaleBaseChangeProjection B S hS f U).op

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coveringPrecoverage_le_of_isFiner
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021N and its companions.**  Along the chain, the precoverages of jointly surjective
families of schemes are nested: an open immersion is étale, an étale morphism is smooth, a smooth
morphism is syntomic, and a syntomic morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation.
declarations.comment: the five precoverages of schemes are nested along the chain of topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smoothPrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc: **Stacks 021N.** Every smooth covering family is an fppf covering family.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etalePrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc: **Stacks 021N.** Every étale covering family is an fppf covering family.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etalePrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage :
    Scheme.etalePrecoverage ≤ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.syntomicPrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021N.** Every syntomic covering family is an fppf covering family: a syntomic
morphism is flat by Stacks 01UL and locally of finite presentation by Stacks 01UK.
declarations.statement:
public theorem syntomicPrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage :
    Scheme.precoverage (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ≤ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpens_isStandardFppfCovering
declarations.doc:
Every fppf covering `{Tᵢ ⟶ T}` of an affine scheme `T` is refined by a finite fppf covering
`{Uⱼ ⟶ T}_{j < m}` in which every `Uⱼ` is an affine open subscheme of some `T_{i(j)}`, the map
`Uⱼ ⟶ T` being the inclusion `Uⱼ ⟶ T_{i(j)}` followed by `T_{i(j)} ⟶ T`; in particular the
refinement is a standard fppf covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpens_isStandardFppfCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    (𝒰 : T.Cover Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (i : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) (U : ∀ j, (𝒰.X (i j)).affineOpens),
      Presieve.ofArrows (fun j ↦ (U j : (𝒰.X (i j)).Opens).toScheme)
          (fun j ↦ (U j : (𝒰.X (i j)).Opens).ι ≫ 𝒰.f (i j)) ∈
        Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardFppfCovering
        (fun j ↦ (U j : (𝒰.X (i j)).Opens).toScheme)
        (fun j ↦ (U j : (𝒰.X (i j)).Opens).ι ≫ 𝒰.f (i j))
declarations.comment: finite fppf refinement by affine opens of the members

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardFppfCovering
declarations.doc:
A family `fᵢ : Uᵢ ⟶ T` is a **standard fppf covering** if it is finite, its
source and target schemes are affine, every `fᵢ` is flat and of finite presentation,
and the images of the `fᵢ` cover `T`.
declarations.statement:
public structure IsStandardFppfCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T) : Prop

A big fppf site, retaining all choices in the construction: the initial set of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.IsCovering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffineFppfInclusion_isCocontinuous

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021W.** The morphism of big fppf topoi induced by postcomposition along
`f`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigFppfMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (B.topology.over T) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (B.topology.over S) (Type (u + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigFppfLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021W.** The left adjoint of the inverse image is sheaf pullback along
postcomposition.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigFppfLowerShriekAdjunction :
    (Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (B.topology.over T) (B.topology.over S) ⊣
        (bigFppfMorphism B T S f).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigFppfLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks

        (B.topology.over T) (B.topology.over S))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigFppfMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021X.** Composition of the morphisms of big fppf topoi agrees, naturally on
sheaves, with the morphism attached to the composite map of schemes.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigFppfMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) {X Y Z : B.Schemes}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    (bigFppfMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)).pushforward ≅
      ((bigFppfMorphism B Y Z g).comp
        (bigFppfMorphism B X Y f)).pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigFppfMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021X.** The inverse-image comparison is the mate of the direct-image
comparison.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigFppfMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) {X Y Z : B.Schemes}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    (bigFppfMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)).inverseImage ≅
      ((bigFppfMorphism B Y Z g).comp
        (bigFppfMorphism B X Y f)).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigFppfMorphism_comp_adjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 021X.** The two canonical comparisons respect the units of the geometric
morphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bigFppfMorphism_comp_adjunction
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) {X Y Z : B.Schemes}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (V : Sheaf (B.topology.over Z) (Type (u + 1))) :
    let h := bigFppfMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)
    let k := (bigFppfMorphism B Y Z g).comp
      (bigFppfMorphism B X Y f)
    h.adj.unit.app V ≫
        h.pushforward.map ((bigFppfMorphism_comp_inverseImageIso B f g).hom.app V) ≫
        (bigFppfMorphism_comp_pushforwardIso B f g).hom.app
          (k.inverseImage.obj V) = k.adj.unit.app V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smoothPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
The smooth precoverage on the category of schemes: its covering families are the jointly
surjective families of smooth morphisms.
declarations.statement: public def smoothPrecoverage : Precoverage Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage_le_smoothPrecoverage
declarations.doc: Every Zariski covering is a smooth covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem zariskiPrecoverage_le_smoothPrecoverage :
    zariskiPrecoverage.{u} ≤ smoothPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.singleton_mem_smoothPrecoverage_of_isIso
declarations.doc: The singleton family of an isomorphism `T' ⟶ T` is a smooth covering of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem singleton_mem_smoothPrecoverage_of_isIso {T' T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    [IsIso f] : Presieve.singleton f ∈ smoothPrecoverage T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ofArrows_comp_mem_smoothPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
If `{fᵢ : Tᵢ ⟶ T}` is a smooth covering and `{gᵢⱼ : Tᵢⱼ ⟶ Tᵢ}` is a smooth covering of each
`Tᵢ`, then the composite family `{gᵢⱼ ≫ fᵢ : Tᵢⱼ ⟶ T}` is a smooth covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ofArrows_comp_mem_smoothPrecoverage {I : Type w} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    {T' : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows T' f ∈ smoothPrecoverage T) {J : I → Type w'}
    {T'' : ∀ i, J i → Scheme.{u}} (g : ∀ i j, T'' i j ⟶ T' i)
    (hg : ∀ i, Presieve.ofArrows (T'' i) (g i) ∈ smoothPrecoverage (T' i)) :
    Presieve.ofArrows (fun p : Σ i, J i ↦ T'' p.1 p.2) (fun p ↦ g p.1 p.2 ≫ f p.1) ∈
      smoothPrecoverage T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ofArrows_pullback_mem_smoothPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
If `{fᵢ : Tᵢ ⟶ T}` is a smooth covering and `g : T' ⟶ T` is a morphism of schemes, then the
family of first projections `{T' ×_T Tᵢ ⟶ T'}` is a smooth covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ofArrows_pullback_mem_smoothPrecoverage {I : Type w} {T T' : Scheme.{u}}
    {Tᵢ : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows Tᵢ f ∈ smoothPrecoverage T) (g : T' ⟶ T) :
    Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ pullback g (f i)) (fun i ↦ pullback.fst g (f i)) ∈
      smoothPrecoverage T'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_affine_standardSmooth_refinement
declarations.doc:
A smooth covering of an affine scheme has a finite refinement by affine schemes which are
standard smooth over the target; each member of the refinement is an open subscheme of a member of
the original covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_affine_standardSmooth_refinement {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    (U : T.Cover.{v} (Scheme.precoverage (@Smooth.{u}))) :
    ∃ (V : T.AffineCover.{u} (@Smooth.{u}))
        (refinement : V.cover.toPreZeroHypercover.Hom U.toPreZeroHypercover),
      Finite V.I₀ ∧
        (∀ j, IsStandardSmooth (V.f j)) ∧
          ∀ j, IsOpenImmersion (refinement.h₀ j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardSmoothCovering
declarations.doc:
A finite family `fᵢ : Uᵢ ⟶ T` of morphisms between affine schemes is a
**standard smooth covering** if every `fᵢ` is standard smooth and their images
cover `T`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStandardSmoothCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    {I : Type v} [Finite I] (U : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (U i)]
    (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSyntomicCovering
declarations.doc:
A family `fᵢ : Tᵢ ⟶ T` is a **syntomic covering** if every `fᵢ` is
syntomic and their images cover `T`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsSyntomicCovering {T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    {I : Type v} (X : I → AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSyntomicCovering_of_mem_smoothPrecoverage
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0226.** Every smooth covering is a syntomic covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSyntomicCovering_of_mem_smoothPrecoverage
    {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} {X : I → Scheme.{u}} {f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T}
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.precoverage (@Smooth.{u}) T) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSyntomicCovering_of_mem_etalePrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_isFpqcCoveringFamily
declarations.doc:
A family lies in Mathlib's `Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage` if and only if it is an fpqc covering
in the sense of Stacks 022B: every member is flat and every affine open of the target is the
union of the images of finitely many affine opens of the sources.  Mathlib's quasi-compactness
condition asks for quasi-compact opens instead of affine ones; a quasi-compact open is a finite
union of affine opens, and an affine open is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public lemma ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_isFpqcCoveringFamily :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ↔ IsFpqcCoveringFamily X f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff
declarations.doc:
**The fpqc coverings of a scheme.** A family `{f i : X i ⟶ T}` lies in Mathlib's fpqc
precoverage `Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage` if and only if it is an fpqc covering in the sense of the
source: every `f i` is flat, and every affine open `U` of `T` is the union of the images
`f (a j) '' V j` of finitely many affine opens `V j` of the `X (a j)`, `j : Fin n`.

Mathlib's precoverage also asks for the family to be jointly surjective; the source remarks right
after the definition that this follows from the covering condition, and the right-hand side here
does not ask for it.
declarations.statement:
public lemma ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, Flat (f i)) ∧
        ∀ U : T.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
          ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → I) (V : ∀ j, (X (a j)).Opens),
            (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
              ⋃ j, f (a j) '' (V j : Set (X (a j))) = (U : Set T))
declarations.comment: the fpqc coverings: Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage, with the definition's condition

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage
registrations.comment: fpqc coverings: the families that are flat, jointly surjective and quasi-compact (QuasiCompactCover, which carries Mathlib's own 022B attribution, is the quasi-compactness condition alone)

declarations.name: isFpqcCoveringFamily_of_isIso_and_comp_and_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 022D.** Let `T` be a scheme.
1. If `T' ⟶ T` is an isomorphism, then `{ T' ⟶ T }` is an fpqc covering of `T`.
2. If `{ T i ⟶ T }` is an fpqc covering and for each `i` the family `{ T i j ⟶ T i }` is an
   fpqc covering, then `{ T i j ⟶ T }` (indexed by all pairs `(i, j)`) is an fpqc covering.
3. If `{ T i ⟶ T }` is an fpqc covering and `T' ⟶ T` is a morphism of schemes, then
   `{ T' ×_T T i ⟶ T' }` is an fpqc covering.

Here "fpqc covering" is Stacks' own notion `IsFpqcCoveringFamily` (Definition 022B).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFpqcCoveringFamily_of_isIso_and_comp_and_pullback :
    (∀ {T T' : Scheme.{u₁}} (f : T' ⟶ T) [IsIso f],
      IsFpqcCoveringFamily (fun _ : Unit => T') (fun _ => f)) ∧
    (∀ {ι : Type w₁} {T : Scheme.{u₁}} {T' : ι → Scheme.{u₁}} {f : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ T}
      {J : ι → Type w₂} {T'' : ∀ i, J i → Scheme.{u₁}} {g : ∀ i j, T'' i j ⟶ T' i},
      IsFpqcCoveringFamily T' f → (∀ i, IsFpqcCoveringFamily (T'' i) (g i)) →
      IsFpqcCoveringFamily (fun p : Σ i, J i => T'' p.1 p.2) (fun p => g p.1 p.2 ≫ f p.1)) ∧
    (∀ {ι : Type w₁} {T : Scheme.{u₁}} {T' : ι → Scheme.{u₁}} {f : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ T}
      {S : Scheme.{u₁}} (g : S ⟶ T), IsFpqcCoveringFamily T' f →
      IsFpqcCoveringFamily (fun i => pullback g (f i)) (fun i => pullback.fst g (f i)))
declarations.comment: all three parts, for fpqc coverings in the sense of Definition 022B (`IsFpqcCoveringFamily`: flat members, every affine open of the base covered by the images of finitely many affine opens): (1) an isomorphism is an fpqc covering, (2) composites of fpqc coverings are fpqc coverings, (3) base changes of fpqc coverings are fpqc coverings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_affineCover_flat_refinement

An fpqc covering of an affine scheme admits a refinement by a standard fpqc

public theorem exists_finite_affineCover_flat_refinement {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]

      Finite V.I₀ ∧ V.cover.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ∧
        ∀ j, IsOpenImmersion (refinement.h₀ j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_iff_and_standardCovering_iff_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 022H.** A presheaf of sets `F` on the category of schemes satisfies the sheaf
property for the fpqc topology if and only if it satisfies
(1) the sheaf property for every Zariski covering, that is, every jointly surjective family of
open immersions, and
(2) the sheaf property for every standard fpqc covering, that is, every finite jointly surjective
family of flat morphisms with affine sources over an affine base.
Moreover, in the presence of (1), property (2) is equivalent to
(2') the sheaf property for `{V ⟶ U}` with `V` and `U` affine and `V ⟶ U` faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_fpqcTopology_iff_and_standardCovering_iff_faithfullyFlat
    (F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :
    (Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u} F ↔
      (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (R : Presieve T), R ∈ Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage T →
          Presieve.IsSheafFor F R) ∧
        ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (𝒱 : T.AffineCover.{w} (@Flat.{u})), Finite 𝒱.I₀ →
          Presieve.IsSheafFor F 𝒱.cover.presieve₀) ∧
    ((∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (R : Presieve T), R ∈ Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage T →
        Presieve.IsSheafFor F R) →
      ((∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (𝒱 : T.AffineCover.{w} (@Flat.{u})), Finite 𝒱.I₀ →
          Presieve.IsSheafFor F 𝒱.cover.presieve₀) ↔
        ∀ {V U : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine V] [IsAffine U] (g : V ⟶ U), Flat g → Surjective g →
          Presieve.IsSheafFor F (Presieve.singleton g)))
declarations.comment: both statements of the lemma: the fpqc sheaf condition is equivalent to (1) ∧ (2), and under (1), (2) is equivalent to (2')

    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : S.size < cutoff τ B) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toposRetraction
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def toposRetraction {τ : CoveringTopology}
    (B B' : BigSite.{u} τ) (h : IsContained B B') :
    let J := siteTopology τ B
    let K := siteTopology τ B'
    let F := inclusion (Classical.choose h)
    let : F.IsCocontinuous J K := inclusion_isCocontinuous B B' h
    let : F.IsContinuous J K := (inclusion_isMorphismOfSites B B' h).toIsContinuous
    ToposRetraction (siteCategory B) (siteCategory B') J K F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toposRetractionOver
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def toposRetractionOver {τ : CoveringTopology}
    (B B' : BigSite.{u} τ) (h : IsContained B B')
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : S.size < cutoff τ B) :
    let J := overTopology τ B S hS
    let K := overTopology τ B' S (largerContains h hS)
    let F := inclusionOver h S hS
    let : F.IsCocontinuous J K := inclusionOver_isCocontinuous B B' h S hS
    let : F.IsContinuous J K := (inclusionOver_isMorphismOfSites B B' h S hS).toIsContinuous
    ToposRetraction (Over (base B S hS))
      (Over (base B' S (largerContains h hS))) J K F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeOverPoints

**Stacks Project, Tag 022S** (1). A group scheme over `S`: a scheme `G` over `S` together
with a multiplication morphism `m : G ×_S G ⟶ G` of schemes over `S`, such that for every
scheme `T` over `S` the induced multiplication makes the set of `T`-valued points
`G(T) = Hom_{Over S}(T, G)` into a group.

`S`: a morphism `ψ : G ⟶ G'` of schemes over `S` such that for every scheme `T` over `S`, the
induced map `ψ : G(T) ⟶ G'(T)` is a homomorphism of groups.

declarations.comment: morphisms of group schemes over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.grpObjPullbackObj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.pointsMulEquiv
declarations.doc:
For every scheme `T` over `S'`, the pair `(G_{S'}(T), m_{S'})` is a group, and composition
with the projection `G ×_S S' ⟶ G` identifies it with the group `(G(T), m)` of morphisms
`T ⟶ G` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointsMulEquiv (T : Over S') :
    (T ⟶ (Over.pullback f).obj G) ≃* ((Over.map f).obj T ⟶ G)
