declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoMultiplicativeGroupPoints_hom_app
declarations.doc:
The forward map in `AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoMultiplicativeGroupPoints` is
composition with the first pullback projection. This characterizes the isomorphism and its
canonical orientation.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangePointsIsoMultiplicativeGroupPoints_hom_app
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ)
    (f : T.unop ⟶ Scheme.asOver (multiplicativeGroupBaseChange S) S) :
    (baseChangePointsIsoMultiplicativeGroupPoints S).hom.app T f =
      f.left ≫ pullback.fst
        (multiplicativeGroupULift ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
        (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022U.** The group of `T`-points of the multiplicative group over `S` is
canonically the unit group `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)ˣ`, naturally in the `S`-scheme `T`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    yonedaGrpObj (Scheme.asOver (multiplicativeGroupBaseChange S) S) ≅ globalUnits S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits_hom_app
declarations.doc:
The forward map in `AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits` sends a point to the
pullback of the Laurent coordinate along its composite with the first pullback projection.
Besides characterizing the natural isomorphism, this pins down the multiplication on the group
scheme as multiplication of global units.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits_hom_app
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ)
    (f : T.unop ⟶ Scheme.asOver (multiplicativeGroupBaseChange S) S) :
    (baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits S).hom.app T f =
    multiplicativeGroupPointUnit
        (f.left ≫ pullback.fst
          (multiplicativeGroupULift ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
          (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022V.** The underlying scheme of the additive group over the integers
is the spectrum of the polynomial ring `ℤ[X]`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev additiveGroup : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupCanonicallyOver
declarations.doc:
The canonical structure morphism from the additive group scheme to the spectrum of the
universe-polymorphic copy of `ℤ`, induced by the inclusion of constant polynomials.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance additiveGroupCanonicallyOver :
    additiveGroup.CanonicallyOver (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additionMorphism_pullbackSpecIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022V.** Under the canonical identification of the fibre product
with `Spec (R[X] ⊗[R] R[X])`, addition is induced by the ring map sending
`X` to `X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ X`.
declarations.statement:
lemma additionMorphism_pullbackSpecIso :
    (pullbackSpecIso (ULift.{u} ℤ) (Polynomial (ULift.{u} ℤ))
      (Polynomial (ULift.{u} ℤ))).inv ≫ additionMorphism =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom additionRingHom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupGrpObj
declarations.doc: The group-object structure on the affine line over the integers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance additiveGroupGrpObj :
    GrpObj (Over.mk (additiveGroup ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupGrpObj_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022V.** Multiplication in the additive group scheme is the usual
addition morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem additiveGroupGrpObj_mul :
    μ[Over.mk (additiveGroup ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))].left = additionMorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupBaseChangeGrpObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022V.** The base change of the additive group scheme to every scheme
`S` is a group scheme over `S`, with the canonical pullbacks of the integral group operations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance additiveGroupBaseChangeGrpObj (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    GrpObj (Scheme.asOver (additiveGroupBaseChange S) S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.globalSections_representableBy_additiveGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022V.** The set-valued global-sections functor on schemes is
represented by the additive group scheme `Spec (ℤ[X])`.
declarations.statement:
theorem globalSections_representableBy_additiveGroup :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).RepresentableBy (additiveGroup : Scheme.{u}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupBaseChangePointsIsoGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022V.** For every scheme `S`, the group-valued functor of points of
the additive group scheme over `S` is naturally isomorphic to the additive group of global
sections of the varying `S`-scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def additiveGroupBaseChangePointsIsoGlobalSections (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    yonedaGrpObj (Scheme.asOver (additiveGroupBaseChange S) S) ≅ globalSectionsAdditive S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupBaseChangePointsIsoGlobalSections_hom_app
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical identification of additive-group points with global sections, a point is
sent to the pullback of the universal polynomial coordinate along its projection to the integral
additive group. This characterizes the natural isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem additiveGroupBaseChangePointsIsoGlobalSections_hom_app
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ)
    (f : T.unop ⟶ Scheme.asOver (additiveGroupBaseChange S) S) :
    (additiveGroupBaseChangePointsIsoGlobalSections S).hom.app T f =
      additiveGroupPointSection
        (f.left ≫ pullback.fst
          (additiveGroup ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
          (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearScheme
declarations.doc: The general linear scheme `GL_n` over the integers.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev generalLinearScheme (n : ℕ) : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearGroup_representableBy_generalLinearScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022W.** The functor of invertible `n` by `n`
matrices over global sections is represented by the general linear scheme `GL_n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalLinearGroup_representableBy_generalLinearScheme (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((generalLinearGroupFunctor.{u} n ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy
      (generalLinearScheme.{u} n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearSchemeGrpObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022W.** The general linear scheme over the integers is a group
scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance generalLinearSchemeGrpObj (n : ℕ) :
    GrpObj (Over.mk (generalLinearStructureMorphism.{u} n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_multiplicationRingHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022W.** Multiplication on the general linear scheme is induced by
the coordinate-ring homomorphism sending `xᵢⱼ` to `∑ k, xᵢₖ ⊗ xₖⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_multiplicationRingHom (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ f : generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n →+* generalLinearTensorSquare.{u} n,
      ((pullbackSpecIso (ULift.{u} ℤ) (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n)
          (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n)).inv ≫
          μ[Over.mk (generalLinearStructureMorphism.{u} n)].left =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f)) ∧
        ∀ i j : Fin n,
          f (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
              (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n) (MvPolynomial.X (i, j))) =
            ∑ k : Fin n,
          @TensorProduct.tmul (ULift.{u} ℤ) CommRing.toCommSemiring
                (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n) (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n)
                CommRing.toCommSemiring.toAddCommMonoid
                CommRing.toCommSemiring.toAddCommMonoid
                Algebra.toModule Algebra.toModule
                (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
                  (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n) (MvPolynomial.X (i, k)))
                (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
                  (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{u} n) (MvPolynomial.X (k, j)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearBaseChange
declarations.doc: The general linear group scheme over `S`, obtained by base change from `Spec ℤ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev generalLinearBaseChange (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) : Over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoGeneralLinearPoints
declarations.doc: Points of the base change are naturally points of the integral general linear scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangePointsIsoGeneralLinearPoints (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    yoneda.obj (generalLinearBaseChange n S) ≅
      (Over.forget S).op ⋙ yoneda.obj (generalLinearScheme n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePointsIsoGeneralLinearPoints_hom_app
declarations.doc: The pointwise map of the base-change comparison is composition with the first projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangePointsIsoGeneralLinearPoints_hom_app (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) (f : T.unop ⟶ generalLinearBaseChange n S) :
    (baseChangePointsIsoGeneralLinearPoints n S).hom.app T f =
      f.left ≫ pullback.fst (generalLinearStructureMorphism.{u} n)
        (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearBaseChangeGrpObj
declarations.doc: Base change preserves the group-scheme structure of the general linear group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance generalLinearBaseChangeGrpObj (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    GrpObj (generalLinearBaseChange n S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangeGroupPointsIso
declarations.doc:
The group-valued points of the base-changed scheme are invertible matrices over global
sections, naturally in the scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeGroupPointsIso (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    yonedaGrpObj (generalLinearBaseChange n S) ≅ generalLinearGroupOverFunctor n S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangeGroupPointsIso_hom_app
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison sends an `S`-point to the invertible matrix obtained by pulling
back the generic coordinates from the integral general linear scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeGroupPointsIso_hom_app (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) (f : T.unop ⟶ generalLinearBaseChange n S) (i j : Fin n) :
    ((baseChangeGroupPointsIso n S).hom.app T f).val i j =
      (Scheme.Γ.map
        (f.left ≫ pullback.fst (generalLinearStructureMorphism.{u} n)
          (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S)).op).hom (generalLinearCoordinateSection n i j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearSchemeGrpObjOverIntegers
declarations.doc: The group scheme structure of `GLₙ` over the integers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance generalLinearSchemeGrpObjOverIntegers (n : ℕ) :
    GrpObj (Over.mk (generalLinearStructureMorphismOverIntegers n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.generalLinearSchemeGrpObjOverIntegers_mul
declarations.doc: Multiplication on `GLₙ` is matrix multiplication, on generic matrix entries.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalLinearSchemeGrpObjOverIntegers_mul (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ m : generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n →+* generalLinearTensorSquareOverIntegers n,
      (pullbackSpecIso ℤ (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n)
        (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n)).inv ≫
          μ[Over.mk (generalLinearStructureMorphismOverIntegers n)].left =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom m) ∧
      (∀ i j : Fin n,
        m (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{0} ℤ))
          (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n) (MvPolynomial.X (i, j))) =
          ∑ k : Fin n,
          @TensorProduct.tmul ℤ CommRing.toCommSemiring
              (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n) (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n)
              CommRing.toCommSemiring.toAddCommMonoid CommRing.toCommSemiring.toAddCommMonoid
              Algebra.toModule Algebra.toModule
              (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{0} ℤ))
                (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n) (MvPolynomial.X (i, k)))
                (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{0} ℤ))
                  (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n) (MvPolynomial.X (k, j))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverIntegers
declarations.doc: The determinant as a morphism of group schemes over `Spec ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverIntegers (n : ℕ) :
    Grp.mk (Over.mk (generalLinearStructureMorphismOverIntegers n)) ⟶
      Grp.mk (multiplicativeGroup.asOver (Spec (.of ℤ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverIntegers_spec
declarations.doc: On coordinate rings, determinant sends the Laurent variable to the generic determinant.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverIntegers_spec (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ g : LaurentPolynomial ℤ →+* generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n,
      (determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverIntegers n).hom.hom.left =
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g) ∧
        g (LaurentPolynomial.T 1) =
          algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) (ULift.{0} ℤ))
            (generalLinearCoordinateRing.{0} n) (generalLinearDeterminant.{0} n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverULiftIntegers
declarations.doc: The determinant morphism of group schemes over the universe-lifted integers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverULiftIntegers (n : ℕ) :
    Grp.mk (Over.mk (generalLinearStructureMorphism.{u} n)) ⟶
      Grp.mk (multiplicativeGroupULift.asOver (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphism
declarations.doc:
The determinant morphism from the base-changed general linear group scheme to the
base-changed multiplicative group scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantGroupSchemeMorphism (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    Grp.mk (generalLinearBaseChange n S) ⟶
      Grp.mk (Scheme.asOver (multiplicativeGroupBaseChange S) S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphism_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The underlying scheme morphism is the pullback of the universal determinant
over the universe-lifted integers, for every base scheme in that universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantGroupSchemeMorphism_isBaseChange (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    (determinantGroupSchemeMorphism n S).hom.hom =
      (Over.pullback (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S)).map
        (determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverULiftIntegers n).hom.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphism_apply
declarations.doc:
The base-changed determinant sends an invertible matrix over the global sections of
an `S`-scheme to its determinant, viewed as a global unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantGroupSchemeMorphism_apply (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) (f : T.unop ⟶ generalLinearBaseChange n S) :
    (baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits S).hom.app T
        (((yonedaGrp.map (determinantGroupSchemeMorphism n S)).app T) f) =
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det ((baseChangeGroupPointsIso n S).hom.app T f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.determinantGroupSchemeMorphism_baseChange
declarations.doc:
After projecting the base-changed morphism to the integral models, it is the
integral determinant morphism. The coefficient map compares `ℤ` with `ULift ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantGroupSchemeMorphism_baseChange (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{0}) :
    (determinantGroupSchemeMorphism n S).hom.hom.left ≫
        pullback.fst (multiplicativeGroupULift ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{0} ℤ)))
          (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S) ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapRingHom ℤ
            (ULift.ringEquiv.{0, 0}.symm.toRingHom : ℤ →+* ULift.{0} ℤ))) =
      pullback.fst (generalLinearStructureMorphism.{0} n) (specULiftZIsTerminal.from S) ≫
        (determinantGroupSchemeMorphismOverIntegers n).hom.hom.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeOverPoints.Action
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022Z** (1). An action of the group scheme `G` over `S` on the scheme
`X` over `S`: a morphism `a : G ×_S X ⟶ X` of schemes over `S` such that for every scheme `T`
over `S` the map `G(T) × X(T) ⟶ X(T)`, `(g, x) ↦ a ∘ (g, x)`, defines the structure of a
`G(T)`-set on `X(T)`, namely the identity of `G(T)` acts trivially and `(g h) x = g (h x)`.
declarations.statement: structure Action (X : Over S)
declarations.comment: part (1): an action of a group scheme on a scheme over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeOverPoints.Action.IsEquivariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022Z** (2). A morphism `ψ : X ⟶ Y` of schemes over `S`, where `X` and
`Y` carry actions `A` and `B` of `G`, is `G`-equivariant if for every scheme `T` over `S` the
map `ψ : X(T) ⟶ Y(T)` is a morphism of `G(T)`-sets.
declarations.statement: def IsEquivariant (A : G.Action X) (B : G.Action Y) (ψ : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeOverPoints.Action.equivModObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022Z** (1), compared with Mathlib. Actions of the group scheme `G`
on `X` in the functor-of-points sense are the same as module objects `ModObj` over the
internal group object `G.grpObj` of `Over S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivModObj (X : Over S) :
    G.Action X ≃ (letI := G.grpObj; ModObj G.obj X)
declarations.comment: part (1): actions are the module objects over the internal group object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeOverPoints.Action.isEquivariant_iff_isModHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 022Z** (2), compared with Mathlib. A morphism `ψ : X ⟶ Y` over `S` is
`G`-equivariant for actions `A` and `B` exactly when it is a morphism `IsModHom` of the
associated module objects over the internal group object `G.grpObj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivariant_iff_isModHom (A : G.Action X) (B : G.Action Y) (ψ : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsEquivariant A B ψ ↔
      letI := G.grpObj
      letI := A.modObj
      letI := B.modObj
      IsModHom G.obj ψ
declarations.comment: part (2): equivariant morphisms are the morphisms of module objects

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.eq_id_of_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
In a groupoid, a family of endomorphisms which is a right unit for composition is the family
of identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_id_of_comp_eq (e : ∀ X : C, X ⟶ X) (he : ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), f ≫ e Y = f)
    (X : C) : e X = 𝟙 X
declarations.comment: the identity map e is uniquely determined

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.eq_inv_of_comp_eq_id
declarations.doc: In a groupoid, a right inverse of a morphism is its inverse.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_inv_of_comp_eq_id (i : ∀ {X Y : C}, (X ⟶ Y) → (Y ⟶ X))
    (hi : ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), f ≫ i f = 𝟙 X) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    i f = Groupoid.inv f
declarations.comment: the inverse map i is uniquely determined

declarations.name: Prefunctor.map_id_of_map_comp
declarations.doc: A map of groupoids compatible with composition preserves identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_id_of_map_comp (F : C ⥤q D)
    (hF : ∀ {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), F.map (f ≫ g) = F.map f ≫ F.map g) (X : C) :
    F.map (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (F.obj X)
declarations.comment: a map of groupoids compatible with composition preserves identities

declarations.name: Prefunctor.map_inv_of_map_comp
declarations.doc: A map of groupoids compatible with composition preserves inverses.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_inv_of_map_comp (F : C ⥤q D)
    (hF : ∀ {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), F.map (f ≫ g) = F.map f ≫ F.map g)
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : F.map (Groupoid.inv f) = Groupoid.inv (F.map f)
declarations.comment: a map of groupoids compatible with composition preserves inverses

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme
declarations.doc:
A groupoid object in schemes over `S`.

The fields `identity` and `inverse` are included as data, although they are uniquely determined
by `source`, `target` and `comp`.
declarations.statement: structure GroupoidScheme (S : Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.Hom
declarations.doc: A morphism of groupoid schemes.
declarations.statement: structure Hom {S : Scheme.{u}} (G H : GroupoidScheme S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.groupoidPreRelation_isPreEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc: The pre-relation underlying a groupoid scheme is a pre-equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem groupoidPreRelation_isPreEquivalenceRelation {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPreEquivalenceRelation (groupoidPreRelation G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_groupoidScheme_of_isEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
An equivalence relation on a scheme over `S` extends in a unique way to a groupoid scheme
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_groupoidScheme_of_isEquivalenceRelation (j : PreRelation R U)
    [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source] :
    ∃! G : GroupoidScheme S, ExtendsRelation j G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.groupoidSchemeOfAction
declarations.doc:
The action groupoid scheme of a group scheme action, with objects `X`, arrows `G ×_Y X`,
and the source, target, composition, identity, and inverse maps given by the standard
formulas.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def groupoidSchemeOfAction : ActionGroupoidConstruction Y G X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stabilizerGroupStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0235.** The stabilizer of a groupoid scheme is canonically a group
scheme over its object scheme, with multiplication induced by groupoid composition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerGroupStructure {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    { h : GrpObj (stabilizer G) // IsStabilizerGroupStructure G h }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stabilizerGroupStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0235.** The stabilizer of a groupoid scheme is canonically a group
scheme over its object scheme, with multiplication induced by groupoid composition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerGroupStructure {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    { h : GrpObj (stabilizer G) // IsStabilizerGroupStructure G h }
declarations.comment: the stabilizer group scheme of a groupoid scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stabilizerAction
declarations.doc:
The stabilizer group scheme acts canonically on the arrow scheme over the object scheme via
the target map; the action is induced by composition in the groupoid.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerAction {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    { h : ModObj (stabilizer G) (arrowsOverTarget G) // IsStabilizerAction G h }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData
declarations.doc:
Descent data for quasicoherent sheaves relative to a family `f i : X i ⟶ S`.

The underlying descent datum supplies the transition isomorphisms and their cocycle condition.
Morphisms in this full subcategory are componentwise morphisms commuting with every transition
isomorphism.  For chosen binary and triple fibre products,
`Pseudofunctor.DescentData'.descentDataEquivalence` is component-preserving and identifies this
with the full subcategory of the source's fibre-product presentation on quasicoherent objects.
declarations.statement:
abbrev QuasicoherentDescentData {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : I → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.pullFunctor
declarations.doc:
Pullback along a morphism of families defines a functor on quasicoherent descent data.

Its underlying functor is `Pseudofunctor.DescentData.pullFunctor`; quasicoherence of its
components follows from preservation of quasicoherence by pullback.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullFunctor (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 g) :
    QuasicoherentDescentData 𝒱.f ⥤ QuasicoherentDescentData 𝒰.f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.pullFunctor_comp_ι
declarations.doc:
After forgetting quasicoherence, `pullFunctor` is exactly the usual pullback functor on
descent data.  Thus its objects have components `g_i^* F_{α(i)}` and the pulled-back transition
isomorphisms, and its action on morphisms is componentwise pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullFunctor_comp_ι (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 g) :
    pullFunctor Φ ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ = ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙
        Pseudofunctor.DescentData.pullFunctor modulePullbackPseudofunctor
          (f := 𝒱.f) (p := g) (f' := 𝒰.f) (α := Φ.s₀) (p' := Φ.h₀) Φ.w₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.pullFunctorIsoOfEq
declarations.doc:
Morphisms of families inducing the same morphism of targets give naturally isomorphic
pullback functors on quasicoherent descent data.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullFunctorIsoOfEq {g' : U ⟶ V} (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 g)
    (Φ' : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 g') (h : g = g') : pullFunctor Φ ≅ pullFunctor Φ'
declarations.comment: part (3), functorial isomorphism when the maps of targets agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalDescentFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor sending a quasicoherent module on `S` to its canonical descent datum relative to
the family `f i : X i ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalDescentFunctor {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S) :
    Functor (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory
      (QuasicoherentDescentData f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.trivialDescentData
declarations.doc:
The trivial descent datum on a quasicoherent module, relative to the singleton family whose
only morphism is the identity of the base scheme.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.trivialDescentComponentIso
declarations.doc:
The sole component of the trivial descent datum is naturally isomorphic to the original
quasicoherent module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def trivialDescentComponentIso {S : Scheme.{u}} :
    trivialDescentComponentFunctor (S := S) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).ι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullTrivialDescentIso
declarations.doc:
Pulling the trivial descent datum back along a family gives, naturally in the
quasicoherent module, its canonical descent datum for that family.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullTrivialDescentIso {S : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{v} S) :
    canonicalDescentFunctor (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{0} (𝟙 S)).f ⋙
        QuasicoherentDescentData.pullFunctor (toTrivialFamily 𝒰) ≅
      canonicalDescentFunctor 𝒰.f
declarations.comment: part (2), pullback of the trivial datum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.IsEffective
declarations.doc:
A quasicoherent descent datum is effective if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent
datum of a quasicoherent module on the target.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEffective (D : QuasicoherentDescentData f) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.isEffective_zariski
declarations.doc:
**The effectivity half of Stacks 023E.**  Every quasi-coherent descent datum for a family
of open immersions whose images cover the target is effective.  This is
`Stacks.Descent.isEffective_of_essSurj_zariski` with its standing essential-surjectivity
hypothesis discharged by `Stacks.Descent.essSurj_toDescentData_zariski`; the full faithfulness
half is `Stacks.Descent.nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor_zariski`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor_zariski
declarations.doc:
**The full faithfulness half of Stacks 023E.**  For a family of open immersions whose images
cover the target, the canonical descent functor of Stacks 023D on quasi-coherent modules is fully
faithful.

This is the full faithfulness clause of Stacks 023E; the effectivity clause is *not* proved
here.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor_zariski
    (hf : ⨆ i, (f i).opensRange = ⊤) :
    Nonempty (canonicalDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData
declarations.doc:
A descent datum for modules for an `R`-algebra `A`.

The transition is bundled as an `A ⊗[R] A`-linear equivalence, and `cocycle` is the equality
`φ₁₂ ∘ φ₀₁ = φ₀₂`.
declarations.statement: structure DescentData

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of module descent data is an `A`-linear map commuting with the transition
isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (D E : DescentData.{u, v, w} R A)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.exists_descentCosimplicialModuleFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023H.** To a descent datum `(N, φ)` one can associate a
cosimplicial module over the Čech algebra `(A / R)_•` by the rules
`N_n = N_{n, n}` and `N_•(β) = φᵐ_{β(n), m} ∘ N_{β, n}`, functorially in the
descent datum.

declarations.name: ModuleCat.descentCosimplicialModuleFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor which associates to a descent datum `(N, φ)` its cosimplicial
module over the Čech algebra `(A / R)_•`.  It is characterised by
`descentCosimplicialModuleFunctor_obj` and
`descentCosimplicialModuleFunctor_map`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def descentCosimplicialModuleFunctor :
    DescentData.{u, v, w} R A ⥤ CechModule.{u, v, w} R A

declarations.name: ModuleCat.cechTensorModule
declarations.doc:
The Čech cosimplicial algebra tensored with `M`, together with its
degreewise and cosimplicial-map specification.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cechTensorModule (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    {T : CechModule.{u, v, w} R A // IsCechTensorModule R A M T}

declarations.name: ModuleCat.canonicalDescent_cosimplicialModule
declarations.doc:
The cosimplicial module associated to a canonical descent datum is
isomorphic to the Čech cosimplicial algebra tensored with its base module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalDescent_cosimplicialModule
    (M : ModuleCat.{w} R)
    (D : DescentData.{u, v, w} R A)
    (e : (A ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[A] D.module)
    (he : ∀ (a b : A) (m : M),
      D.transition ((e (a ⊗ₜ[R] m)) ⊗ₜ[R] b) =
        a ⊗ₜ[R] (show restrictModule R A D.module from
          e (b ⊗ₜ[R] m))) :
    Nonempty (((descentCosimplicialModuleFunctor R A).obj D) ≅
      (cechTensorModule R A M).1)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData.IsEffective
declarations.doc:
A module descent datum is effective if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum
obtained by extending scalars from an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
abbrev DescentData.IsEffective (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (D : DescentData.{u, v, w} R A) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.augmentedDescentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Equation 023K: the augmented descent complex** `0 → M → A ⊗[R] M → A ⊗[R] A ⊗[R] M → ⋯`
of the ring map `R → A` with coefficients in `M`. It is the alternating coface map complex of
`(A/R)• ⊗[R] M`, augmented by `M` along `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def augmentedDescentComplex : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℕ
declarations.comment: the augmented complex 0 → M → A ⊗ M → A ⊗ A ⊗ M → ⋯

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.augmentedDescentComplexXIso
declarations.doc: **The degree-`(n + 1)` term of the augmented descent complex is `A^{⊗(n + 1)} ⊗[R] M`.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def augmentedDescentComplexXIso (n : ℕ) :
    ModuleCat.of R ((tensorPowerAlg R A n : Type u) ⊗[R] M) ≅
      (augmentedDescentComplex R A M).X (n + 1)
declarations.comment: its degree-(n+1) term is A^{⊗(n+1)} ⊗_R M

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023L.** If `R → A` admits a section, then the extended Amitsur
cochain complex with coefficients in any `R`-module `M` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_section
    (h : Nonempty (A →ₐ[R] R)) :
    (amitsurExtendedCochainComplex R A M).Acyclic

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023M.** For a faithfully flat algebra `A` over a commutative ring `R` and an
arbitrary `R`-module `M`, the extended Amitsur cochain complex
`M → A ⊗[R] M → (A ⊗[R] A) ⊗[R] M → ⋯`
is exact in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    (amitsurExtendedCochainComplex R A M).Acyclic

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023M**, and **Stacks Lemma 03OA**.  The extended Amitsur cochain complex of a
faithfully flat algebra is exact for every module of coefficients.  Exactness of the extended
complex `M → A ⊗[R] M → A ⊗[R] A ⊗[R] M → ⋯` says both that the unaugmented complex is exact in
positive degrees and that its degree-zero cohomology is `M`, which is the form 03OA states.
declarations.statement:
theorem amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) (M : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    (amitsurExtendedCochainComplex R A M).Acyclic

declarations.name: ModuleCat.baseExtensionUnitEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 023M in degrees `−1` and `0`.** For a universally injective ring map
the unit `m ↦ 1 ⊗ m` of the base-extension adjunction is an isomorphism of `M` onto the
invariants of the base-extended descent datum.

Exactness of the extended cochain complex `0 → M → A ⊗[R] M → A ⊗[R] A ⊗[R] M → ⋯` at `M` is
injectivity of the unit, and exactness at `A ⊗[R] M` says that the kernel of the next
differential — which is `ModuleCat.invariantSubmodule R A` of the canonical descent datum on
`A ⊗[R] M` — is the image of the unit. Together they are bijectivity of the unit onto the
invariants. The source assumes `R → A` faithfully flat; faithful flatness is used only through
universal injectivity (Tag 08WL), which is the hypothesis here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseExtensionUnitEquiv
    (h : Algebra.UniversallyInjective R A) (M : ModuleCat.{max u w} R) :
    M ≃ₗ[R] invariantSubmodule R A
      ((baseExtension.{u, u, w} R A).functor.obj M)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.isEffectiveDescentMorphismForModules_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 023N, part (2).** For a faithfully flat ring map `R → A`, base extension
`M ↦ (A ⊗[R] M, can)` is an equivalence from `R`-modules onto the category of descent data for
modules along `R → A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveDescentMorphismForModules_of_faithfullyFlat :
    IsEffectiveDescentMorphismForModules.{u, u, w} R A

declarations.name: ModuleCat.baseExtension_essSurj_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 023N, part (1).** Every descent datum on modules along a faithfully flat ring map
`R → A` is effective, that is, lies in the essential image of base extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseExtension_essSurj_of_faithfullyFlat :
    (baseExtension.{u, u, w} R A).functor.EssSurj

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData.isEffective_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 023N, part (1).** Every descent datum for modules along a faithfully flat ring map
`R → A` is effective: it is isomorphic, as a descent datum, to the canonical datum on the
extension of scalars of an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem DescentData.isEffective_of_faithfullyFlat
    (D : DescentData.{u, u, max u w} R A) : D.IsEffective R A

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.faithfullyFlatInvariantsEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 023N, part (3).** For a faithfully flat ring map `R → A` the functor
`M ↦ (A ⊗[R] M, can)` from `R`-modules to descent data for modules along `R → A` is an
equivalence whose inverse functor is `(N, φ) ↦ H⁰(s(N_•))`, the kernel of the descent complex.
Only part (3) is registered here; part (2), that the functor is an equivalence, is
`ModuleCat.isEffectiveDescentMorphismForModules_of_faithfullyFlat`.
declarations.statement:
def faithfullyFlatInvariantsEquivalence [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    ModuleCat.{max u w} R ≌ DescentData.{u, u, max u w} R A

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.faithfullyFlatInvariantsEquivalence_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 023N, part (3).** The inverse functor of the equivalence of Stacks 023N is
`ModuleCat.pushforward`, that is `(N, φ) ↦ H⁰(s(N_•))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlatInvariantsEquivalence_inverse [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    (faithfullyFlatInvariantsEquivalence.{u, w} R A).inverse = pushforward R A

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.faithfullyFlat_standardCoverAlgebra
declarations.doc: The product of the principal localizations of a standard cover is faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem faithfullyFlat_standardCoverAlgebra
    (hf : PrimeSpectrum.IsStandardOpenCoverOfSpectrum f) :
    Module.FaithfullyFlat R (∀ i : Fin m, Localization.Away (f i))

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.standardCoverCechDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
In degree `d`, the Čech algebra of a standard cover is the product of the
localizations at all `(d + 1)`-fold products of its covering elements.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def standardCoverCechDegreeEquiv (d : ℕ) :
    ((Arrow.mk (CommAlgCat.ofHom
      (Algebra.ofId R (∀ i : Fin m, Localization.Away (f i))))).cechConerve).obj
        (SimplexCategory.mk d) ≃ₐ[R]
      (∀ i : Fin (d + 1) → Fin m, Localization.Away (∏ j, f (i j)))

declarations.name: isUniversalEffectiveEpi_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Main statement (Stacks Tag 023Q).**
Every fpqc covering of schemes is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of
schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversalEffectiveEpi_of_isFpqcCovering
    {ι : Type*} {T : Scheme} (T' : ι → Scheme) (f : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ T)
    (hf : IsFpqcCoveringFamily T' f) :
    IsUniversalEffectiveEpi T' f
declarations.comment: every fpqc covering family of schemes is a universal effective epimorphism, in the unpacked equalizer form of Stacks 00WP: along every base change of the family, a morphism to any scheme is determined by, and glues from, a pullback-compatible family on the members

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor_standardFpqc
declarations.doc:
**The full faithfulness half of [Stacks, Tag 023S]**: let `S` be an affine scheme and let
`{f i : X i ⟶ S}` be a standard fpqc covering of `S` in the sense of Stacks 022F.  Then the
functor from quasi-coherent `O_S`-modules to quasi-coherent descent data for the family is fully
faithful.

The content is the unconditional
`…QuasicoherentDescentData.nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage`,
which holds for an arbitrary fpqc covering family of an arbitrary scheme; all that is done here
is to supply the covering hypothesis in the elementary form in which Stacks 022F states it, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.presieve₀_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_standardFpqc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor_standardFpqc
    (𝒲 : PreZeroHypercover.{0} S) [Finite 𝒲.I₀] [∀ i, IsAffine (𝒲.X i)] [∀ i, Flat (𝒲.f i)]
    (hsurj : ⋃ i, Set.range (𝒲.f i) = Set.univ) :
    Nonempty (canonicalDescentFunctor 𝒲.f).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.isEffective_standardFpqc_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**The effectivity half of [Stacks, Tag 023S]**: let `S` be an affine scheme and let
`{f i : X i ⟶ S}` be a standard fpqc covering of `S` in the sense of Stacks 022F — a finite
family of flat morphisms from affine schemes whose images cover `S`.  Then every quasi-coherent
descent datum for the family is effective, i.e. isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a
quasi-coherent module on `S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.isEffective_standardFpqc`, whose base is
literally of the form `Spec R`, transported to an arbitrary affine base along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isoSpec`.  The transport runs in the vocabulary of
`Stacks.Descent.qcohPseudofunctor`, where `Stacks.Descent.essSurj_toDescentData_of_baseIso` is
available; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_standardFpqc_of_isAffine (𝒲 : PreZeroHypercover.{0} S) [Finite 𝒲.I₀]
    [∀ i, IsAffine (𝒲.X i)] [∀ i, Flat (𝒲.f i)]
    (hsurj : ⋃ i, Set.range (𝒲.f i) = Set.univ)
    (D : QuasicoherentDescentData 𝒲.f) : D.IsEffective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor'
declarations.doc:
For every fpqc covering family the functor from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the
descent data with respect to that family is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor' {I : Type (u + 1)}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hfpqc : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} S) :
    Nonempty (canonicalDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.isEffective_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
Every quasi-coherent descent datum for an fpqc covering family of an arbitrary scheme is
effective, at an arbitrary index universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_fpqcPrecoverage {S : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{v} S)
    (h𝒰 : 𝒰.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} S) (D : QuasicoherentDescentData 𝒰.f) :
    D.IsEffective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.isEquivalence_canonicalDescentFunctor_fpqc
declarations.doc:
For an fpqc covering family of a scheme `S`, indexed in `Type (u + 1)`, the canonical descent
functor from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the descent data with respect to that family is an
equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_canonicalDescentFunctor_fpqc {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type (u + 1)}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hfpqc : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} S) :
    (canonicalDescentFunctor f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: both assertions in one statement: the canonical descent functor is an equivalence. The index universe is u + 1, fixed by the full-faithfulness half nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalDescentFunctor'; effectivity on its own is isEffective_fpqcPrecoverage above, at an arbitrary index universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum
declarations.doc:
Descent data for schemes relative to a single morphism `f : X ⟶ S`: a scheme `V` over
`X` together with an isomorphism `V ×_S X ≅ X ×_S V` of schemes over `X ×_S X` satisfying the
cocycle condition. This is the one-member family case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData`.
declarations.statement: abbrev DescentDatum (f : X ⟶ S)
declarations.comment: (1) descent datum for V/X/S, (2) descent datum relative to X ⟶ S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of descent data relative to `f : X ⟶ S`: a morphism of `X`-schemes commuting
with the two gluing isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: abbrev Hom (D E : DescentDatum f)
declarations.comment: (3) morphisms of descent data relative to X ⟶ S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData
declarations.doc: Descent data for schemes relative to a family of morphisms with common target.
declarations.statement: structure DescentData

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of descent data is a family of maps over the family members,
compatible with the gluing isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (D E : DescentData f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.familyCoproductEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Descent data relative to a family `X i ⟶ S` are canonically equivalent to descent data
relative to the single morphism `(∐ i, X i) ⟶ S`. Under this equivalence both objects and gluing
maps are formed by coproduct, as specified by `FamilyCoproductEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def familyCoproductEquivalence :
    FamilyCoproductEquivalence f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.pullbackFunctors
declarations.doc:
The pullback functors on descent data along the morphisms completing a commutative square
over `h`, together with the canonical isomorphisms between any two of them.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackFunctors {S S' X X' : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (a' : X' ⟶ S') (h : S' ⟶ S) :
    PullbackFunctors a a' h

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.trivialFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor sending a scheme over `S` to its trivial descent datum relative to the
singleton family consisting of `𝟙 S`.
declarations.statement:
def trivialFunctor (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    Over S ⥤ DescentData (S := S) (X := fun _ : Unit ↦ S) (fun _ ↦ 𝟙 S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.canonicalFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor sending a scheme over `S` to its canonical descent datum relative to
`f : X ⟶ S`, obtained by pulling back its trivial descent datum.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalFunctor {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Over S ⥤ DescentData (S := S) (X := fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.IsEffective
declarations.doc:
A descent datum relative to `f : X ⟶ S` is effective if it is isomorphic to the
canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsEffective
    (D : DescentData (S := S) (X := fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0240.** Pullback of descent data along a surjective flat morphism
is faithful.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0241.** Pullback along an fpqc covering over a fixed
base scheme is fully faithful on descent data.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.selfPullbackFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
Pullback of descent data along a selfmap `f : X ⟶ X` over `S` is isomorphic to the identity
functor on the category of descent data relative to `X ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
def selfPullbackFunctorIso {S X : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ X) (hf : f ≫ a = a) :
    (pullbackFunctor a a (𝟙 S) f (by simpa using hf)).functor ≅ 𝟭 _

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_isEquivalence_of_exists_reverse
declarations.doc:
Pullback of descent data along `f : X' ⟶ X` is an equivalence if there is a morphism
`X ⟶ X'` over the same base scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFunctor_isEquivalence_of_exists_reverse
    {S X X' : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (a' : X' ⟶ S) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (comm : f ≫ a = a') (h : ∃ g : X ⟶ X', g ≫ a' = a) :
    (DescentData.pullbackFunctor a a' (𝟙 S) f (by simpa using comm)).functor.IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `{X i ⟶ S}` be a covering family of `S` for the fpqc topology, and
let `D` be a descent datum relative to that family all of whose structure morphisms `V i ⟶ X i`
are affine. Then `D` is effective: it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over
`S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isAffineHom {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S) (D : DescentData f)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAffineHom (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: for a covering family indexed in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0245](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0245) over an affine base.** Let `S`
be an affine scheme, let `{X i ⟶ S}` be an fpqc covering family and let `D` be a descent datum
relative to it whose structure morphism over each `X i` is affine. Then `D` is effective: it is
isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isAffineHom {ι : Type u} {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
    {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hP : ∀ i, IsAffineHom (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: the case of an affine base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isAffineHom_of_anyIndex
declarations.doc:
**Effective descent for affine morphisms along an fpqc covering family indexed in an arbitrary
universe.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `{X i ⟶ S}` be a covering family of `S` for the fpqc topology,
indexed by a type in an arbitrary universe, and let `D` be a descent datum relative to that family
all of whose structure morphisms `V i ⟶ X i` are affine. Then `D` is effective: it is isomorphic to
the canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_isAffineHom_of_anyIndex {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S) (D : DescentData f)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAffineHom (D.obj i).hom) : D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: for a covering family indexed in an arbitrary universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Quasi-affine morphisms descend effectively along the surjective étale morphisms of the big
fppf site of `S`.** If the base change of a morphism of sheaves `f : X ⟶ Y` along a surjective
étale chart `q : c ⟶ a` of a representable `yoneda.obj a ⟶ Y` is representable by quasi-affine
morphisms, then so is `X ×[Y] yoneda.obj a ⟶ yoneda.obj a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isQuasiAffineHom
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    IsEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale B S hS
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: effective descent along a surjective étale chart of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0247](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0247).** Let `S` be a scheme, let
`{X i ⟶ S}` be an fpqc covering family, indexed by a type in an arbitrary universe, and let `D`
be a descent datum relative to it each of whose component morphisms `V i ⟶ X i` is quasi-affine.
Then `D` is effective: it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.

Quasi-affineness is stable under arbitrary base change (Stacks 01SO) and, being Zariski local on
the target, closed under finite disjoint unions, so the general-base fpqc reduction of Stacks
02W3, `AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_fpqc_of_affineSingleton_of_anyIndex`,
reduces the statement to a covering given by a single surjective flat morphism of affine schemes.
That case is the affine-hull argument of
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_isIndQuasiAffineHom`, applied to a quasi-affine,
hence ind-quasi-affine (Stacks 0F1W), morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_isQuasiAffineHom {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hD : ∀ i, IsQuasiAffineHom (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.NatTrans.Equifibered
registrations.comment: more general: an equifibered natural transformation of functors J ⥤ C; here J = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ and C = Scheme, so a morphism of simplicial schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.simplicialScheme
declarations.doc:
The simplicial scheme `(X/S)_•` associated to `f : X ⟶ S`: its degree-`n` part is the
`(n + 1)`-fold fibre product of `X` over `S`, i.e. it is the Čech nerve of `f`.
declarations.statement: def simplicialScheme : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.toDescentDatum
declarations.doc:
**The descent datum `(V, φ)` relative to `f : X ⟶ S`** attached to a descent datum on
`(X/S)_•`.
declarations.statement:
def toDescentDatum (D : Stacks.Simplicial.Descent.DescentDatum (simplicialScheme f)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum f
declarations.comment: the descent datum (V, φ) attached to a descent datum on (X/S)_•

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isPullback_cartesianLeft
declarations.doc: **`(d¹₁, pr₁ ∘ π₁) : Y₁ ⟶ V ×_S X` is an isomorphism.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isPullback_cartesianLeft (Y : Stacks.Simplicial.Descent.Cartesian (simplicialScheme f)) :
    IsPullback (Y.1.left.δ (1 : Fin 2)) (Y.1.hom.app (op ⦋1⦌) ≫ proj f 1 1)
      ((descentObj (cartesianDatum Y)).hom ≫ f) f
declarations.comment: the isomorphism V ×_S X ← Y_1 given by (d¹_1, pr_1 ∘ π_1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isPullback_cartesianRight
declarations.doc: **`(pr₀ ∘ π₁, d¹₀) : Y₁ ⟶ X ×_S V` is an isomorphism.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isPullback_cartesianRight (Y : Stacks.Simplicial.Descent.Cartesian (simplicialScheme f)) :
    IsPullback (Y.1.hom.app (op ⦋1⦌) ≫ proj f 1 0) (Y.1.left.δ (0 : Fin 2)) f
      ((descentObj (cartesianDatum Y)).hom ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the isomorphism Y_1 → X ×_S V given by (pr_0 ∘ π_1, d¹_0)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.cartesian_actMap
declarations.doc:
`φ` is the isomorphism induced by `d¹₀` and `π₁`: a point of `V ×_S X` lifted to a point
`y` of `Y₁` is sent to the zeroth face of `y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cartesian_actMap (Y : Stacks.Simplicial.Descent.Cartesian (simplicialScheme f)) {W : Over S}
    (q : W ⟶ (Over.map f).obj (descentObj (cartesianDatum Y)) ⨯ Over.mk f)
    (y : W.left ⟶ Y.1.left.obj (op ⦋1⦌))
    (h₁ : y ≫ Y.1.left.δ (1 : Fin 2) = (q ≫ prod.fst).left)
    (h₂ : y ≫ Y.1.hom.app (op ⦋1⦌) ≫ proj f 1 1 = (q ≫ prod.snd).left) :
    (q ≫ actMap (cartesianDatum Y)).left = y ≫ Y.1.left.δ (0 : Fin 2)
declarations.comment: φ is the isomorphism resulting from d¹_0 and π_1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.cartesianDescentDatum
declarations.doc:
**`(V, φ)` is a descent datum relative to `X ⟶ S`**, for `V = Y₀` over `X` and `φ` the
isomorphism `V ×_S X ≅ X ×_S V` induced by `d¹₀`, `d¹₁` and `π₁` on a cartesian simplicial
scheme `Y` over `(X/S)_•`.
declarations.statement:
def cartesianDescentDatum (Y : Stacks.Simplicial.Descent.Cartesian (simplicialScheme f)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum f
declarations.comment: (V, φ) is a descent datum relative to X ⟶ S, for cartesian Y over (X/S)_•

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.cartesianDescentDatumFunctor_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The construction of Lemma 024B, from cartesian schemes over `(X/S)_•` to descent data
relative to `X/S`, is an equivalence of categories.**
declarations.statement:
instance cartesianDescentDatumFunctor_isEquivalence (f : X ⟶ S) :
    (cartesianDescentDatumFunctor f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.isEquivalenceRelation_faceMaps_of_equifibered
declarations.doc:
If a simplicial object maps cartesianly to the Čech nerve of `f`, its two
face maps from degree one form an internal equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceRelation_faceMaps_of_equifibered {X S : C} (f : X ⟶ S)
    {Y : SimplicialObject C} (π : Y ⟶ (Arrow.mk f).cechNerve)
    (hπ : NatTrans.Equifibered π) :
    IsEquivalenceRelation (Y.δ (1 : Fin 2)) (Y.δ (0 : Fin 2))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Simplicial.pointClass
declarations.doc: The points reached from `y` by a one-simplex whose first face is `y`.
declarations.statement:
def pointClass (Y : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}) (y : Y _⦋0⦌) :
    Set (Y _⦋0⦌)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Simplicial.mem_pointClass_self
declarations.doc: A point belongs to the subset of points reachable from it.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_pointClass_self {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    {Y : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ (Arrow.mk f).cechNerve)
    (hπ : NatTrans.Equifibered π) (y : Y _⦋0⦌) :
    y ∈ pointClass Y y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Simplicial.pointClass_eq_of_nonempty_inter
declarations.doc: If two subsets of reachable points meet, they are the same subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointClass_eq_of_nonempty_inter {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    {Y : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ (Arrow.mk f).cechNerve)
    (hπ : NatTrans.Equifibered π) (y y' : Y _⦋0⦌)
    (h : (pointClass Y y ∩ pointClass Y y').Nonempty) :
    pointClass Y y = pointClass Y y'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Simplicial.isCompact_relatedPoints
declarations.doc:
The vertices connected to a fixed vertex in a cartesian simplicial scheme
over the Čech nerve of a quasi-compact morphism form a quasi-compact set.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_iso_sigma_spec_isArtinianRing
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact, flat, surjective morphism of schemes and let `(V, φ)` be a
descent datum relative to `X/S`. If `V` is a disjoint union of spectra of Artinian rings then
`(V, φ)` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_of_iso_sigma_spec_isArtinianRing [QuasiCompact f] [Flat f] [Surjective f]
    (D : DescentDatum f)
    (hV : ∃ (ι : Type u) (A : ι → CommRingCat.{u}), (∀ i, IsArtinianRing (A i)) ∧
      Nonempty (D.over.left ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (A i))) :
    DescentData.IsEffective D
declarations.comment: effectivity of a datum carried by a disjoint union of Artinian spectra

declarations.name: RingHom.IsUnramifiedLocalHom
declarations.doc:
A local homomorphism `f : A → B` of local rings is an *unramified homomorphism of local
rings* if `𝔪_A B = 𝔪_B`, the residue field `κ(𝔪_B)` is a finite separable extension of
`κ(𝔪_A)`, and `B` is essentially of finite type over `A`.
declarations.statement: structure IsUnramifiedLocalHom (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.isUnramifiedLocalHom_algebraMap_iff
declarations.doc:
The structure map of a local algebra `B` over `A` is an unramified homomorphism of local rings
if and only if `B` is formally unramified and essentially of finite type over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramifiedLocalHom_algebraMap_iff :
    (algebraMap A B).IsUnramifiedLocalHom ↔
      Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B ∧ Algebra.EssFiniteType A B
declarations.comment: Equivalently, `A → B` is formally unramified and essentially of finite type.

declarations.name: RingHom.isUnramifiedLocalHom_iff
declarations.doc:
A local homomorphism of local rings is an unramified homomorphism of local rings if and only
if it is formally unramified and essentially of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramifiedLocalHom_iff (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] :
    f.IsUnramifiedLocalHom ↔ f.FormallyUnramified ∧ f.EssFiniteType
declarations.comment: Equivalently, `f` is formally unramified and essentially of finite type.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StalkwiseUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is unramified at `x` if its
map on local rings at `x` is unramified.
declarations.statement:
abbrev StalkwiseUnramifiedAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StalkwiseUnramified
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is unramified if it is
unramified at every point of its source.
declarations.statement:
class StalkwiseUnramified {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024P.** Let `Y` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism
locally of finite type and `x` a point of `X`. Then `f` is unramified at `x` if and only if the
stalk at `x` of the sheaf of relative differentials of `f` vanishes, and if and only if the
diagonal `Δ_{X/Y}` is a local isomorphism at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_tfae (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      StalkwiseUnramifiedAt f x,
      Subsingleton ((Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).presheaf.stalk x),
      ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpenImmersion (U.ι ≫ pullback.diagonal f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_iff_hasDifferentialPresentationAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024P, condition (3).** For a morphism locally of finite type to a
locally Noetherian scheme, unramifiedness at `x` is equivalent to the existence of a local closed
immersion into an affine space over an open of the target whose defining ideal has generating
differentials at the image of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_iff_hasDifferentialPresentationAt (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    StalkwiseUnramifiedAt f x ↔ HasDifferentialPresentationAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_tfae₄
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024P.** Let `Y` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism
locally of finite type and `x` a point of `X`. The following are equivalent: `f` is unramified at
`x`; the stalk at `x` of the sheaf of relative differentials of `f` vanishes; `f` restricts near
`x` to a closed immersion into an affine space over an open of `Y` whose defining ideal has
generating differentials at the image of `x`; and the diagonal `Δ_{X/Y}` is a local isomorphism
at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_tfae₄ (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      StalkwiseUnramifiedAt f x,
      Subsingleton ((Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).presheaf.stalk x),
      HasDifferentialPresentationAt f x,
      ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpenImmersion (U.ι ≫ pullback.diagonal f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_iff_injective_hom_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 024R.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes with `S` locally Noetherian and `f`
locally of finite type. Then `f` is unramified if and only if it is formally unramified in the
functorial sense: for every affine `S`-scheme `T` and every subscheme `T₀` of `T` defined by a
square-zero ideal, the natural map `Hom_S(T, X) → Hom_S(T₀, X)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_iff_injective_hom_restriction {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    Unramified f ↔
      ∀ (T T₀ : Over S) (_ : IsAffine T.left) (i : T₀ ⟶ T),
        Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening i.left →
          Function.Injective fun g : T ⟶ Over.mk f => i ≫ g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.section_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc: A section of an unramified morphism is an open immersion.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.section_isOpenImmersion_and_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
A section of an unramified separated morphism is both an open immersion and a closed
immersion.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.isClopen_range_section
declarations.doc: The image of a section of an unramified separated morphism is open and closed.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_of_isSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024T, part (1).** A section of an unramified morphism is an open
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_of_isSection (hs : s ≫ g = 𝟙 S) [Unramified g] :
    IsOpenImmersion s
declarations.comment: part (1): a section of an unramified morphism is an open immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_of_isSection_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024T, part (2).** A section of a separated morphism is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_isSection_of_isSeparated (hs : s ≫ g = 𝟙 S) [IsSeparated g] :
    IsClosedImmersion s
declarations.comment: part (2): a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClopen_range_of_isSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024T, part (3).** A section of an unramified separated morphism is open
and closed: its image is an open and closed subset of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClopen_range_of_isSection (hs : s ≫ g = 𝟙 S) [Unramified g] [IsSeparated g] :
    IsClopen (Set.range s.base)
declarations.comment: part (3): a section of an unramified separated morphism is open and closed

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjSeparated.isClosedImmersion_of_section
declarations.doc: **A section of a separated morphism of schemes is a closed immersion.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedImmersion_of_section {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f]
    (σ : Y ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) : IsClosedImmersion σ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.section_isIso_onto_connectedComponent
declarations.doc:
A section of a separated unramified morphism onto a connected target is an isomorphism onto
a connected component of its source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem section_isIso_onto_connectedComponent {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [ConnectedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [Unramified f] [IsSeparated f]
    (s : Y ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (sU : Y ⟶ U.toScheme),
      (∃ x : X, (U : Set X) = connectedComponent x) ∧ IsIso sU ∧ sU ≫ U.ι = s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.sections_equiv_connectedComponents
declarations.doc:
Sections correspond to the connected components on which the morphism is an isomorphism; the
component corresponding to a section is exactly its image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sections_equiv_connectedComponents {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [ConnectedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [Unramified f] [IsSeparated f] :
    ∃ e : {s : Y ⟶ X // s ≫ f = 𝟙 Y} ≃
      {U : X.Opens // (∃ x : X, (U : Set X) = connectedComponent x) ∧ IsIso (U.ι ≫ f)},
      ∀ s, ((e s).1 : Set X) = Set.range (fun y : Y => s.1 y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.section_eq_of_common_point
declarations.doc:
At most one section of a separated unramified morphism passes through a given point of its
source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem section_eq_of_common_point {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [ConnectedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [Unramified f] [IsSeparated f]
    (s t : Y ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) (ht : t ≫ f = 𝟙 Y)
    (x : X) (y z : Y) (hsy : s y = x) (htz : t z = x) : s = t

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.eq_of_residueFieldMap_eq
declarations.doc:
Two morphisms from a connected scheme to a separated unramified scheme over a base are equal
if they induce the same point and the same residue-field map there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eq_of_residueFieldMap_eq {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ S)
    [Unramified π] [IsSeparated π] [ConnectedSpace Y]
    (f g : Y ⟶ X) (hover : f ≫ π = g ≫ π) (y : Y) (hy : f y = g y)
    (hκ : f.residueFieldMap y = (X.residueFieldCongr hy).hom ≫ g.residueFieldMap y) :
    f = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffine_of_unramified_quasiCompact
declarations.doc: A quasi-compact unramified scheme over a field is affine.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffine_of_unramified_quasiCompact
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [StalkwiseUnramified f] [QuasiCompact f] : IsAffine X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_quasiCompact_iff_iso_finite_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
A morphism to the spectrum of a field is quasi-compact and unramified exactly when its
source is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions, compatibly
with the map to the base field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_quasiCompact_iff_iso_finite_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    ((∃ h : LocallyOfFiniteType f, letI := h; StalkwiseUnramified f) ∧ QuasiCompact f) ↔
      ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Finite I) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite k (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable k (K i))
        (e : X ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
        e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (K i)))) = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_spec_finite_separable_of_connected_unramified
declarations.doc:
A connected unramified scheme over a field is the spectrum of one finite separable field
extension, over the base field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_spec_finite_separable_of_connected_unramified
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [StalkwiseUnramified f] [ConnectedSpace X] :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (_ : Module.Finite k K)
      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k K) (e : X ≅ Spec (.of K)),
      e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)) = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_unramified_over_field
declarations.doc: Over a field, a morphism is étale exactly when it is locally of finite type and unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_iff_unramified_over_field
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    Etale f ↔ ∃ h : LocallyOfFiniteType f, letI := h; StalkwiseUnramified f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramifiedAt_iff_ramificationIdx_eq_one_and_isSeparable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024Z.** At a nonzero prime of the larger ring of integers,
scheme-theoretic unramifiedness is equivalent to ramification index one together with
separability of the residue extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramifiedAt_iff_ramificationIdx_eq_one_and_isSeparable
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [NumberField K] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum (RingOfIntegers L)) (hq : q.asIdeal ≠ ⊥) :
    letI : Module.Finite (RingOfIntegers K) (RingOfIntegers L) :=
      IsIntegralClosure.finite (RingOfIntegers K) K L (RingOfIntegers L)
    letI : IsFinite (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) := (IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).2
      (IsIntegralClosure.finite (RingOfIntegers K) K L (RingOfIntegers L))
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) := inferInstance
    StalkwiseUnramifiedAt (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) q ↔
      (letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver
          (q.asIdeal.under (RingOfIntegers K)) q.asIdeal
       Ideal.ramificationIdx q.asIdeal (RingOfIntegers K) = 1 ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparable (q.asIdeal.under (RingOfIntegers K)).ResidueField
          q.asIdeal.ResidueField)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramifiedAt_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024Z.** The morphism on spectra of rings of integers is unramified at
the generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramifiedAt_genericPoint
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [NumberField K] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] :
    letI : Module.Finite (RingOfIntegers K) (RingOfIntegers L) :=
      IsIntegralClosure.finite (RingOfIntegers K) K L (RingOfIntegers L)
    letI : IsFinite (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) := (IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).2
      (IsIntegralClosure.finite (RingOfIntegers K) K L (RingOfIntegers L))
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) := inferInstance
    StalkwiseUnramifiedAt (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L)
      (⟨⊥, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum (RingOfIntegers L))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_ringOfIntegersSpecMap
declarations.doc: The morphism on spectra of rings of integers is flat.
declarations.statement: instance flat_ringOfIntegersSpecMap : Flat (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L)
declarations.comment: the morphism Spec(O_L) -> Spec(O_K) is flat (on all of Spec(O_L), so in particular on X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_ringOfIntegersSpecMap_iff
declarations.doc:
The points of `Spec(𝒪_L)` where `f : Spec(𝒪_L) → Spec(𝒪_K)` is unramified in the sense of
schemes are the points where it is unramified in the conventional sense: the generic point, and the
nonzero primes with ramification index one and separable residue field extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkwiseUnramifiedAt_ringOfIntegersSpecMap_iff (q : PrimeSpectrum (𝓞 L)) :
    StalkwiseUnramifiedAt (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) q ↔
      (q.asIdeal ≠ ⊥ →
        (letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver (q.asIdeal.under (𝓞 K)) q.asIdeal
         Ideal.ramificationIdx q.asIdeal (𝓞 K) = 1 ∧
          Algebra.IsSeparable (q.asIdeal.under (𝓞 K)).ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
declarations.comment: the points where f is unramified in our sense are the points where f is unramified in the conventional sense, at every point of Spec(O_L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zeroLocus_differentIdeal
declarations.doc:
In the conventional sense, the locus of ramification in `Spec(𝒪_L)` is the vanishing set of the
different: a point of `Spec(𝒪_L)` lies in the vanishing set of the different exactly when it is a
nonzero prime whose ramification index is not one or whose residue field extension is not
separable.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroLocus_differentIdeal :
    zeroLocus (differentIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) : Set (𝓞 L)) =
      {q | q.asIdeal ≠ ⊥ ∧
        ¬ (letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver (q.asIdeal.under (𝓞 K)) q.asIdeal
           Ideal.ramificationIdx q.asIdeal (𝓞 K) = 1 ∧
            Algebra.IsSeparable (q.asIdeal.under (𝓞 K)).ResidueField
              q.asIdeal.ResidueField)}
declarations.comment: in the conventional sense, the locus of ramification in Spec(O_L) is the vanishing set of the different

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.algebraDiscriminantIdeal_ringOfIntegers_eq_relNorm_differentIdeal
declarations.doc:
The discriminant of `L/K`, an ideal of `𝒪_K` — the discriminant ideal of the finite locally
free algebra `𝒪_L` over `𝒪_K`, the zeroth Fitting ideal of the cokernel of its trace pairing — is
the norm of the different.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraDiscriminantIdeal_ringOfIntegers_eq_relNorm_differentIdeal :
    Stacks.Discriminant.algebraDiscriminantIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) =
      Ideal.relNorm (𝓞 K) (differentIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L))
declarations.comment: the discriminant is an ideal in O_K, namely it is the norm of the different

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zeroLocus_algebraDiscriminantIdeal
declarations.doc:
The vanishing set of the discriminant is precisely the set of points of `Spec(𝒪_K)` which
ramify in `L`: the primes of `𝒪_K` lying under a nonzero prime of `𝒪_L` whose ramification index is
not one or whose residue field extension is not separable.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroLocus_algebraDiscriminantIdeal :
    zeroLocus (Stacks.Discriminant.algebraDiscriminantIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) : Set (𝓞 K)) =
      {p | ∃ q : PrimeSpectrum (𝓞 L), comap (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L)) q = p ∧
        q.asIdeal ≠ ⊥ ∧
        ¬ (letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver (q.asIdeal.under (𝓞 K)) q.asIdeal
           Ideal.ramificationIdx q.asIdeal (𝓞 K) = 1 ∧
            Algebra.IsSeparable (q.asIdeal.under (𝓞 K)).ResidueField
              q.asIdeal.ResidueField)}
declarations.comment: the vanishing set of the discriminant is precisely the set of points of Spec(O_K) which ramify in L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkwiseUnramified_flat_and_etale_differentOpen
declarations.doc:
Denote by `X` the complement of the closed subset defined by the different in `Spec(𝒪_L)`. The
morphism `X → Spec(𝒪_K)` is unramified; it is furthermore flat, and hence it is actually étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkwiseUnramified_flat_and_etale_differentOpen :
    StalkwiseUnramified ((differentOpen K L).ι ≫ ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) ∧
      Flat ((differentOpen K L).ι ≫ ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L) ∧
        Etale ((differentOpen K L).ι ≫ ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L)
declarations.comment: the morphism X -> Spec(O_K) is unramified, flat, and hence etale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_and_etale_morphismRestrict_discriminantOpen
declarations.doc:
If `L/K` is finite Galois and `Y` is the complement of the closed subset defined by the
discriminant in `Spec(𝒪_K)`, then the preimage of `Y` is the complement `X` of the closed subset
defined by the different in `Spec(𝒪_L)`, and `X → Y` is a finite étale morphism, which is moreover
surjective: a finite étale covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_and_etale_morphismRestrict_discriminantOpen [IsGalois K L] :
    ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L ⁻¹ᵁ discriminantOpen K L = differentOpen K L ∧
      IsFinite (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L ∣_ discriminantOpen K L) ∧
        Etale (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L ∣_ discriminantOpen K L) ∧
          Surjective (ringOfIntegersSpecMap K L ∣_ discriminantOpen K L)
declarations.comment: if L/K is finite Galois, X is the preimage of Y and X -> Y is finite etale (and surjective): a finite etale covering

declarations.name: NumberField.differentIdeal_eq_annihilator_kaehlerDifferential_general
declarations.doc:
**The different of an extension of number rings is the annihilator of the module of
differentials.** For an arbitrary extension of number fields `L/K`,

  `differentIdeal 𝒪_K 𝒪_L = Module.annihilator 𝒪_L Ω[𝒪_L⁄𝒪_K]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentIdeal_eq_annihilator_kaehlerDifferential_general :
    differentIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) = Module.annihilator (𝓞 L) Ω[(𝓞 L)⁄(𝓞 K)]
declarations.comment: the different is the annihilator of the module of differentials

declarations.name: RingHom.Flat.of_injective_of_isDiscreteValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 024Z.** An injective ring homomorphism from a discrete valuation ring
to a domain is flat. In particular any extension of discrete valuation rings — an injective local
homomorphism of discrete valuation rings — is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.Flat.of_injective_of_isDiscreteValuationRing {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] (f : R →+* S)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) : f.Flat
declarations.comment: any local homomorphism of discrete valuation rings is flat, in the corrected form for injective local homomorphisms (extensions of discrete valuation rings), proved here for any injective homomorphism from a discrete valuation ring to a domain
