declarations.name: Module.flat_quotient_smul_of_isSMulRegular_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0252.** A finite module flat over the base remains flat after
quotienting by an element that acts injectively on its closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_quotient_smul_of_isSMulRegular_maximalIdeal
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] [Module.Flat R M] {f : S}
    (hf : IsSMulRegular
      (M ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S M))) f) :
    Module.Flat R (M ⧸ (Ideal.span {f} • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatAt_iff_flat_stalkMap
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is flat at `x`, as a morphism of the underlying ringed spaces, if and
only if its map on local rings `O_{Y, f(x)} → O_{X, x}` is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatAt_iff_flat_stalkMap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X) :
    IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x ↔ (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat
declarations.comment: (2) flat at `x` is flatness of the stalk map `O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_iff_forall_isFlatAt
declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes is flat if and only if it is flat at every point of its source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_iff_forall_isFlatAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Flat f ↔ ∀ x : X, IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x
declarations.comment: (3) flat is flat at every point of `X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FaithfullyFlat
declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes is faithfully flat if it is flat and surjective.
declarations.statement: public abbrev FaithfullyFlat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

registrations.comment: (1) `F` flat over `Y` at `x`, for a module `F` over a morphism `f`, applied as `IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x` to any `F : X.Modules`

**Stacks Project, Tag 0255.** The flat locus of a morphism locally of finite type to a

declarations.name: RingHom.IsEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
A local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings is étale if it is flat, formally
unramified, and essentially of finite type.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsEtaleLocalHom {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsEtaleAt
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism over a locally Noetherian scheme is étale at
`x` when the induced local homomorphism on stalks is étale.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsEtaleAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_forall_isEtaleAt
declarations.doc:
Over a locally Noetherian scheme, a locally finite type morphism is étale
if and only if it is étale at each point in the local-ring sense.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_iff_forall_isEtaleAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Etale f ↔ ∀ x : X, IsEtaleAt f x
declarations.comment: global étaleness is étaleness at every point

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_standardEtalePair_localization
declarations.doc:
If `A → B` is an étale local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, then `B` is isomorphic as
an `A`-algebra to the localization of a standard étale `A`-algebra at a prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardEtalePair_localization
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (h : RingHom.IsEtaleLocalHom (algebraMap A B)) :
    ∃ (P : StandardEtalePair A) (q : Ideal P.Ring) (hq : q.IsPrime),
      letI := hq
      Nonempty (B ≃ₐ[A] Localization.AtPrime q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBJ, étale case.** At a point where the morphism is étale, the
immersion of `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_unramifiedAt` may
be chosen to be an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_isOpenImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_etaleAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) (V : S.Opens)
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : f x ∈ V) (hf : EtaleAt f x) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U)
      (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (P : StandardEtalePair Γ(S, V)),
      P.g = P.f.derivative ∧
        ∃ (j : U.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.Ring)),
          IsOpenImmersion j ∧
            j ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (aeval P.X).toRingHom) ≫
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Polynomial.C : Γ(S, V) →+* Γ(S, V)[X])) =
              f.resLE V U hUV ≫ hV.isoSpec.hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.tfae_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 025G.** For a morphism of schemes, being an open immersion, being
universally injective and étale, and being a flat monomorphism locally of finite presentation
are all equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isOpenImmersion {A B : Scheme.{u}} (g : A ⟶ B) :
    List.TFAE [IsOpenImmersion g, UniversallyInjective g ∧ Etale g,
      Flat g ∧ Mono g ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g]

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.bijective_pullbackHom_of_etale
declarations.doc:
Base change along a closed immersion with the same underlying space induces a bijection on
morphisms into an étale scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_pullbackHom_of_etale
    {S S₀ : Scheme.{u}} (i : S₀ ⟶ S) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : Function.Surjective i.base) (X Y : Over S) [Etale X.hom] :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : Y ⟶ X => (Over.pullback i).map f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallyEtale
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is étale exactly when it is locally of finite presentation and formally
étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallyEtale
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Etale f ↔ (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ FormallyEtale f)
declarations.comment: étale iff the unique-lifting property, for a morphism locally of finite

declarations.name: RingHom.depth_eq_of_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
An étale local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings
preserves depth.
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_eq_of_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : IsEtaleLocalHom f) :
    Module.depth A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A =
      Module.depth B (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B
declarations.comment:
Proposition 039T of the section: for an étale homomorphism `A → B` of
Noetherian local rings, `depth(A) = depth(B)`.

declarations.name: RingHom.isReduced_iff_of_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
An étale local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings
preserves and reflects reducedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_iff_of_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : IsEtaleLocalHom f) :
    IsReduced A ↔ IsReduced B
declarations.comment:
Proposition 025O of the section: for an étale homomorphism `A → B` of
Noetherian local rings, `A` is reduced if and only if `B` is reduced.

declarations.name: RingHom.isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_iff_of_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
Cohen-Macaulayness is preserved and reflected by an étale
local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_iff_of_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : IsEtaleLocalHom f) :
    IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing A ↔ IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing B
declarations.comment:
Proposition 025Q of the section: for an étale homomorphism `A → B` of

    ringKrullDim A = ringKrullDim B
declarations.comment:
Lemma 039S of the section: for an étale homomorphism `A → B` of
Noetherian local rings, `dim(A) = dim(B)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasSchemeProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 025V.** A representable map of presheaves `a : F ⟶ G` on the big fppf site of `S`
*has property `P`*, for `P` a property of morphisms of schemes, when for every object `U` of
the site and every `ξ : h_U ⟶ G` the resulting morphism of schemes `V_ξ ⟶ U` has `P`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Space.HasSchemeProperty (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (a : F ⟶ G) :
    Prop

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.presheaf
registrations.comment:
a representable map of presheaves has a property of morphisms of schemes when every
  represented base change of it has that property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_diag_tfae_bigFppfOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 025W.** For a presheaf `F` on the big fppf site of `S`, representability of the
diagonal of `F`, representability of every scheme-valued point of `F`, and representability of
the fibre product of every pair of scheme-valued points of `F` are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_diag_tfae_bigFppfOver
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) :
    List.TFAE
      [yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (Limits.diag F),
        ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ξ : F.obj (Opposite.op U)),
          yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ),
        ∀ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ξ : F.obj (Opposite.op U))
          (ξ' : F.obj (Opposite.op V)),
          (Limits.pullback (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ) (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ')).IsRepresentable]

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_diag_tfae
registrations.comment:
stated for the Yoneda embedding of an arbitrary category with binary products and fibre
  products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 025Y.** A presheaf of sets on the big fppf site of `S` is an *algebraic space*
over `S` when it is an fppf sheaf, has representable diagonal, and admits a surjective
étale morphism from a representable presheaf.
declarations.statement:
structure IsAlgebraicSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 025Z.** The representable presheaf of a scheme over `S` is an algebraic space
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (yoneda.obj T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoequalizer_of_surjective_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0262**, part (3), with the étale hypothesis on the chart weakened to flatness
together with local finite presentation.  A surjective flat chart locally of finite
presentation of an algebraic space is the coequalizer, in fppf sheaves of sets, of its kernel
pair.

The three conditions are the relative properties of Tag 02YN: they are asked of every
represented base change of the chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoequalizer_of_surjective_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F) (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) f f)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f)
    (hflat : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f)
    (hlfp : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f) :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology B S hS
    ∃ (hRsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj R))
      (hUsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj U)),
      let RF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj R, hRsh⟩
      let UF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj U, hUsh⟩
      let FF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨F, hF.isSheaf⟩
      let sf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map s⟩
      let tf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map t⟩
      let ff : UF ⟶ FF := ⟨f⟩
    let w : sf ≫ ff = tf ≫ ff := by
        apply Sheaf.hom_ext
        exact hR.w
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ ff w))
declarations.comment: part (3), with the étale chart of the source replaced by a surjective flat chart locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoequalizer_of_surjectiveFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0262**, part (3), for a surjective finite locally free chart in place of a
surjective étale one.  Such a chart of an algebraic space is the coequalizer, in fppf sheaves
of sets, of its kernel pair.

Finite local freeness is read in the representable sense, condition (1) of Stacks 03ZW, and
gives flatness and local finite presentation of every represented base change by the
scheme-level equivalence Tag 02KB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoequalizer_of_surjectiveFiniteLocallyFree
    (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F) (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) f f)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f)
    (hflf : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f) :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology B S hS
    ∃ (hRsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj R))
      (hUsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj U)),
      let RF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj R, hRsh⟩
      let UF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj U, hUsh⟩
      let FF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨F, hF.isSheaf⟩
      let sf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map s⟩
      let tf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map t⟩
      let ff : UF ⟶ FF := ⟨f⟩
    let w : sf ≫ ff = tf ≫ ff := by
        apply Sheaf.hom_ext
        exact hR.w
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ ff w))
declarations.comment: part (3), for a surjective finite locally free chart of the source in place of a surjective étale one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalenceRelation_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The kernel pair of a map from a representable presheaf defines an equivalence
relation over the base scheme. This includes monicity of `R ⟶ U ×_S U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceRelation_of_isPullback
    (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) f f) :
    IsEquivalenceRelation ((Over.post B.inclusion).map s)
      ((Over.post B.inclusion).map t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoequalizer_of_surjectiveEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0262**, part (3). A surjective étale atlas of an algebraic space is the
coequalizer, in fppf sheaves of sets, of its kernel pair: every map to a sheaf which
identifies the two projections descends uniquely.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoequalizer_of_surjectiveEtale
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {R U : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F) (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) f f)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hetale : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology B S hS
    ∃ (hRsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj R))
      (hUsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj U)),
      let RF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj R, hRsh⟩
      let UF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj U, hUsh⟩
      let FF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨F, hF.isSheaf⟩
      let sf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map s⟩
      let tf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map t⟩
      let ff : UF ⟶ FF := ⟨f⟩
    let w : sf ≫ ff = tf ≫ ff := by
        apply Sheaf.hom_ext
        exact hR.w
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ ff w))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0263.** An étale presentation of an algebraic space by a scheme over `S` together
with an étale equivalence relation on it.
declarations.statement:
structure Presentation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0265, the algebraic-space property.** The quotient sheaf of an étale equivalence
relation on an object of the big fppf site of `S` is an algebraic space over `S`. Stacks 0265
assumes the underlying scheme of `U` affine; the proof does not use it.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_quasiAffineDescent` with its
hypothesis `h0247` discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (quotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Over.post B.inclusion) j).obj
declarations.comment: the quotient sheaf is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_toQuotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0265, surjectivity of the quotient map.** This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_toQuotientSheaf_of_quasiAffineDescent` with its hypothesis
`h0247` discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_toQuotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (yonedaEquiv.symm
        ((toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
          (Over.post B.inclusion) j).app (Opposite.op U)
          (𝟙 ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etale_toQuotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0265, étaleness of the quotient map.** This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etale_toQuotientSheaf_of_quasiAffineDescent` with its hypothesis `h0247`
discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_toQuotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (yonedaEquiv.symm
        ((toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
          (Over.post B.inclusion) j).app (Opposite.op U)
          (𝟙 ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U))))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.morRestrict_id
declarations.doc: Restricting a section of `Mor(x, y)` along an identity of `𝒮/U` leaves it unchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma morRestrict_id (x y : p.Fiber U) (g : Over U)
    (m : pullbackFiber p x g.hom ⟶ pullbackFiber p y g.hom) :
    morRestrict p x y (𝟙 g) m = m

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.morRestrict_comp
declarations.doc:
Restricting a section of `Mor(x, y)` along a composite is restricting along the two factors in
turn.
declarations.statement:
lemma morRestrict_comp (x y : p.Fiber U) {g₁ g₂ g₃ : Over U} (h₁ : g₁ ⟶ g₂) (h₂ : g₂ ⟶ g₃)
    (m : pullbackFiber p x g₃.hom ⟶ pullbackFiber p y g₃.hom) :
    morRestrict p x y (h₁ ≫ h₂) m = morRestrict p x y h₁ (morRestrict p x y h₂ m)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.SieveDescentDatum
declarations.doc:
A descent datum relative to a sieve `R` on `U`: an object of the fibre over `V` for each arrow
`f : V ⟶ U` of `R`, and for each pair of arrows of `R` and each pair of morphisms `ε`, `ε'` into
their sources agreeing over `U`, an isomorphism between the chosen pullbacks along `ε` and `ε'` of
the two attached objects, compatible with composition and with base change.
declarations.statement: structure SieveDescentDatum (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) [p.IsFibered] {U : 𝒮} (R : Sieve U)
declarations.comment: (1), sieve-indexed, with no chosen fibre products `U i ×_U U j`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FamilyDescentDatum
declarations.doc:
The category of *descent data relative to a family of morphisms with fixed target*
`𝒰 = {U i ⟶ U}` for a fibred category `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮`: an object of the fibre `𝒳_{U i}` for every
`i`, together with a gluing isomorphism between the two pullbacks of these objects to any object
`Y` mapping to `U i` and to `U i'` compatibly over `U`, subject to the cocycle condition and to
compatibility with further base change.
declarations.statement: abbrev FamilyDescentDatum (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) [p.IsFibered] {U : 𝒮} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U)
declarations.comment:
The category `DD(𝒰)` for a fibred category: its objects (1), its morphisms (2) and
  its category structure (3). Indexed by an arbitrary object mapping to two members of the family
  in place of the chosen fibre products `U i ×_U U i'`, which the two presentations agree over
  whenever those exist, by
  `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData'.descentDataEquivalence`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DescentDatum.eq_id_of_isRestrictionOf_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 026C (1).** Let `D` be a descent datum for any functor `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` (in particular
for any fibred category, not necessarily fibred in groupoids), and `Δ : V i ⟶ Vij i i` a
diagonal, i.e. `Δ ≫ pr₁ i i = 𝟙` and `Δ ≫ pr₂ i i = 𝟙`. A fibre endomorphism `e` of `x i`
which is the pullback `Δ^* φ i i` of the gluing isomorphism `φ i i` along `Δ` is the identity.

The proof is the source's: pulling back the cocycle condition for `(i, i, i)` along the
diagonal `Δ₁₂₃ : V i ⟶ Vijk i i i` gives `e ≫ e = e`, and `e` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentDatum.eq_id_of_isRestrictionOf_diagonal
    (D : DescentDatum p V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij Vijk s₁₂ s₂₃ hVijk q₁ q₂ q₃ hq₁ hq₂ hq₃)
    (i : I) {Δ : V i ⟶ Vij i i}
    (hΔ₁ : 𝟙 (V i) = Δ ≫ pr₁ i i) (hΔ₂ : 𝟙 (V i) = Δ ≫ pr₂ i i)
    {e : D.x i ⟶ D.x i}
    (he : FibreHom p (D.x i) (D.x i) (D.hx i) (D.hx i) e)
    (hr : IsRestrictionOf p Δ hΔ₁ hΔ₂ (D.xrij i i) (D.xrji i i)
      (Restriction.id p (D.x i) (D.hx i)) (Restriction.id p (D.x i) (D.hx i)) (D.φ i i) e) :
    e = 𝟙 (D.x i)
declarations.comment: (1): `Δ^*φ_ii = id` for a general fibred category

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DescentDatum.isRestrictionOf_diagonal_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 026C (1).** For a descent datum `D` for any functor `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` and a diagonal
`Δ : V i ⟶ Vij i i`, the identity of `x i` is the pullback `Δ^* φ i i` of the gluing
isomorphism `φ i i` along `Δ`: the pullback exists and equals the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentDatum.isRestrictionOf_diagonal_id
    (D : DescentDatum p V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij Vijk s₁₂ s₂₃ hVijk q₁ q₂ q₃ hq₁ hq₂ hq₃)
    (i : I) {Δ : V i ⟶ Vij i i}
    (hΔ₁ : 𝟙 (V i) = Δ ≫ pr₁ i i) (hΔ₂ : 𝟙 (V i) = Δ ≫ pr₂ i i) :
    IsRestrictionOf p Δ hΔ₁ hΔ₂ (D.xrij i i) (D.xrji i i)
      (Restriction.id p (D.x i) (D.hx i)) (Restriction.id p (D.x i) (D.hx i)) (D.φ i i)
      (𝟙 (D.x i))
declarations.comment: (1): the pullback of `φ_ii` along the diagonal is `id_{X_i}`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DescentDatum.gluing_comp_eq_id_of_isRestrictionOf_switch
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 026C (2).** Let `D` be a descent datum for any functor `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` (in particular
for any fibred category), and `σ : Vij i j ⟶ Vij j i` the switching morphism, i.e.
`σ ≫ pr₁ j i = pr₂ i j` and `σ ≫ pr₂ j i = pr₁ i j`. If the fibre morphism `σφ` is the pullback
`σ^* φ j i` of `φ j i` along `σ`, then `σφ ∘ φ i j = id`, i.e. `φ i j ≫ σφ = 𝟙`.

The proof is the source's: pull back the cocycle condition for `(i, j, i)` along
`Δ₁₃ : Vij i j ⟶ Vijk i j i`; the `(i, i)` term is the pullback of `Δ^* φ i i`, which is the
identity by part (1) (`DescentDatum.isRestrictionOf_diagonal_id`).
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentDatum.gluing_comp_eq_id_of_isRestrictionOf_switch
    (D : DescentDatum p V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij Vijk s₁₂ s₂₃ hVijk q₁ q₂ q₃ hq₁ hq₂ hq₃)
    (i j : I) {σ : Vij i j ⟶ Vij j i}
    (hσ₁ : pr₂ i j = σ ≫ pr₁ j i) (hσ₂ : pr₁ i j = σ ≫ pr₂ j i)
    {σφ : (D.xrji i j).pt ⟶ (D.xrij i j).pt}
    (hσφ : FibreHom p (D.xrji i j).pt (D.xrij i j).pt (D.xrji i j).hpt (D.xrij i j).hpt σφ)
    (hr : IsRestrictionOf p σ hσ₁ hσ₂ (D.xrij j i) (D.xrji j i) (D.xrji i j) (D.xrij i j)
      (D.φ j i) σφ) :
    D.φ i j ≫ σφ = 𝟙 (D.xrij i j).pt
declarations.comment: (2): `(σ^*φ_ji) ∘ φ_ij = id` for a general fibred category

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DescentDatum.isRestrictionOf_switch_inv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 026C (2).** For a descent datum `D` for any functor `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` and the switching
morphism `σ : Vij i j ⟶ Vij j i`, the inverse of `φ i j` is the pullback `σ^* φ j i` of `φ j i`
along `σ`: the pullback exists and `(σ^* φ j i) ∘ φ i j = id`.
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentDatum.isRestrictionOf_switch_inv
    (D : DescentDatum p V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij Vijk s₁₂ s₂₃ hVijk q₁ q₂ q₃ hq₁ hq₂ hq₃)
    (i j : I) {σ : Vij i j ⟶ Vij j i}
    (hσ₁ : pr₂ i j = σ ≫ pr₁ j i) (hσ₂ : pr₁ i j = σ ≫ pr₂ j i) :
    IsRestrictionOf p σ hσ₁ hσ₂ (D.xrij j i) (D.xrji j i) (D.xrji i j) (D.xrij i j)
      (D.φ j i) (CategoryTheory.inv (I := D.φ_iso i j) (D.φ i j))
declarations.comment: (2): the pullback of `φ_ji` along the switching morphism is `φ_ij⁻¹`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.pullbackFiberComparison_comp_compIso
declarations.doc:
The comparison of two chosen pullbacks of a chosen pullback is the comparison of the two
chosen pullbacks along the composites.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFiberComparison_comp_compIso {T : 𝒮} (y : p.Fiber T) {V W Z : 𝒮} {g : V ⟶ T}
    {g' : W ⟶ T} (ε : Z ⟶ V) (ε' : Z ⟶ W) (heq : ε ≫ g = ε' ≫ g') :
    (pullbackFiberComparison y ε ε' heq).hom ≫ (pullbackFiberCompIso y g' ε').hom =
      (pullbackFiberCompIso y g ε).hom ≫ (pullbackFiberCongr y heq).hom
declarations.comment:
`can_ij = (α_{pr₁, f_j})_X ∘ (α_{pr₀, f_i})_X⁻¹`, where `can` is the gluing
  isomorphism `pullbackFiberComparison` of the canonical descent datum of Stacks 026E (2); stated
  as the commuting square, with `α⁻¹` the contraction `pullbackFiberCompIso` of Stacks 02XO and
  `f_i ∘ pr₀ = f_j ∘ pr₁` carried by `pullbackFiberCongr`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.SieveDescentDatum.ofFiber
declarations.doc:
The descent datum of an object `x` of the fibre over `U`: its chosen pullbacks, glued by the
canonical comparisons of their iterated chosen pullbacks.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofFiber (x : p.Fiber U) (R : Sieve U) : SieveDescentDatum p R
declarations.comment:
(1) and (2) are one construction, read at two sieves: the trivial descent datum
  `(X, id_X)` on `{𝟙 U}` is this datum at the sieve generated by `𝟙 U`, and the canonical descent
  datum `(f_i^* X, can)` on `{f_i : U_i → U}` is this datum at the sieve that family generates,
  with `can` the canonical comparison `CategoryTheory.Functor.pullbackFiberComparison`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.SieveDescentDatum.IsEffective
declarations.doc:
A descent datum is effective when it comes from an object `x` of the fibre over `U`: there is a
cartesian morphism from each of its objects to `x`, compatibly with the gluing isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: def IsEffective : Prop
declarations.comment:
(3), effectivity of a descent datum, stated as the existence of an object `x` of the
  fibre over `U` and a cartesian morphism from each object of the datum to `x` compatible with the
  gluing isomorphisms, in place of an isomorphism with `(f_i^* X, can)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStack
declarations.doc:
The three conditions of Stacks 026F for a functor `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮`: `p` is a fibred category, the
presheaves `Mor(x, y)` of Stacks 02ZB are sheaves, and descent along a covering sieve is
effective.

Condition (2) refers to the chosen pullbacks that condition (1) provides, which is why its field
reintroduces `isFibered` as an instance.
declarations.statement: structure IsStack (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒮) : Prop
declarations.comment: for a functor, the three conditions being the three fields

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isStack_structureFunctor
declarations.doc:
The 2-fibre product of stacks over a site `(𝒞, J)` is a stack, with the hom universe of the
site independent of the hom universe of the three categories of the cospan: if `p𝒳`, `p𝒴`, `p𝒮`
are stacks over `(𝒞, J)` and `F`, `G` are 1-morphisms of fibred categories over `𝒞`, then the
structure functor of the explicit 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴` is again a stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_structureFunctor
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮)
    (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) (h𝒳 : Functor.IsStack p𝒳 J) (h𝒴 : Functor.IsStack p𝒴 J)
    (h𝒮 : Functor.IsStack p𝒮 J) (hF : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒳 p𝒮 F)
    (hG : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒴 p𝒮 G) :
    Functor.IsStack (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) J

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 026O.** A category over the big fppf site of `S` is an *algebraic stack* when it is
fibred in groupoids, is a stack for the fppf topology, has a diagonal representable
by algebraic spaces, and has a presentation by a scheme: a 1-morphism from the category
represented by a scheme `U` over `S`, representable by algebraic spaces, which is surjective and
smooth in the sense that every algebraic space representing its base change along a scheme-valued
point of the stack has surjective and smooth structural morphism.

The stack clause is a conjunction of the two renderings of Stacks 02ZJ, the sieve-indexed
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStack` of Stacks 026F and the family-indexed
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStackInGroupoids` of Stacks 02ZI at the descent universe `w`. The
second conjunct is a consequence of the first — see the implementation notes.

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_isVariety_normalization_isQuasiAffine_not_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0272.** Over any field there is a variety whose normalization is
quasi-affine but which is itself not quasi-affine: the punctured plane with its two punctured
coordinate axes glued to one another.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isVariety_normalization_isQuasiAffine_not_isQuasiAffine
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
      (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety k f ∧
        Scheme.IsQuasiAffine (Scheme.normalizationScheme X hX) ∧
        ¬ Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.InjectiveTilde.exists_injective_tilde_not_flasque
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0274.** An injective module can have a nonflasque associated sheaf
on its affine spectrum.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_tilde_not_flasque :
    ∃ (A : CommRingCat) (J : ModuleCat A),
      Injective J ∧ ¬ TopCat.Presheaf.IsFlasque (tilde J).presheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.InjectiveTilde.exists_injective_tilde_basicOpen_restriction_not_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0274.** Even restriction to a standard open can fail to be
surjective for the associated sheaf of an injective module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_tilde_basicOpen_restriction_not_surjective :
    ∃ (A : CommRingCat) (J : ModuleCat A) (f : A),
      Injective J ∧
        ¬ Function.Surjective
          ((tilde J).presheaf.map
            (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤)).op)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.ArtinianSpace
declarations.doc: A topological space is Artinian if its ascending chains of closed subsets stabilize.
declarations.statement: abbrev ArtinianSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop

declarations.name: Ideal.ringKrullDim_quotient_localization_eq_height_map
declarations.doc:
For `q ≤ p` with `p` prime, the Krull dimension of `Aₚ/qAₚ` is the height of the prime
ideal `p/q` of `A/q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_quotient_localization_eq_height_map
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (q p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (hqp : q ≤ p) :
    ringKrullDim
        (Localization.AtPrime p ⧸ q.map (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p))) =
      ((p.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk q)).height : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Ring.IsHeightCatenary
declarations.doc:
A ring `A` is **catenary** in the sense of relative heights if for all primes
`p₁ ⊆ p₂ ⊆ p₃` the height of `p₃/p₁` in `A/p₁` is the sum of the height of `p₃/p₂` in `A/p₂`
and the height of `p₂/p₁` in `A/p₁`. The source defines this for Noetherian rings; the condition
is stated here for any commutative ring, and for Noetherian rings it agrees with the chain
condition `Ring.IsCatenary` (`Ring.isHeightCatenary_iff_isCatenary`).
declarations.statement: def IsHeightCatenary (A : Type*) [CommRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: Polynomial.IsNumerical
declarations.doc: A polynomial over `ℚ` is numerical if it takes an integer value at every integer.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsNumerical (f : Polynomial ℚ) : Prop

declarations.name: GradedModule.IsLocallyFinite
declarations.doc:
A graded module is locally finite when every homogeneous piece is finitely generated over
the base ring.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyFinite (piece : ℤ → Submodule A M) [DirectSum.Decomposition piece] : Prop

declarations.name: GradedModule.EulerPoincareFunction
declarations.doc:
An Euler–Poincaré function assigns an integer to every finitely generated module and is
additive in short exact sequences.
declarations.statement: structure EulerPoincareFunction (A : Type u) [Ring A]

declarations.name: GradedModule.hilbertFunction
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert function of a locally finite graded module with respect to an Euler–Poincaré
function: its value at `n` is the value of the function on the degree-`n` piece.
declarations.statement:
def hilbertFunction (piece : ℤ → Submodule A M) [DirectSum.Decomposition piece]
    (hpiece : IsLocallyFinite piece) (φ : EulerPoincareFunction.{u, v} A) : ℤ → ℤ

declarations.name: GradedModule.HasHilbertPolynomial
declarations.doc:
A locally finite graded module has a Hilbert polynomial with respect to `φ` when its Hilbert
function eventually agrees, on integer arguments, with a numerical polynomial.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasHilbertPolynomial (piece : ℤ → Submodule A M) [DirectSum.Decomposition piece]
    (hpiece : IsLocallyFinite piece) (φ : EulerPoincareFunction.{u, v} A) : Prop

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsCohenMacaulayOfDimension
declarations.doc:
A local ring `A` is *Cohen--Macaulay of dimension `d`* if its Krull dimension is `d` and
there is a system of parameters `x₁, ..., x_d` such that every `xᵢ` is a nonzerodivisor on the
quotient by its predecessors.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCohenMacaulayOfDimension (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (d : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FiniteFilteredObject.filteredAcyclic
declarations.doc:
A complex of finite filtered objects is filtered acyclic when every graded-piece complex
is acyclic.
declarations.statement:
abbrev filteredAcyclic (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    (K : CochainComplex (FiniteFilteredObject A) ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsInvertible
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is invertible if every point has an open neighbourhood on which it is
isomorphic to the structure sheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsTrivial
declarations.doc: A sheaf of modules is trivial if it is globally isomorphic to the structure sheaf.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.exists_covering_localLifts
declarations.doc:
If `ψ : ℱ₂ ⟶ ℱ₃` is locally surjective for the topology of open covers, then every section `τ`
of `ℱ₃` over an open `W` admits an open covering of `W` together with a `0`-cochain of `ℱ₂`
lifting the restrictions of `τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_covering_localLifts {W : Opens X} (τ : ToType (ℱ₃.obj (op W)))
    (hψ : CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) ψ) :
    ∃ (I₀ : Type uX) (U₀ : I₀ → Opens X) (hU₀ : W = ⨆ i, U₀ i) (lift : Cochain U₀ ℱ₂ 0),
      ∀ i : Fin 1 → I₀,
        ψ.app (op (inter U₀ i)) (lift i) = restr ℱ₃ (inter_le_of_eq_iSup hU₀ i) τ
declarations.comment: existence of a covering with lifts

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.deltaCochain
declarations.doc:
The Čech `1`-cochain `(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀}|_{U_{i₀i₁}} - τ̃_{i₁}|_{U_{i₀i₁}}` attached to a
`0`-cochain `τ̃`: the assignment of Stacks 02AP. It is the negative of the Čech coboundary of `τ̃`
(`deltaCochain_eq_neg_cechD`).
declarations.statement:
def deltaCochain {ℱ : TopCat.Presheaf AddCommGrpCat.{v} X} (t : Cochain U ℱ 0) :
    Cochain U ℱ 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.exists_cocycle_deltaCochain_of_localLifts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AP, the cocycle.** Let `φ : ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂` be injective on sections and
`ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃` exact in the middle on sections. If `τ` is a section of `ℱ₃` over `W` and `τ̃` is a
`0`-cochain of `ℱ₂` lifting the restrictions of `τ`, then the cochain
`(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀}|_{U_{i₀i₁}} - τ̃_{i₁}|_{U_{i₀i₁}}` is the image of a `1`-cocycle of `ℱ₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cocycle_deltaCochain_of_localLifts
    (hmono : ∀ V : Opens X, Function.Injective (φ.app (op V)))
    (hexact : ∀ (V : Opens X) (b : ToType (ℱ₂.obj (op V))), ψ.app (op V) b = 0 →
      ∃ a, φ.app (op V) a = b)
    (hlift : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U i)) (lift i) = restr ℱ₃ (hle i) τ) :
    ∃ c : cocycles1 U ℱ₁, push U φ 1 (c : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift
declarations.comment: the cocycle `(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀} - τ̃_{i₁}` with values in `ℱ₁`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.cls_eq_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AP, independence of the lifts.** Let `φ : ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂` be injective on sections and
`ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃` exact in the middle on sections. Two systems of lifts of the same section give
cocycles `(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀} - τ̃_{i₁}` with the same class in `Ȟ¹(𝒰, ℱ₁)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cls_eq_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
    (hmono : ∀ V : Opens X, Function.Injective (φ.app (op V)))
    (hexact : ∀ (V : Opens X) (b : ToType (ℱ₂.obj (op V))), ψ.app (op V) b = 0 →
      ∃ a, φ.app (op V) a = b)
    {lift' : Cochain U ℱ₂ 0}
    (hlift : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U i)) (lift i) = restr ℱ₃ (hle i) τ)
    (hlift' : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U i)) (lift' i) = restr ℱ₃ (hle i) τ)
    {c c' : cocycles1 U ℱ₁}
    (hc : push U φ 1 (c : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift)
    (hc' : push U φ 1 (c' : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift') :
    cls U ℱ₁ c = cls U ℱ₁ c'
declarations.comment: the class `δ(τ)` does not depend on the lifts

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.cls_add_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AP, additivity of `δ`.** Let `φ : ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂` be injective on sections. The class of
the cocycle `(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀} - τ̃_{i₁}` attached to the sum of two systems of local lifts is the
sum of the two classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cls_add_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
    (hmono : ∀ V : Opens X, Function.Injective (φ.app (op V)))
    {lift' : Cochain U ℱ₂ 0} {c c' d : cocycles1 U ℱ₁}
    (hc : push U φ 1 (c : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift)
    (hc' : push U φ 1 (c' : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift')
    (hd : push U φ 1 (d : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U (lift + lift')) :
    cls U ℱ₁ d = cls U ℱ₁ c + cls U ℱ₁ c'

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.cls_eq_of_refinement_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AP, independence of the covering on a common refinement.** Let `φ : ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂` be
injective on sections and `ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃` exact in the middle on sections. Let `𝒰` and `𝒰'` be
two families of opens over `W`, each with a system of lifts of the same section `τ` of `ℱ₃`, and
let `𝒱` be a common refinement of the two. Then the classes of the two cocycles
`(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀} - τ̃_{i₁}` have the same image in `Ȟ¹(𝒱, ℱ₁)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cls_eq_of_refinement_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
    (U' : I' → Opens X) (V : K → Opens X)
    (r : K → I) (hr : ∀ k, V k ≤ U (r k))
    (r' : K → I') (hr' : ∀ k, V k ≤ U' (r' k))
    (hle' : ∀ i : Fin 1 → I', inter U' i ≤ W)
    (hmono : ∀ V₀ : Opens X, Function.Injective (φ.app (op V₀)))
    (hexact : ∀ (V₀ : Opens X) (b : ToType (ℱ₂.obj (op V₀))), ψ.app (op V₀) b = 0 →
      ∃ a, φ.app (op V₀) a = b)
    {lift' : Cochain U' ℱ₂ 0}
    (hlift : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U i)) (lift i) = restr ℱ₃ (hle i) τ)
    (hlift' : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U' i)) (lift' i) = restr ℱ₃ (hle' i) τ)
    {c : cocycles1 U ℱ₁} {c' : cocycles1 U' ℱ₁}
    (hc : push U φ 1 (c : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift)
    (hc' : push U' φ 1 (c' : Cochain U' ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U' lift') :
    refinementCechH1 U V r hr ℱ₁ (cls U ℱ₁ c) =
      refinementCechH1 U' V r' hr' ℱ₁ (cls U' ℱ₁ c')
declarations.comment: the class `δ(τ)` agrees on a given common refinement of two coverings

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechBoundary.exists_common_refinement_cls_eq_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AP, independence of the covering.** Let `φ : ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂` be injective on sections
and `ℱ₁ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₃` exact in the middle on sections. Two families of opens covering `W`, each with
a system of lifts of the same section `τ` of `ℱ₃`, admit a common refinement covering `W`, the
family of their pairwise intersections, on which the classes of the two cocycles
`(i₀, i₁) ↦ τ̃_{i₀} - τ̃_{i₁}` agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_common_refinement_cls_eq_of_push_eq_deltaCochain
    (U' : I' → Opens X) (hU : W = ⨆ i, U i) (hU' : W = ⨆ i', U' i')
    (hmono : ∀ V₀ : Opens X, Function.Injective (φ.app (op V₀)))
    (hexact : ∀ (V₀ : Opens X) (b : ToType (ℱ₂.obj (op V₀))), ψ.app (op V₀) b = 0 →
      ∃ a, φ.app (op V₀) a = b)
    {lift' : Cochain U' ℱ₂ 0}
    (hlift : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U i)) (lift i) = restr ℱ₃ (inter_le_of_eq_iSup hU i) τ)
    (hlift' : ∀ i, ψ.app (op (inter U' i)) (lift' i) = restr ℱ₃ (inter_le_of_eq_iSup hU' i) τ)
    {c : cocycles1 U ℱ₁} {c' : cocycles1 U' ℱ₁}
    (hc : push U φ 1 (c : Cochain U ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U lift)
    (hc' : push U' φ 1 (c' : Cochain U' ℱ₁ 1) = deltaCochain U' lift') :
    ∃ (V : I × I' → Opens X) (r : I × I' → I) (hr : ∀ k, V k ≤ U (r k))
      (r' : I × I' → I') (hr' : ∀ k, V k ≤ U' (r' k)),
      W = ⨆ k, V k ∧
        refinementCechH1 U V r hr ℱ₁ (cls U ℱ₁ c) =
          refinementCechH1 U' V r' hr' ℱ₁ (cls U' ℱ₁ c')
declarations.comment: the class `δ(τ)` does not depend on the covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.mono_toTotalQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (6).** The structure sheaf of a scheme is a subsheaf of its sheaf of
total quotient rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.mono_toTotalQuotientSheaf (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
    Mono Y.toTotalQuotientSheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.shortExact_unitGroupSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (6).** The sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒪_X^* ⟶ 𝒦_X^* ⟶ 𝒦_X^*/𝒪_X^* ⟶ 0` of
unit-group sheaves of a scheme is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.shortExact_unitGroupSheaf (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (unitGroupSheafMap Y.toTotalQuotientSheaf)
      (unitGroupQuotientMap Y.toTotalQuotientSheaf) (by
        change (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.toPresheafedSpace)
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map (unitGroupMap Y.toTotalQuotientSheaf) ≫
          (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.toPresheafedSpace)
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
            (cokernel.π (unitGroupMap Y.toTotalQuotientSheaf)) = 0
        rw [← Functor.map_comp]
        simp)).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (7).** A Cartier divisor on a scheme is a global section of the quotient
sheaf `𝒦_X^*/𝒪_X^*`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Scheme.CartierDivisor (Y : Scheme.{u}) : Type u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_local_representation
declarations.doc:
**Tag 02AR part (8), the local presentation of clause (b).** Near any point of a locally
Noetherian integral scheme, a Cartier divisor is the image of a unit of the sheaf of total
quotient rings over an affine open neighbourhood, and that unit is the fraction `a / b` of two
regular functions on that neighbourhood with `b` nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_local_representation [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (τ : X.CartierDivisor) (x : X) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U) (a b : Γ(X, U)) (_ : b ≠ 0)
      (v : (unitGroupPresheaf X.totalQuotientSheaf).obj (op U)),
      (Additive.toMul v).val * X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U) b =
          X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U) a ∧
        (unitGroupQuotientSheaf X.toTotalQuotientSheaf).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op τ =
          (rawUnitGroupQuotientMap X.toTotalQuotientSheaf).app (op U) v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartierWeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (8).** The Weil divisor `[τ] = Σ v_Z(τ) [Z]` of a Cartier divisor on a
Noetherian integral scheme.
declarations.statement: def cartierWeilDivisor [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X] (τ : X.CartierDivisor) : WeilDivisor X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartierWeilDivisor_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (8).** The coefficient of `[τ]` at a prime divisor is the order
`v_Z(τ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cartierWeilDivisor_apply [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X] (τ : X.CartierDivisor)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) :
    (cartierWeilDivisor τ).1 Z = cartierMultiplicity τ Z.genericPoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_germ_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (8), clause (a).** The coefficient of `[τ]` vanishes at a prime divisor at
whose generic point the germ of `τ` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem cartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_germ_eq_zero [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (τ : X.CartierDivisor) (Z : PrimeDivisor X)
    (hτ : (unitGroupQuotientSheaf X.toTotalQuotientSheaf).presheaf.Γgerm Z.genericPoint τ = 0) :
    (cartierWeilDivisor τ).1 Z = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_local_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (8), clause (b).** The coefficient of `[τ]` at a prime divisor computed
from a local presentation `a / b` of `τ` on an open neighbourhood of its generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem cartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_local_eq [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (τ : X.CartierDivisor) (Z : PrimeDivisor X) (U : X.Opens) (hξ : Z.genericPoint ∈ U)
    (a b : Γ(X, U)) (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (v : (unitGroupPresheaf X.totalQuotientSheaf).obj (op U))
    (hab : (Additive.toMul v).val * X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U) b =
      X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U) a)
    (hτ : (unitGroupQuotientSheaf X.toTotalQuotientSheaf).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op τ =
      (rawUnitGroupQuotientMap X.toTotalQuotientSheaf).app (op U) v) :
    (cartierWeilDivisor τ).1 Z =
      ((Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) ⧸
          Ideal.span {X.presheaf.germ U Z.genericPoint hξ a})).toNat : ℤ) -
      ((Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) ⧸
          Ideal.span {X.presheaf.germ U Z.genericPoint hξ b})).toNat : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierWeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (5).** The Weil divisor `[D] = Σ v_Z(D) [Z]` of an effective Cartier
divisor on a Noetherian integral scheme.

The hypothesis is not used by the term — the coefficient family of an arbitrary ideal sheaf is
already finitely supported — but it is what makes the coefficients the orders of Tag 02AR,
since only for an effective Cartier divisor is the local length finite.
declarations.statement:
def effectiveCartierWeilDivisor [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (_hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I) : WeilDivisor X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierWeilDivisor_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (5).** The coefficient of `[D]` at a prime divisor is the order
`v_Z(D)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierWeilDivisor_apply [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) :
    (effectiveCartierWeilDivisor I hI).1 Z = effectiveCartierMultiplicity I Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_notMem_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (5), clause (a).** The coefficient of `[D]` at a prime divisor whose
generic point lies outside `D` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_notMem_support [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) (hZ : Z.genericPoint ∉ I.support) :
    (effectiveCartierWeilDivisor I hI).1 Z = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_ideal_eq_span
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (5), clause (b).** When the generic point of `Z` lies in `D`, the
coefficient of `[D]` at `Z` is the length of `𝒪_{X, Z} / (f)` for the nonzerodivisor `f` that
defines `D` on an affine open neighbourhood of that generic point, as in part (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierWeilDivisor_apply_of_ideal_eq_span [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    {I : X.IdealSheafData} (hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) {U : X.affineOpens} (hxU : Z.genericPoint ∈ U.1) {f : Γ(X, U.1)}
    (hf : I.ideal U = Ideal.span {f}) :
    (effectiveCartierWeilDivisor I hI).1 Z =
      ((Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) ⧸
          Ideal.span {(X.presheaf.germ U.1 Z.genericPoint hxU).hom f})).toNat : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.totalQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of total quotient rings of a scheme. It is the sheafification of the presheaf
which, on each open set, localizes the ring of regular functions at the sections whose germs
are nonzerodivisors everywhere on that open set.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev Scheme.totalQuotientSheaf (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
    TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.toTotalQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism from the structure sheaf to the sheaf of total quotient rings,
giving the latter its structure as a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Scheme.toTotalQuotientSheaf (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
    Y.sheaf ⟶ Y.totalQuotientSheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PrimeDivisor.algebraMap_stalk_functionField_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (2), the local ring as a subring.** On an integral scheme the local ring
`𝒪_{X, Z}` at the generic point of a prime divisor `Z` embeds into the function field `K(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.algebraMap_stalk_functionField_injective [IsIntegral X]
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) :
    Function.Injective
      (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) X.functionField)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rationalFunctionWeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (3).** The Weil divisor `Σ v_Z(f) [Z]` of a nonzero rational function `f`
on a Noetherian integral scheme: the coefficient at a prime divisor `Z` is the order of vanishing
of `f` at the generic point of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
def rationalFunctionWeilDivisor [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X] (f : X.functionFieldˣ) :
    WeilDivisor X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (3).** The coefficient of the Weil divisor of a rational function at a
prime divisor `Z` is the order `v_Z(f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X.functionFieldˣ) (Z : PrimeDivisor X) :
    (rationalFunctionWeilDivisor X f).1 Z = X.ord (f : X.functionField) Z.genericPoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply_of_eq_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (3), clause (b).** If the rational function `f` lies in the local ring
`𝒪_{X, Z}`, its coefficient at `Z` is the length of `𝒪_{X, Z} / (f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply_of_eq_algebraMap [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X.functionFieldˣ) (Z : PrimeDivisor X) (a : X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
    (hf : (f : X.functionField) = algebraMap _ X.functionField a) :
    (rationalFunctionWeilDivisor X f).1 Z =
      ((Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) ⧸ Ideal.span {a})).toNat : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply_of_eq_algebraMap_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (3), clause (a).** If the rational function `f` is a unit of the local
ring `𝒪_{X, Z}`, its coefficient at `Z` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply_of_eq_algebraMap_unit [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X.functionFieldˣ) (Z : PrimeDivisor X) (u : (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)ˣ)
    (hf : (f : X.functionField) =
      algebraMap _ X.functionField (u : X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)) :
    (rationalFunctionWeilDivisor X f).1 Z = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply_of_eq_div
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (3), clause (c).** If the rational function is a fraction `f = a / b` of
two elements of the local ring `𝒪_{X, Z}`, its coefficient at `Z` is the difference of the
lengths of `𝒪_{X, Z} / (a)` and `𝒪_{X, Z} / (b)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionWeilDivisor_apply_of_eq_div [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X.functionFieldˣ) (Z : PrimeDivisor X) (a b : X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
    (hf : (f : X.functionField) =
      algebraMap _ X.functionField a / algebraMap _ X.functionField b) :
    (rationalFunctionWeilDivisor X f).1 Z =
      ((Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) ⧸ Ideal.span {a})).toNat : ℤ) -
      ((Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk Z.genericPoint) ⧸ Ideal.span {b})).toNat : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem_submonoidPresheafOfStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02AR part (6), the denominators are nonzerodivisors.** For a sheaf of commutative
rings, a section over an open set whose germ at every point of that open set is a nonzerodivisor
is itself a nonzerodivisor in the ring of sections. This is the inclusion of the denominator
submonoid `S_U` of the total quotient presheaf into the nonzerodivisors, and it needs no
hypothesis on the open set.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem_submonoidPresheafOfStalk
    (O : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X) {U : Opens X} {b : O.presheaf.obj (op U)}
    (hb : b ∈ (O.presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk
      fun y => (O.presheaf.stalk y)⁰).obj (op U)) :
    b ∈ (O.presheaf.obj (op U))⁰

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.Cohomology.projectivePlane_exists_iso_twistingSheaf_and_sections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02AX.** Let `k` be a field and `ℙ²_k = Proj k[X₀, X₁, X₂]`.

1. Every invertible sheaf on `ℙ²_k` is isomorphic to `𝒪(n)` for some `n ∈ ℤ`.
2. For `n ≥ 0` the canonical map `k[X₀, X₁, X₂]_n ⟶ Γ(ℙ²_k, 𝒪(n))` is bijective.
3. For every `n ∈ ℤ`, `Γ(ℙ²_k, 𝒪(n))` is the degree-`n` part of `k[X₀, X₁, X₂]` (the grading
   extended by zero, so both sides vanish for `n < 0`).

The twist `ℱ(n) = ℱ ⊗ 𝒪(n)` of the last sentence of the source is the definition
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafOfModules`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectivePlane_exists_iso_twistingSheaf_and_sections (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    (∀ L : (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (2 + 1)) k)).Modules,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
          (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (2 + 1)) k)).presheaf
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
          (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (2 + 1)) k)).ringCatIsSheaf L →
      ∃ m : ℤ, Nonempty
        (L ≅ twistingSheaf (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (2 + 1)) k) m)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
      (degreeSection (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (2 + 1)) k) n)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty (twistTopSections k 2 n ≃+
      integerGrading (S := MvPolynomial (Fin (2 + 1)) k)
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (2 + 1)) k) n))
declarations.comment: invertible sheaves on ℙ²_k are the twists 𝒪(n), and Γ(ℙ²_k, 𝒪(n)) is the degree-n part of k[X₀, X₁, X₂] for every n ∈ ℤ (through the canonical map for n ≥ 0)

declarations.name: IsLocalization.Away.subsingleton_iff_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
A localization `R_f` of `R` away from `f` is the zero ring if and only if `f` is nilpotent
in `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_iff_isNilpotent [IsLocalization.Away f S] :
    Subsingleton S ↔ IsNilpotent f
declarations.comment:
Item 2: `A_f = 0` if and only if `f` is nilpotent in `A`, for every localization
`A_f` of `A` with respect to `f`.

registrations.name: LocalizedModule
registrations.comment:
Items 1 and 2: for an `A`-module `M`, the localization `M_𝔭` at a prime `𝔭`
is `LocalizedModule 𝔭.primeCompl M`, and the localization `M_f` with respect to `f ∈ A` is
`LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M`.

declarations.name: IsLocalization.isLocalization_sup_of_isLocalization_map
declarations.doc:
**Localization in two stages.** If `B` is the localization of `A` at `S'` and `T` is the
localization of `B` at the image `S̄` of `S`, then `T` is the localization of `A` at the
product submonoid `S ⊔ S' = SS'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalization_sup_of_isLocalization_map [IsLocalization S' B]
    [IsLocalization (S.map (algebraMap A B)) T] : IsLocalization (S ⊔ S') T
declarations.comment:
Stated as `IsLocalization (S ⊔ S') T`: in a commutative monoid `S ⊔ S'` is
the set of products `s * s'`, which is Stacks' `SS'`; the isomorphism itself is
`IsLocalization.algEquivSupOfIsLocalizationMap`.

declarations.name: LocalizedModule.equivLocalizedModuleLocalizedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02C7.**  Iterated localization of modules: for multiplicative subsets
`S, S' ⊆ R` and an `R`-module `M`, the localization of `M` at the multiplicative set
`SS' = S ⊔ S'` is the localization at `S` of the `R`-module `S'⁻¹M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivLocalizedModuleLocalizedModule :
    LocalizedModule (S ⊔ S') M ≃ₗ[R] LocalizedModule S (LocalizedModule S' M)

declarations.name: prod_field_isJacobsonRing
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an infinite type and `(k α)` a family of fields. Then the product ring `∀ α, k α` is
a Jacobson ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem prod_field_isJacobsonRing
    (A : Type*) [Infinite A] (k : A → Type*) [∀ α, Field (k α)] :
    IsJacobsonRing (∀ α, k α)

declarations.name: Module.setOf_minimal_support_eq_setOf_minimal_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `M` a finite `R`-module. The primes minimal in `Supp(M)` are
exactly the primes minimal in `Ass(M)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setOf_minimal_support_eq_setOf_minimal_associatedPrimes {R M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    {q : PrimeSpectrum R | Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q} =
      {q : PrimeSpectrum R | Minimal (· ∈ PrimeSpectrum.asIdeal ⁻¹' associatedPrimes R M) q}
declarations.comment: Parts (1) and (2); the equality with part (3) is the first conclusion of Stacks 00L7, which the source's own proof cites for that step.

declarations.name: Polynomial.monic_aeval_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_int
declarations.doc:
Substitution by a monic integral polynomial of positive degree is finite locally free
of rank equal to its degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem monic_aeval_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_int (h : Polynomial ℤ)
    (hh : h.Monic) (hd : 0 < h.natDegree) :
    letI : Algebra (Polynomial ℤ) (Polynomial ℤ) := (Polynomial.aeval h).toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Module (Polynomial ℤ) (Polynomial ℤ) := Algebra.toModule
    Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (Polynomial ℤ) (Polynomial ℤ) h.natDegree

declarations.name: Polynomial.monic_aeval_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_zmod
declarations.doc:
After reduction modulo a prime, substitution by the reduced monic polynomial is
finite locally free of the original degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem monic_aeval_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_zmod (h : Polynomial ℤ)
    (hh : h.Monic) (hd : 0 < h.natDegree) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    let g : Polynomial (ZMod p) := h.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))
    letI : Algebra (Polynomial (ZMod p)) (Polynomial (ZMod p)) :=
      (Polynomial.aeval g).toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Module (Polynomial (ZMod p)) (Polynomial (ZMod p)) := Algebra.toModule
    Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (Polynomial (ZMod p))
      (Polynomial (ZMod p)) h.natDegree

declarations.name: exists_isIdempotentElem_isLocalization_away_of_unramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02FL.** If `R → S` is unramified, then there is an idempotent
`e ∈ S ⊗[R] S` such that the multiplication map `μ : S ⊗[R] S → S` exhibits `S`
as the localization of `A := S ⊗[R] S` away from `e`. Equivalently (the standard
reading of "isomorphic as objects under `A`"), the localization map `A → A_e` is
isomorphic to `μ` under `A`.

Here the `(S ⊗[R] S)`-algebra structure on `S` is the one induced by the
multiplication map `μ = Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIdempotentElem_isLocalization_away_of_unramified (R S : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.Unramified R S] :
    ∃ e : S ⊗[R] S, IsIdempotentElem e ∧
      letI : Algebra (S ⊗[R] S) S := (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' R).toRingHom.toAlgebra
      IsLocalization.Away e S

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_map_eq_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02FM.** Let `R → S` be of finite type and let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over the
prime `p` of `R`. If `p S_q` is the maximal ideal of `S_q` and `κ(q)/κ(p)` is finite separable,
then `R → S` is unramified at `q`: there is `g ∉ q` such that `R → S_g` is unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unramified_away_of_map_eq_maximalIdeal {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    [q.LiesOver p] [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Localization.AtPrime.IsLiesOverAlgebra p q]
    (hmax : p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
    (_hfin : Module.Finite p.ResidueField q.ResidueField)
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField q.ResidueField) :
    ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Unramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Unramified at `q` is written as in Definition 00UT (3), as `R → S_g` unramified
for some `g ∉ q`, and `κ(q)/κ(p)` is the extension induced by `R_p → S_q`.

registrations.name: Stacks.SpaceTorsor.Action.IsTorsor
registrations.comment: the torsor condition on an action

registrations.name: Stacks.SpaceTorsor.PresheafOfGroups.trivialAction
registrations.comment: the action defining the trivial torsor

declarations.name: Stacks.SpaceTorsor.torsor_trivial_iff_global_section
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a topological space, `G` a sheaf of (possibly non-commutative) groups on `X`, and
`F` a sheaf of sets with an action `a` of `G` making it a `G`-torsor. Then `F` is trivial if and
only if `F(X)` is nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsor_trivial_iff_global_section
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (G : SheafOfGroups.{u, v} X) (F : SheafOfSets.{u, v} X)
    (a : Action G.toPresheafOfGroups F.toPresheafOfSets)
    (htorsor : a.IsTorsor) :
    a.IsTrivial ↔ Nonempty (F.obj ⊤)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SheafTorsor.torsorCohomologyClassification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FQ.** The canonical classification, with the
transition-cocycle, trivial-torsor and contracted-product laws.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def torsorCohomologyClassification (X : TopCat.{u})
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    (H : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} X) :
    TorsorCohomologyClassification X H

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SheafTorsor.torsorClassEquivSheafCohomologyOne

declarations.name: Stacks.CechTotalComplex.CoveringResolution.isColimitCoveringTermCofan
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FT, third displayed formula.** Let `(X, R)` be a ringed space, let
`X = ⋃ i, U i` be a locally finite open covering and let `F` be a sheaf of `R`-modules. Then the
degree-`p` term `𝔠ᵖ(𝒰, F) = ∏ (j_{i₀ … i_p})_* F_{i₀ … i_p}` of the covering resolution of
Tag 02FU, together with the canonical injections `coveringTermInj`, is a coproduct of the
factors: `𝔠ᵖ(𝒰, F) = ⨁ (j_{i₀ … i_p})_* F_{i₀ … i_p}`.

The covering hypothesis is the source's; the proof uses only local finiteness.
declarations.statement:
def isColimitCoveringTermCofan (_hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤) (hlf : LocallyFinite fun i => (U i : Set X))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R) (p : ℕ) :
    IsColimit (Cofan.mk (((coveringComplex.{u, v, w, t} X R U).obj F).X p)
      (coveringTermInj.{u, v, w, t} X R U F p))
declarations.comment:
(third displayed formula: the terms of the complex of Tag 02FU are
𝔠ᵖ(𝒰, F) = ⨁ (j_{i₀…i_p})_* F_{i₀…i_p})

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyFiniteCover.isColimitCofanProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FT, second displayed formula.** Let `X = ⋃ i, U i` be a locally
finite open covering of a topological space, let `j i : U i → X` be the inclusions and let
`F i` be an abelian sheaf on `U i`. Then the product of the `(j i)_* (F i)`, equipped with
the canonical injections `deltaInj`, is a coproduct of the `(j i)_* (F i)`: that is
`⨁ i, (j i)_* (F i) = ∏ i, (j i)_* (F i)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimitCofanProduct (_hcov : IsOpenCover U)
    (hlf : LocallyFinite fun i => (U i : Set X)) : IsColimit (productCofan U F)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyFiniteCover.isIso_coproductToProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FT, second displayed formula.** For a locally finite open
covering the canonical map from the direct sum of the `(j i)_* (F i)` to their direct product
is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coproductToProduct (hcov : IsOpenCover U)
    (hlf : LocallyFinite fun i => (U i : Set X)) : IsIso (coproductToProduct U F)
declarations.comment: (second displayed formula, as an isomorphism from ∐ to ∏)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyFiniteCover.isIso_sectionsComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FT, first displayed formula.** With `X = ⋃ i, U i` a locally
finite open covering and `𝒢 = ⨁ i, (j i)_* (F i)`, for every open `V` of `X` the canonical
comparison from `Γ (V, 𝒢)` to `∏ i, (F i) (V ∩ U i)` is an isomorphism: the sections of the
direct sum over `V` are the *product* of the groups `(F i) (V ∩ U i)`.

The comparison is the sections over `V` of the canonical map from the direct sum to the
product, followed by the canonical comparison from the sections of a product of sheaves to
the product of their sections. The `i`-th factor of the target is
`(sectionsFunctor V).obj (pushforwardOpen U F i)`, which is `(F i) (V ∩ U i)` by
`Stacks.LocallyFiniteCover.sectionsFunctor_obj_pushforwardOpen`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sectionsComparison (hcov : IsOpenCover U)
    (hlf : LocallyFinite fun i => (U i : Set X)) (V : Opens X) :
    IsIso ((sectionsFunctor V).map (coproductToProduct U F) ≫
      piComparison (sectionsFunctor V) (fun i => pushforwardOpen U F i))
declarations.comment: (first displayed formula: Γ(V, 𝒢) = ∏ F_i(V ∩ U_i))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoveringResolutionQuasiIso.exists_coveringResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FU.** Every open covering of a ringed space gives a canonical
augmented Čech resolution, functorial in the module sheaf: the complex, its augmentation,
the product coordinates of its terms with Equation 01EE for the differential, the existence
of homology, and the quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringResolution (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤) :
    Nonempty (Stacks.CechTotalComplex.CoveringResolution.{u, v, w, t} X R U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If `X ⟶ S` is locally of finite presentation and `Y ⟶ S` is locally of finite
type, then a factor `X ⟶ Y` is locally of finite presentation.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If `X ⟶ S` is of finite presentation and `Y ⟶ S` is quasi-separated and locally
of finite type, then a factor `X ⟶ Y` is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (f ≫ g))
    [QuasiSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_krullDimOfRing_stalk_add_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FX.** For a morphism locally of finite type, the dimension of the
fibre at a point is the dimension of the local ring of the fibre there plus the transcendence
degree of the residue-field extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_krullDimOfRing_stalk_add_trdeg
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x)) +
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) :
          WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg
declarations.doc:
For a morphism locally of finite type, the dimension of the fibre at a point is the Krull
dimension of the local ring of the fibre there plus the transcendence degree of the residue field
extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x)) +
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) :
          WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FY part (1).** In a fibre product diagram with `f` locally of finite
type, the fibre of the base change `f'` has the same dimension at `x'` as the fibre of `f` has
at the image of `x'`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiberMap_ringKrullDim_stalk_add_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FY part (2).** In a fibre product diagram with `f` locally of finite
type, the dimension of the local ring at `x'` of the fibre of the induced morphism of fibres, plus
the dimension of the local ring of `X_s` at `x = g' x'`, is the dimension of the local ring of
`X'_{s'}` at `x'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fiberMap_ringKrullDim_stalk_add_eq (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x' : X') :
    ringKrullDim (((fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x')).fiber
            (fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x') (f'.asFiber x'))).presheaf.stalk
          ((fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x')).asFiber (f'.asFiber x'))) +
        ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (g (f' x'))).presheaf.stalk
          (fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x') (f'.asFiber x'))) =
      ringKrullDim ((f'.fiber (f' x')).presheaf.stalk (f'.asFiber x'))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiberMap_ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FY part (2).** The same dimension is the loss of residue-field
transcendence degree: the dimension of the local ring at `x'` of the fibre of the induced
morphism of fibres, plus `trdeg_{κ(s')} κ(x')`, is `trdeg_{κ(s)} κ(x)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fiberMap_ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg_eq (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x' : X') :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap (g' x')).hom.toAlgebra
    letI := (f'.residueFieldMap x').hom.toAlgebra
    ringKrullDim (((fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x')).fiber
            (fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x') (f'.asFiber x'))).presheaf.stalk
          ((fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x')).asFiber (f'.asFiber x'))) +
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg ↥(S'.residueField (f' x')) ↥(X'.residueField x')) :
          WithBot ℕ∞) =
      (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg ↥(S.residueField (f (g' x'))) ↥(X.residueField (g' x'))) :
        WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_fiber_le_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FY part (2).** The dimension of the local ring of a fibre cannot drop
under base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_fiber_le_of_baseChange (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x' : X') :
    ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (g (f' x'))).presheaf.stalk
        (fiberMap f' g' g f hsq.w (f' x') (f'.asFiber x'))) ≤
      ringKrullDim ((f'.fiber (f' x')).presheaf.stalk (f'.asFiber x'))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.trdeg_residueField_le_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FY part (2).** The transcendence degree of the residue-field
extension cannot grow under base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem trdeg_residueField_le_of_baseChange (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x' : X') :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap (g' x')).hom.toAlgebra
    letI := (f'.residueFieldMap x').hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.trdeg ↥(S'.residueField (f' x')) ↥(X'.residueField x') ≤
      Algebra.trdeg ↥(S.residueField (f (g' x'))) ↥(X.residueField (g' x'))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pullback_point_preserving_fibre_dimension_and_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02FY part (3).** In a fibre product diagram with `f` locally of finite
type, let `s'` be a point of `S'` and `x` a point of `X` with the same image `s` in `S`. Then
there is a common lift `x'` of `x` and `s'` to `X'` at which neither the dimension of the local
ring of the fibre nor the transcendence degree of the residue-field extension changes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pullback_point_preserving_fibre_dimension_and_trdeg
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (s' : S') (x : X) (h : f x = g s') :
    ∃ (x' : X') (_hx : g' x' = x) (hs' : f' x' = s'),
      ringKrullDim ((f'.fiber s').presheaf.stalk ((f'.fiberHomeo s').symm ⟨x', hs'⟩)) =
          ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (g s')).presheaf.stalk
            ((f.fiberHomeo (g s')).symm ⟨x, h⟩)) ∧
        (letI := ((S.residueFieldCongr h).inv ≫ f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
         letI := ((S'.residueFieldCongr hs').inv ≫ f'.residueFieldMap x').hom.toAlgebra
         Algebra.trdeg ↥(S.residueField (g s')) ↥(X.residueField x) =
           Algebra.trdeg ↥(S'.residueField s') ↥(X'.residueField x'))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRetrocompact_setOf_fiberDimensionAt_le

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isFiniteLocallyFree_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of relative differentials of a smooth morphism of
schemes is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.isFiniteLocallyFree_relativeDifferentials (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
      (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_stalk_relativeDifferentials_eq_fiberDimensionAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02G1.** For a smooth morphism of schemes, the rank at a point of the
sheaf of relative differentials is the local dimension of the fibre at that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_stalk_relativeDifferentials_eq_fiberDimensionAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Smooth f] (x : X) :
    (Module.finrank (ToType (X.sheaf.presheaf.stalk x))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).val.presheaf x)) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02G2.** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is smooth of relative dimension `d` if it
is smooth and its sheaf of relative differentials `Ω_{X/S}` is finite locally free of constant
rank `d`.
declarations.statement: def IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smoothOfRelativeDimension_iff_smooth_and_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02G2, Mathlib's notion.** A morphism of schemes is smooth of relative dimension `d`
in the chart-wise sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension` exactly when it is
smooth and its sheaf of relative differentials is finite locally free of rank `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothOfRelativeDimension_iff_smooth_and_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ S) :
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f ↔
      Smooth f ∧ SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
        (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) d
declarations.comment: Mathlib's chart-wise definition agrees with Stacks'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.UnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is unramified at `x : X` if there are affine open
neighbourhoods `U` of `x` and `V` of its image, with `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, such that the induced map on

rings of sections is G-unramified.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_and_isZero_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is unramified if and only if it is locally of finite type and its
sheaf of relative differentials is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramified_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_and_isZero_relativeDifferentials (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Unramified f ↔

declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is G-unramified if and only if it is locally of finite presentation
and its sheaf of relative differentials is zero.
