      (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ IsZero (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_tfae
declarations.doc:
The four characterizations of an unramified morphism: the global condition, the condition on
every compatible pair of affine opens, an open-covering criterion, and an affine-open-covering
criterion on rings of sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Unramified f,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) := (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.Unramified Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            ∀ i, Unramified
              (f.resLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i,
                let hUV : U i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j := (le_iSup U i).trans hU.le
                letI : Algebra Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i) := (f.appLE (V j) (U i) hUV).hom.toAlgebra
                Algebra.Unramified Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramified_tfae
declarations.doc:
The four characterizations of a G-unramified morphism: the global condition, the condition on
every compatible pair of affine opens, an open-covering criterion, and an affine-open-covering
criterion on rings of sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gUnramified_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      GUnramified f,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) := (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.GUnramified Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            ∀ i, GUnramified
              (f.resLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i,
                let hUV : U i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j := (le_iSup U i).trans hU.le
                letI : Algebra Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i) := (f.appLE (V j) (U i) hUV).hom.toAlgebra
                Algebra.GUnramified Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_resLE
declarations.doc:
Restricting an unramified morphism to compatible open subschemes of its source and target
is unramified.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramified_resLE
declarations.doc:
Restricting a G-unramified morphism to compatible open subschemes of its source and target
is G-unramified.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_iff_iso_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02G7, part (1).** A morphism to the spectrum of a field is unramified
if and only if its source is, over that spectrum, a coproduct of spectra of finite separable
field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_iff_iso_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    Unramified f ↔
      ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite k (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable k (K i))
        (e : X ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
        e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (K i)))) = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.exists_iso_fiber_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02G7, part (2).** Every fibre of an unramified morphism is, over the
residue field of the base point, a coproduct of spectra of finite separable field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Unramified.exists_iso_fiber_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Unramified f] (s : S) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra (S.residueField s) (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite (S.residueField s) (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField s) (K i))
      (e : f.fiber s ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
      e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (K i)))) =
        f.fiberToSpecResidueField s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_of_fibres
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite type whose fibres are disjoint unions of spectra of finite
separable extensions of the corresponding residue fields is unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_of_fibres {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (h : ∀ s : S,
      ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (e : f.fiber s ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
        e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (K i)))) =
            f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) :
    Unramified f
declarations.comment:
part (2): a morphism locally of finite type all of whose fibres are disjoint
unions of spectra of finite separable extensions of the residue field of the base point is
unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramified_of_fibres
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite presentation whose fibres are disjoint unions of spectra of
finite separable extensions of the corresponding residue fields is G-unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gUnramified_of_fibres {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (h : ∀ s : S,
      ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (e : f.fiber s ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
        e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (K i)))) =
            f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) :
    GUnramified f
declarations.comment:
part (3): a morphism locally of finite presentation all of whose fibres are
disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable extensions of the residue field of the base point
is G-unramified

      (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ IsZero (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramifiedAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02GF.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type
and a point `x` of `X` with image `s = f x`, the following are equivalent: `f` is unramified at
`x`; the fibre `X_s` is unramified over `κ(s)` at `x`; the `𝒪_{X,x}`-module `Ω_{X/S,x}` is zero;
the `𝒪_{X_s,x}`-module `Ω_{X_s/s,x}` is zero; the `κ(x)`-vector space
`Ω_{X_s/s,x} ⊗ κ(x) = Ω_{X/S,x} ⊗ κ(x)` is zero, in either of its two canonically identified
spellings; and `𝔪_s 𝒪_{X,x} = 𝔪_x` with `κ(x)/κ(s)` finite separable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramifiedAt_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      UnramifiedAt f x,
      UnramifiedAt (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x)) (f.asFiber x),
      Subsingleton (relativeDifferentialStalk f x),
      Subsingleton (relativeDifferentialStalk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x))
        (f.asFiber x)),
      Subsingleton (fiberRelativeCotangentSpace f x),
      Subsingleton (relativeCotangentSpace f x),
      Ideal.map (f.stalkMap x).hom
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk (f x))) =
          IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧
        (letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
         Module.Finite (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) ∧
           Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramifiedAt_iff_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02GF, the G-unramified clause.** A morphism of schemes locally of
finite presentation is G-unramified at a point exactly when it is unramified there: the affine
chart witnessing either notion witnesses the other, local finite presentation of the morphism
supplying finite presentation of the map of sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gUnramifiedAt_iff_unramifiedAt (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (x : X) : GUnramifiedAt f x ↔ UnramifiedAt f x
declarations.comment:
the G-unramified reading of condition (1): for `f` locally of finite presentation,
G-unramified at `x` is equivalent to unramified at `x`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramifiedAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02GF, the G-unramified reading.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`
locally of finite presentation and a point `x` of `X` with image `s = f x`, the following are
equivalent: `f` is G-unramified at `x`; `f` is unramified at `x`; the fibre `X_s` is unramified
over `κ(s)` at `x`; the `𝒪_{X,x}`-module `Ω_{X/S,x}` is zero; the `𝒪_{X_s,x}`-module
`Ω_{X_s/s,x}` is zero; the `κ(x)`-vector space `Ω_{X_s/s,x} ⊗ κ(x) = Ω_{X/S,x} ⊗ κ(x)` is zero,
in either of its two canonically identified spellings; and `𝔪_s 𝒪_{X,x} = 𝔪_x` with
`κ(x)/κ(s)` finite separable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gUnramifiedAt_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      GUnramifiedAt f x,
      UnramifiedAt f x,
      UnramifiedAt (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x)) (f.asFiber x),
      Subsingleton (relativeDifferentialStalk f x),
      Subsingleton (relativeDifferentialStalk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x))
        (f.asFiber x)),
      Subsingleton (fiberRelativeCotangentSpace f x),
      Subsingleton (relativeCotangentSpace f x),
      Ideal.map (f.stalkMap x).hom
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk (f x))) =
          IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧
        (letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
         Module.Finite (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) ∧
           Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x))]
declarations.comment:
the `resp. G-unramified` reading, under local finite presentation; the unramified
reading is `AlgebraicGeometry.unramifiedAt_tfae`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_of_comp
declarations.doc: If the composite `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` is unramified, then `X ⟶ Y` is unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [Unramified (f ≫ g)] : Unramified f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramified_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If the composite `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` is G-unramified and `Y ⟶ S` is locally of finite type, then
`X ⟶ Y` is G-unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gUnramified_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [GUnramified (f ≫ g)] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] : GUnramified f
declarations.comment: part (2): carries the hypothesis that `g` is locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is étale at `x` if it induces an étale map on the
coordinate rings of some affine open neighbourhood of `x` and some affine
open neighbourhood of its image.
declarations.statement: public abbrev EtaleAt (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardEtale
declarations.doc:
A morphism of affine schemes is *standard étale* if its map on global sections is a
standard étale ring map.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStandardEtale {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_resLE
declarations.doc:
If `f` is étale then so is its restriction `U → V` to any opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ S` with
`f(U) ⊆ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_resLE {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : Etale f) (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens)
    (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) : Etale (f.resLE V U e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_tfae
declarations.doc:
Étaleness of a morphism of schemes can be checked on all pairs of affine opens, on open
coverings of the target and of the preimages of their members, or on affine such coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Etale f,
      ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.Etale,
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens) (I : J → Type u) (U : ∀ j, I j → X.Opens),
        ⨆ j, V j = ⊤ ∧ (∀ j, ⨆ i, U j i = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j) ∧
          ∀ j i, ∃ e : U j i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j, Etale (f.resLE (V j) (U j i) e),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.affineOpens) (I : J → Type u) (U : ∀ j, I j → X.affineOpens),
        ⨆ j, (V j).1 = ⊤ ∧ (∀ j, ⨆ i, (U j i).1 = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j).1) ∧
          ∀ j i, ∃ e : (U j i).1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j).1, (f.appLE (V j) (U j i) e).hom.Etale]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_tfae_and_resLE
declarations.doc:
The whole statement: the four characterizations of étaleness agree, and étaleness passes to
restrictions to open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_tfae_and_resLE (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Etale f,
      ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.Etale,
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens) (I : J → Type u) (U : ∀ j, I j → X.Opens),
        ⨆ j, V j = ⊤ ∧ (∀ j, ⨆ i, U j i = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j) ∧
          ∀ j i, ∃ e : U j i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j, Etale (f.resLE (V j) (U j i) e),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.affineOpens) (I : J → Type u) (U : ∀ j, I j → X.affineOpens),
        ⨆ j, (V j).1 = ⊤ ∧ (∀ j, ⨆ i, (U j i).1 = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j).1) ∧
          ∀ j i, ∃ e : (U j i).1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j).1, (f.appLE (V j) (U j i) e).hom.Etale] ∧
    (Etale f → ∀ (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), Etale (f.resLE V U e))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_iff_smoothAt_and_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is étale at a point if and only if it is smooth and
unramified at that point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAt_iff_smoothAt_and_unramifiedAt {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    EtaleAt f x ↔
      (InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x ∧ UnramifiedAt f x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleAt_iff_isSmoothAt_and_isUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is étale at a point of its source if and only if it
is smooth and unramified at that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleAt_iff_isSmoothAt_and_isUnramifiedAt
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    IsEtaleAt B S hS f x ↔ IsSmoothAt B S hS f x ∧ IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment: for algebraic spaces, at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_iso_fiber_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02GL, part (2).** Every fibre of an étale morphism is, over the
residue field of the base point, a coproduct of spectra of finite separable field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Etale.exists_iso_fiber_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Etale f] (s : S) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra (S.residueField s) (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite (S.residueField s) (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField s) (K i))
      (e : f.fiber s ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
      e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (K i)))) =
        f.fiberToSpecResidueField s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_of_flat_of_fibers_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
A flat, locally finitely presented morphism with fibres that are disjoint unions of spectra
of finite separable extensions of residue fields is étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_of_flat_of_fibers_finite_separable
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (h : ∀ s : S,
      ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField s) (K i))
        (e : f.fiber s ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
        e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (K i)))) =
            f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) :
    Etale f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_of_etale
declarations.doc: An étale morphism of schemes is syntomic.
declarations.statement: lemma syntomic_of_etale {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Etale f] : Syntomic f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_etale
declarations.doc: An étale morphism of schemes is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
lemma locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_etale {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Etale f] :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_etale
declarations.doc: An étale morphism of schemes is flat.
declarations.statement: lemma flat_of_etale {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Etale f] : Flat f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_iff_exists_isStandardEtale_restrict
declarations.doc:
A scheme morphism is étale at a point if and only if, over any fixed
affine open neighbourhood of its image, it is standard étale on some affine
open neighbourhood of the point.
declarations.statement:
public lemma etaleAt_iff_exists_isStandardEtale_restrict
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) (V : S.Opens)
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : f x ∈ V) :
    EtaleAt f x ↔
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        @AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardEtale
          U.toScheme V.toScheme hU hV (f.resLE V U hUV)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02GU.** Ten equivalent criteria for a morphism of schemes locally of
finite presentation to be étale at a point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAt_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      EtaleAt f x,
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        EtaleAt (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x)) (f.asFiber x),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        UnramifiedAt (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x)) (f.asFiber x),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        Subsingleton (relativeDifferentialStalk f x),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        Subsingleton (fiberRelativeCotangentSpace f x),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        Subsingleton (relativeCotangentSpace f x),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        (Ideal.map (f.stalkMap x).hom
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk (f x))) =
          IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧
          (letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
           Module.Finite (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) ∧
             Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x))),
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, U.1) :=
          (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension 0 Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, U.1),
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (hxU : x ∈ U.1)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, U.1) :=
          (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.toAlgebra
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (P : Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation
            Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, U.1) (Fin n) (Fin n)),
          P.jacobian ∉ (U.2.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxU⟩).asIdeal,
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        IsStandardEtale (f.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV),
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (hxU : x ∈ U.1)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
          (p q : Γ(S, V.1)[X]),
        p.Monic ∧
          ∃ e : Γ(X, U.1) ≃+* StandardEtale.StandardEtaleAlg Γ(S, V.1) p q,
            e.toRingHom.comp (f.appLE V U hUV).hom =
              StandardEtale.standardEtaleMap Γ(S, V.1) p q ∧
            e.symm ((Ideal.Quotient.mk
              (Ideal.span {(algebraMap Γ(S, V.1)[X]
                (Localization.Away q)) p}))
              ((algebraMap Γ(S, V.1)[X] (Localization.Away q))
                (derivative p))) ∉
              (U.2.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxU⟩).asIdeal]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_iff_isFlatAt_and_gUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is étale at a point if and only if it is flat and
G-unramified at that point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAt_iff_isFlatAt_and_gUnramifiedAt {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    EtaleAt f x ↔
      (IsFlatAt (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map f.toLRSHom) x ∧
        GUnramifiedAt f x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_flat_and_gUnramified
declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes is étale if and only if it is flat and G-unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_iff_flat_and_gUnramified {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Etale f ↔ (Flat f ∧ GUnramified f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_of_etale_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02GW.** A morphism between two schemes that are étale over a common
base, and which commutes with the structure morphisms, is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_of_etale_over {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) {p : X ⟶ S} {q : Y ⟶ S}
    (h : f ≫ q = p) [Etale p] [Etale q] : Etale f

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is **formally smooth** when it has the infinitesimal
lifting property: for every first-order thickening `i : T ⟶ T'` of affine schemes, every
commutative square
```
T  --g--→ X
|         |
i         f
↓         ↓
T' --h--→ S
```
has a diagonal filler `g' : T' ⟶ X`, that is a morphism with `g' ≫ f = h` and `i ≫ g' = g`.
declarations.statement: abbrev FormallySmoothScheme {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth.comp
declarations.doc: A composition of formally smooth morphisms is formally smooth.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth.pullback_snd
declarations.doc: An arbitrary base change of a formally smooth morphism is formally smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormallySmooth.pullback_snd {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (g : S' ⟶ S) (hf : FormallySmooth f) :
    FormallySmooth (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth.resLE
declarations.doc: Formal smoothness is preserved by restriction to compatible open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormallySmooth.resLE {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    (hf : FormallySmooth f) (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens)
    (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    FormallySmooth (f.resLE V U hUV)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmooth.resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02H3.** Formal smoothness passes to the restriction of a morphism to
opens of the source and of the target. The point is that a first-order thickening of affine
schemes is surjective on points, so a lift over the ambient morphism has the same image as the
morphism it extends and therefore factors through the given open of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormallySmooth.resLE {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : FormallySmooth f)
    {U : S.Opens} {V : X.Opens} (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) : FormallySmooth (f.resLE U V e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.formallySmooth_iff_appTop_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
A morphism of affine schemes is formally smooth if and only if its map on global sections is
formally smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_iff_appTop_formallySmooth
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) :
    FormallySmooth f ↔ f.appTop.hom.FormallySmooth

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.existsUnique_derivationActionGlobal
declarations.doc:
**A derivation acts in exactly one way on a lift of a map**, [Stacks Project, Tag 02H5].
Let `S` be a scheme, let `i : X ⟶ X'` and `j : Y ⟶ Y'` be first-order thickenings, let
`p : X' ⟶ S` and `q : Y' ⟶ S` be the structure morphisms, and let `(a, a')` be a morphism of
thickenings `(X ⊂ X') ⟶ (Y ⊂ Y')` over `S`. Then for every `𝒪_X`-linear map
`θ : a^*Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` there is exactly one morphism `b' : X' ⟶ Y'` such that `(a, b')` is
again a morphism of thickenings over `S` — conditions (1) and (2) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04FG] for the pair `(a', b')` — and the derivation `D` of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04FG] attached to the pair is related to `θ` by Equation
[Stacks Project, Tag 04BV], `D = θ ∘ d_{Y/S}`.

Nothing is affine, and the datum is the one of the source: a morphism of sheaves of
`𝒪_X`-modules out of the pulled-back sheaf of relative differentials.

Tag 04FG numbers two conditions; with Equation 04BV they make the three requirements written out
on sections below. Condition (1), that the two reductions agree,
is `comm_b : i ≫ b' = a ≫ j`, the same `a` as for `a'`; that `b'` is a morphism over `S` is
`b' ≫ q = p`. Condition (2), that the two induced maps `a^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` of
[Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] agree, is the first conjunct: for a first-order thickening `j` the
conormal sheaf `𝒞_{Y/Y'}` *is* the defining ideal of `j` and the induced map is the comorphism,
so the condition says that `(a')^♯` and `(b')^♯` agree on the sections killed by `j^♯`. Equation
[Stacks Project, Tag 04BV] is the second conjunct: the difference `(b')^♯ - (a')^♯`, which is the
derivation `D` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04FG] read through the inclusion `𝒞_{X/X'} ⟶ 𝒪_{X'}` of
`Stacks.Thickenings.firstOrderImmersionConormalSheafι`, is `θ` applied to the pulled-back
universal differential `Stacks.Smooth.pullbackD`.

Because `d_{Y/S}` kills `j^♯` of a section of the defining ideal of `j`, the second conjunct
implies the first, so the morphism characterised here is the same whether condition (2) is read
as above or as the equality of the two maps of conormal sheaves. For the same reason `j` need
only be a morphism of schemes: the source asks it to be a first-order thickening, and at that
hypothesis the first conjunct is exactly its condition (2), since `𝒞_{Y/Y'}` is then the
defining ideal of `j` and the map of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] is the comorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_derivationActionGlobal (ha' : a' ≫ q = p) :
    ∃! b' : X' ⟶ Y', ∃ (comm_b : i ≫ b' = a ≫ j) (_ : b' ≫ q = p),
      (∀ (W : Y'.Opens) (V : X'.Opens) (hA : V ≤ a' ⁻¹ᵁ W) (g : Γ(Y', W)),
          (j.app W).hom g = 0 →
            (b'.appLE W V (le_preimage_of_comm hsq comm_a comm_b hA)).hom g
              = (a'.appLE W V hA).hom g)
        ∧ ∀ (W : Y'.Opens) (V : X'.Opens) (hA : V ≤ a' ⁻¹ᵁ W) (g : Γ(Y', W)),
            (b'.appLE W V (le_preimage_of_comm hsq comm_a comm_b hA)).hom g
              = (a'.appLE W V hA).hom g
                + derivationSection hsq θ W V (preimage_le_of_comm comm_a hA) g

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.smooth_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
**A scheme morphism is smooth exactly when it is locally of finite presentation and formally
smooth.** This is the infinitesimal lifting criterion for smoothness.

The implication from the right is `Stacks.Smooth.smooth_of_formallySmoothScheme`, and
the implication to the right is `Stacks.Smooth.formallySmoothScheme_of_smooth` together with the
fact that a smooth morphism is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth f ↔
      (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ FormallySmoothScheme f)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified
registrations.comment: Mathlib's definition: the ring maps on affine opens are formally unramified

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.hom_ext
registrations.comment: a formally unramified morphism has at most one dotted arrow, for any nilpotent closed immersion (in particular a first order thickening)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.of_hom_ext
registrations.comment: conversely, at most one dotted arrow for first order thickenings of affine schemes implies formally unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.formallyUnramified_iff_isZero_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is formally unramified if and only if its sheaf of relative
differentials is a zero object.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyUnramified_iff_isZero_relativeDifferentials (f : X ⟶ S) :
    FormallyUnramified f ↔ IsZero (relativeDifferentials f)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.instHasRingHomPropertyFormallyUnramified
registrations.comment: formally unramified is the affine-local property of formally unramified ring maps, hence local on the source and on the target

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE
registrations.comment: a property local on the source and the target is preserved by restriction f|_U : U → V

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.instHasRingHomPropertyFormallyUnramified
registrations.comment: formally unramified is the affine-local property of formally unramified ring maps

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasRingHomProperty.iff_of_isAffine
registrations.comment: for X and S affine, such a property holds iff it holds for the ring map on global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_and_formallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is unramified if and only if it is locally of finite type and formally
unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_and_formallyUnramified (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Unramified f ↔ (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ FormallyUnramified f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramified_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is G-unramified if and only if it is locally of finite presentation and
formally unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gUnramified_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallyUnramified (f : X ⟶ S) :
    GUnramified f ↔ (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ FormallyUnramified f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyEtale
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is **formally étale** when it has the unique infinitesimal
lifting property: for every first-order thickening `i : T ⟶ T'` of affine schemes, every
commutative square
```
T  --g--→ X
|         |
i         f
↓         ↓
T' --p--→ S
```
has exactly one diagonal filler `h : T' ⟶ X`, that is exactly one morphism with `i ≫ h = g` and
`h ≫ f = p`.
declarations.statement: abbrev FormallyEtale {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.formallyEtale_iff_formallySmooth_and_formallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is formally étale if and only if it is formally smooth and formally
unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyEtale_iff_formallySmooth_and_formallyUnramified
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    FormallyEtale f ↔ (FormallySmooth f ∧ FormallyUnramified f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyEtale.comp
declarations.doc: A composition of formally étale morphisms is formally étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormallyEtale.comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (hf : FormallyEtale f) (hg : FormallyEtale g) :
    FormallyEtale (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyEtale.pullback_snd
declarations.doc: A base change of a formally étale morphism is formally étale.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyEtale.resLE
declarations.doc:
Formal étaleness is preserved when a morphism is restricted to compatible open subschemes of
its source and target.
declarations.statement:
lemma FormallyEtale.resLE {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (hf : FormallyEtale f) :
    FormallyEtale (f.resLE V U hUV)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.formallyEtale_iff_globalSectionsMap_formallyEtale
declarations.doc:
A morphism of affine schemes is formally étale if and only if its pullback map on global
functions is a formally étale ring map.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyEtale_iff_globalSectionsMap_formallyEtale
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) :
    FormallyEtale f ↔ (Scheme.Γ.map f.op).hom.FormallyEtale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallyEtale
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is étale exactly when it is locally of finite presentation and formally
étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallyEtale
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Etale f ↔ (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ FormallyEtale f)

declarations.name: split_injection_of_arbitrarily_large_split_mod_pow
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 02HO, Lemma 10.74.1).**
Let `R` be a Noetherian commutative ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal contained in the Jacobson
radical of `R`, and `N`, `M` finite `R`-modules. Let `φ : N → M` be `R`-linear. If for
arbitrarily large `n` the induced map `φ̄ₙ : N / Iⁿ N → M / Iⁿ M` is a split injection,
then `φ` itself is a split injection.
declarations.statement:
theorem split_injection_of_arbitrarily_large_split_mod_pow
    {R N M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥) (φ : N →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ForArbitrarilyLarge (fun n => IsSplitInjection (inducedMapModPow φ I n))) :
    IsSplitInjection φ

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.split_exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange_of_section
declarations.doc:
Let `R → P → S` be commutative rings, let `I = ker(P → S)`, and suppose there is an
`R`-algebra map `g : S → P ⧸ I²` that is a right inverse to `P ⧸ I² → S`. Then the exact sequence
`0 → I/I² → S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] → Ω[S⁄R] → 0` is split short exact: it is isomorphic to the trivial
sequence, by an isomorphism `S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] ≃ I/I² × Ω[S⁄R]` carrying
`KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor R P S` to `LinearMap.inl` and
`KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange R P S` to `LinearMap.snd`. Nothing is required of `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem split_exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange_of_section {R P S : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing P] [CommRing S] [Algebra R P] [Algebra P S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsScalarTower R P S] (g : S →ₐ[R] P ⧸ RingHom.ker (algebraMap P S) ^ 2)
    (hg : (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R P S).kerSquareLift.comp g = AlgHom.id R S) :
    ∃ e : S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] ≃ₗ[P] (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P S)).Cotangent × Ω[S⁄R],
      kerCotangentToTensor R P S =
          e.symm ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl P (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P S)).Cotangent Ω[S⁄R] ∧
        (mapBaseChange R P S).restrictScalars P =
          LinearMap.snd P (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P S)).Cotangent Ω[S⁄R] ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap
declarations.comment:
Recorded in full, as the decomposition of the middle term of the sequence of 00RU
carrying its two maps to `LinearMap.inl` and `LinearMap.snd`. The hypothesis is a section of
`P ⧸ I² → S` rather than of `P → S`, and surjectivity of `P → S` is derived from it rather than
assumed.

declarations.name: kaehlerReductionMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02HQ (Lemma 10.131.11).**
For a ring map `R → S`, an ideal `I ⊆ S`, and an integer `n ≥ 1`, with
`S' = S/I^{n+1}`, the comparison map

  Φ : Ω[S/R] ⊗[S] (S/I^n) → Ω[S'/R] ⊗[S'] (S/I^n)

induced by the functoriality map `dπ : Ω[S/R] → Ω[S'/R]` is bijective (an
isomorphism).
declarations.statement:
theorem kaehlerReductionMap_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (kaehlerReductionMap R S I n)

declarations.name: InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension
declarations.doc:
A ring map `φ : B' → B` is a *small extension* (Stacks tag 02HS) if `B'` and
`B` are local Artinian rings, `φ` is surjective, and the kernel `ker φ` has
length `1` as a `B'`-module.
declarations.statement: def IsSmallExtension {B' B : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : B' ⟶ B) : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let `S` be an `R`-algebra of finite type and let `q` be a prime
of `S`. The following are equivalent:

1. `R → S` is smooth at `q`;
2. for every surjection `f : B' → B` of local `R`-algebras whose kernel has square zero and every
   `R`-algebra map `g : S → B` with `q` the contraction of the maximal ideal of `B`, there is an
   `R`-algebra map `g' : S → B'` with `f ∘ g' = g`;
3. the same, with `f` ranging over small extensions, that is, surjections of Artinian local rings
   whose kernel is a simple `B'`-module (equivalently, has length `1`);
4. the same, with `f` ranging over small extensions along which `g` additionally induces an
   isomorphism `κ(q) ≅ κ(𝔪)`, that is, along which the canonical map `κ(q) → κ(𝔪)` attached to
   `q = g⁻¹(𝔪)` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothAt_tfae {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    List.TFAE
      [ Algebra.IsSmoothAt R q,
        ∀ (B' B : Type max u v) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B]
          [Algebra R B'] [Algebra R B] (f : B' →ₐ[R] B), Function.Surjective f →
          RingHom.ker (f : B' →+* B) ^ 2 = ⊥ →
          ∀ g : S →ₐ[R] B, (maximalIdeal B).comap (g : S →+* B) = q →
            ∃ g' : S →ₐ[R] B', f.comp g' = g,
        ∀ (B' B : Type max u v) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B]
          [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [Algebra R B'] [Algebra R B]
          (f : B' →ₐ[R] B), Function.Surjective f →
          IsSimpleModule B' (RingHom.ker (f : B' →+* B)) →
          ∀ g : S →ₐ[R] B, (maximalIdeal B).comap (g : S →+* B) = q →
            ∃ g' : S →ₐ[R] B', f.comp g' = g,
        ∀ (B' B : Type max u v) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B]
          [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [Algebra R B'] [Algebra R B]
          (f : B' →ₐ[R] B), Function.Surjective f →
          IsSimpleModule B' (RingHom.ker (f : B' →+* B)) →
          ∀ (g : S →ₐ[R] B) (hq : (maximalIdeal B).comap (g : S →+* B) = q),
            Function.Surjective (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ q (maximalIdeal B) g hq.symm) →
            ∃ g' : S →ₐ[R] B', f.comp g' = g ]
declarations.comment:
Smoothness at `q` is `Algebra.IsSmoothAt`, the source's Definition 02HN by the
finite presentation of `S`. A small extension (Definition 02HS) is a surjection `f : B' →ₐ[R] B`
of Artinian local rings with `IsSimpleModule B' (ker f)`, and `κ(q) ≅ κ(𝔪)` is surjectivity of
`Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ q (maximalIdeal B) g`, the canonical map out of the residue field of
`S_q` — not of `S → κ(𝔪)`, which would force `q` maximal. The source's prime `𝔭` under `q` is not
used. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteType_iff_residueField_comp_finiteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism from the spectrum of an Artinian local ring is of finite type if and only if
its composite with the spectrum of the residue field is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteType_iff_residueField_comp_finiteType
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsArtinianRing A]
    (f : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ S) :
    (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) ↔
      (LocallyOfFiniteType
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue A)) ≫ f) ∧
        QuasiCompact
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue A)) ≫ f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_iff_lifts_finiteType_smallExtensions
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme
is smooth exactly when it lifts against all Artinian small extensions whose map to the base is
of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smooth_iff_lifts_finiteType_smallExtensions
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    Smooth f ↔
      ∀ ⦃B' B : CommRingCat.{u}⦄ (φ : B' ⟶ B),
        InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension φ →
        ∀ (α : Spec B ⟶ X) (β : Spec B' ⟶ S),
          (LocallyOfFiniteType β ∧ QuasiCompact β) →
          α ≫ f = Spec.map φ ≫ β →
          ∃ γ : Spec B' ⟶ X, Spec.map φ ≫ γ = α ∧ γ ≫ f = β

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02HZ.** Every nonempty Kolmogorov Noetherian topological space has a closed
point: it is quasi-compact, so Stacks 005E applies to the closed set `Set.univ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_isClosed_singleton
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [Nonempty X] [NoetherianSpace X] [T0Space X] :
    ∃ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyNoetherianNoClosedPoint.isLocallyNoetherianSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02HZ.** The space of Stacks 02HZ is locally Noetherian: for each `x`, the open
neighbourhood `Set.Iic x = {0, …, x}` is finite, hence Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherianSpace :
    letI : TopologicalSpace ℕ := iicTopology
    IsLocallyNoetherianSpace ℕ

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyNoetherianNoClosedPoint.not_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02HZ.** The space of Stacks 02HZ has no closed point: every open set is a lower
set, so `x + 1 ∈ closure {x}` while `x + 1 ≠ x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isClosed_singleton :
    letI : TopologicalSpace ℕ := iicTopology
    ∀ x : ℕ, ¬ IsClosed ({x} : Set ℕ)

declarations.name: IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace
declarations.doc:
A topological space `X` is *catenary* if for every pair of irreducible closed subsets
`Y ⊆ Y'`, the codimension `topCodim Y Y'` is finite and every *maximal* chain of irreducible
closed subsets from `Y` to `Y'` has length equal to it.
declarations.statement: def IsCatenarySpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop

declarations.name: CatenaryTopologicalSpace.isCatenary_iff_hasOpenCoveringByCatenarySpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I2.** A topological space is catenary if and only if it has an open covering by
catenary spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenary_iff_hasOpenCoveringByCatenarySpaces (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    IsCatenarySpace X ↔ HasOpenCoveringByCatenarySpaces X

declarations.name: CatenaryTopologicalSpace.isCatenary_of_isLocallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I2, moreover clause.** Every locally closed subspace of a catenary space is
catenary: a locally closed `Z` is open in `closure Z`, which is a closed — hence catenary —
subspace of `X`, and catenarity passes to open subspaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenary_of_isLocallyClosed (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (hX : IsCatenarySpace X)
    (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsLocallyClosed Z) : IsCatenarySpace Z
declarations.comment: moreover: locally closed subspace is catenary

declarations.name: codimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I3**.
The codimension of an irreducible closed subset `Y` of a topological space `X`, defined as the
coheight of `Y` in the poset of irreducible closed subsets of `X` ordered by inclusion. This
equals the supremum of the lengths of strict chains `Y = Y₀ ⊊ Y₁ ⊊ … ⊊ Y_e` of irreducible
closed subsets starting with `Y`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def codimension {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (Y : IrreducibleCloseds X) : ℕ∞

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.height_vanishingIdeal_preimage
declarations.doc:
**The exact codimension of an irreducible closed subset, read as a height on an open affine
piece.** Let `Spec R` be an open subspace of a space `X` through an open embedding `f` and let
`Y ⊆ X` be an irreducible closed subset meeting it. Then the prime ideal of `R` cutting out the
trace `f ⁻¹' Y` has height exactly `codim(Y, X)`.

This is the *equality* strengthening of
`PrimeSpectrum.le_height_of_mem_minimalPrimes_of_isOpenEmbedding`, available because the
irreducible closed subset is pinned rather than quantified over: the trace is an irreducible
closed subset of `Spec R` whose codimension there is the height of its prime
(`PrimeSpectrum.codimension_eq_height_vanishingIdeal`) and is `codim(Y, X)` by [Stacks, Tag 02I4]
(`TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds.coheight_comapOpenEmbedding`).
declarations.statement:
theorem height_vanishingIdeal_preimage (hf : Topology.IsOpenEmbedding f)
    (Y : IrreducibleCloseds X) (hne : (f ⁻¹' (Y : Set X)).Nonempty) :
    (vanishingIdeal (f ⁻¹' (Y : Set X))).height = codimension Y
declarations.comment: the codimension of one irreducible closed subset, as a height on an affine open

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds.coheight_comapOpenEmbedding
declarations.doc:
For an open embedding `f : W → X`, the codimension of an irreducible closed subset `Y ⊆ X`
meeting the image of `f` equals the codimension of its trace `f ⁻¹' Y` in `W`. No sobriety
or separation hypothesis is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem coheight_comapOpenEmbedding (Y : IrreducibleCloseds X) (hf : IsOpenEmbedding f)
    (h : (f ⁻¹' (Y : Set X)).Nonempty) :
    Order.coheight Y = Order.coheight (Y.comapOpenEmbedding hf h)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds.coheight_restrictOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I4**.
Let `X` be a topological space, `Y ⊆ X` an irreducible closed subset and `U ⊆ X` an open subset
with `Y ∩ U ≠ ∅`. Then the codimension of `Y` in `X` equals the codimension of `Y ∩ U` in `U`:

    codim (Y, X) = codim (Y ∩ U, U).

Codimension is `Order.coheight` in the poset of irreducible closed subsets; see the module
docstring. No sobriety or separation hypothesis is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem coheight_restrictOpen (Y : IrreducibleCloseds X) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (h : ((Y : Set X) ∩ U).Nonempty) :
    Order.coheight Y = Order.coheight (Y.restrictOpen hU h)

declarations.name: X.noetherianSpace_and_coheight_zeroAsIC_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I5**.
The space `X = [0, 1]` with the topology generated by the sets `(1 - 1/n, 1]` is a Noetherian
topological space containing an irreducible closed subset `Y = {0}` of infinite codimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_and_coheight_zeroAsIC_eq_top :
    NoetherianSpace X ∧ IsIrreducible ({zero} : Set X) ∧
      IsClosed ({zero} : Set X) ∧ Order.coheight zeroAsIC = (⊤ : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: isCatenarySpace_iff_codim_additive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I6**.
A topological space `X` is catenary iff for every pair of irreducible closed subsets `Y ⊆ Y'`
the codimension is finite, and for every triple `Y ⊆ Y' ⊆ Y''` of irreducible closed subsets we
have the additivity formula `topCodim Y Y'' = topCodim Y Y' + topCodim Y' Y''`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenarySpace_iff_codim_additive (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    IsCatenarySpace X ↔
      (∀ Y Y' : IrreducibleCloseds X, Y ≤ Y' → topCodim Y Y' ≠ ⊤) ∧
      (∀ Y Y' Y'' : IrreducibleCloseds X, Y ≤ Y' → Y' ≤ Y'' →
        topCodim Y Y'' = topCodim Y Y' + topCodim Y' Y'')

declarations.name: main_theorem02I7
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02I7**. If `X` is a Kolmogorov topological space with a basis of quasi-compact open
sets and `X` is not Jacobson, then there exists a point `x ∈ X` such that `{x}` is not closed
in `X` and `{x}` is locally closed in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem02I7
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [T0Space X]
    (hB : PrespectralSpace X) (hJ : ¬ JacobsonSpace X) :
    ∃ x : X, ¬ IsClosed ({x} : Set X) ∧ IsLocallyClosed ({x} : Set X)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.isImmediateSpecialization_iff
declarations.doc:
A specialization is immediate exactly when it is non-trivial and admits no intermediate
point: every `z` with `x ⤳ z ⤳ y` is one of the two endpoints.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmediateSpecialization_iff (x y : X) :
    IsImmediateSpecialization x y ↔
      x ⤳ y ∧ x ≠ y ∧ ∀ z : X, x ⤳ z → z ⤳ y → z = x ∨ z = y

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.exists_dimensionFunction_iff
declarations.doc:
A function `δ : X → ℤ` is the underlying function of a dimension function exactly when it
is strictly decreasing along non-trivial specializations and drops by exactly one along
immediate specializations.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dimensionFunction_iff (δ : X → ℤ) :
    (∃ d : DimensionFunction X, ∀ x, d x = δ x) ↔
      (∀ x y : X, x ⤳ y → x ≠ y → δ y < δ x) ∧
        (∀ x y : X, IsImmediateSpecialization x y → δ x = δ y + 1)

declarations.name: isCatenarySpace_and_topCodim_eq_of_isDimensionFunction
declarations.doc:
A sober topological space `X` admitting a dimension function `δ` is catenary, and for every
specialization `x ⤳ y` we have `codim(closure {y}, closure {x}) = δ x - δ y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenarySpace_and_topCodim_eq_of_isDimensionFunction (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hSober : StacksSober X) (δ : X → ℤ) (hδ : IsDimensionFunctionForCatenary δ) :
    IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace X ∧
      ∀ x y : X, x ⤳ y →
        IrreducibleClosedsCodim.topCodim (closureSingleton y) (closureSingleton x)
          = ((δ x - δ y).toNat : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.DimensionFunction.isLocallyConstant_sub
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02IB.** On a locally Noetherian sober topological space `X`, the difference of two
dimension functions `δ, δ' : X → ℤ` is locally constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem DimensionFunction.isLocallyConstant_sub [QuasiSober X] [T0Space X]
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X) (δ δ' : DimensionFunction X) :
    IsLocallyConstant (fun x : X => δ x - δ' x)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.exists_open_nhd_with_dimension_function
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a topological space that is locally Noetherian, sober (i.e. `QuasiSober` and
`T0Space`), and catenary. Then every point of `X` has an open neighbourhood `U ⊆ X` such that
the subspace `U` admits a dimension function `δ : U → ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_nhd_with_dimension_function
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [QuasiSober X] [T0Space X]
    (hLN : IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X)
    (hCat : IsTopologicallyCatenary X)
    (x : X) :
    ∃ U : Set X, IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ Nonempty (DimensionFunction U)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.DimensionFunction.nonempty_dimensionFunction_iff_dimensionObstruction_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ID.** On a catenary, locally Noetherian, sober topological space `X`, the
obstruction to having a dimension function is an element of `H¹(X, ℤ)`: the element
`dimensionObstruction` of first sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf `ℤ`, which does not depend
on any choice (`obstructionH1_eq_dimensionObstruction`), vanishes if and only if `X` has a
dimension function.

The element is the image of the Čech class of the cocycle `δ i - δ j` of local dimension
functions (tags 02IC and 02IB) under the injective comparison `Ȟ¹(𝒰, ℤ) → H¹(X, ℤ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_dimensionFunction_iff_dimensionObstruction_eq_zero
    (hLN : IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X) (hCat : IsTopologicallyCatenary X) :
    Nonempty (DimensionFunction X) ↔ dimensionObstruction hLN hCat = 0
declarations.comment: the obstruction element of H¹(X, ℤ), first right-derived global sections of the constant sheaf ℤ, independent of all choices, vanishes iff a dimension function exists

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.DimensionFunction.nonempty_dimensionFunction_iff_dimensionObstructionExt_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ID**, with `H¹(X, ℤ)` read as Mathlib's `Sheaf.H`: on a catenary, locally
Noetherian, sober topological space a dimension function exists if and only if the obstruction
element of `Sheaf.H ℤ 1` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_dimensionFunction_iff_dimensionObstructionExt_eq_zero
    (hLN : IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X) (hCat : IsTopologicallyCatenary X) :
    Nonempty (DimensionFunction X) ↔ dimensionObstructionExt hLN hCat = 0
declarations.comment: the same statement with H¹(X, ℤ) read as Mathlib's Ext-group cohomology Sheaf.H

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_radical_ofList_append_eq_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Dimension of a quotient by part of a system of parameters.** Let `(R, m)` be a Noetherian
local ring and let `x₁, …, x_d ∈ m` generate an ideal of definition of `R`, with
`d ≤ dim R` — equivalently, `x₁, …, x_d` is a system of parameters. Then killing any part
`l` of the sequence drops the dimension by exactly the number of elements killed:
`dim R/(l) + |l| = dim R`. Taking `l` to be the prefix `x₁, …, x_i` gives
`dim R/(x₁, …, x_i) = d - i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_radical_ofList_append_eq_maximalIdeal
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (l l' : List R)
    (hdef : (Ideal.ofList (l ++ l')).radical = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hdim : ((l.length + l'.length : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim R) :
    ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList l) + l.length =
      ringKrullDim R

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.infinite_of_two_le_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
A nonempty open subset of the spectrum of a Noetherian local domain of dimension at least
two is infinite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem infinite_of_two_le_ringKrullDim (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] (hR : 2 ≤ ringKrullDim R) (U : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hU' : U.Nonempty) : U.Infinite

declarations.name: Catenary.isCatenaryRing_iff_isCatenarySpace_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
A commutative ring `R` is catenary if and only if the poset of irreducible closed subsets of
`PrimeSpectrum R` is a catenary order.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenaryRing_iff_isCatenarySpace_primeSpectrum (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    IsCatenaryRing R ↔ IsCatenaryOrder (IrreducibleCloseds (PrimeSpectrum R))

declarations.name: height_add_trdeg_residue_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02IJ**.
For `R` Noetherian, `S` a finite-type domain extension of the domain `R`, and `q` a prime of `S`
lying over `p`, `q.height + trdeg_{κ(p)} κ(q) ≤ p.height + trdeg_R S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem height_add_trdeg_residue_le
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (p : Ideal R) (q : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] :
    letI := Ideal.ResidueField.algebraOfLiesOver p q
    q.height + (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg p.ResidueField q.ResidueField) : ℕ∞)
      ≤ p.height + (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg R S) : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: height_add_trdeg_residue_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02IJ**.
If in addition `R` is universally catenary, the dimension formula is an equality:
`q.height + trdeg_{κ(p)} κ(q) = p.height + trdeg_R S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem height_add_trdeg_residue_eq
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) (hcat : IsUniversallyCatenary R)
    (p : Ideal R) (q : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] :
    letI := Ideal.ResidueField.algebraOfLiesOver p q
    q.height + (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg p.ResidueField q.ResidueField) : ℕ∞)
      = p.height + (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg R S) : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
A locally closed subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme is locally Noetherian: the source
of an immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_of_isImmersion [IsImmersion f] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsLocallyNoetherian Z
declarations.comment: the locally Noetherian case, for the source of an arbitrary immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNoetherian_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
A locally closed subscheme of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian: the source of an immersion
into a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian.
declarations.statement: theorem isNoetherian_of_isImmersion [IsImmersion f] [IsNoetherian X] : IsNoetherian Z
declarations.comment: the Noetherian case, for the source of an arbitrary immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.closedPoints_nonempty
declarations.doc: Every nonempty locally Noetherian scheme has a closed point.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPoints_nonempty (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Nonempty X] :
    (closedPoints X).Nonempty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_inter_closedPoints_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
Every nonempty closed subset of a locally Noetherian scheme contains a point that is
closed in the ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_inter_closedPoints_of_isClosed (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {Z : Set X} (hZ : Z.Nonempty) (hZ' : IsClosed Z) :
    (Z ∩ closedPoints X).Nonempty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_specializes_closedPoint
declarations.doc: Every point of a locally Noetherian scheme specializes to a closed point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_specializes_closedPoint (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X) :
    ∃ y ∈ closedPoints X, Specializes x y

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.jacobsonSpace_compl_closedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02IM, part (1).** The punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is
a Jacobson space.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_compl_closedPoint
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    JacobsonSpace ↥(({IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))ᶜ)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.jacobsonSpace_compl_zeroLocus_jacobson
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02IM, part (2).** The complement of the vanishing locus of the Jacobson
radical of a Noetherian ring is a Jacobson space.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_compl_zeroLocus_jacobson
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    JacobsonSpace
      ↥((PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Ring.jacobson R : Set R))ᶜ)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.jacobsonSpace_compl_zeroLocus_of_le_jacobson
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02IM, part (3).** If `(R, I)` is a Noetherian Zariski pair, that is if
`R` is Noetherian and `I` is contained in the Jacobson radical of `R`, then `Spec R \ V(I)` is a
Jacobson space.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_compl_zeroLocus_of_le_jacobson
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Ring.jacobson R) :
    JacobsonSpace ↥((PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R))ᶜ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Cohen–Macaulay scheme.** A scheme `X` is Cohen–Macaulay if every point belongs to an
affine open `U` whose ring of sections `Γ(X, U)` is Noetherian and Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement: public def IsCohenMacaulay (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_tfae_stalk
declarations.doc:
A scheme is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if it is locally Noetherian with Cohen–Macaulay
local rings at every point, if and only if it is locally Noetherian with Cohen–Macaulay local
rings at closed points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_tfae_stalk (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsCohenMacaulay X,
      IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧
        (∀ x : X, ∃ h : IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x),
          @IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) _ h _),
      IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧
        (∀ x : X, x ∈ closedPoints X →
          ∃ h : IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x),
            @IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) _ h _)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_tfae_cover
declarations.doc:
Cohen–Macaulayness of a scheme is equivalent to the Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay condition on
every affine coordinate ring, to that condition on one affine open covering, and to having an
open covering by Cohen–Macaulay schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_tfae_cover (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsCohenMacaulay X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, ∃ h : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, U.val),
        @IsCohenMacaulayRing Γ(X, U.val) _ h,
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        (⨆ i, (U i).val) = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i, ∃ h : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, (U i).val),
            @IsCohenMacaulayRing Γ(X, (U i).val) _ h,
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, IsCohenMacaulay (U i).toScheme]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay.restrict
declarations.doc: Every open subscheme of a Cohen–Macaulay scheme is Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsCohenMacaulay.restrict {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X) (U : X.Opens) :
    IsCohenMacaulay U.toScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular
declarations.doc:
A scheme is regular, or nonsingular, if every point has an affine open neighbourhood whose
ring of sections is Noetherian and regular.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment:
the source's requirement on `𝒪_X(U)`, Noetherian *and* regular, is Mathlib's
  class `IsRegularRing`: it extends `IsNoetherianRing`, and its further field is that the
  localization at every prime is a regular local ring. Both halves of the requirement are
  therefore written into this definition, the Noetherian one recoverable as
  `IsRegularRing.toIsNoetherian`; see the module docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_tfae
declarations.doc:
A scheme is regular if and only if it is locally Noetherian with regular local rings at
every point, if and only if it is locally Noetherian with regular local rings at closed points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegular_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsRegular X,
      IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧ ∀ x : X, IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x),
      IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧
        (∀ x : X, x ∈ closedPoints X → IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_tfae_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02IU.** A scheme is regular if and only if the ring of sections is
regular on every affine open, if and only if it is regular on the members of one affine open
covering, if and only if the scheme has an open covering by regular open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegular_tfae_cover (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsRegular X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsRegularRing Γ(X, U),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        (⨆ i, (U i).val) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, IsRegularRing Γ(X, U i),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, IsRegular (U i).toScheme]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular.restrict
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 02IU.** Every open subscheme of a regular scheme is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRegular.restrict {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : IsRegular X) (U : X.Opens) :
    IsRegular U.toScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCatenarySpace_tfae
declarations.doc:
A scheme is catenary exactly when this holds on an open covering, or when the rings of
sections of every affine open (equivalently, of one affine open covering) are catenary.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCatenarySpace_tfae (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsCatenarySpace S,
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧ ∀ i, IsCatenarySpace (U i).toScheme,
      ∀ U : S.affineOpens, Ring.IsCatenary Γ(S, U),
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → S.affineOpens),
        IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : S.Opens)) ∧
          ∀ i, Ring.IsCatenary Γ(S, U i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCatenarySpace.of_isImmersion
declarations.doc: A locally closed subscheme of a catenary scheme is catenary.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsCatenarySpace.of_isImmersion {S Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ S)
    [IsImmersion i] (hS : IsCatenarySpace S) : IsCatenarySpace Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCatenarySpace_iff_locally_dimensionFunction
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is catenary if and only if every point has an open
neighbourhood admitting a dimension function.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCatenarySpace_iff_locally_dimensionFunction
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace S ↔
      ∀ x : S, ∃ U : Set S, IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ Nonempty (DimensionFunction U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.codimension_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02IZ**.
Let `X` be a scheme, let `Y ⊆ X` be an irreducible closed subset and let `ξ` be the generic
point of `Y`. Then the codimension of `Y` in `X`, in the sense of Stacks 02I3, is the Krull
dimension of the local ring `𝒪_{X, ξ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimension_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk {X : Scheme.{u}} (Y : IrreducibleCloseds X) (ξ : X)
    (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ (Y : Set X)) :
    (codimension Y : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk ξ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCatenarySpace_iff_stalk_isCatenary
declarations.doc: A scheme is catenary if and only if each of its local rings is catenary.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint
declarations.doc:
A point `s` of a scheme `S` is a finite type point if the canonical morphism
`Spec(κ(s)) ⟶ S` is of finite type.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsFiniteTypePoint {S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (s : S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteTypePoints
declarations.doc: The set of finite type points of a scheme.
declarations.statement: abbrev Scheme.finiteTypePoints (S : Scheme.{u}) : Set S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteTypePoints_eq_iUnion_closedPoints
declarations.doc:
The set of finite type points of a scheme `S` is the union, over the open subschemes `U` of
`S`, of the sets of closed points of `U`; the same union taken over the affine open subschemes
of `S` has the same value.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.finiteTypePoints_eq_iUnion_closedPoints (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    S.finiteTypePoints = (⋃ U : S.Opens, Subtype.val '' closedPoints ↑U) ∧
      S.finiteTypePoints = ⋃ U : S.affineOpens, Subtype.val '' closedPoints ↑U.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mapsTo_finiteTypePoints
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism of schemes sends finite type points to finite type
points.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapsTo_finiteTypePoints {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    Set.MapsTo f.base T.finiteTypePoints S.finiteTypePoints

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inter_finiteTypePoints_nonempty
declarations.doc: Every nonempty locally closed subset of a scheme contains a finite type point.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.closure_inter_finiteTypePoints
declarations.doc: The finite type points lying in a closed subset of a scheme are dense in that subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem closure_inter_finiteTypePoints {S : Scheme.{u}} {T : Set S}
    (hT : IsClosed T) : closure (T ∩ S.finiteTypePoints) = T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_integers
declarations.doc: A scheme locally of finite type over the integers is Jacobson.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_integers {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ ⊤_ Scheme.{u}) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : JacobsonSpace X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_oneDimensionalNoetherianDomain
declarations.doc:
A scheme locally of finite type over a one-dimensional Noetherian domain with infinitely
many prime ideals is Jacobson.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_oneDimensionalNoetherianDomain
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (hprimes : {p : Ideal A | p.IsPrime}.Infinite)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    JacobsonSpace X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The punctured spectrum `Spec R \ {𝔪}` of a Noetherian local ring `R` is a Jacobson
scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_puncturedSpectrum (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    JacobsonSpace (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum R).toScheme
declarations.comment: part (4): the punctured spectrum itself, R Noetherian local

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
A scheme locally of finite type over the punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is
Jacobson.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_puncturedSpectrum
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum R).toScheme)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : JacobsonSpace X
declarations.comment: part (4): schemes lft over the punctured spectrum, R Noetherian local

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsUniversallyCatenary
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme `S` is **universally catenary** if every scheme locally of
finite type over `S` is catenary.
declarations.statement: def IsUniversallyCatenary (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A scheme locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme is
universally catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hS : IsUniversallyCatenary S) :
    @IsUniversallyCatenary X
      (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a locally Noetherian scheme, universal catenarity is equivalent to holding on an open
covering, to universal catenarity of the ring of sections over every affine open, and to that
ring-theoretic condition holding over the members of one affine open covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_tfae (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsUniversallyCatenary S,
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧ ∀ i, IsUniversallyCatenary (U i).toScheme,
      ∀ U : S.affineOpens, Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary Γ(S, U),
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → S.affineOpens),
        IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : S.Opens)) ∧
          ∀ i, Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary Γ(S, U i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_iff_stalk_isUniversallyCatenary
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is universally catenary if and only if each of its local rings
is universally catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_iff_stalk_isUniversallyCatenary
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    IsUniversallyCatenary S ↔
      ∀ s : S, Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary (S.presheaf.stalk s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JB, part (1).** A scheme locally of finite type over a field is
universally catenary.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_isCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JB, part (2).** A scheme locally of finite type over a locally
Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay scheme is universally catenary.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_int
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JB, part (3).** A scheme locally of finite type over the integers is
universally catenary. The base is `Spec (ULift ℤ)`, the terminal scheme of the ambient universe,
so this is the statement for a scheme in an arbitrary universe.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_dimOneDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JB, part (4).** A scheme locally of finite type over a
one-dimensional Noetherian domain is universally catenary.

declarations.name: Topology.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_surjective_of_specializingMap_or_generalizingMap
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X → Y` be a continuous surjection of topological spaces with `Y`
sober. If specializations lift along `f`, or generalizations lift along `f`, then the Krull
dimension of `Y` is at most the Krull dimension of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_of_surjective_of_specializingMap_or_generalizingMap
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [QuasiSober Y] [T0Space Y]
    (f : X → Y) (hf : Continuous f) (hsurj : Function.Surjective f)
    (h : SpecializingMap f ∨ GeneralizingMap f) :
    topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ topologicalKrullDim X

declarations.name: IsLocalization.algebraMap_surjective_of_isClosed_range_comap
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a multiplicative subset of a ring `R`. If the image of
`Spec(S⁻¹R) → Spec(R)` is closed, then `R → S⁻¹R` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraMap_surjective_of_isClosed_range_comap
    [IsLocalization S A]
    (hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R A)))) :
    Function.Surjective (algebraMap R A)
declarations.comment:
Surjectivity of `R → S⁻¹R`; the isomorphism `R/I ≅ S⁻¹R` with `I` the kernel
is `IsLocalization.quotientKerAlgEquivOfIsClosedRangeComap`.

declarations.name: IsLocalization.quotientKerAlgEquivOfIsClosedRangeComap
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a multiplicative subset of a ring `R`, and let `I` be the kernel of
`R → S⁻¹R`. If the image of `Spec(S⁻¹R) → Spec(R)` is closed, then the canonical map
`R ⧸ I → S⁻¹R` is an isomorphism of `R`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientKerAlgEquivOfIsClosedRangeComap
    [IsLocalization S A]
    (hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R A)))) :
    (R ⧸ RingHom.ker (algebraMap R A)) ≃ₐ[R] A
declarations.comment:
The isomorphism `R/I ≅ S⁻¹R`, `I` the kernel of `R → S⁻¹R`, for any
localization `A` of `R` at `S`.

declarations.name: IsLocalization.exists_ringEquiv_prod_fst_eq_algebraMap_of_isClosed_range
declarations.doc:
Let `S ⊆ R` be a multiplicative subset such that the image of `Spec(S⁻¹R) → Spec R` is
closed. If `R` is Noetherian, or `Spec R` is a Noetherian topological space, or `S` is finitely
generated as a monoid, then `S⁻¹R` is a direct factor of `R`: there is a ring `R'` and an
isomorphism `R ≅ S⁻¹R × R'` whose first component is the localization map `R → S⁻¹R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringEquiv_prod_fst_eq_algebraMap_of_isClosed_range
    (hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range (comap (algebraMap R A))))
    (h : IsNoetherianRing R ∨ NoetherianSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) ∨ S.FG) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (φ : R ≃+* A × R'), ∀ r, (φ r).1 = algebraMap R A r
declarations.comment:
The isomorphism is the one of the proof (via 02JH and 00EM): its first component
is the localization map `R → S⁻¹R`.

declarations.name: Algebra.finite_iff_exists_finset_adjoin_eq_top_and_isIntegral
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.finite_iff_exists_finset_adjoin_eq_top_and_isIntegral
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    Module.Finite R S ↔
      ∃ (s : Finset S), Algebra.adjoin R (s : Set S) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, IsIntegral R x

registrations.name: RingHom.finite_ofLocalizationSpan
