declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.isRegular_iff_ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Regular sequences in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring are those cutting out the right
dimension.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local Cohen–Macaulay ring and let `xs = x₁, …, x_c` be
a list of elements of `𝔪`. Then `xs` is a regular sequence if and only if
`dim(R/(x₁, …, x_c)) + c = dim(R)`, and in that case `xs` extends by elements of `𝔪` to a regular
sequence of length `dim(R)` and each `R/(x₁, …, x_i)` is a Cohen–Macaulay local ring of dimension
`dim(R) - i`. The source's subtraction is moved to the other side of the equations, Krull
dimensions being valued in `WithBot ℕ∞`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.isRegular_iff_ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R) (xs : List R)
    (hxs : ∀ x ∈ xs, x ∈ maximalIdeal R) :
    (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R xs ↔
        ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList xs) + xs.length = ringKrullDim R) ∧
      (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R xs →
        (∃ ys : List R, (∀ y ∈ ys, y ∈ maximalIdeal R) ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R (xs ++ ys) ∧
            ((xs ++ ys).length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R) ∧
        ∀ i ≤ xs.length, ∃ _ : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (xs.take i)),
          Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (xs.take i))
              (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (xs.take i)) ∧
            ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (xs.take i)) + i = ringKrullDim R)
declarations.comment: `R` Cohen–Macaulay is `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R` (Definition 00NF at `M = R`, equal to Definition 00N8 by `Module.supportDim_self_eq_ringKrullDim`); the source's `dim(R/(x₁, …, x_i)) = dim(R) - i` is stated additively, as in `ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isRegular`; the extension is an append, and the local ring structures on the quotients are existentially bound. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.eventually_flat_of_directed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02JO (3).** Let `R → S` be of finite presentation and let `M` be a finitely
presented `S`-module which is flat over `R`. Let `(R → S, M) = colim_λ (R_λ → S_λ, M_λ)` be a
directed colimit such that `R_μ ⊗_{R_λ} S_λ → S_μ` and `S_μ ⊗_{S_λ} M_λ → M_μ` are isomorphisms
for `μ ≥ λ`, each `R_λ → S_λ` is of finite presentation and each `M_λ` is a finitely presented
`S_λ`-module. Then `M_λ` is flat over `R_λ` for all sufficiently large `λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.eventually_flat_of_directed {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M] [Module.Flat R M]
    {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)]
    {A B : ι → Type v} [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i, CommRing (B i)] [∀ i, Algebra (A i) (B i)]
    {N : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (N i)] [∀ i, Module (B i) (N i)]
    (a : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i →+* A j) (b : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → B i →+* B j)
    (n : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), N i →ₛₗ[b i j h] N j)
    [DirectedSystem A fun i j h => a i j h] [DirectedSystem B fun i j h => b i j h]
    [DirectedSystem N fun i j h => n i j h]
    (hab : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j),
      (b i j h).comp (algebraMap (A i) (B i)) = (algebraMap (A j) (B j)).comp (a i j h))
    (ρ : ∀ i, A i →+* R) (σ : ∀ i, B i →+* S) (ν : ∀ i, N i →ₛₗ[σ i] M)
    (hρ : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j) x, ρ j (a i j h x) = ρ i x)
    (hσ : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j) x, σ j (b i j h x) = σ i x)
    (hν : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j) x, ν j (n i j h x) = ν i x)
    (hρσ : ∀ i, (σ i).comp (algebraMap (A i) (B i)) = (algebraMap R S).comp (ρ i))
    (hρs : ∀ r, ∃ i x, ρ i x = r) (hρz : ∀ i x, ρ i x = 0 → ∃ j, ∃ h : i ≤ j, a i j h x = 0)
    (hσs : ∀ s, ∃ i x, σ i x = s) (hσz : ∀ i x, σ i x = 0 → ∃ j, ∃ h : i ≤ j, b i j h x = 0)
    (hνs : ∀ m, ∃ i x, ν i x = m) (hνz : ∀ i x, ν i x = 0 → ∃ j, ∃ h : i ≤ j, n i j h x = 0)
    (hpush : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), CategoryTheory.IsPushout (CommRingCat.ofHom (a i j h))
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A i) (B i))) (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A j) (B j)))
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (b i j h)))
    (hbc : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), letI := algebraB b h
      letI := Module.compHom (N j) (b i j h)
      haveI : IsScalarTower (B i) (B j) (N j) := .of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
      IsBaseChange (B j) (transLinear b n h))
    (hfp : ∀ i, Algebra.FinitePresentation (A i) (B i))
    (hfpN : ∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation (B i) (N i)) :
    ∃ i, ∀ j, i ≤ j →
      letI := Module.compHom (N j) (algebraMap (A j) (B j)); Module.Flat (A j) (N j)

declarations.name: Module.Flat.exists_finiteType_model
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02JO (1).** Let `R → S` be of finite presentation and let `M` be a finitely
presented `S`-module which is flat over `R`. Then there are a ring `R₀` of finite type over `ℤ`,
an `R₀`-algebra `S₀` of finite type and a finite `S₀`-module `M₀` flat over `R₀`, together with
ring maps `R₀ → R`, `S₀ → S` and an `S₀`-linear map `M₀ → M`, such that `S = R ⊗_{R₀} S₀` and
`M = S ⊗_{S₀} M₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.exists_finiteType_model {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M] [Module.Flat R M] :
    ∃ (R₀ S₀ M₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing R₀) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀)
      (_ : Algebra R₀ R) (_ : Algebra S₀ S) (_ : Algebra R₀ S) (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ R S)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ S) (_ : AddCommGroup M₀) (_ : Module S₀ M₀) (_ : Module R₀ M₀)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ M₀) (_ : Module S₀ M) (_ : IsScalarTower S₀ S M)
      (f : M₀ →ₗ[S₀] M),
      Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ Algebra.FiniteType R₀ S₀ ∧ Module.Finite S₀ M₀ ∧
        Module.Flat R₀ M₀ ∧ Algebra.IsPushout R₀ R S₀ S ∧ IsBaseChange S f

declarations.name: Module.Flat.exists_finitePresentation_model_of_directed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02JO (2).** Let `R → S` be of finite presentation and let `M` be a finitely
presented `S`-module which is flat over `R`. If `R = colim_λ R_λ` is a directed colimit, then
there are `λ`, an `R_λ`-algebra `S_λ` of finite presentation and a finitely presented
`S_λ`-module `M_λ` which is flat over `R_λ`, with an algebra map `S_λ → S` and an `S_λ`-linear
map `M_λ → M` exhibiting `S = R ⊗_{R_λ} S_λ` and `M = S ⊗_{S_λ} M_λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.exists_finitePresentation_model_of_directed {R S : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M]
    [Module.Flat R M] {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)]
    {A : ι → Type v} [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] (a : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i →+* A j)
    [DirectedSystem A fun i j h => a i j h] (ρ : ∀ i, A i →+* R)
    (hρ : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j) x, ρ j (a i j h x) = ρ i x) (hs : ∀ r, ∃ i x, ρ i x = r)
    (hz : ∀ i x, ρ i x = 0 → ∃ j, ∃ h : i ≤ j, a i j h x = 0) :
    ∃ i, letI := (ρ i).toAlgebra
      ∃ (T P : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra (A i) T) (_ : Algebra T S)
        (_ : Algebra (A i) S) (_ : IsScalarTower (A i) R S) (_ : IsScalarTower (A i) T S)
        (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module T P) (_ : Module (A i) P) (_ : IsScalarTower (A i) T P)
        (_ : Module T M) (_ : IsScalarTower T S M) (f : P →ₗ[T] M),
        Algebra.FinitePresentation (A i) T ∧ Module.FinitePresentation T P ∧
          Module.Flat (A i) P ∧ Algebra.IsPushout (A i) R T S ∧ IsBaseChange S f

declarations.name: Module.Flat.exists_flat_models_and_eventually_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02JO.** Let `R → S` be of finite presentation and let `M` be a finitely presented
`S`-module which is flat over `R`. Then:

1. there are a ring `R₀` of finite type over `ℤ`, an `R₀`-algebra `S₀` of finite type and a finite
   `S₀`-module `M₀` flat over `R₀`, with maps to `R`, `S` and `M` exhibiting `S = R ⊗_{R₀} S₀` and
   `M = S ⊗_{S₀} M₀`;
2. if `R = colim_λ R_λ` is a directed colimit, such a model already exists over some `R_λ`, with
   `R_λ → S_λ` of finite presentation and `M_λ` a finitely presented `S_λ`-module;
3. if `(R → S, M) = colim_λ (R_λ → S_λ, M_λ)` is a directed colimit of finitely presented pairs
   with cartesian transition squares, then `M_λ` is flat over `R_λ` for all large `λ`.

This is the packaged three-part form of the tag, stated at the universe generality the source
asserts: the index `I`, the three colimits `R`, `S`, `M`, the stage families `A`, `B`, `N` and the
model `R₀`, `S₀`, `M₀` of part (1) all live in independent universes. The three parts are also
available separately as `Module.Flat.exists_finiteType_model`,
`Module.Flat.exists_finitePresentation_model_of_directed` and
`Module.Flat.eventually_flat_of_directed`, which are proved with `R` and `S` in one universe (and,
in part (1), with the model in that universe); this statement is deduced from them by the universe
transport of the previous section, with no repetition of the spreading-out argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.exists_flat_models_and_eventually_flat
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} {M : Type uM}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S M] [Module.Flat R M] :
    (∃ (R₀ : Type uR₀) (S₀ : Type uS₀) (M₀ : Type uM₀)
        (_ : CommRing R₀) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀)
        (_ : Algebra R₀ R) (_ : Algebra S₀ S) (_ : Algebra R₀ S)
        (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ R S) (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ S)
        (_ : AddCommGroup M₀) (_ : Module S₀ M₀) (_ : Module R₀ M₀)
        (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ M₀) (_ : Module S₀ M) (_ : IsScalarTower S₀ S M)
        (f : M₀ →ₗ[S₀] M),
      Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ Algebra.FiniteType R₀ S₀ ∧ Module.Finite S₀ M₀ ∧
        Module.Flat R₀ M₀ ∧ Algebra.IsPushout R₀ R S₀ S ∧ IsBaseChange S f) ∧
    (∀ (I : Type uI) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
        (A : I → Type uA) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (A i))
        (a : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i →+* A j)
        (_ : DirectedSystem A (fun i j h ↦ a i j h))
        (ρ : ∀ i, A i →+* R),
      (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), ρ j ∘ a i j h = ρ i) →
      (∀ x : R, ∃ i y, ρ i y = x) →
      (∀ i y, ρ i y = 0 → ∃ (j : I) (h : i ≤ j), a i j h y = 0) →
      ∃ i : I,
        letI : Algebra (A i) R := (ρ i).toAlgebra
        ∃ (T : Type (max uA uS)) (P : Type (max (max uA uS) uM))
            (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra (A i) T)
            (_ : Algebra T S) (_ : Algebra (A i) S)
            (_ : IsScalarTower (A i) R S) (_ : IsScalarTower (A i) T S)
            (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module T P) (_ : Module (A i) P)
            (_ : IsScalarTower (A i) T P) (_ : Module T M) (_ : IsScalarTower T S M)
            (f : P →ₗ[T] M),
          algebraMap (A i) R = ρ i ∧
            Algebra.FinitePresentation (A i) T ∧ Module.FinitePresentation T P ∧
            Module.Flat (A i) P ∧ Algebra.IsPushout (A i) R T S ∧ IsBaseChange S f) ∧
    (∀ (I : Type uI) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
        (A : I → Type uA) (B : I → Type uB) (N : I → Type uN)
        (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (A i)) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (B i))
        (_ : ∀ i, AddCommGroup (N i)) (_ : ∀ i, Module (B i) (N i))
        (a : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i →+* A j)
        (b : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → B i →+* B j)
        (_ : DirectedSystem A (fun i j h ↦ a i j h))
        (_ : DirectedSystem B (fun i j h ↦ b i j h))
        (g : ∀ i, A i →+* B i)
        (n : ∀ i j, (h : i ≤ j) → N i →ₛₗ[b i j h] N j)
        (ρ : ∀ i, A i →+* R) (σ : ∀ i, B i →+* S)
        (ν : ∀ i, N i →+ M)
        (hg : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), (g j).comp (a i j h) = (b i j h).comp (g i)),
      (∀ i x, n i i le_rfl x = x) →
      (∀ i j k (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) x,
        n j k hjk (n i j hij x) = n i k (hij.trans hjk) x) →
      (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), ρ j ∘ a i j h = ρ i) →
      (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), σ j ∘ b i j h = σ i) →
      (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j) x, ν j (n i j h x) = ν i x) →
      (∀ i, (algebraMap R S).comp (ρ i) = (σ i).comp (g i)) →
      (∀ i x m, ν i (g i x • m) = ρ i x • ν i m) →
      (∀ i y m, ν i (y • m) = σ i y • ν i m) →
      (∀ x : R, ∃ i y, ρ i y = x) →
      (∀ i y, ρ i y = 0 → ∃ (j : I) (h : i ≤ j), a i j h y = 0) →
      (∀ x : S, ∃ i y, σ i y = x) →
      (∀ i y, σ i y = 0 → ∃ (j : I) (h : i ≤ j), b i j h y = 0) →
      (∀ x : M, ∃ i y, ν i y = x) →
      (∀ i y, ν i y = 0 → ∃ (j : I) (h : i ≤ j), n i j h y = 0) →
      (∀ i,
        letI : Algebra (A i) (B i) := (g i).toAlgebra
        Algebra.FinitePresentation (A i) (B i)) →
      (∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation (B i) (N i)) →
      (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j),
        letI : Algebra (A i) (B i) := (g i).toAlgebra
        letI : Algebra (A i) (A j) := (a i j h).toAlgebra
        letI : Algebra (B i) (B j) := (b i j h).toAlgebra
        letI : Algebra (A j) (B j) := (g j).toAlgebra
        letI : Algebra (A i) (B j) := ((g j).comp (a i j h)).toAlgebra
        letI : IsScalarTower (A i) (A j) (B j) :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
        letI : IsScalarTower (A i) (B i) (B j) :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun x y ↦ by
            change b i j h (g i x) * y = g j (a i j h x) * y
            exact congrArg (fun z : B j ↦ z * y)
              (by simpa using (RingHom.congr_fun (hg i j h) x).symm)
        Algebra.IsPushout (A i) (A j) (B i) (B j)) →
      (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j),
        letI : Algebra (B i) (B j) := (b i j h).toAlgebra
        letI : Module (B i) (N j) := Module.compHom (N j) (b i j h)
        letI : IsScalarTower (B i) (B j) (N j) :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
        IsBaseChange (B j)
          (⟨(n i j h).toAddHom, fun x y ↦ (n i j h).map_smul' x y⟩ :
            N i →ₗ[B i] N j)) →
      ∃ i, ∀ j, i ≤ j →
        letI : Module (A j) (N j) := Module.compHom (N j) (g j)
        Module.Flat (A j) (N j))

declarations.name: exists_isRegular_ofList_eq_ker_algebraMap_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Descent of regular sequences along a flat square of local rings.** Let
```
B ← S
↑   ↑
A ← R
```
be a commutative square of rings in which `R` is a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring, `S` is
a Noetherian local ring, `A = R/I` and `B = S/J` are quotients, and `R → S` and `A → B` are flat.
If `J` is generated by a regular sequence, and the image `J̄` of `J` in `S̄ = S/𝔪_R S` is
generated by a regular sequence, then `I` is generated by a regular sequence.

The quotients are encoded by the surjectivity of `R → A` and `S → B`, the ideals `I` and `J`
being their kernels. See the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRegular_ofList_eq_ker_algebraMap_of_flat
    {R S A B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra S B] [Algebra R B]
    [IsScalarTower R A B] [IsScalarTower R S B]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [Module.Flat R S] [Module.Flat A B]
    (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R)
    (hA : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R A)) (hB : Function.Surjective (algebraMap S B))
    (hJ : ∃ rs : List S, IsRegular S rs ∧ Ideal.ofList rs = RingHom.ker (algebraMap S B))
    (hJbar : ∃ rs : List (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)),
      IsRegular (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) rs ∧
        Ideal.ofList rs = (RingHom.ker (algebraMap S B)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk _)) :
    ∃ rs : List R, IsRegular R rs ∧ Ideal.ofList rs = RingHom.ker (algebraMap R A)
declarations.comment:
The square is `IsScalarTower R A B` and `IsScalarTower R S B` with `R → A` and
`S → B` surjective, `I` and `J` being their kernels, and `J̄` is the image of `J` in
`S ⧸ 𝔪_R S`. Stated more generally than the source: `R` is only assumed Cohen-Macaulay
(regular local rings are, by 00NQ), and `S̄` is not assumed regular, which the argument does not
use. `S` is assumed Noetherian, as the source's appeals to 00MG and 00ME require. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_valuationRing_of_image_point
declarations.doc:
Every point of the scheme-theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism is reached
by a map from a valuation ring whose generic point factors through the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_valuationRing_of_image_point
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] (z : f.image) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : ValuationRing A)
      (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra A K) (_ : IsFractionRing A K)
      (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X) (h : Spec (.of A) ⟶ f.image),
      g ≫ f.toImage =
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)) ≫ h ∧
      h (closedPoint A) = z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_specializes_of_image_point
declarations.doc:
A point of the scheme-theoretic image is a specialization of a point coming
from the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_specializes_of_image_point
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] (z : f.image) :
    ∃ x : X, f x ⤳ f.imageι z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isImmersion_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JR.** Every quasi-compact immersion of schemes is
quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasiAffineHom_of_isImmersion_of_quasiCompact
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsQuasiAffineHom f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_comp_le_add
declarations.doc:
For two morphisms locally of finite type, the dimension at a point of a fibre of their
composition is at most the sum of the dimensions, at the corresponding points, of the two
successive fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_comp_le_add (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (x : X) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt ((f ≫ g).fiber ((f ≫ g) x)) ((f ≫ g).asFiber x) ≤
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) +
        topologicalKrullDimAt (g.fiber (g (f x))) (g.asFiber (f x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_comp_eq_add_of_isFlatAt_fiberMapOfComp
declarations.doc:
The dimension inequality for a composition is an equality as soon as the induced morphism
between the fibres is flat at the point.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_comp_eq_add_of_isFlatAt_fiberMapOfComp (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (x : X)
    (hflat : IsFlatAt (fiberMapOfComp f g ((f ≫ g) x)).toLRSHom.toShHom
      ((f ≫ g).asFiber x)) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt ((f ≫ g).fiber ((f ≫ g) x)) ((f ≫ g).asFiber x) =
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) +
        topologicalKrullDimAt (g.fiber (g (f x))) (g.asFiber (f x))
declarations.comment: equality for a flat morphism of fibres

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_comp_eq_add_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
The dimension inequality for a composition is an equality as soon as the first morphism is
flat at the point.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_comp_eq_add_of_isFlatAt (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (x : X)
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt ((f ≫ g).fiber ((f ≫ g) x)) ((f ≫ g).asFiber x) =
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) +
        topologicalKrullDimAt (g.fiber (g (f x))) (g.asFiber (f x))
declarations.comment: equality when the first morphism is flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg_residueField_le
declarations.doc:
The dimension formula for a dominant morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type between
integral schemes over a locally Noetherian base:
`dim 𝒪_{X, x} + trdeg_{κ(f x)} κ(x) ≤ dim 𝒪_{S, f x} + trdeg_{R(S)} R(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg_residueField_le
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral S] [IsDominant f]
    (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) :=
      (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra S.functionField X.functionField := f.functionFieldMap.hom.toAlgebra
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) +
        (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) : WithBot ℕ∞)
      ≤ ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) +
        (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg S.functionField X.functionField) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg_residueField_eq
declarations.doc:
Over a universally catenary base the dimension formula is an equality:
`dim 𝒪_{X, x} + trdeg_{κ(f x)} κ(x) = dim 𝒪_{S, f x} + trdeg_{R(S)} R(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_add_trdeg_residueField_eq
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral S] [IsDominant f]
    (hS : Scheme.IsUniversallyCatenary S) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) :=
      (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra S.functionField X.functionField := f.functionFieldMap.hom.toAlgebra
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) +
        (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) : WithBot ℕ∞)
      = ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) +
        (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg S.functionField X.functionField) : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: equality for a universally catenary base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.localDimension_add_trdeg_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02JU.** The dimension formula for a dominant locally finite-type morphism of
integral schemes over a locally Noetherian base: the dimension of the local ring at `x` plus
the transcendence degree of `κ(x)/κ(f x)` is at most the dimension of the local ring at `f x`
plus the transcendence degree of the function field extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem localDimension_add_trdeg_le {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral S] [IsDominant f] (x : X) :
    letI := (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) +
        (Cardinal.toENat
          (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
      ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) +
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg S.functionField X.functionField) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.localDimension_add_trdeg_eq
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02JU.** Over a universally catenary base the dimension formula is an equality.
declarations.statement:
theorem localDimension_add_trdeg_eq {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral S] [IsDominant f]
    (hS : Scheme.IsUniversallyCatenary S) (x : X) :
    letI := (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) +
        (Cardinal.toENat
          (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) +
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg S.functionField X.functionField) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.relativeDimension_isDimensionFunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02JW.** A dimension function on a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme
propagates along every locally finite-type morphism by adding the transcendence degree of the
residue-field extension: `relativeDimension δ f` is the underlying function of a dimension
function on the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimension_isDimensionFunction {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : Scheme.IsUniversallyCatenary S)
    (δ : DimensionFunction S) (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    ∃ d : DimensionFunction X, ∀ x, d x = relativeDimension δ f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_le_add_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JX.** For a dominant morphism of integral schemes locally of finite
type over a locally Noetherian base, the dimension of the source is at most the dimension of the
target plus the transcendence degree of the extension of function fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_add_trdeg (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsDominant f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    letI := (functionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    topologicalKrullDim X ≤ topologicalKrullDim Y +
      (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg Y.functionField X.functionField) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_eq_add_trdeg_of_isClosedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JX.** For a *closed* dominant morphism of integral schemes locally of
finite type over a locally Noetherian base — in particular for a proper one — the bound on the
dimension of the source is an equality.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_add_trdeg_of_isClosedMap (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsDominant f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : IsClosedMap f) :
    letI := (functionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    topologicalKrullDim X = topologicalKrullDim Y +
      (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg Y.functionField X.functionField) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.isOpen_iff_isOpen_preimage
declarations.doc:
A subset of the target of a quasi-compact, surjective, flat morphism of schemes is open if and
only if its preimage is open.
declarations.statement: public theorem Flat.isOpen_iff_isOpen_preimage {T : Set Y} : IsOpen T ↔ IsOpen (f ⁻¹' T)
declarations.comment: the open half: `T` is open if and only if `f ⁻¹' T` is open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.isClosed_iff_isClosed_preimage
declarations.doc:
A subset of the target of a quasi-compact, surjective, flat morphism of schemes is closed if
and only if its preimage is closed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Flat.isClosed_iff_isClosed_preimage {T : Set Y} :
    IsClosed T ↔ IsClosed (f ⁻¹' T)
declarations.comment: the closed half: `T` is closed if and only if `f ⁻¹' T` is closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_comp_of_surjective_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JZ (second global consequence).** If `f : X ⟶ Y`
is surjective and flat and `X` is flat over `S`, then `Y` is flat over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_comp_of_surjective_flat
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ S)
    [Surjective f] [Flat f] [Flat (f ≫ q)] : Flat q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_iff_modulePullback_isFlatOverAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JZ (pointwise assertion).** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is
flat at `x`, then a module `G` on `Y` is flat over `S` at
`f(x)` if and only if its pullback to `X` is flat over `S` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatOverAt_iff_modulePullback_isFlatOverAt
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ S)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (x : X) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt q.toLRSHom.toShHom G (f.base x) ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt (f ≫ q).toLRSHom.toShHom
        ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G) x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOver_iff_modulePullback_isFlatOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02JZ (first global consequence).** Pullback along a
surjective flat morphism detects whether a module is flat over
the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatOver_iff_modulePullback_isFlatOver
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ S)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    [Surjective f] [Flat f] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver q.toLRSHom.toShHom G ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver (f ≫ q).toLRSHom.toShHom
        ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiberDimensionAt_eq_card_sub_card
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02K0.** For a presentation
`S = R[x₁, …, xₙ]/(f₁, …, fᶜ)` which is a relative global complete intersection, the
dimension at every point of the fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` is `n - c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fiberDimensionAt_eq_card_sub_card
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ] (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ)
    [P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection] (x : Spec (.of S)) :
    let f : Spec (.of S) ⟶ Spec (.of R) := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S))
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      ((Nat.card ι - Nat.card σ : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstant_fiberDimensionAt
declarations.doc: The local dimension of the fibre of a syntomic morphism is locally constant on its source.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLocallyConstant_fiberDimensionAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : Syntomic f) :
    IsLocallyConstant (fun x : X => topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SyntomicOfRelativeDimension
declarations.doc: A syntomic morphism whose fibres have local dimension `d` at every point.
declarations.statement: abbrev SyntomicOfRelativeDimension (d : ℕ) {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Syntomic.syntomic_of_comp_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02K3.** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` be morphisms of schemes with `X ⟶ Y`
surjective and syntomic and the composite `X ⟶ S` syntomic. If `Y ⟶ S` is locally of finite
presentation, then `Y ⟶ S` is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_of_comp_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ S) [Surjective f]
    (hf : Syntomic f) (hcomp : Syntomic (f ≫ q)) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation q] :
    Syntomic q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toRelativeDifferentials_shortExact
declarations.doc:
For morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ S` with `f` formally smooth, the canonical
sequence `0 ⟶ f^* Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` of `𝒪_X`-modules is short exact. The case of a
smooth `f` is the special case obtained from
`Stacks.Smooth.smooth_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toRelativeDifferentials_shortExact (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) (hf : FormallySmooth f) :
    ∃ h : relativeDifferentialsMap f g (f ≫ g) (𝟙 S) (Category.comp_id (f ≫ g)).symm ≫
        f.toRelativeDifferentials g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.smooth_of_comp_surjective_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KM (smooth case).** If `f` is surjective and smooth and `f ≫ q` is
smooth, then `q` is smooth.

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KA.** A morphism of schemes is finite locally free if it is affine
and the direct image of its structure sheaf is a finite locally free module.
declarations.statement:
class IsFiniteLocallyFree {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop
    extends IsAffineHom f,
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (pushforwardStructureSheaf.{u} f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KB.** A morphism of schemes is finite locally free if and only if it
is finite, flat, and locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree f ↔
      IsFinite f ∧ Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KB.** Over a locally Noetherian base, a morphism of schemes is finite
locally free if and only if it is finite and flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBaseChangeIso.isIso_baseChangeNatTrans_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**The base-change assertion of Stacks Tag 02KG.**  The base-change morphism of a cartesian
square of schemes whose right-hand morphism is affine is invertible at every quasi-coherent
module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_baseChangeNatTrans_of_isAffineHom (hw : IsPullback g' f' f g) [IsAffineHom f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsIso ((AffinePushforward.baseChangeNatTrans hw.w).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePushforward.pushforward_isQuasicoherent_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KG.** The direct image of a quasi-coherent module along an affine
morphism is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
instance pushforward_isQuasicoherent_of_isAffineHom {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (F : X.Modules) [IsAffineHom f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag02KGDerivedComparison.isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02KG], comparison with the derived direct image.** For an affine morphism
`f : X ⟶ S` of schemes and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the canonical map from the ordinary
direct image `f_* F`, placed in degree zero, to the total derived direct image `R f_*(F[0])` is an
isomorphism. Equivalently: a quasi-coherent module has no higher direct images along an affine
morphism, so the unit of `R f_*` is already invertible on degree-zero complexes.

This is `Stacks.AffineHigherDirectImage.rightAcyclic_pushforward`, [Stacks, Tag 01XC], read at the
unfolding of `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightAcyclic`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_of_isAffineHom
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) [IsAffineHom f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith.app
      ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F))
declarations.comment: comparison with the derived direct image

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FlatBaseChangeDerived.isIso_baseChangeMap_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Flat base change in the derived category ([Stacks, Tag 02KH], part (1)).** For a cartesian
square of schemes with `g` flat and `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the base change map `g^* Rf_* ℱ ⟶ Rf'_* (g')^* ℱ` of [Stacks, Tag 02N7] is an
isomorphism in `D⁺(𝒪_{S'})`. Taking cohomology sheaves, the base change maps
`g^* R^i f_* ℱ ⟶ R^i f'_* (g')^* ℱ` are isomorphisms for every `i`
(`isIso_higherBaseChangeMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_baseChangeMap_of_flat (H : IsPullback g' f' f g) [Flat g] [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cohomology.FlatBaseChange.baseChangeMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom
      f'.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom g'.toLRSHom.toShHom
      (congrArg (fun h => h.toLRSHom.toShHom) H.w) (isFlat_toShHom g)
      (isFlat_toShHom_of_isPullback H)).app ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
declarations.comment: part (1): the base change map of Tag 02N7 is an isomorphism in D⁺(𝒪_{S'}), hence in every degree i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FlatBaseChangeDerived.isIso_higherBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02KH], part (1).** For a cartesian square of schemes with `g` flat and `f`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the base change map
`g^* R^i f_* ℱ ⟶ R^i f'_* (g')^* ℱ` is an isomorphism for every `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMap (H : IsPullback g' f' f g) [Flat g] [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (i : ℤ) :
    IsIso (higherBaseChangeMap H F i)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FlatBaseChangeDerived.cohomologyBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02KH], part (2).** For a cartesian square of schemes with `S` and `S'`
affine, `g` flat and `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module
`ℱ`,

`H^i(X, ℱ) ⊗_{Γ(S, 𝒪_S)} Γ(S', 𝒪_{S'}) ≅ H^i(X', (g')^* ℱ)`

as `Γ(S', 𝒪_{S'})`-modules, for every `i`. The isomorphism is the one given by the base change
map of [Stacks, Tag 02N7]: it is the global sections over `S'` of the isomorphism
`g^* R^i f_* ℱ ≅ R^i f'_* (g')^* ℱ` of part (1), read through the identifications
`H^i(X, ℱ) = Γ(S, R^i f_* ℱ)` of [Stacks, Tag 01XK] (for `f` and for `f'`) and
`Γ(S', g^* 𝒢) = Γ(S, 𝒢) ⊗_{Γ(S, 𝒪_S)} Γ(S', 𝒪_{S'})` for the quasi-coherent
`𝒢 = R^i f_* ℱ` ([Stacks, Tag 01XJ]).
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyBaseChangeIso (H : IsPullback g' f' f g) [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S'] [Flat g]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (i : ℤ) :
    (ModuleCat.extendScalars g.appTop.hom).obj (cohomologyOver f F i) ≅
      cohomologyOver f' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F) i

    (hff : g.FaithfullyFlat) (hfp : g.FinitePresentation) : f.FinitePresentation

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KM (smooth case).** If `f` is surjective and smooth and `f ≫ q` is
smooth, then `q` is smooth.

This is also Stacks 02K5: there the target of `f ≫ q` is additionally assumed locally of finite
presentation, which that source's own footnote observes is implied by the other hypotheses.

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.etale_of_comp_surjective_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02KM**, étale case. If `f : X ⟶ Y` is surjective and étale and the composite
`f ≫ q` is étale, then `q : Y ⟶ S` is étale.

The missing hypothesis of Tag 02K6, that `q` be locally of finite presentation, follows from
Tag 02KL: `f` is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and `f ≫ q` is locally
of finite presentation because it is étale.

declarations.name: Stacks.Syntomic.syntomic_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KM (syntomic case).** Syntomicity descends along a surjective
syntomic morphism: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is surjective and syntomic and `f ≫ q` is syntomic, then
`q : Y ⟶ S` is syntomic.

This is the syntomic one of the lemma's three cases; the étale case is
`Stacks.Etale.etale_of_comp_surjective_etale` and the smooth case is
`Stacks.Smooth.smooth_of_comp_surjective_smooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_of_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ S) [Surjective f] (hf : Syntomic f)
    (hcomp : Syntomic (f ≫ q)) : Syntomic q

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.isLocalAtTarget_fpqcPrecoverage_of_affineDescent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KP** for the fpqc topology. Let `P` be a property of morphisms of
schemes. Assume that

1. `P` is stable under base change along flat morphisms;
2. `P` is Zariski local on the base;
3. for every surjective flat morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` of affine schemes and every morphism of
   schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, the property `P` holds for `f` if it holds for the base change
   `S' ×_S X ⟶ S'`.

Then `P` is fpqc local on the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtTarget_fpqcPrecoverage_of_affineDescent
    (hdesc : ∀ {S S' T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S'] (g : S' ⟶ S), Surjective g →
      Flat g → ∀ f : T ⟶ S, P (pullback.snd f g) → P f) :
    P.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtTarget_precoverage_of_affineDescent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KP** for the fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic topologies. Let `P` be
a property of morphisms of schemes and let `τ` be one of fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic.
Assume that

1. `P` is preserved by base change along the morphisms belonging to `τ`, that is along flat
   morphisms locally of finite presentation, syntomic, smooth or étale morphisms depending on
   whether `τ` is fppf, syntomic, smooth or étale;
2. `P` is Zariski local on the base;
3. for every surjective morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` of affine schemes belonging to `τ` and every
   morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, the property `P` holds for `f` if it holds for the base
   change `S' ×_S X ⟶ S'`.

Then `P` is `τ` local on the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtTarget_precoverage_of_affineDescent (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (τ : CoveringTopology) (hτ : τ ≠ .zariski)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChangeAgainst (coveringMorphismProperty τ)]
    [IsZariskiLocalAtTarget P]
    (hdesc : ∀ {S S' X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S'] (g : S' ⟶ S), Surjective g →
      coveringMorphismProperty τ g → ∀ f : X ⟶ S, P (pullback.snd f g) → P f) :
    P.IsLocalAtTarget (Scheme.precoverage (coveringMorphismProperty τ))
declarations.comment: the fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic cases

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_iff_of_fpqcCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02KW.** Universal injectivity is fpqc local on the base: for an fpqc
covering `𝒰` of `Y`, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is universally injective if and only if each base
change `𝒰.X i ×_Y X ⟶ 𝒰.X i` is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_iff_of_fpqcCover {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (𝒰 : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{w} Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage Y) :
    UniversallyInjective f ↔ ∀ i, UniversallyInjective (pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i))

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02L4.** Being an isomorphism is fpqc local on the base: for every fpqc
covering `{Yᵢ ⟶ Y}` and every morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, the morphism `f` is an
isomorphism if and only if each base change `Yᵢ ×_Y X ⟶ Yᵢ` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
instance isomorphisms_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (MorphismProperty.isomorphisms Scheme.{u}).IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02L9**, the descent step. Integral morphisms satisfy fpqc descent: if
the base change of `g` along a surjective flat quasi-compact morphism is integral, then so is
`g`.

Integrality is universal closedness together with affineness
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegralHom.eq_universallyClosed_inf_isAffineHom`), and both factors
descend along surjective flat quasi-compact morphisms, the second by Tag 02L5.

    MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong (@IsIntegralHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact)

the fpqc topology.

A finite morphism is an integral morphism which is locally of finite type, integrality is
universal closedness together with affineness, and of those three constituents only affineness
was missing; it is Tag 02L5, `Stacks.Descent.isAffineHom_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc`. So this is
`Stacks.Morphisms.isFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc_of_isAffineHom` with its hypothesis
discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@IsFinite.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
An *étale neighbourhood* of a scheme `S` at a point `s` is a scheme which is étale over `S`,
together with a distinguished point lying over `s`.
declarations.statement: structure EtaleNeighborhood (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleNeighborhood.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of étale neighbourhoods of `(S, s)` is a morphism of schemes over `S` which
carries the distinguished point to the distinguished point.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (U V : EtaleNeighborhood S s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleNeighborhood.IsElementary
declarations.doc:
An étale neighbourhood is *elementary* if the induced extension of residue fields is
trivial.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsElementary (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_residueField_algEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LF.** Every finite separable extension of the
residue field at a point is realized by the residue field at the chosen point
of an étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_residueField_algEquiv
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S) (k : Type v) [Field k]
    [Algebra (S.residueField s) k]
    [Module.Finite (S.residueField s) k]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField s) k] :
    ∃ U : EtaleNeighborhood S s,
      letI := U.residueFieldMap.hom.toAlgebra
      Nonempty (U.scheme.residueField U.point ≃ₐ[S.residueField s] k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topologies.Etale.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_surjective_locally_lift_etaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LG.** After restricting the base to an affine open neighbourhood of
the point, an étale neighbourhood is locally dominated, at every point above the distinguished
point, by a surjective finite locally free morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_surjective_locally_lift_etaleNeighborhood
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {s : S} (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) :
    ∃ (V : S.affineOpens) (hs : s ∈ V.1) (T : Scheme.{u}) (π : T ⟶ V.1)
      (_ : Surjective π) (_ : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree π),
      ∀ (t : T) (_ : π t = ⟨s, hs⟩),
        ∃ (W : T.Opens) (ht : t ∈ W) (h : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ U.scheme),
          W.ι ≫ π ≫ V.1.ι = h ≫ U.toBase ∧ h ⟨t, ht⟩ = U.point

declarations.name: Stacks.Topologies.Etale.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_surjective_finite_openCover_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LH.** A surjective étale morphism of affine schemes is dominated
by a surjective finite locally free morphism whose source has a finite open covering lifting
to the given étale cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_surjective_finite_openCover_lift
    {U S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine U] [IsAffine S] (f : U ⟶ S) [Etale f] [Surjective f] :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (p : T ⟶ S),
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree p ∧ Surjective p ∧
        ∃ 𝒯 : T.OpenCover.{u}, Finite 𝒯.I₀ ∧
          ∃ g : ∀ i, 𝒯.X i ⟶ U, ∀ i, 𝒯.f i ≫ p = g i ≫ f

declarations.name: Stacks.Topologies.Etale.exists_zariski_finiteLocallyFree_refinement
declarations.doc:
An étale covering is refined, after a Zariski covering of the base, by Zariski coverings of
schemes which are finite locally free and surjective over the corresponding members of the base
covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_zariski_finiteLocallyFree_refinement {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} S) (hE : E.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.etalePrecoverage S) :
    ∃ (V : S.OpenCover.{u}) (W : V.I₀ → Scheme.{u}) (p : ∀ j, W j ⟶ V.X j),
      (∀ j, Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree (p j)) ∧
        (∀ j, Surjective (p j)) ∧
          ∃ U : ∀ j, (W j).OpenCover.{u},
            Nonempty
              ((V.toPreZeroHypercover.bind fun j ↦
                (U j).toPreZeroHypercover.pushforward (p j)).Hom E)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_hasPullback
registrations.comment: the cartesian square X_U = U ×_S X of the basic diagram

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.exists_etaleNeighborhood_finiteAt
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism becomes finite near a point isolated in its fibre after an
elementary étale base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_finiteAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (hx : IsIsolatedPoint (f.asFiber x)) :
    Nonempty (FiniteNeighborhoodAt f x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.isFiniteNeighborhoodAt_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The pullback of a finite neighbourhood along any further elementary étale neighbourhood is
again a finite neighbourhood: finite over the new base, with a unique distinguished-fibre point
having the same residue field as the original point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteNeighborhoodAt_baseChange {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (U : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x))
    (V : (pullback f U.toBase).Opens) (hV : IsFiniteNeighborhoodAt f x U V)
    (U' : EtaleNeighborhood U.scheme U.point) (hU' : U'.IsElementary) :
    IsFiniteNeighborhoodAt f x
      { scheme := U'.scheme
        point := U'.point
        toBase := U'.toBase ≫ U.toBase
        map_point := by simp [U'.map_point, U.map_point] }
      ((pullback.map f (U'.toBase ≫ U.toBase) f U.toBase
        (𝟙 X) U'.toBase (𝟙 S) (by simp) (by simp)) ⁻¹ᵁ V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.exists_etaleNeighborhood_finite_opens_of_isolated_fiber_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LL.** Several isolated points of one fibre can simultaneously be
made finite over a single elementary étale neighbourhood of the base point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_finite_opens_of_isolated_fiber_points
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s)
    (hx_isolated : ∀ i, IsIsolatedPoint (f.asFiber (x i))) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (_ : U.IsElementary)
      (V : Fin n → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens)
      (v : ∀ i, V i),
      (∀ i, IsFinite ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)) ∧
      (∀ i, {y : V i | ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point} = {v i}) ∧
      (∀ i, ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) (v i) = x i) ∧
      (∀ i, IsIso (((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase).residueFieldMap (v i)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_finite_opens_of_isolated_fiber_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LL.** Several isolated points in one fibre can
simultaneously be made finite over an elementary étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_finite_opens_of_isolated_fiber_points
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s)
    (hx_isolated : ∀ i, IsIsolatedPoint (f.asFiber (x i))) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (_ : U.IsElementary)
      (V : Fin n → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens)
      (v : ∀ i, V i),
      (∀ i, IsFinite ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)) ∧
      (∀ i, {y : V i | ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point} = {v i}) ∧
      (∀ i, ((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) (v i) = x i) ∧
      (∀ i, IsIso (((V i).ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase).residueFieldMap (v i)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_finite_opens_of_isolated_fiber_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LM.** Finitely many distinct isolated points of a fibre of a morphism
locally of finite type have, after a single étale base change, finite open neighbourhoods meeting
the distinguished fibre in exactly one point, with finite purely inseparable residue extension,
and these points exhaust the base change of the chosen points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_finite_opens_of_isolated_fiber_points
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (n : ℕ) (s : S) (x : Fin n → X) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s)
    (hx_injective : Function.Injective x)
    (hx_isolated : ∀ i, IsIsolatedPoint (f.asFiber (x i))) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s)
      (m : Fin n → ℕ)
      (V : ∀ i, Fin (m i) → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens)
      (v : ∀ i j, V i j),
      (∀ i j,
        let g := (V i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase
        IsFinite g ∧
          g ⁻¹' {U.point} = {v i j} ∧
          ((V i j).ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) (v i j) = x i ∧
          ∃ hvu : g (v i j) = U.point,
            RingHom.Finite (((U.scheme.residueFieldCongr hvu).inv ≫
              g.residueFieldMap (v i j)).hom) ∧
            ((U.scheme.residueFieldCongr hvu).inv ≫
              g.residueFieldMap (v i j)).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) ∧
      Function.Injective (fun p : Σ i, Fin (m i) ↦ (V p.1 p.2).ι (v p.1 p.2)) ∧
      (∀ i (y : ↥(pullback f U.toBase)),
        (pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point →
        (pullback.fst f U.toBase) y = x i →
        ∃ j, (V i j).ι (v i j) = y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.exists_etaleNeighborhood_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LN.** Finitely many distinct isolated points of a fibre of a
separated morphism locally of finite type split into separate finite open-and-closed pieces
after an elementary étale base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_decomposition
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f]
    (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s)
    (hx_injective : Function.Injective x)
    (hx_isolated : ∀ i, IsOpen {f.asFiber (x i)}) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (_ : U.IsElementary)
      (P : Option (Fin n) → Scheme.{u})
      (j : ∀ a, P a ⟶ pullback f U.toBase)
      (_ : ∀ a, IsOpenImmersion (j a))
      (_ : ∀ a, IsClosedImmersion (j a))
      (_ : IsIso (Sigma.desc j))
      (v : ∀ i, P (some i))
      (_ : ∀ i, IsFinite (j (some i) ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)),
      (∀ i, (j (some i) ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) (v i) = x i) ∧
      (∀ i, {y : P (some i) |
          (j (some i) ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point} = {v i}) ∧
      (∀ i, IsIso ((j (some i) ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase).residueFieldMap (v i))) ∧
      (∀ y : P none,
        (j none ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point →
          ∀ i, (j none ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) y ≠ x i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LN.** Finitely many distinct isolated points of a
fibre of a separated morphism locally of finite type split into separate finite
open-and-closed pieces after an elementary étale base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_decomposition
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f]
    (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s)
    (hx_injective : Function.Injective x)
    (hx_isolated : ∀ i, IsOpen {f.asFiber (x i)}) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (_ : U.IsElementary)
      (P : Option (Fin n) → Scheme.{u})
      (j : ∀ a, P a ⟶ pullback f U.toBase)
      (_ : ∀ a, IsOpenImmersion (j a))
      (_ : ∀ a, IsClosedImmersion (j a))
      (_ : IsIso (Sigma.desc j))
      (v : ∀ i, P (some i))
      (_ : ∀ i, IsFinite (j (some i) ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)),
      (∀ i, (j (some i) ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) (v i) = x i) ∧
      (∀ i, {y : P (some i) |
          (j (some i) ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point} = {v i}) ∧
      (∀ i, IsIso ((j (some i) ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase).residueFieldMap (v i))) ∧
      (∀ y : P none,
        (j none ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point →
          ∀ i, (j none ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) y ≠ x i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_purelyInseparable_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LO.** Finitely many pairwise distinct isolated points of a fibre of
a separated morphism locally of finite type split into finite open-and-closed pieces after an
étale base change.  Each distinguished piece has singleton fibre and purely inseparable
residue-field extension, and the residual piece contains none of the specified points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_purelyInseparable_decomposition
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f]
    (n : ℕ) (s : S) (x : Fin n → f.fiber s) (hx : Function.Injective x)
    (hxi : ∀ i, IsIsolatedPoint (x i)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s)
      (m : Fin n → ℕ)
      (D : Option (Σ i, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens)
      (v : ∀ i j, D (some ⟨i, j⟩)),
      Set.PairwiseDisjoint Set.univ (fun k ↦ (D k).1) ∧
      (⋃ k, (D k).1) = Set.univ ∧
      (∀ k, IsClopen (D k).1) ∧
      (∀ i j,
        let V := D (some ⟨i, j⟩)
        let g := V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase
        IsFinite g ∧
          g ⁻¹' {U.point} = {v i j} ∧
          (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) (v i j) = f.fiberι s (x i) ∧
          ∃ hvu : g (v i j) = U.point,
            ((U.scheme.residueFieldCongr hvu).inv ≫
              g.residueFieldMap (v i j)).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) ∧
      (∀ w : D none,
        ((D none).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) w = U.point →
          ∀ i, ((D none).ι ≫ pullback.fst f U.toBase) w ≠ f.fiberι s (x i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_isCompl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LP.** After an elementary étale base change, the isolated
part of a fibre of a separated morphism locally of finite type splits off as a finite
open-and-closed subscheme.  The complementary fibre has no isolated points and is empty
when the original set-theoretic fibre is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_isCompl
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f] (s : S)
    (hfinite : {x : f.fiber s | IsIsolatedPoint x}.Finite) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s),
      U.IsElementary ∧
      ∃ (W V : (pullback f U.toBase).Opens),
        IsCompl W V ∧
        IsFinite (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) ∧
        (∀ x : (W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point,
          ¬ IsIsolatedPoint x) ∧
        ((f ⁻¹' {s}).Finite →
          IsEmpty ((W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtale_isCompl_not_quasiFiniteAt_of_finite_isolatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LP**, the main assertion. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated and locally of
finite type and let `s : S` be such that the fibre `X_s` has only finitely many isolated points,
i.e. only finitely many points of `X` over `s` at which `f` is quasi-finite. Then there is an
elementary étale neighbourhood `(U, u)` of `s` — an étale `g : U ⟶ S` with `g u = s` inducing an
isomorphism of residue fields — and a decomposition of `U ×_S X` into two complementary
open-and-closed pieces `V` and `W` such that `V ⟶ U` is finite and the fibre `W_u` contains no
isolated point, i.e. the second projection is quasi-finite at no point of `W` over `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtale_isCompl_not_quasiFiniteAt_of_finite_isolatedPoints
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f] {s : S}
    (hfin : {x : X | f.base x = s ∧ f.QuasiFiniteAt x}.Finite) :
    ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ S) (u : U), Etale g ∧ g.base u = s ∧
        IsIso (g.residueFieldMap u) ∧
      ∃ V W : (pullback f g).Opens, IsCompl V W ∧
        IsFinite (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) ∧
        ∀ w : W, (pullback.snd f g).base (W.ι.base w) = u →
          ¬ (pullback.snd f g).QuasiFiniteAt (W.ι.base w)
declarations.comment: the main assertion: `V ⟶ U` is finite and `W_u` has no isolated point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtale_isCompl_isEmpty_fiber_of_finite_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LP**, the final assertion. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated and locally of
finite type with finite fibre over `s : S`. Then there is an elementary étale neighbourhood
`(U, u)` of `s` and a decomposition of `U ×_S X` into two complementary open-and-closed pieces `V`
and `W` such that `V ⟶ U` is finite and `W` has no point over `u` at all.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtale_isCompl_isEmpty_fiber_of_finite_fiber {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f] {s : S}
    (hfin : (f.base ⁻¹' {s}).Finite) :
    ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ S) (u : U), Etale g ∧ g.base u = s ∧
        IsIso (g.residueFieldMap u) ∧
      ∃ V W : (pullback f g).Opens, IsCompl V W ∧
        IsFinite (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) ∧
        ∀ w : W, (pullback.snd f g).base (W.ι.base w) ≠ u
declarations.comment: the final assertion: `W_u = ∅` when the fibre over `s` is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_toNormalization_and_isIntegralHom_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LR, the factorization.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a separated quasi-finite
morphism of schemes. Then the morphism from `X` to the normalization of `S` in `X` is a
quasi-compact open immersion, and the normalization is integral over `S`.

Both clauses are Mathlib instances; the open immersion is Mathlib's form of Stacks 03GW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_toNormalization_and_isIntegralHom_fromNormalization [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsOpenImmersion f.toNormalization ∧ QuasiCompact f.toNormalization ∧
      IsIntegralHom f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LR, quasi-affineness.** A separated quasi-finite morphism of schemes
is quasi-affine.

It factors as the morphism to the normalization of the target in the source, which is a
quasi-compact open immersion and hence quasi-affine, followed by the normalization, which is
integral and hence affine and hence quasi-affine; quasi-affine morphisms are stable under
composition by Stacks 01SN.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_of_locallyQuasiFinite [IsSeparated f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : IsQuasiAffineHom f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_inf_quasiFinite_le_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02LR** as a containment of morphism properties: the separated
quasi-finite morphisms of schemes — separated, locally quasi-finite, locally of finite type and
quasi-compact — are quasi-affine.

This is the shape in which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isSeparated_inf_quasiFinite`
takes Stacks 02LR as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_inf_quasiFinite_le_isQuasiAffineHom :
    (@IsSeparated.{u} ⊓ @LocallyQuasiFinite ⊓ @LocallyOfFiniteType ⊓ @QuasiCompact :
        MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ≤ @IsQuasiAffineHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.tfae_isProper_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` the following are equivalent: `f` is finite; `f` is
proper with finite fibres; `f` is proper and locally quasi-finite; `f` is universally closed,
separated, locally of finite type and has finite fibres. The fibre over `s` is its underlying set
`f ⁻¹' {s}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFinite.tfae_isProper_locallyQuasiFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsFinite f,
        IsProper f ∧ ∀ s : S, (f ⁻¹' {s}).Finite,
        IsProper f ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite f,
        UniversallyClosed f ∧ IsSeparated f ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧
          ∀ s : S, (f ⁻¹' {s}).Finite]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_iff_isProper_and_forall_finite_preimage_singleton
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02LS], condition (1) ⟺ condition (2).** A morphism of schemes is finite
exactly when it is proper and all of its fibres are finite.

The source's properness is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, which contains
`AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed` and hence `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact`, so no further
hypothesis is needed to pass between finiteness of the fibres and local quasi-finiteness.
declarations.comment: condition (1) <=> condition (2): a morphism of schemes is finite exactly when it is proper with finite fibres. PROVED outright, with no hypothesis beyond the two sides of the equivalence: Mathlib's IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_locallyQuasiFinite is the tag's own (1) <=> (3), and locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton turns local quasi-finiteness into finiteness of the fibres. Properness in Mathlib's sense contains universal closedness and therefore quasi-compactness, so the source's finite-type requirement is met.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_iff_isSeparated_universallyClosed_locallyOfFiniteType_and_finite_fibres
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02LS], condition (1) ⟺ condition (4).** A morphism of schemes is finite
exactly when it is separated, universally closed, locally of finite type and has finite fibres.
This is the previous equivalence with `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper` unfolded into its three
parents.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_iff_isSeparated_universallyClosed_locallyOfFiniteType_and_finite_fibres
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsFinite f ↔ (IsSeparated f ∧ UniversallyClosed f ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType f) ∧
      ∀ s : S, (f ⁻¹' {s}).Finite
declarations.comment: condition (1) <=> condition (4): a morphism of schemes is finite exactly when it is separated, universally closed, locally of finite type and has finite fibres. PROVED outright from condition (1) <=> condition (2) by unfolding Mathlib's IsProper into its three parents.

declarations.name: fractionRing_equiv_fractionRing_localization
declarations.doc:
The total ring of fractions of `R` is isomorphic (as a ring) to the total ring of fractions of
`S⁻¹R`, whenever `S` is a multiplicative subset of `R` consisting of nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem fractionRing_equiv_fractionRing_localization
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R) (hS : S ≤ nonZeroDivisors R) :
    Nonempty (FractionRing R ≃+* FractionRing (Localization S))

declarations.name: fractionRing_equiv_fractionRing_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
The total ring of fractions of `R` is isomorphic to the total ring of fractions of its own
total ring of fractions: `Q(R) ≅ Q(Q(R))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fractionRing_equiv_fractionRing_fractionRing
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    Nonempty (FractionRing R ≃+* FractionRing (FractionRing R))

declarations.name: total_fraction_ring_isoProd_localization_atPrime
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring whose set of minimal primes is finite and enumerated without
repetition as `q_1, ..., q_t` (encoded by an injective family `q : Fin t → Ideal R` of minimal
primes; the zerodivisor hypothesis forces it to enumerate every minimal prime). Assume moreover
that the union of the minimal primes equals the set of zerodivisors of `R`. Then the total ring of
fractions `Q(R) = FractionRing R` is isomorphic, as an `R`-algebra, to the finite product of the
localizations `R_{q_i}`.

(An `R`-algebra isomorphism between these localizations is automatically the canonical map
induced by the universal property, since it must commute with the structure maps from `R`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem total_fraction_ring_isoProd_localization_atPrime
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (t : ℕ) (q : Fin t → Ideal R)
    (hmin : ∀ i, q i ∈ minimalPrimes R)
    (hinj : Function.Injective q)
    (hzd : zeroDivisorsSet R = ⋃ i, (q i : Set R)) :
    haveI : ∀ i, (q i).IsPrime := fun i => (hmin i).isPrime
    Nonempty (FractionRing R ≃ₐ[R] (∀ i, Localization.AtPrime (q i)))

registrations.name: Module.length_eq_height
registrations.comment: as a supremum over chains of submodules

declarations.name: length_eq_sum_residue_degree_mul_localized_length
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02M0.** Length over a local ring `A` of a finite-length module
`M` over a semi-local `A`-algebra `B`, expressed as a sum over the (finitely
many) maximal ideals of `B` of the residue degrees times the lengths of the
localizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_eq_sum_residue_degree_mul_localized_length
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [Algebra A B]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
    (n : ℕ) (𝔪 : Fin n → Ideal B)
    -- `B` is semi-local with the `𝔪 i` being exactly its maximal ideals:
    (hmax : ∀ i, (𝔪 i).IsMaximal)
    (hinj : Function.Injective 𝔪)
    (hsurj : ∀ I : Ideal B, I.IsMaximal → ∃ i, 𝔪 i = I)
    -- each `𝔪 i` lies over the maximal ideal of `A`:
    (hlies : ∀ i, IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A = (𝔪 i).comap (algebraMap A B))
    -- `M` has finite length over `B`:
    (hM : IsFiniteLength B M) :
    -- introduce the residue-field algebra structures and the primality of the `𝔪 i`:
    letI : ∀ i, (𝔪 i).IsMaximal := hmax
    letI : ∀ i, Algebra (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).ResidueField (𝔪 i).ResidueField :=
      fun i => residueFieldAlgebra (𝔪 i) (hlies i)
    -- finiteness of residue degrees `[κ(𝔪 i) : κ(𝔪)] < ∞`:
    (∀ i, Module.Finite (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).ResidueField (𝔪 i).ResidueField) →
      -- `M` has finite length over `A`, and the length formula holds in `ℕ∞`:
      IsFiniteLength A M ∧
        Module.length A M
          = ∑ i : Fin n,
              (Module.finrank (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).ResidueField (𝔪 i).ResidueField : ℕ∞)
                * Module.length (Localization.AtPrime (𝔪 i))
                    (LocalizedModule (𝔪 i).primeCompl M)

declarations.name: length_baseChange_eq_length_mul_length_quotient
declarations.doc:
For a flat local homomorphism `A → B` of local rings and
every `A`-module `M`, the length of `M` over `A` times the length of `B / m_A B` over `B`
equals the length of the base change `B ⊗[A] M` over `B`, as an identity in `ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_baseChange_eq_length_mul_length_quotient
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A B]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    Module.length A M *
      Module.length B (B ⧸ extendedMaximalIdeal A B) =
      Module.length B (B ⊗[A] M)

declarations.name: finite_length_iff_finite_length_baseChange
declarations.doc:
For a flat local homomorphism `A → B` of local rings such that `B / m_A B` has finite length
over `B`, an `A`-module `M` has finite length over `A` if and only if its base change `B ⊗[A] M`
has finite length over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_length_iff_finite_length_baseChange
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A B]
    (hfin : Module.length B (B ⧸ extendedMaximalIdeal A B) < ⊤)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    Module.length A M < ⊤ ↔ Module.length B (B ⊗[A] M) < ⊤

declarations.name: length_quotient_maximalIdeal_map_mul_eq
declarations.doc:
For flat local homomorphisms of local rings `f : A → B` and
`g : B → C`, the length of `B / m_A B` over `B` times the length of `C / m_B C`
over `C` equals the length of `C / m_A C` over `C`, where `m_A C` is the extension
of `m_A` along the composite `A → C`. The equality holds in `ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quotient_maximalIdeal_map_mul_eq
    (_hf_local : IsLocalHom f) (hg_local : IsLocalHom g)
    (_hf_flat : f.Flat) (hg_flat : g.Flat) :
    Module.length B (B ⧸ Ideal.map f (maximalIdeal A)) *
        Module.length C (C ⧸ Ideal.map g (maximalIdeal B))
      = Module.length C (C ⧸ Ideal.map (g.comp f) (maximalIdeal A))

declarations.name: assStacks_subset_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02M3, first inclusion.** Let `0 → X → Y → Z → 0` be a short exact sequence of modules
over a commutative ring `S`. Then `Ass(X) ⊆ Ass(Y)`, where `Ass = assStacks` is the set of primes
that are the annihilator of an element (Stacks 00LA). Mathlib's `associatedPrimes` asks instead that
a prime be the radical of such an annihilator, which is the same notion over a Noetherian ring;
the statement here is for `assStacks` and for an arbitrary ring.
declarations.comment: (1) Ass(M') ⊆ Ass(M) for a short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 over any commutative ring, with Ass the set of primes equal to the annihilator of an element (00LA)

declarations.name: assStacks_subset_union_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02M3, second inclusion.** Let `0 → X → Y → Z → 0` be a short exact sequence of
modules over a commutative ring `S`. Then `Ass(Y) ⊆ Ass(X) ∪ Ass(Z)`, where `Ass = assStacks` is
the set of primes that are the annihilator of an element (Stacks 00LA). Mathlib's
`associatedPrimes` asks instead that a prime be the radical of such an annihilator, which is the
same notion over a Noetherian ring; the statement here is for `assStacks` and for an arbitrary
ring.
declarations.comment: (2) Ass(M) ⊆ Ass(M') ∪ Ass(M'') for a short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 over any commutative ring, with Ass the set of primes equal to the annihilator of an element (00LA)

declarations.name: assStacks_prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02M3, direct sum.** For modules `X` and `Z` over a commutative ring `S`,
`Ass(X ⊕ Z) = Ass(X) ∪ Ass(Z)`, where `Ass = assStacks` is the set of primes that are the
annihilator of an element (Stacks 00LA) and the direct sum is the product `X × Z`. Mathlib's
`associatedPrimes` asks instead that a prime be the radical of such an annihilator, which is the
same notion over a Noetherian ring; the statement here is for `assStacks` and for an arbitrary
ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.assStacks_prod :
    _root_.assStacks S (X × Z) = _root_.assStacks S X ∪ _root_.assStacks S Z
declarations.comment: (3) Ass(M' ⊕ M'') = Ass(M') ∪ Ass(M'') over any commutative ring, the direct sum being the product M' × M'' and Ass the set of primes equal to the annihilator of an element (00LA)

declarations.name: IsEmbeddedAssociatedPrimeStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02M5 (1).** Let `R` be a ring and `M` an `R`-module. A prime `𝔭` is an
*embedded associated prime of `M`* if it is an associated prime of `M` (Stacks 00LA: `𝔭` is
exactly the annihilator of some element of `M`) which is not minimal among the associated
primes of `M`.
declarations.statement:
def IsEmbeddedAssociatedPrimeStacks
    (R M : Type*) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (𝔭 : Ideal R) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1) embedded associated primes of a module

declarations.name: IsEmbeddedPrimeStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02M5 (2).** The *embedded primes of a ring* `R` are the embedded associated
primes of `R` regarded as a module over itself.
declarations.statement: def IsEmbeddedPrimeStacks (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (𝔭 : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: Module.exists_isGreatest_isNowhereDense_support
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `M` a finite `R`-module. The set of `R`-submodules
`K ⊆ M` whose support is nowhere dense in `Supp(M)` has a largest element `K`, and the
quotient `M' = M / K` satisfies: (1) `Supp(M) = Supp(M')`; (2) every associated prime of `M'`
is minimal among the associated primes of `M'`, that is, `M'` has no embedded associated
primes; (3) for every `f ∈ R` lying in all embedded associated primes of `M`, the localization
of `M → M'` at the powers of `f` is bijective, so `M_f ≅ M'_f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isGreatest_isNowhereDense_support :
    ∃ K : Submodule R M,
      IsGreatest {K : Submodule R M |
          IsNowhereDense (Subtype.val ⁻¹' support R ↥K : Set ↥(support R M))} K ∧
        support R (M ⧸ K) = support R M ∧
        (∀ p ∈ associatedPrimes R (M ⧸ K), Minimal (· ∈ associatedPrimes R (M ⧸ K)) p) ∧
        ∀ f : R, (∀ p ∈ associatedPrimes R M, ¬ Minimal (· ∈ associatedPrimes R M) p → f ∈ p) →
          Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) K.mkQ)

declarations.name: Module.isGreatest_isNowhereDense_support_localized'
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `M` a finite `R`-module, and let `K ⊆ M` be the largest
`R`-submodule whose support is nowhere dense in `Supp(M)`, as produced by
`Module.exists_isGreatest_isNowhereDense_support`. Let `Rₚ` be the localization of `R` at a
submonoid `p` and `g : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ` the localization of `M` at `p`. Then the localized submodule
`Kₚ ⊆ Mₚ` is the largest `Rₚ`-submodule of `Mₚ` whose support is nowhere dense in `Supp(Mₚ)`.
Since `(M ⧸ K)ₚ = Mₚ ⧸ Kₚ`, this says that removing the embedded associated primes commutes
with localization: `(M')ₚ = (Mₚ)'`.

declarations.name: hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes_quotient_annihilator
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 02M8).** Let `R` be a Noetherian commutative ring and
`M` a finite `R`-module having no embedded associated primes. Let `I` be the
annihilator of `M`. Then `R ⧸ I`, viewed as a module over itself, has no embedded
associated primes (i.e. the ring `R ⧸ I` has no embedded primes, in the sense of
`HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes_quotient_annihilator
    (R M : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (hM : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes R M) :
    HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M)

declarations.name: Module.free_of_flat_of_preconnectedSpace
declarations.doc:
**A finite locally free module over a semi-local ring with connected spectrum is free.**
Let `R` be a semi-local ring, so with finitely many maximal ideals, whose spectrum is
(pre)connected, and let `M` be a finite locally free `R`-module, spelled here as finitely
presented and flat. Then `M` is free. The rank of `M` is a locally constant function on
`Spec(R)`, hence constant, and a finite locally free module of constant rank over a semi-local
ring is free (`Module.free_of_flat_of_finrank_eq`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.free_of_flat_of_preconnectedSpace (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum R)] [PreconnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M] [Module.Flat R M] :
    Module.Free R M
declarations.comment: The second assertion; the first, for a module of constant rank, is Mathlib's `Module.free_of_flat_of_finrank_eq`.

declarations.name: Ideal.primesOver_finite_and_forall_height_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Generically finite maps are quasi-finite in codimension one.**
Let `A ⊆ B` be an extension of domains with `A` Noetherian, `B` algebraic and of finite type over
`A`, and let `p` be a prime of `A` of height one. Then only finitely many primes of `B` lie over
`p`, and each of them has height one. Algebraicity of `B` over `A` is, under the finite type
hypothesis, finiteness of the induced extension of fraction fields.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.primesOver_finite_and_forall_height_eq_one {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B]
    [Algebra A B] [FaithfulSMul A B] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (hp : p.height = 1) :
    (p.primesOver B).Finite ∧ ∀ q ∈ p.primesOver B, q.height = 1
declarations.comment:
Finiteness of the induced extension of fraction fields is stated as
`Algebra.IsAlgebraic A B`, to which it is equivalent for `B` of finite type over `A`; see the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.length_quotient_span_mul_eq_add_and_ne_top
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring of Krull dimension at most one and `a`, `b ∈ R` nonzerodivisors.
Then `length_R(R/(ab)) = length_R(R/(a)) + length_R(R/(b))`, and these three lengths are
finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.length_quotient_span_mul_eq_add_and_ne_top [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R] {a b : R} (ha : a ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    (hb : b ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) :
    Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a * b}) =
        Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a}) + Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {b}) ∧
      Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a * b}) ≠ ⊤ ∧
      Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a}) ≠ ⊤ ∧ Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {b}) ≠ ⊤
declarations.comment:
Semi-locality is dropped, being used by neither assertion, and dimension `1` is
weakened to dimension at most `1` (`Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R`). The additivity is the case `M = R` of
`Module.length_quotSMulTop_mul`, which holds for any module and `b` acting injectively, with no
hypothesis on `R`; the finiteness is Mathlib's `isFiniteLength_quotient_span_singleton` (Stacks
00PF for `M = R`).
