affine open of the target is equivalent to the generic point of the source being the only point
above the generic point of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_isFinite_restrict_iff_eq_genericPoint
    (hsep_or_qc : IsSeparated f ∨ QuasiCompact f) :
    (∃ V : Y.affineOpens, (V.1 : Set Y).Nonempty ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ V.1)) ↔
      (∀ x : X, f x = genericPoint Y → x = genericPoint X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.trdeg_functionField_eq_zero_of_eq_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NX, the implication to condition (1).** If the generic point of the
source is the only point above the generic point of the target, then the induced extension of
function fields has transcendence degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem trdeg_functionField_eq_zero_of_eq_genericPoint
    (h : ∀ x : X, f x = genericPoint Y → x = genericPoint X) :
    letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    Algebra.trdeg Y.functionField X.functionField = 0
declarations.comment:
the implication from condition (4) -- equivalently (3), or (5) -- to condition
(1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.trdeg_functionField_eq_zero_iff_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NX, conditions (1) and (2).** For a dominant morphism locally of
finite type between integral schemes, the extension of function fields `R(Y) ⊆ R(X)` has
transcendence degree zero exactly when it is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem trdeg_functionField_eq_zero_iff_finite :
    letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    Algebra.trdeg Y.functionField X.functionField = 0 ↔
      Module.Finite Y.functionField X.functionField
declarations.comment:
conditions (1) and (2): the extension of function fields has transcendence degree
zero if and only if it is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_genericPoint_of_trdeg_functionField_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NX, the implication from condition (1) to condition (4).** If the
extension of function fields has transcendence degree zero, then the generic point of the source
is the only point above the generic point of the target: on a pair of affine opens the point in
question cuts out a prime contracting to the zero ideal, and over an algebraic extension of
fraction fields such a prime is zero, which is the prime cut out by the generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_genericPoint_of_trdeg_functionField_eq_zero
    (h : letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField :=
        (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
      Algebra.trdeg Y.functionField X.functionField = 0) :
    ∀ x : X, f x = genericPoint Y → x = genericPoint X
declarations.comment: the implication from condition (1) to condition (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tfae_trdeg_functionField_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NX, conditions (1)–(4).** For a dominant morphism locally of finite
type between integral schemes the following are equivalent: the extension of function fields
`R(Y) ⊆ R(X)` has transcendence degree zero; that extension is finite; `f` is finite on some
pair of nonempty affine opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ Y` with `f(U) ⊆ V`; the generic point of `X` is the
only point of `X` above the generic point of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_trdeg_functionField_eq_zero :
    letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    List.TFAE
      [Algebra.trdeg Y.functionField X.functionField = 0,
        Module.Finite Y.functionField X.functionField,
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
          (U.1 : Set X).Nonempty ∧ (V.1 : Set Y).Nonempty ∧ IsFinite (f.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV),
        ∀ x : X, f x = genericPoint Y → x = genericPoint X]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.degreeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NY.** The *degree of `X` over `Y`* for a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
integral schemes which is locally of finite type and dominant: the degree
`deg(X/Y) = [R(X) : R(Y)]` of the extension of function fields induced by `f`.

This is a positive integer whenever that extension is finite, which is the case the source
defines it in; see `AlgebraicGeometry.degreeOver_pos`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degreeOver (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsDominant f] : ℕ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_functionField_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NZ.** The degree of a tower of dominant morphisms of integral
schemes is the product of the two degrees: if the function field of `X` is finite over that of
`Y` and the function field of `Y` is finite over that of `Z`, then
`[R(X) : R(Z)] = [R(X) : R(Y)] * [R(Y) : R(Z)]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_functionField_comp
    [FiniteDimensional Y.functionField X.functionField]
    [FiniteDimensional Z.functionField Y.functionField]
    (hf : algebraMap Y.functionField X.functionField = dominantFunctionFieldMap f)
    (hg : algebraMap Z.functionField Y.functionField = dominantFunctionFieldMap g)
    (hfg : algebraMap Z.functionField X.functionField = dominantFunctionFieldMap (f ≫ g)) :
    Module.finrank Z.functionField X.functionField =
      Module.finrank Y.functionField X.functionField *
        Module.finrank Z.functionField Y.functionField

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AmpleTwistAcyclicity.exists_isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_tensorPowModule
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02O1], with no hypothesis.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism of schemes
with `S` Noetherian, let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module ample relative to `f`. Then there is an `n₀` such that for all `n ≥ n₀`,

`R ᵖ f_* (ℱ ⊗ ℒ ^⊗ n) = 0` for every `p > 0`,

with the **one** bound `n₀` serving every positive degree.

This is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeAmpleTwistVanishing`
`.exists_isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_tensorPowModule` with its hypothesis `haffine`
discharged by `vanishingOverAffineBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_tensorPowModule {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] [IsProper f] (F L : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n p : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → 0 < p →
      IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedPlus (p : ℤ)).obj
        (tensorModules X F (tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyProjectiveCoherentImage.isCoherent_rightDerived_of_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02O4].** For `S` locally Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ S` locally H-projective and `ℱ`
a coherent `𝒪_X`-module, the higher direct image `R^i f_* ℱ` is coherent for every `i ≥ 0`.

Local H-projectivity supplies an open cover of `S` over whose members `f` is H-projective — the
definition states this for `pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i)`, which is isomorphic as an arrow to
`f ∣_ (𝒰.f i).opensRange` — and coherence of a higher direct image is local on the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_rightDerived_of_isLocallyProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hf : IsLocallyProjectiveMorphism f) (F : X.Modules)
    (hF : F.IsCoherent) (i : ℕ) :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F).IsCoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.higherDirectImageIsCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Coherence of higher direct images.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be proper and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then `R ⁱ f_* F` is a coherent
`𝒪_S`-module for every `i ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement: theorem higherDirectImageIsCoherent : HigherDirectImageIsCoherent.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.isCoherent_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Coherence of the direct image.** For `f : X ⟶ S` proper onto a locally Noetherian base and
`F` coherent, `f_* F` is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_pushforward {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsCoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.moduleFinite_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Finiteness of cohomology.** Let `S = Spec A` with `A` Noetherian, let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper
and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then `Hⁱ(X, F)` is a finite `A`-module for every `i ≥ 0`.
Here the base is an affine locally Noetherian scheme and `A` is its ring of global sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_cohomology {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [IsAffine S]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (i : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite Γ(S, ⊤) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f.appTop.hom).obj
      (((moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived i).obj F))

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.pushforwardReesGradedModule
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02O7]: the graded `⨁ₙ ℐⁿ`-module `⨁ₙ f_*(ℐⁿℱ)` on the base, in degree
zero.**  The maps `pushforwardReesSmul` make the pushforwards of the ideal-power multiples of
`ℱ` a graded module over the Rees algebra of `ℐ` on `Y`.

Since `f_*` is left exact it is `R ⁰ f_*`, so this is the structure the source puts on
`⨁ₙ R ᵖ f_*(ℐⁿℱ)` for `p = 0`.  Each axiom is the corresponding axiom of
`Stacks.Blowup.reesGradedModule` on `X`, transported along the multiplicativity and unitality of
`Stacks.Blowup.reesPieceComap`; the compatibility with restriction on `Y` is inherited from
`reesPieceComap` being a morphism of sheaves.
declarations.statement: public def pushforwardReesGradedModule : SheafOfModules.GradedModule (reesGradedAlgebra I)
declarations.comment: ⨁ₙ f_*(ℐⁿℱ) is a graded ⨁ₙ ℐⁿ-module on the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02O7]: the graded `⨁ₙ ℐⁿ`-module `⨁ₙ R ᵖ f_*(ℐⁿℱ)` on the base, in every
degree `p`.**  This is the structure the setup paragraph of the source obtains "by localizing and
then sheafifying": the maps `ℐⁱ ⊗_{𝒪_Y} R ᵖ f_*(ℐⁿℱ) ⟶ R ᵖ f_*(ℐⁿ⁺ⁱℱ)`, presented as the
biadditive maps on sections that `SheafOfModules.GradedModule` consumes, together with the four
laws.

`Stacks.Blowup.pushforwardReesGradedModule` is the same statement for `p = 0`, and is **not**
superseded by this one: there the action is the multiplication of the Rees algebra on sections,
by `rfl`, whereas here it divides by the higher direct image of the unit of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction`, and the two agree at `p = 0` only through
`R ⁰ f_* ≅ f_*`.
declarations.statement:
public def pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus (f : X ⟶ Y) (I : Y.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules)
    (p : ℕ) : SheafOfModules.GradedModule (reesGradedAlgebra I)
declarations.comment: ⨁ₙ R ᵖ f_*(ℐⁿℱ) is a graded ⨁ₙ ℐⁿ-module on the base, in every degree p

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.isCohomologyReesFinite
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02O8].** For `A` Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` proper and `ℱ` coherent, the
graded module `⨁_{n ≥ 0} Hᵖ(X, Iⁿℱ)` is a finite module over the Rees algebra
`B = ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Iⁿ`.

This is `Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.isCohomologyReesFinite_of_isCoherent`, the reduction
of the tag to [Stacks, Tag 0897] part (1) at a graded `⨁ₙ ℐⁿ`-module, with that hypothesis
supplied by `Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.isCohomologyReesFiniteOfGradedModule`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohomologyReesFinite [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : X.left.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (p : ℕ)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper X.hom) :
    IsCohomologyReesFinite I X F p

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType_pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02O9.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes, `ℱ` an `𝒪_X`-module
and `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Y` a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and assume `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` proper
and `ℱ` coherent. Then the graded `𝒜 = ⨁ₙ ℐⁿ`-module
`ℳ = ⨁ₙ R ᵖ f_*(ℐⁿℱ) = Stacks.Blowup.pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus f ℐ ℱ p`
is **quasi-coherent** — every homogeneous piece is — and **of finite type** over `𝒜`.

This is the source's own argument. Quasi-coherence of a piece is [Stacks, Tag 01XJ] applied to
`ℐⁿℱ`. Finite type is local on `Y`, and over an affine open `V` it is [Stacks, Tag 02O8] on the
chart `f⁻¹(V) ⟶ Spec Γ(Y, V)`, turned into the spanning family the affine criterion
`SheafOfModules.GradedModule.isFiniteType_of_affine_span` consumes by
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_affine_span_pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus`.

Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f` and quasi-coherence of `ℱ` are consequences of
the source's hypotheses and are derived, not assumed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType_pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] [F.IsCoherent] :
    (∀ n : ℤ, ((Stacks.Blowup.pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus f I F p).piece n).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      (Stacks.Blowup.pushforwardReesGradedModulePlus f I F p).IsFiniteType
        (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OA].** For `A` Noetherian, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` proper and
`ℱ` coherent there is one integer `c ≥ 0` such that

1. the multiplication map `Iʳ⁻ᶜ ⊗ Hᵖ(X, Iᶜℱ) → Hᵖ(X, Iʳℱ)` is surjective for `r ≥ c`;
2. the image of `Hᵖ(X, Iⁿ⁺ᵐℱ) → Hᵖ(X, Iⁿℱ)` is contained in `Iᵐ⁻ᵉHᵖ(X, Iⁿℱ)` with
   `e = max(0, c - n)`, whenever `n + m ≥ c` — and, in the shape where the target is `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)`
   itself rather than `Hᵖ(X, I⁰ℱ)`, the image of `Hᵖ(X, Iʳℱ) → Hᵖ(X, ℱ)` is contained in
   `Iʳ⁻ᶜHᵖ(X, ℱ)` for `r ≥ c`, which is the source's `n = 0`;
3. `Ker(Hᵖ(X, Iᵏℱ) → Hᵖ(X, ℱ)) = Ker(Hᵖ(X, Iᵏℱ) → Hᵖ(X, Iᵐℱ))` whenever `m + c ≤ k`, which is
   the source's part (3) in the case `m = k - c`;
4. there are `A`-linear maps `cmp : IⁿHᵖ(X, ℱ) → Hᵖ(X, Iⁿ⁻ᶜℱ)` for `n ≥ c` whose two
   composites with the canonical maps are canonical: `cmp` followed by
   `Hᵖ(X, Iⁿ⁻ᶜℱ) → Hᵖ(X, ℱ)` is the inclusion of `IⁿHᵖ(X, ℱ)` — which, read inside
   `Iⁿ⁻²ᶜHᵖ(X, ℱ)`, where the image of `Hᵖ(X, Iⁿ⁻ᶜℱ) → Hᵖ(X, ℱ)` lies by part (2), is the
   source's composite `IⁿHᵖ(X, ℱ) → Hᵖ(X, Iⁿ⁻ᶜℱ) → Iⁿ⁻²ᶜHᵖ(X, ℱ)` — and, for `n ≥ 2c`, the
   image under `cmp` of the class of `x ∈ Hᵖ(X, Iⁿℱ)` in `Iⁿ⁻ᶜHᵖ(X, ℱ)` (the hypothesis
   `(y : Hᵖ(X, ℱ)) = ...` below says that `y` is that class, which lies in `Iⁿ⁻ᶜHᵖ(X, ℱ)` by
   part (2)) is the canonical image of `x` in `Hᵖ(X, Iⁿ⁻²ᶜℱ)`;
5. the two inverse systems `(Hᵖ(X, Iⁿℱ))` and `(IⁿHᵖ(X, ℱ))` are pro-isomorphic, in the
   explicit up-to-refinement sense `InverseSequence.ProIso`.

Parts (1), (2) and (3) are the Artin-Rees argument for Rees systems,
`Stacks.RingTheory.ReesSystem.exists_uniform_bound_rees`, run on
`Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.cohomologyIdealPowerSystem`: its finiteness input is
[Stacks, Tag 02O8], `Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.isCohomologyReesFinite`, and its two
compatibility laws are `cohomologyIdealPowerSystem_isTrMulCompatible`. Parts (4) and (5) are
`Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.exists_comparison_cohomology`, whose hypotheses are those
three parts.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_of_isProper [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper X.hom) [F.IsCoherent] (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : ℕ,
      (∀ r : ℕ, c ≤ r → Function.Surjective
        ((cohomologyTr I X F p (show r ≤ r - c + c by omega)).comp
          (cohomologyMulTensor I X F p (r - c) c))) ∧
      (∀ n m : ℕ, c ≤ n + m →
        LinearMap.range (cohomologyTr I X F p (Nat.le_add_right n m)) ≤
          I ^ (m - (c - n)) • (⊤ : Submodule A (cohomologyIdealPower I X F p n))) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, c ≤ r → LinearMap.range (cohomologyProj I X F p r) ≤
        I ^ (r - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (cohomology X F p))) ∧
      (∀ (m k : ℕ) (hmk : m + c ≤ k),
        LinearMap.ker (cohomologyProj I X F p k) =
          LinearMap.ker (cohomologyTr I X F p
            (show m ≤ k from le_trans (Nat.le_add_right m c) hmk))) ∧
      (∃ cmp : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
          ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (cohomology X F p))) →ₗ[A]
            cohomologyIdealPower I X F p (n - c),
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : c ≤ n) (y : ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (cohomology X F p)))),
            cohomologyProj I X F p (n - c) (cmp n hn y) = (y : cohomology X F p)) ∧
          ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : c + c ≤ n) (x : cohomologyIdealPower I X F p n)
            (y : ↥(I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (cohomology X F p)))),
            (y : cohomology X F p) = cohomologyProj I X F p n x →
            cmp (n - c) (Nat.le_sub_of_add_le hn) y =
              cohomologyTr I X F p ((Nat.sub_le (n - c) c).trans (Nat.sub_le n c)) x) ∧
      Nonempty (InverseSequence.ProIso (cohomologyIdealPowerFunctor I X F p)
        (Stacks.RingTheory.idealPowerSmulSystem I (cohomology X F p)))
declarations.comment: all five parts, for a proper scheme over a Noetherian ring and a coherent module

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_idealPowerQuotient_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OB].** For `A` Noetherian, `J ⊆ A` an ideal, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` proper and
`ℱ` coherent there is a single `c ≥ 0` such that, with `𝓙 = J · 𝒪_X`:

1. `Ker(Hᵖ(X, ℱ) → Hᵖ(X, ℱ / 𝓙ⁿℱ)) ⊆ Jⁿ⁻ᶜHᵖ(X, ℱ)` for every `n ≥ c`;
2. the inverse system `n ↦ Hᵖ(X, ℱ / 𝓙ⁿℱ)` satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition;
3. for every `k ≥ n + c` the image of `Hᵖ(X, ℱ / 𝓙ᵏℱ)` in `Hᵖ(X, ℱ / 𝓙ⁿℱ)` equals the image of
   `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)`.

This is
`Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_idealPowerQuotient_of_02O8`
with its hypothesis, [Stacks, Tag 02O8] in general form, discharged by
`Stacks.FormalFunctions.isReesFinite_cohomologyIdealPowerSystem`. It is the only registration of
[Stacks, Tag 02OB]: the two statements it is assembled from,
`exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_idealPowerQuotient_of_02O8` and
`exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_idealPowerQuotient`, take [Stacks, Tag 02O8] and two clauses of
[Stacks, Tag 02OA] as inputs and carry no registration.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_idealPowerQuotient_of_isProper [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f) [G.IsCoherent] (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : ℕ,
      (∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
          LinearMap.ker (cohomologyOverBaseMap A f p
              (cokernel.π (C := X.Modules)
                (idealPowerMultiple (baseIdealSheaf A J f) n G).ι)).hom ≤
            J ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (cohomologyOverBase A f p G))) ∧
        IsMittagLefflerCategorical
          (adicQuotientSystem (baseIdealSheaf A J f) G ⋙
            (Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived p) ∧
        ∀ n k : ℕ, (hk : n + c ≤ k) →
          LinearMap.range
              (((Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived p).map
                (idealPowerQuotientDrop (baseIdealSheaf A J f)
                  ((Nat.le_add_right n c).trans hk) G)).hom =
            LinearMap.range
              (((Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived p).map
                (cokernel.π (C := X.Modules)
                  (idealPowerMultiple (baseIdealSheaf A J f) n G).ι)).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.exists_formalFunctionsEquiv_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OC].** For `A` Noetherian, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` proper and
`ℱ` coherent, the maps `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)/IⁿHᵖ(X, ℱ) → Hᵖ(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)` assemble into an isomorphism

  `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧_I ≅ limₙ Hᵖ(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)`

of `A`-modules, and that isomorphism is a homeomorphism for the limit topologies.

The second component says that the `n`-th projection of the isomorphism carries the image of a
class `x ∈ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)` to the image of `x` in `Hᵖ(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)`, so the isomorphism is the one the
source's system of maps defines and not merely some isomorphism between the two modules. The
third is the source's further assertion: the limit topology on `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧_I = limₙ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)/Iⁿ`
and the limit topology on `limₙ Hᵖ(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)` correspond under it. By
`Stacks.IntertwinedFiltration.adicCompletionModuleLimitTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology` the
topology on the left is equally the `I`-adic topology of the completion, which is the source's
own footnote to the statement.

The module isomorphism is `Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.formalFunctionsEquiv` together
with `formalFunctionsEquiv_proj_of`, and the homeomorphism is
`Stacks.IntertwinedFiltration.isHomeomorph_adicCompletionEquivTowerLimit_limitTopology` for the
same map; the hypotheses of all three are clauses (1) and (3) of [Stacks, Tag 02OB], which come
from `exists_uniform_bound_cohomology_idealPowerQuotient_of_isProper`, together with the
finite generation of `I` that `IsNoetherianRing A` supplies. Those three declarations carry no
registration under [Stacks, Tag 02OC]: each takes clauses (1) and (3) of [Stacks, Tag 02OB] as
inputs and states one component of the theorem, and this theorem, which states all three
components with the source's hypotheses, is the registered form of [Stacks, Tag 02OC].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_formalFunctionsEquiv_of_isProper [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f) [F.IsCoherent] (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : AdicCompletion I (cohomologyOverBase A f p F) ≃ₗ[A]
        towerLimit (adicCohomologyTower A f I F p) (adicCohomologyTowerMap A f I F p),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : cohomologyOverBase A f p F),
          towerLimit.proj n (e (AdicCompletion.of I (cohomologyOverBase A f p F) x)) =
            adicCohomologyProj A f I F p n x) ∧
        @IsHomeomorph _ _
          (adicCompletionModuleLimitTopology (M := cohomologyOverBase A f p F) I)
          (towerLimit.limitTopology (adicCohomologyTower A f I F p)
            (adicCohomologyTowerMap A f I F p)) e

declarations.name: Stacks.FormalFunctions.nonempty_adicCompletionHigherDirectImageStalkEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes with `Y`
locally Noetherian, let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `y` be a point of `Y`. Let
`X_n = Spec (𝒪_{Y, y}/𝔪_y ⁿ) ×_Y X` be the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the fibre `X_y` and
`ℱ_n = i_n ^* ℱ`. Then in every degree `p`

`(R ᵖ f_* ℱ) _y ^∧ ≅ lim_n H ᵖ (X_n, ℱ_n)`

as `𝒪 ^∧_{Y, y}`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_adicCompletionHigherDirectImageStalkEquiv (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (y : Y) (p : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (stalkMaximalIdeal y) (higherDirectImageStalk f F y p) ≃ₗ[
          AdicCompletion (stalkMaximalIdeal y) (Y.presheaf.stalk y)]
        towerLimit (infinitesimalCohomology f F y p) (infinitesimalCohomologyMap f F y p))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FormalFunctions.pushforwardPullbackBaseIdealIso
declarations.doc:
**`i_{n*} ℱ_n ≅ ℱ / I ⁿ ℱ`.** The direct image of the restriction of `ℱ` to the infinitesimal
neighbourhood `X_n = X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A / I ⁿ)` is the quotient of `ℱ` by the `n`-th power of
the ideal sheaf `I · 𝒪_X`.

This is the **second step of the proof of [Stacks, Tag 02OD]**, not its conclusion: the source
derives `H ᵖ (X_n, ℱ_n) = H ᵖ (X, ℱ / 𝔪 ⁿ ℱ)` from it by the Leray spectral sequence for `i_n`
together with [Stacks, Tag 01Y6]. At `p = 0` no spectral sequence is needed, because a direct
image does not change global sections, so the global sections of this isomorphism are that
identification. The tag's conclusion — that the completed stalk of `R ᵖ f_* ℱ` at `y` is the limit
of the `H ᵖ (X_n, ℱ_n)` — is **not** asserted here: it needs in addition [Stacks, Tag 02OC], which
rests on [Stacks, Tag 02O8], and flat base change [Stacks, Tag 02KH] to reduce `Y` to
`Spec 𝒪_{Y,y}`, which is the reduction that makes `i_n` a closed immersion in the first place.

The underlying mathematics is [Stacks, Tag 0EL1], already proved in the library as
`Stacks.Algebraization.idealQuotientPushforwardIso`; what is asserted here is that the fibre
product of the source's diagram is a presentation it applies to.
declarations.statement:
public def pushforwardPullbackBaseIdealIso :
    (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (baseNeighbourhoodι A I f n)).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseNeighbourhoodι A I f n)).obj F) ≅
      idealPowerQuotient (baseIdealSheaf A I f) n F
declarations.comment: the second step of the tag's proof: the identification i_{n*} ℱ_n ≅ ℱ / 𝔪ⁿ ℱ, over an affine base and for the quotient by the n-th power of the ideal sheaf generated by an ideal of that base. The tag's conclusion is NOT asserted: that needs Tag 02OC, which rests on Tag 02O8, together with Tag 02KH

declarations.name: Stacks.FormalFunctions.infinitesimalNeighbourhood
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th infinitesimal neighbourhood `X_n = Spec (𝒪_{Y,y}/𝔪_y ^ n) ×_Y X` of the fibre of
`f : X ⟶ Y` over `y`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev infinitesimalNeighbourhood (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : Y) (n : ℕ) : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: the infinitesimal neighbourhoods X_n = X ×_Y Spec(𝒪_{Y,y}/𝔪ⁿ) of the fibre, the setup paragraph of the tag. The conclusion -- that the completed stalk of R^p f_* ℱ at y is the limit of the H^p(X_n, ℱ_n) -- is NOT asserted here: see the implementation notes for its three inputs and which of them are now available

declarations.name: Stacks.FormalFunctions.isZero_stalk_higherDirectImage_of_finite_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OE.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and let `y : Y`.
Assume `Y` is locally Noetherian, `f` is proper, and the fibre `f ⁻¹' {y}` is finite. Then for
every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` and every `p > 0` the stalk `(R ᵖ f_* F)_y` vanishes.

This is `isZero_stalk_higherDirectImage_of_finite_preimage`, which needs neither hypothesis;
coherence of `F` gives quasi-coherence through [Stacks, Tag 01BW]
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentTFAE.isQuasicoherent_isFiniteType_of_isCoherent`), for which
no hypothesis on `Y` is needed either. Both hypotheses are kept here because the tag states
them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_stalk_higherDirectImage_of_finite_fibre {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] (y : Y) (hfin : (f ⁻¹' {y}).Finite) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero
      ((((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedPlus p).obj F).presheaf.stalk y)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.tfae_isProper_finite_preimage_singleton
registrations.comment:
the equivalence of the first two conditions, for an arbitrary target; the
  source assumes it locally Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.FormalFunctions.exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_finite_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OH.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and let `y : Y`.
Assume `Y` is locally Noetherian, `f` is proper, and the fibre `f ⁻¹' {y}` is finite. Then `y` has
an open neighbourhood `V` over which `f` is finite, that is, `f ∣_ V : f ⁻¹ᵁ V ⟶ V` is finite.

This is Zariski's main theorem in the form of [Stacks, Tag 02UP]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_finite_preimage_singleton`), which needs
no hypothesis on `Y`; local Noetherianness is kept here because the tag states it. The source
instead deduces the lemma from Tag 02OG, finiteness being equivalent to properness with finite
fibres over a locally Noetherian base; that route is unavailable here, and it would in any case be
circular, since Tag 02OG rests on Tag 02OE above.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_finite_fibre {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] (y : Y) (hfin : (f ⁻¹' {y}).Finite) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, y ∈ V ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
A point `x` is *associated* to an `𝒪_X`-module `F` when the maximal ideal of the local ring
`𝒪_{X, x}` is an associated prime of the stalk `F_x`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAssociatedPoint (F : X.Modules) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
declarations.doc: The set `Ass(F)` of points associated to an `𝒪_X`-module `F`.
declarations.statement: abbrev associatedPoints (F : X.Modules) : Set X

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
The associated points `Ass(X)` of a scheme `X` are the associated points of its structure
sheaf.
declarations.statement: abbrev schemeAssociatedPoints (X : Scheme.{u}) : Set X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAssociatedPoint_of_isAssociatedPrime_sections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OK, part (1).** An associated prime of the sections of a quasi-coherent sheaf on
an affine open gives an associated point of the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAssociatedPoint_of_isAssociatedPrime_sections {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ U)
    (h : IsAssociatedPrimeStacks Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U) (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsAssociatedPoint F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAssociatedPrime_sections_of_isAssociatedPoint_of_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OK, part (2).** If the prime corresponding to an associated point is finitely
generated, then it is associated to the module of sections on the affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAssociatedPrime_sections_of_isAssociatedPoint_of_fg {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ U)
    (hfg : (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal.FG) (h : Stacks.Divisors.IsAssociatedPoint F x) :
    IsAssociatedPrimeStacks Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U) (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAssociatedPrime_sections_iff_isAssociatedPoint_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OK, locally Noetherian case.** On a locally Noetherian scheme, the prime
corresponding to a point of an affine open is associated to the module of sections exactly when
the point is associated to the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAssociatedPrime_sections_iff_isAssociatedPoint_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : IsAffineOpen U) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ U) :
    IsAssociatedPrimeStacks Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U) (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal ↔
      Stacks.Divisors.IsAssociatedPoint F x

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentSubquotients.exists_greatest_isNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OL].** Among the coherent subsheaves of a coherent sheaf `F` on a locally
Noetherian scheme whose support is nowhere dense in the support of `F` there is a greatest
one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_greatest_isNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ K : Subobject F,
      IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K ∧
        ∀ L : Subobject F, IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F L → L ≤ K

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentSubquotients.supp_cokernel_eq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OL], part (1).** The quotient of `F` by a coherent subsheaf with nowhere
dense support has the same support as `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supp_cokernel_eq {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (K : Subobject F)
    (hK : IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K) :
    (⟨(cokernel K.arrow).val, (cokernel K.arrow).isSheaf⟩ :
      RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp =
      (⟨F.val, F.isSheaf⟩ : RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentSubquotients.cokernel_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OL], part (2).** The quotient of `F` by a coherent subsheaf with nowhere
dense support has no embedded associated points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cokernel_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (K : Subobject F)
    (hK : IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K)
    (hmax : ∀ L : Subobject F, IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F L → L ≤ K) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints (cokernel K.arrow)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentSubquotients.exists_denseOpen_cokernel_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OL], part (3).** There is a dense open subset, meeting the support of `F`
densely, over every open subset of which the quotient map is an isomorphism on sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_denseOpen_cokernel_iso
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (K : Subobject F)
    (hK : IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens,
      Dense (U : Set X) ∧
      Dense {x : ↥((⟨F.val, F.isSheaf⟩ :
            RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp) | (x : X) ∈ U} ∧
          ∀ V : X.Opens, V ≤ U →
            IsIso ((cokernel.π K.arrow).val.app (op V))
declarations.comment: part (3): agreement on a dense open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.EmbeddedPoints.exists_greatest_isNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OL, maximal subsheaf.** The coherent subsheaves whose support is
nowhere dense in the support of `F` have a greatest member.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_greatest_isNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ K : Subobject F,
      IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K ∧
        ∀ L : Subobject F, IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F L → L ≤ K

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.EmbeddedPoints.supp_cokernel_eq
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 02OL, part (1).** The quotient has the same support.
declarations.statement:
theorem supp_cokernel_eq [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (K : Subobject F)
    (hK : IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K) :
    (⟨(cokernel K.arrow).val, (cokernel K.arrow).isSheaf⟩ :
      RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp =
      (⟨F.val, F.isSheaf⟩ : RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.EmbeddedPoints.cokernel_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OL, part (2).** The quotient by a greatest nowhere dense coherent
subobject has no embedded associated points.
declarations.statement:
theorem cokernel_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (K : Subobject F)
    (hK : IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K)
    (hmax : ∀ L : Subobject F, IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F L → L ≤ K) :
    HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints (cokernel K.arrow)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.EmbeddedPoints.exists_denseOpen_cokernel_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OL, part (3).** The canonical quotient map becomes an isomorphism on
a dense open meeting the support densely.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_denseOpen_cokernel_iso [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (K : Subobject F) (hK : IsNowhereDenseCoherentSubobject F K) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens,
      Dense (U : Set X) ∧
      Dense {x : ↥((⟨F.val, F.isSheaf⟩ :
            RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp) | (x : X) ∈ U} ∧
          ∀ V : X.Opens, V ≤ U →
            IsIso ((cokernel.π K.arrow).val.app (op V))
declarations.comment: part (3): agreement on a dense open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasNoEmbeddedPoints_annihilatorIdeal_subscheme
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM].** The closed subscheme cut out by the annihilator of a coherent module
with no embedded associated points has no embedded points.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoEmbeddedPoints_annihilatorIdeal_subscheme [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F) :
    HasNoEmbeddedPoints (annihilatorIdeal' F).subscheme
declarations.comment: absence of embedded points on the support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCoherent_submodule_eq_annihilatorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM].** The ideals cutting out the scheme-theoretic support over the affine
opens are the sections of a coherent subsheaf of the structure sheaf, namely the annihilator
sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0H2H].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_submodule_eq_annihilatorIdeal [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ I : (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).Submodule,
      I.toSheafOfModules.IsCoherent ∧
        I = Stacks.SheafOfModules.annihilatorSheaf X.toRingedSpace F ∧
          ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (annihilatorIdeal' F).ideal U =
            (show Ideal Γ(X, U.1) from I.toSubmodule.obj (op U.1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_of_pushforward_iso_annihilatorIdeal_subscheme
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM].** Every quasi-coherent module on the scheme-theoretic support whose
direct image is `F` is itself coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_pushforward_iso_annihilatorIdeal_subscheme [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (G : (annihilatorIdeal' F).subscheme.Modules)
    [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (annihilatorIdeal' F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F) :
    G.IsCoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints_of_pushforward_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM].** Every quasi-coherent module on the scheme-theoretic support whose
direct image is `F` inherits from `F` the absence of embedded associated points.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints_of_pushforward_iso [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F)
    (G : (annihilatorIdeal' F).subscheme.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (annihilatorIdeal' F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F) :
    HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints G
declarations.comment: absence of embedded associated points on the descended sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_coherent_module_on_annihilatorIdeal_subscheme
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM].** A coherent module with no embedded associated points on a locally
Noetherian scheme descends along the inclusion of its scheme-theoretic support to a coherent
module with full support and again no embedded associated points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coherent_module_on_annihilatorIdeal_subscheme [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F) :
    ∃ G : (annihilatorIdeal' F).subscheme.Modules,
      G.IsCoherent ∧ HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints G ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp G = Set.univ ∧
          Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
            (annihilatorIdeal' F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: existence and properties of the descended sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.annihilatorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM] the ideal sheaf cutting out the scheme-theoretic support.** The
annihilators of the sections of a coherent module on a locally Noetherian scheme form an ideal
sheaf; the closed subscheme it cuts out is the scheme-theoretic support of the module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def annihilatorIdeal [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    X.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the ideal sheaf cutting out the support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_subschemeι_annihilatorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM], the descended module.** A coherent module on a locally Noetherian
scheme is the direct image of a coherent module on its scheme-theoretic support.

This is [Stacks, Tag 087T]'s coherent descent applied to `annihilatorIdeal_smul_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_subschemeι_annihilatorIdeal [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ G : (annihilatorIdeal F).subscheme.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (annihilatorIdeal F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: existence of the coherent module on the support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasNoEmbeddedPoints_subscheme_annihilatorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM], no embedded points on the support.** If a coherent module on a locally
Noetherian scheme has no embedded associated points, then the closed subscheme cut out by its
annihilator has no embedded points.

The subscheme's ring of functions over the preimage of an affine open `U` is
`Γ(X, U) ⧸ Ann Γ(F, U)`, which has no embedded primes by Tag 02M8 because `Γ(F, U)` has none by
`sections_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes`; an embedded point of the subscheme would give two
nested associated primes there.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoEmbeddedPoints_subscheme_annihilatorIdeal [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] (hF : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F) :
    HasNoEmbeddedPoints (annihilatorIdeal F).subscheme
declarations.comment: absence of embedded points on the support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_of_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OM].** A coherent module without embedded associated points on a locally
Noetherian scheme is the direct image of a coherent module on a closed subscheme without
embedded points, and that module has full support.

This is the source's statement with clause (b) — that the descended module itself has no embedded
associated points — omitted; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_pushforward_iso_of_hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F) :
    HasNoEmbeddedPoints (annihilatorIdeal F).subscheme ∧
      ∃ G : (annihilatorIdeal F).subscheme.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp G = Set.univ ∧
        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (annihilatorIdeal F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: the descended module on a support without embedded points

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.annihilatorIdeal'
registrations.comment: the ideal sheaf cutting out the support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_mul_eq_of_le
declarations.doc:
Let `D` and `D'` be effective Cartier divisors on a scheme `X` with `D ⊆ D'` as closed
subschemes, that is, with `ℐ_{D'} ⊆ ℐ_D`.  Then there is an effective Cartier divisor `E` with
`D' = D + E`, in the ideal-sheaf presentation `ℐ_{D'} = ℐ_D · ℐ_E`.

The divisor `E` is the quotient of ideal sheaves `ℐ_{D'} : ℐ_D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_mul_eq_of_le (D D' : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hD' : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D') (h : D' ≤ D) :
    ∃ E : X.IdealSheafData, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor E ∧ D' = D * E

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isPullbackDefined_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OO (6).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor along a flat
morphism is defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (D : Y.IdealSheafData) [Flat f]
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) :
    IsPullbackDefined f D

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isPullbackDefined_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OO (3).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ Y` along a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` out of a reduced scheme is defined as soon as `f` carries no generic point of an
irreducible component of `X` into the support of `D`: on a reduced scheme those generic points
are exactly the weakly associated points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_isReduced {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsReduced X]
    (D : Y.IdealSheafData) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    (hf : ∀ ξ ∈ genericPoints X, f ξ ∉ D.supportSet) :
    IsPullbackDefined f D
declarations.comment: part (3): a reduced source whose generic points avoid the support

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isPullbackDefined_of_isDominant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OO (2).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor is defined along a dominant
morphism of integral schemes: the generic point of the source is its only weakly associated
point, and dominance sends it to the generic point of the target, which an effective Cartier
divisor misses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_isDominant {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsIntegral Y] [IsDominant f] (D : Y.IdealSheafData) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) :
    IsPullbackDefined f D
declarations.comment: part (2): a dominant morphism of integral schemes

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isPullbackDefined_of_notMem_support_of_associated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OO (4).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ Y` along a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` out of a locally Noetherian scheme is defined as soon as `f` carries no associated
point of `X` into the support of `D`: on a locally Noetherian scheme the associated points are
exactly the weakly associated points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_notMem_support_of_associated {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : Y.IdealSheafData) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ schemeAssociatedPoints X, f x ∉ D.supportSet) :
    IsPullbackDefined f D
declarations.comment: part (4): a locally Noetherian source whose associated points avoid the support

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isPullbackDefined_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OO (5).** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ Y` along a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` out of a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points is defined as soon as `f`
carries no generic point of an irreducible component of `X` into the support of `D`: without
embedded points those generic points are exactly the weakly associated points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) (D : Y.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hf : ∀ ξ ∈ genericPoints X, f ξ ∉ D.supportSet) :
    IsPullbackDefined f D
declarations.comment: part (5): no embedded points, generic points avoiding the support

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isPullbackDefined_of_notMem_support_of_weaklyAssociated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OO (1), the scheme case.** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ Y`
along a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is defined as soon as `f` carries no weakly associated
point of `X` into the support of `D`.

The question is affine-local: near a point `x` of the support of the inverse image, `D` is cut
out on an affine open `V ∋ f x` by a nonzerodivisor `t`, and on an affine open `U ∋ x` inside
`f⁻¹(V)` the inverse image is cut out by the image `φ t` of `t`.  Were `φ t` a zerodivisor, a
minimal prime `q` over the annihilator of a witness would be a weakly associated prime of
`Γ(X, U)` containing `φ t`, hence by Stacks 056M a weakly associated point `x₀` of `X` with
`t` in the prime of `f x₀`; so `f x₀` would lie in the support of `D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_of_notMem_support_of_weaklyAssociated {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (D : Y.IdealSheafData) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X, f x ∉ D.supportSet) :
    IsPullbackDefined f D
declarations.comment: part (1): a morphism carrying no weakly associated point into the support

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafSumIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification `𝒪_X(D) ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(D') ≅ 𝒪_X(D + D')` of the tensor product
of the invertible sheaves of two effective Cartier divisors with the invertible sheaf of their
sum, carrying the pure tensor `1_D ⊗ 1_{D'}` of the canonical sections to the canonical section
`1_{D + D'}`.
declarations.statement:
def invertibleSheafSumIso [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D'] :
    sumSheaf D D' ≅ invertibleSheaf' (D * D')

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafSumIso_canonicalSection
declarations.doc:
Under `Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafSumIso` the pure tensor `1_D ⊗ 1_{D'}` of the canonical
sections of `𝒪_X(D)` and `𝒪_X(D')` is the canonical section `1_{D + D'}` of `𝒪_X(D + D')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleSheafSumIso_canonicalSection
    [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D'] :
    Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (invertibleSheafSumIso D D').hom ⊤ (canonicalSectionTensor D D') =
      (canonicalSection' (D * D')).val (op ⊤)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafSumIso_unique
declarations.doc:
An isomorphism `𝒪_X(D) ⊗ 𝒪_X(D') ≅ 𝒪_X(D + D')` carrying `1_D ⊗ 1_{D'}` to `1_{D + D'}` is
`Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafSumIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleSheafSumIso_unique
    [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D']
    (e : sumSheaf D D' ≅ invertibleSheaf' (D * D'))
    (he : Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom ⊤ (canonicalSectionTensor D D') =
      (canonicalSection' (D * D')).val (op ⊤)) :
    e = invertibleSheafSumIso D D'

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OQ.** The quasi-coherent ideal sheaf cutting out the zero scheme of a global
section `s` of an invertible module `L` on `X`: on an affine open `U` it is generated by the
values `φ (s|_U)` of the `Γ(X, U)`-linear functionals `φ` on `Γ(L, U)`. The closed subscheme
itself is `(zeroScheme X L s).subscheme`, with closed immersion
`(zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev zeroScheme (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) : X.IdealSheafData

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OQ**, the defining ideal. The ideal of the zero scheme of a global section `s` of
an invertible module `L` on an affine open `U` is generated by the values `φ (s|_U)` of the
`Γ(X, U)`-linear functionals on `Γ(L, U)`: the prescribed affine-local family is already an ideal
sheaf, so `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals` leaves it untouched.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroScheme_ideal (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    (zeroScheme X L s).ideal U =
      Ideal.span {a : Γ(X, U.1) | ∃ φ : Γ(L, U.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)] Γ(X, U.1),
        a = φ (L.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op s)}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
The zero scheme of a global section `s` of an invertible module `L`, as a quasi-coherent sheaf
of ideals: on an affine open it is the image of the dual map `s : L^{⊗ -1} ⟶ 𝒪_X`, i.e. the ideal
generated by the values of `s` under the linear functionals on the sections of `L`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev zeroScheme (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) : X.IdealSheafData

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zeroScheme_ideal
declarations.doc:
The defining ideal of the zero scheme on an affine open is the ideal generated by the values of
the restricted section under the local linear functionals.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroScheme_ideal (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    (zeroScheme X L s).ideal U =
      Ideal.span {a : Γ(X, U.1) | ∃ φ : Γ(L, U.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)] Γ(X, U.1),
        a = φ (L.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op s)}

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag02OQSectionIdeal.zeroScheme_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02OQ, the defining ideal of the zero scheme.**  On every affine open the ideal of
the zero scheme of a global section of an invertible module is the ideal generated by the values of
the restricted section under all linear functionals there.

`Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals` is a supremum and in general shrinks the family it is applied to;
it does not here, because that family is already compatible with passage to a basic open and hence
is itself an ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroScheme_ideal (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (t : Γ(L, ⊤)) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.zeroScheme X L t).ideal U =
      Ideal.span {a : Γ(X, U.1) | ∃ φ : Γ(L, U.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)] Γ(X, U.1),
        a = φ (L.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op t)}

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.pullbackSection_eq_zero_iff_factorsThrough_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
A global section `s` of an invertible module `L` on `X` vanishes after pullback along
`f : Y ⟶ X` if and only if `f` factors through the zero scheme of `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackSection_eq_zero_iff_factorsThrough_zeroScheme
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    pullbackGlobalSections f L s = 0 ↔
      ∃ g : Y ⟶ (_root_.Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme,
        g ≫ (_root_.Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackSection_eq_zero_iff_factorsThrough_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02OR (2).** A global section of an invertible module vanishes after pullback
along `f` if and only if `f` factors through its zero scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackSection_eq_zero_iff_factorsThrough_zeroScheme (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    pullbackGlobalSections f L s = 0 ↔
      ∃ g : Y ⟶ (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme,
        g ≫ (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zeroScheme_isGreatest_vanishingClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02OR (1).** Among the closed subschemes on which the section pulls back to
zero, the zero scheme is the largest. Closed subschemes are ordered by their ideal sheaves, and
geometric inclusion is the reverse of that order, which is why the statement is about the order
dual.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroScheme_isGreatest_vanishingClosedSubscheme (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) :
    IsGreatest
      {I : (X.IdealSheafData)ᵒᵈ |
        pullbackGlobalSections (OrderDual.ofDual I).subschemeι L s = 0}
      (OrderDual.toDual (zeroScheme X L s))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyPrincipal_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02OR (3).** The zero scheme of a global section of an invertible module is a
locally principal closed subscheme: on the trivializing opens its ideal is generated by the one
function representing the section.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_zeroScheme (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) : Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal (zeroScheme X L s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_iff_isRegularSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OR (4).** The zero scheme of a global section `s` of an invertible
module is an effective Cartier divisor if and only if `s` is a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_iff_isRegularSection (s : L.sections) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))) ↔
      IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property s

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OS part (2).** For a scheme `X` and a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf
`I`, the exceptional divisor of the blowup of `X` in `I` — the inverse image of the closed
subscheme cut out by `I` — is an effective Cartier divisor on the blowup.

Declared as an `instance`, as the tagged statement has it: the head is the ideal sheaf of the
exceptional divisor, so instance search is not widened.
declarations.statement:
instance isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalIdeal {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (exceptionalIdeal I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.ideal_exceptionalIdeal_blowUpAffineChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OS, second assertion, affine-local form.** On the affine open of the
blowup underlying the chart `Spec Γ(S, U)[ℐ(U)/a]`, the exceptional ideal is generated by
`Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalChartSection`.

This is the equation `IA' = aA'` of the proof of Stacks tag 02OS, for the chart supplied by the
second assertion of Stacks tag 0804, transported from
`Stacks.Blowup.ideal_comap_exceptionalIdeal_blowUpAffineChart` across the chart's identification
of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem ideal_exceptionalIdeal_blowUpAffineChart (U : S.affineOpens)
    {a : Γ(S, U.1)} (ha : a ∈ ℐ.ideal U) :
    (exceptionalIdeal ℐ).ideal ⟨blowUpAffineChart ℐ U ha ''ᵁ ⊤,
        (isAffineOpen_top _).image_of_isOpenImmersion _⟩ =
      Ideal.span {exceptionalChartSection ℐ U ha}
declarations.comment: the exceptional ideal is generated by one section on an affine chart

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalChartSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OS, second assertion, affine-local form.** The generator of the
exceptional ideal on an affine chart of the blowup is a nonzerodivisor.

This is the sentence "`a` maps to a nonzerodivisor in `A'`" of the proof of Stacks tag 02OS.
declarations.statement:
theorem exceptionalChartSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors (U : S.affineOpens)
    {a : Γ(S, U.1)} (ha : a ∈ ℐ.ideal U) :
    exceptionalChartSection ℐ U ha ∈
      nonZeroDivisors Γ(blowUp ℐ, blowUpAffineChart ℐ U ha ''ᵁ ⊤)
declarations.comment: the generator on an affine chart is a nonzerodivisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_span_eq_ideal_exceptionalIdeal_blowUpAffineChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OS, second assertion, affine-local form.** On the affine open of the
blowup underlying the chart `Spec Γ(S, U)[ℐ(U)/a]`, the exceptional ideal is generated by a
single section, and that section is a nonzerodivisor.

This is the sentence "Then `IA' = aA'` and `a` maps to a nonzerodivisor in `A'`" of the proof of
Stacks tag 02OS, for the chart supplied by the second assertion of Stacks tag 0804. The generator
is `Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalChartSection`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_span_eq_ideal_exceptionalIdeal_blowUpAffineChart (U : S.affineOpens)
    {a : Γ(S, U.1)} (ha : a ∈ ℐ.ideal U) :
    ∃ t ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(blowUp ℐ, blowUpAffineChart ℐ U ha ''ᵁ ⊤),
      (exceptionalIdeal ℐ).ideal ⟨blowUpAffineChart ℐ U ha ''ᵁ ⊤,
          (isAffineOpen_top _).image_of_isOpenImmersion _⟩ = Ideal.span {t}
declarations.comment: the exceptional ideal is generated by a nonzerodivisor on an affine chart

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isLocallyPrincipal_exceptionalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OS, second assertion, local principality.** The exceptional divisor
of the blowup of a scheme in a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals is a locally principal closed
subscheme: around every point of the blowup there is an affine open on which the exceptional
ideal is generated by one element.

Every point of the blowup lies over an affine open `U` of the base, hence in one of the charts
`Spec Γ(S, U)[ℐ(U)/a]` by the second assertion of Stacks tag 0804
(`Stacks.Blowup.iSup_opensRange_blowUpAffineChart`), and on that chart the exceptional ideal is
principal by `Stacks.Blowup.exists_span_eq_ideal_exceptionalIdeal_blowUpAffineChart`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_exceptionalIdeal :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal (exceptionalIdeal ℐ)
declarations.comment: the exceptional divisor is a locally principal closed subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_blowUp_restrict_compl_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OS.** The blowup of a scheme in a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf is an
isomorphism over the open complement of the closed subscheme the ideal cuts out.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_blowUp_restrict_compl_support (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    IsIso (blowUpToBase I ∣_ (⟨I.supportᶜ, I.support.isClosed.isOpen_compl⟩ : X.Opens))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.twistOneIsoExceptionalIdealModule
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02OS] part (3).** For a scheme `X` and a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ` on
it, the twisting sheaf `𝒪_{X'}(1)` of the blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `ℐ` is the ideal sheaf
of the exceptional divisor, the inverse image `ℐ·𝒪_{X'}` of the centre.

No hypothesis is carried: `X` is an arbitrary scheme and `ℐ` an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals. Parts (1) and (2) of the tag are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_blowUp_restrict_compl_support` and
`Stacks.Blowup.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_exceptionalIdeal`.
declarations.statement: def twistOneIsoExceptionalIdealModule : blowUpTwist I 1 ≅ exceptionalIdealModule I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PullbacksMeromorphicSections
declarations.doc:
Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined for `f` when the pullback to every compatible
pair of opens sends regular sections of the target structure sheaf to regular sections of the
source structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev PullbacksMeromorphicSections
    {X Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_mapsTo_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
If a morphism of schemes maps every weakly associated point of its source to the generic
point of an irreducible component of its target, then pullbacks of meromorphic functions are
defined for the morphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_mapsTo_genericPoints
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : Set.MapsTo f (Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X) (genericPoints Y)) :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_reduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OU (reduced source).** If a morphism from a reduced scheme sends
every generic point of an irreducible component to a generic point of an irreducible component,
then pullbacks of meromorphic functions along it are defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_reduced {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsReduced X] (hf : Set.MapsTo f (genericPoints X) (genericPoints Y)) :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.toLRSHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OU (integral source).** If the source of a morphism of schemes is
integral and its generic point maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of the target,
then pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined.
declarations.statement:
lemma pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isIntegral
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral X]
    (h : f (genericPoint X) ∈ genericPoints Y) :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.toLRSHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isDominant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OU.** Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined along a
dominant morphism between integral schemes.
declarations.statement:
lemma pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isDominant
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsDominant f] :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.toLRSHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_associatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OU (associated points).** If every associated point of a locally
Noetherian source scheme maps to the generic point of an irreducible component of the target,
then pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_associatedPoints
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (h : ∀ x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints X,
      ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents Y, IsGenericPoint (f x) Z) :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.toLRSHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_noEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OU (no embedded points).** If a morphism from a locally Noetherian
scheme without embedded points sends every generic point of an irreducible component to a
generic point of an irreducible component, then pullbacks of meromorphic functions along it are
defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_noEmbeddedPoints
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedPoints X)
    (hf : Set.MapsTo f (genericPoints X) (genericPoints Y)) :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.toLRSHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_flat
declarations.doc: Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined along a flat morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_flat
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections f.toLRSHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalk_totalQuotientSheaf_isFractionRing_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
At every point of a locally Noetherian scheme the stalk of the sheaf of meromorphic
functions is the total quotient ring of the local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalk_totalQuotientSheaf_isFractionRing_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_totalQuotientSheaf_obj_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of meromorphic functions on an affine open of a locally Noetherian scheme.**
The sections of `K_X` over an affine open `U` form the total quotient ring of `Γ(X, U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalization_totalQuotientSheaf_obj_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op U)) :=
      (X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U)).hom.toAlgebra
    IsLocalization Γ(X, U)⁰ (X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_totalQuotientPresheaf_obj_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
On an affine open of a scheme, meromorphic functions form the total quotient ring of the
ring of regular functions. No Noetherian hypothesis is needed: the denominator submonoid of
the total quotient presheaf on an affine open is already all of `nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalization_totalQuotientPresheaf_obj_of_isAffineOpen
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U)
        ((X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf).obj (Opposite.op U)) :=
      (X.presheaf.toTotalQuotientPresheaf.app (Opposite.op U)).hom.toAlgebra
    IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U))
      ((X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf).obj (Opposite.op U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
At a point of a locally Noetherian scheme, the germs of regular local
sections are exactly the non-zero-divisors in the local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X) :
    (⨆ (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U),
      ((X.presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk
        (fun y ↦ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))).obj (Opposite.op U)).map
          (X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom) =
      nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
At every point of a locally Noetherian scheme, the stalk of the presheaf of meromorphic
functions is the total quotient ring of the local ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        X.presheaf.toTotalQuotientPresheaf).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components,
the germs of regular sections at every point are exactly the nonzerodivisors in its local
ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors_of_isReduced (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (x : X) :
    (⨆ (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U),
      ((X.presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk
        (fun y ↦ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))).obj (Opposite.op U)).map
          (X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom) =
      nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components,
the stalk of the presheaf of meromorphic functions at any point is the total quotient ring of
the local ring there.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing_of_isReduced (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        X.presheaf.toTotalQuotientPresheaf).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointCoproduct.meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OW.** On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely
many irreducible components, the `𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the direct sum, over
the generic points of the irreducible components, of the structure sheaves of the local schemes
there, pushed forward to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : GenericPointProduct.FiniteComponentsOnCompactOpens X) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointProduct.meromorphicFunctions_iso_product_genericPointStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OW.** On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many
irreducible components, the `𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the product, over the generic
points of the irreducible components, of the structure sheaves of the local schemes there, pushed
forward to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_product_genericPointStalks (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : FiniteComponentsOnCompactOpens X) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∏ᶜ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OW, displayed direct-sum decomposition.** On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact
opens have finitely many irreducible components, the `𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the
direct sum of the generic-point contributions.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks_of_isReduced (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_product_genericPointStalks_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02OW, part (2), product decomposition.** On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact
opens have finitely many irreducible components, the sheaf of meromorphic sections of a
quasi-coherent module is the product over the generic points of the irreducible components of
the generic-point contributions.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_product_genericPointStalks_of_isReduced
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (meromorphicSections X F ≅
      ∏ᶜ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModuleOf X F η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks_of_isReduced
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02OW, part (2), direct-sum decomposition.**
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks_of_isReduced
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (meromorphicSections X F ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModuleOf X F η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_isReduced
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02OW, part (2), quasi-coherence.**
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_isReduced
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (meromorphicSections X F).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_totalQuotientSheaf_obj_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 02OW].** On an affine open `U` of a reduced scheme whose
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the sections `K_X(U)` of the
*sheaf* of meromorphic functions are the total quotient ring of `Γ(X, U)`, that is, its
localization at its nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalization_totalQuotientSheaf_obj_of_isReduced
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :=
      (X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U)).hom.toAlgebra
    IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.obj.obj (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicQuasicoherent.meromorphicFunctions_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OW, part (1).** On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have
finitely many irreducible components, the sheaf of meromorphic functions is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_isQuasicoherent (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : FiniteComponentsOnCompactOpens X) :
    (meromorphicFunctions X).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSectionsTensor.meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02OW, part (2), quasi-coherence.** On a reduced scheme whose
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the sheaf of meromorphic sections
of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : GenericPointProduct.FiniteComponentsOnCompactOpens X)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (meromorphicSections X F).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_commRing_rationalFunctions_ringEquiv_totalQuotientSheaf_top_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Part (6) of [Stacks, Tag 02OW].** On a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have
finitely many irreducible components, the ring of rational functions is the ring of global
meromorphic functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_commRing_rationalFunctions_ringEquiv_totalQuotientSheaf_top_of_isReduced
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    ∃ _ : CommRing X.rationalFunctions,
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)),
          ∃ ψ : Γ(X, U) →+* X.rationalFunctions,
            ∀ s, ψ s = X.rationalFunctionOfSection U hU s) ∧
        Nonempty (X.rationalFunctions ≃+* X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReducedTotalQuotient.regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc: Germs of regular sections are precisely the nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : FiniteComponentsOnCompactOpens X) (x : X) :
    (⨆ (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U),
      ((X.presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk
        (fun y ↦ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))).obj (Opposite.op U)).map
          (X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom) =
      nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReducedTotalQuotient.stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing
declarations.doc: A stalk of the meromorphic-function sheaf is the total quotient ring of the local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : FiniteComponentsOnCompactOpens X) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        X.presheaf.toTotalQuotientPresheaf).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
A meromorphic section is regular if its induced map from the total quotient sheaf
to the meromorphic section sheaf is injective.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsRegularMeromorphicSection (O : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.ringSheaf (C := Opens X)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) O))
    (s : MeromorphicSection O L) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**The canonical pullback map on meromorphic sections.** When pullbacks of meromorphic
functions are defined for `f`, a meromorphic section of a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `F` pulls
