    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M'] [Module.Finite A M']
    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module A M''] [Module.Finite A M'']
    (i : M →ₗ[A] M') (p : M' →ₗ[A] M'')
    (hi : Function.Injective i) (hp : Function.Surjective p)
    (hip : Function.Exact i p)
    (a b : A)
    (haM : IsSMulRegular M a) (hbM : IsSMulRegular M b)
    (haM' : IsSMulRegular M' a) (hbM' : IsSMulRegular M' b)
    (haM'' : IsSMulRegular M'' a) (hbM'' : IsSMulRegular M'' b)
    (hdimM : Module.supportDim A M = 1)
    (hdimM' : Module.supportDim A M' = 1)
    (hdimM'' : Module.supportDim A M'' = 1) :
    moduleSymbol a b haM' hbM' hdimM' =
      moduleSymbol a b haM hbM hdimM * moduleSymbol a b haM'' hbM'' hdimM''

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.moduleSymbol_eq_of_ker_coker_supportDim_le_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Q4.** The symbol is unchanged by a map of one-dimensional finite
modules whose kernel and cokernel have support dimension at most zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleSymbol_eq_of_ker_coker_supportDim_le_zero
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} {M' : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M'] [Module.Finite A M']
    (α : M →ₗ[A] M') (a b : A)
    (ha : IsSMulRegular M a) (hb : IsSMulRegular M b)
    (ha' : IsSMulRegular M' a) (hb' : IsSMulRegular M' b)
    (hdim : Module.supportDim A M = 1)
    (hdim' : Module.supportDim A M' = 1)
    (hker : Module.supportDim A (LinearMap.ker α) ≤ 0)
    (hcoker : Module.supportDim A (M' ⧸ LinearMap.range α) ≤ 0) :
    moduleSymbol a b ha hb hdim = moduleSymbol a b ha' hb' hdim'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.moduleSymbol_eq_finprod_minimal_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Q5.** The symbol of a finite one-dimensional module is the product
of the symbols of its minimal support quotients, weighted by localization lengths.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleSymbol_eq_finprod_minimal_support
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (a b : A) (ha : IsSMulRegular M a) (hb : IsSMulRegular M b)
    (hdim : Module.supportDim A M = 1) :
    ∃ (haq : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum A // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support A M) q},
        IsSMulRegular (A ⧸ q.1.asIdeal) a),
    ∃ (hbq : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum A // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support A M) q},
        IsSMulRegular (A ⧸ q.1.asIdeal) b),
    ∃ (hdimq : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum A // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support A M) q},
        Module.supportDim A (A ⧸ q.1.asIdeal) = 1),
      moduleSymbol a b ha hb hdim =
        ∏ᶠ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum A // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support A M) q},
          (moduleSymbol (M := A ⧸ q.1.asIdeal) a b
            (haq q) (hbq q) (hdimq q)) ^
            (Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal)
              (LocalizedModule q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M)).toNat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_unit_algebraMap_eq_zpow_div_zpow
declarations.doc:
For a discrete valuation ring `A` with fraction field `K` and nonzero `x, y ∈ K`, the power
product `x ^ (ord_A y) / y ^ (ord_A x)` is the image of a unit of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unit_algebraMap_eq_zpow_div_zpow
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    {K : Type v} [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (x y : Kˣ) :
    ∃ w : Aˣ, algebraMap A K (w : A) =
      (x : K) ^ (ordInt A (y : K) y.ne_zero) / (y : K) ^ (ordInt A (x : K) x.ne_zero)
declarations.comment: the power product is a unit of the valuation ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tameSymbol_eq_negOnePow_mul_residue
declarations.doc:
For a discrete valuation ring `A` with fraction field `K` and nonzero `x, y ∈ K`, the symbol
`d_A(x, y)` is the usual tame symbol: if `w` is a unit of `A` representing
`x ^ (ord_A y) / y ^ (ord_A x)`, then `d_A(x, y)` is the residue of `w` times
`(-1) ^ (ord_A x * ord_A y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbol_eq_negOnePow_mul_residue
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    {K : Type v} [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (x y : Kˣ) (w : Aˣ)
    (hw : algebraMap A K (w : A) =
      (x : K) ^ (ordInt A (y : K) y.ne_zero) / (y : K) ^ (ordInt A (x : K) x.ne_zero)) :
    ((tameSymbol (K := K) (IsDiscreteValuationRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one A) x y :
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)ˣ) : IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) =
      (((-1 : (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)ˣ) ^
            (ordInt A (x : K) x.ne_zero * ordInt A (y : K) y.ne_zero) :
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)ˣ) : IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) *
        IsLocalRing.residue A (w : A)

declarations.name: Stacks.PrepareNonZeroDivisors.exists_finiteExtension_factorization_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Q7.** Let `R` be a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring and let `a`
and `b` be nonzerodivisors. There is a finite ring extension in which they have a common
nonzerodivisor factor and their residual factors generate the unit ideal; moreover, a power of the
maximal ideal annihilates the quotient by `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteExtension_factorization_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) (a b : R)
    (ha : a ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hb : b ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) :
    ∃ (S : Type u) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra R S),
      Module.Finite R S ∧
      Function.Injective (algebraMap R S) ∧
      (∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal R ^ n ≤
        Module.annihilator R (S ⧸ (Algebra.linearMap R S).range)) ∧
      ∃ t a' b' : S,
        t ∈ nonZeroDivisors S ∧
        a' ∈ nonZeroDivisors S ∧
        b' ∈ nonZeroDivisors S ∧
        algebraMap R S a = t * a' ∧
        algebraMap R S b = t * b' ∧
        Ideal.span ({a', b'} : Set S) = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.moduleSymbol_steinberg_prepare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Q8.** Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring, let `a b : A`, and let `M`
be a finite `A`-module of support dimension one on which each of `a`, `b` and `b - a` acts
injectively. Then

`d_M(a, b - a) * d_M(b, b) = d_M(b, b - a) * d_M(a, b)`

in the units of the residue field of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleSymbol_steinberg_prepare
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (a b : A) (ha : IsSMulRegular M a) (hb : IsSMulRegular M b)
    (hba : IsSMulRegular M (b - a))
    (hdim : Module.supportDim A M = 1) :
    moduleSymbol a (b - a) ha hba hdim * moduleSymbol b b hb hb hdim =
      moduleSymbol b (b - a) hb hba hdim * moduleSymbol a b ha hb hdim

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tameSymbol_one_sub
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Q9.** Let `A` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with
fraction field `K`. For `x` a unit of `K` and `y` the unit `1 - x` of `K`, the tame symbol of
Tag 02Q1 satisfies `d_A(x, 1 - x) = 1` in the units of the residue field of `A`.

Asking that both `x` and `1 - x` be units of `K` is the hypothesis `x ∉ {0, 1}` of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbol_one_sub {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] {K : Type v} [Field K]
    [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1)
    (x y : Kˣ) (hy : (y : K) = 1 - (x : K)) :
    tameSymbol (K := K) hdim x y = 1
declarations.comment: two units of the fraction field identified by `(y : K) = 1 - (x : K)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tameSymbol_one_sub_mk0
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Q9.** Let `A` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with
fraction field `K`. For `x ∈ K` other than `0` and `1`, the tame symbol of Tag 02Q1 satisfies
`d_A(x, 1 - x) = 1` in the units of the residue field of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbol_one_sub_mk0 {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] {K : Type v} [Field K]
    [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1)
    (x : K) (hx₀ : x ≠ 0) (hx₁ : x ≠ 1) :
    tameSymbol (K := K) hdim (Units.mk0 x hx₀)
      (Units.mk0 (1 - x) (sub_ne_zero_of_ne hx₁.symm)) = 1
declarations.comment: an element of the fraction field other than `0` and `1`

declarations.name: Module.FiniteLength.injective_iff_bijective_and_length_quotient_range_eq_order
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QB.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, `q` a prime with `R / q` of
dimension one, and `φ : M → N` a map of finite modules each generated by a sequence of `l` terms
whose successive quotients are `R / q`. Then `φ` is injective if and only if its localization at
`q` is an isomorphism, and in this case the cokernel `N / φ(M)` has finite length equal to the
order of the nonzero scalar `f` of the residue field at `q` with
`[φ(x₁), …, φ(xₗ)] = f [y₁, …, yₗ]` in the determinant of the localization of `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_iff_bijective_and_length_quotient_range_eq_order
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (q : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime] (hdim : ringKrullDim (R ⧸ q) = 1)
    (l : ℕ) (x : Fin l → M) (y : Fin l → N)
    (hx : Submodule.span R (Set.range x) = ⊤)
    (hxf : ∀ i : Fin l,
      Nonempty
        (((spanBefore (R := R) x i ⊔ R ∙ x i : Submodule R M) ⧸
            (spanBefore (R := R) x i).comap
              (spanBefore (R := R) x i ⊔ R ∙ x i : Submodule R M).subtype) ≃ₗ[R]
          R ⧸ q))
    (hy : Submodule.span R (Set.range y) = ⊤)
    (hyf : ∀ i : Fin l,
      Nonempty
        (((spanBefore (R := R) y i ⊔ R ∙ y i : Submodule R N) ⧸
            (spanBefore (R := R) y i).comap
              (spanBefore (R := R) y i ⊔ R ∙ y i : Submodule R N).subtype) ≃ₗ[R]
          R ⧸ q))
    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    letI : Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (R ⧸ q) := Ring.krullDimLE_iff.mpr hdim.le
    (Function.Injective φ ↔ Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl φ)) ∧
      (Function.Injective φ →
        ∃ hlen : moduleLength (Localization.AtPrime q) (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N) = l,
          ∃ hadmφ : IsAdmissibleSequence (R := Localization.AtPrime q)
              (fun i ↦ LocalizedModule.mk (φ (x (Fin.cast hlen i))) (1 : q.primeCompl)),
            ∃ hadmy : IsAdmissibleSequence (R := Localization.AtPrime q)
                (fun i ↦ LocalizedModule.mk (y (Fin.cast hlen i)) (1 : q.primeCompl)),
              ∃ f : IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q), ∃ hf : f ≠ 0,
                symbol (⟨_, hadmφ⟩ :
                    AdmissibleSequence (Localization.AtPrime q)
                      (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)) =
                    f • symbol (⟨_, hadmy⟩ :
                      AdmissibleSequence (Localization.AtPrime q)
                        (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)) ∧
                  Module.length R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range φ) ≠ ⊤ ∧
                  ((Module.length R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range φ)).toNat : ℤ) =
                    Multiplicative.toAdd (WithZero.unzero
                      (x := Ring.ordFrac (R ⧸ q) f)
                      ((hf.isUnit.map (Ring.ordFrac (R ⧸ q))).ne_zero)))

declarations.name: Module.FiniteLength.exists_sequence_with_successive_quotients_at_minimal_support_and_length_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QC.** Let `M` be a finite module over a Noetherian ring `R` and
`q` a minimal point of the support of `M`. Then there is a sequence `x₁, …, x_l` in `M` such
that `q` is not in the support of `M / ⟨x₁, …, x_l⟩` and each successive quotient
`⟨x₁, …, x_i⟩ / ⟨x₁, …, x_{i-1}⟩` is isomorphic to `R / q`. Moreover, every sequence with these
two properties has `l` equal to the length of the localization `M_q` over `R_q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sequence_with_successive_quotients_at_minimal_support_and_length_eq
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum R) (hq : Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q) :
    (∃ (l : ℕ) (x : Fin l → M),
      q ∉ Module.support R (M ⧸ Submodule.span R (Set.range x)) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin l,
        Nonempty
          (((spanBefore (R := R) x i ⊔ R ∙ x i : Submodule R M) ⧸
              (spanBefore (R := R) x i).comap
                (spanBefore (R := R) x i ⊔ R ∙ x i : Submodule R M).subtype) ≃ₗ[R]
            R ⧸ q.asIdeal)) ∧
    ∀ (l : ℕ) (x : Fin l → M),
      q ∉ Module.support R (M ⧸ Submodule.span R (Set.range x)) →
      (∀ i : Fin l,
        Nonempty
          (((spanBefore (R := R) x i ⊔ R ∙ x i : Submodule R M) ⧸
              (spanBefore (R := R) x i).comap
                (spanBefore (R := R) x i ⊔ R ∙ x i : Submodule R M).subtype) ≃ₗ[R]
            R ⧸ q.asIdeal)) →
      l = (Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
        (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl M)).toNat
declarations.comment: The ring is not assumed local.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.neg_periodicLength_eq_finsum_ordFrac_periodicDeterminant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QD.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and `(M, φ, ψ)` a
`(2, 1)`-periodic complex with `M` finite, the cohomology of finite length and the support of `M`
of dimension one. Then minus the multiplicity of the complex is the sum, over the minimal points
of the support, of the orders of the periodic determinants of the localizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem neg_periodicLength_eq_finsum_ordFrac_periodicDeterminant
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (φ ψ : Module.End R M) (hφψ : φ * ψ = 0) (hψφ : ψ * φ = 0)
    (hcoh : ∀ i : ZMod 2, IsFiniteLength R ((twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ).homology i))
    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M = 1) :
    ∃ hdim1 : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q},
        Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (R ⧸ q.1.asIdeal),
    ∃ hfin : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q},
        IsFiniteLength (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal)
          (LocalizedModule q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M),
    ∃ hex₁ : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q},
        Function.Exact (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl φ)
          (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl ψ),
    ∃ hex₂ : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q},
        Function.Exact (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl ψ)
          (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl φ),
      -periodicLength (twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ) =
        ∑ᶠ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R // Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q},
          letI := hdim1 q
          Multiplicative.toAdd (WithZero.unzero
            (x := Ring.ordFrac (R ⧸ q.1.asIdeal)
              ((periodicDeterminant (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl φ)
                (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl ψ)
                (hex₁ q) (hex₂ q) (hfin q) : q.1.asIdeal.ResidueField)))
            (((periodicDeterminant (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl φ)
                (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl ψ)
                (hex₁ q) (hex₂ q) (hfin q)).isUnit.map
              (Ring.ordFrac (R ⧸ q.1.asIdeal))).ne_zero))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.length_quotient_sub_length_ker_eq_finsum_ordOfResidueUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QE.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, `M` a finite `R`-module
whose support has dimension at most one, and `ψ : M → M` an `R`-linear map whose kernel and
cokernel have finite length. Then the length of the cokernel minus the length of the kernel is
the sum, over the nonclosed points `q` of the support of `M`, of the order of vanishing along
`R ⧸ q` of the residue-field determinant of the automorphism `ψ_q` of `M_q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quotient_sub_length_ker_eq_finsum_ordOfResidueUnit
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (ψ : Module.End R M)
    (hker : IsFiniteLength R (LinearMap.ker ψ))
    (hcoker : IsFiniteLength R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ))
    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M ≤ 1) :
    ∃ hdim1 : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R //
        q ∈ Module.support R M ∧ q ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R},
        Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (R ⧸ q.1.asIdeal),
    ∃ hfin : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R //
        q ∈ Module.support R M ∧ q ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R},
        IsFiniteLength (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal)
          (LocalizedModule q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M),
    ∃ hbij : ∀ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R //
        q ∈ Module.support R M ∧ q ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R},
        Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl ψ),
      ((Module.length R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ)).toNat : ℤ) -
          ((Module.length R (LinearMap.ker ψ)).toNat : ℤ) =
        ∑ᶠ q : {q : PrimeSpectrum R //
            q ∈ Module.support R M ∧ q ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R},
          @ordOfResidueUnit R _ _ q.1 q.1.isPrime (hdim1 q)
            (determinantAutomorphism
              (LinearEquiv.ofBijective
                (LocalizedModule.map q.1.asIdeal.primeCompl ψ) (hbij q)) (hfin q))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_mul_eq_finsum_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QF.** The multiplicity of the periodic complex `(M, 0, x)` is
the sum, over the nonclosed points in the support of `M`, of the order of `x` modulo that
point times the length of the localization of `M` there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem periodicLength_mul_eq_finsum_support
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (x : R) (hM : Module.supportDim R M ≤ 1)
    (hxM : Module.supportDim R (QuotSMulTop x M) ≤ 0) :
    periodicLength
        (twoPeriodicComplex (0 : Module.End R M) (LinearMap.lsmul R M x)
          (zero_mul _) (mul_zero _)) =
      ∑ᶠ q ∈ {q : PrimeSpectrum R |
          q ∈ Module.support R M ∧ q ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R},
        ((Ring.ord (R ⧸ q.asIdeal) (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal x)).toNat : ℤ) *
          ((Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl M)).toNat : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.length_quotSMulTop_eq_sum_minimal_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QG, first assertion.** If `M` is a finite
Cohen--Macaulay module whose support has dimension one and whose quotient by
`x` has zero-dimensional support, then the length of `M / xM` is the sum of
the colength of `(x, q)` times the length of `M` localized at `q`, over the
minimal points `q` of the support of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem length_quotSMulTop_eq_sum_minimal_support
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (x : R) (hCM : Module.IsCohenMacaulayAtMaximalIdeal R M)
    (hM : Module.supportDim R M = 1)
    (hxM : Module.supportDim R (QuotSMulTop x M) = 0) :
    Module.length R (QuotSMulTop x M) =
      ∑ᶠ q ∈ {q : PrimeSpectrum R | Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q},
        Module.length R (R ⧸ (Ideal.span {x} ⊔ q.asIdeal)) *
          Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.length_quotient_span_sup_eq_sum_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QG, second assertion.** If `x` is a
nonzerodivisor on the one-dimensional quotient `R / I`, then the colength of
`(x, I)` is the sum of the colength of `(x, q)` times the length of
`(R / I)` localized at `q`, over the minimal primes `q` above `I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem length_quotient_span_sup_eq_sum_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (x : R) (I : Ideal R) (hx : IsSMulRegular (R ⧸ I) x)
    (hI : ringKrullDim (R ⧸ I) = 1) :
    Module.length R (R ⧸ (Ideal.span {x} ⊔ I)) =
      ∑ᶠ q ∈ {q : PrimeSpectrum R | q.asIdeal ∈ I.minimalPrimes},
        Module.length R (R ⧸ (Ideal.span {x} ⊔ q.asIdeal)) *
          Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl (R ⧸ I))

declarations.name: Ideal.fraction_smul_denominatorIdeal_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QH, containment assertion.** Multiplying `I M` by `a / b` in the
localization of `M` at the nonzerodivisors lands back in the image of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fraction_smul_denominatorIdeal_le
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (a b : R) (hb : b ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) :
    ∀ x ∈ denominatorIdeal a b • (⊤ : Submodule R M),
      IsLocalization.mk' (FractionRing R) a ⟨b, hb⟩ •
          LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M x ∈
        Set.range (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M)

declarations.name: Ideal.length_fractionalProduct_quotient_sub_length_denominator_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QH, length formula.** The difference between the colength of
`(a / b) I M` and that of `I M` is the sum of the generic lengths of `M`, weighted by the
orders of `a / b` on the irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_fractionalProduct_quotient_sub_length_denominator_quotient
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (a b : R) (ha : a ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hb : b ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    (hRdim : ringKrullDim R = 1)
    (hMembedded : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes R M)
    (hMsupport : Module.support R M = Set.univ) :
    ((Module.length R
        (M ⧸ fractionalProductIdeal a b • (⊤ : Submodule R M))).toNat : ℤ) -
      ((Module.length R
        (M ⧸ denominatorIdeal a b • (⊤ : Submodule R M))).toNat : ℤ) =
      ∑ᶠ q ∈ {q : PrimeSpectrum R | q.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes R},
        ((Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
          (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl M)).toNat : ℤ) *
          (((Ring.ord (R ⧸ q.asIdeal)
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal a)).toNat : ℤ) -
            ((Ring.ord (R ⧸ q.asIdeal)
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal b)).toNat : ℤ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finsum_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QJ: the Key Lemma for `d`.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian
local domain with fraction field `K` and let `f, g ∈ K^*`. Then

`∑_{height(𝔮) = 1} ord_{A/𝔮}(∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)) = 0`,

the sum being over the height-one primes of `A`, with `∂_{A_𝔮}` the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAH on
the one-dimensional Noetherian local ring `A_𝔮`
(`Stacks.Chow.canonicalHeightOneSymbol`). Only finitely many primes contribute, by
`Stacks.Chow.finite_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_support`, which is the first form the source gives the
statement in.

The proof is the source's:
`Stacks.Chow.fracTameSymbolOrderAt_finsum_eq_zero_of_forall_nonZeroDivisors` expands a pair of
fractions into four pairs of nonzerodivisors of `A`, and Stacks 0EAW
(`Stacks.Chow.finsum_tameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero`) kills each of the four.
declarations.statement:
theorem finsum_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero [IsDomain A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (f g : (FractionRing A)ˣ) :
    ∑ᶠ p : HeightOnePrime A,
      fracTameSymbolOrderAt hdim p (canonicalHeightOneSymbol p) f g = 0
declarations.comment: the second displayed form, the sum over all height-one primes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finsum_heightOneOrd_tameSymbol_totalFraction_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EAX: the Key Lemma, for every two-dimensional Noetherian local
ring.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring, not necessarily a domain, with total
ring of fractions `Q(A)`, and let `f, g ∈ Q(A)^*`. Then

`∑_{height(𝔮) = 1} ord_{A/𝔮}(∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)) = 0`,

the sum being over the height-one primes of `A`, with `∂_{A_𝔮}` the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAH on
the one-dimensional Noetherian local ring `A_𝔮`, applied to the images of `f` and `g` under
`Stacks.Chow.heightOneFractionMap`. Only finitely many terms are nonzero, by
`Stacks.Chow.finite_heightOneOrd_tameSymbol_totalFraction_support`.

The proof is the source's: writing `f = a / b`, `g = c / d` expands the sum into four reciprocity
sums of Stacks 0EAW, each of which vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem finsum_heightOneOrd_tameSymbol_totalFraction_eq_zero [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (f g : (FractionRing A)ˣ) :
    ∑ᶠ p : HeightOnePrime A, heightOneOrd hdim p
      (tameSymbolOfKrullDimOne (ringKrullDim_localization_heightOnePrime p)
        (FractionRing (Localization.AtPrime p.1.asIdeal))
        (Units.map (heightOneFractionMap p).toMonoidHom f)
        (Units.map (heightOneFractionMap p).toMonoidHom g)) = 0
declarations.comment: generalization: for every two-dimensional Noetherian local ring, on the total ring of fractions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.localTameSymbol_ne_one_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QJ.** Two units of the fraction field have trivial tame symbol at
all but finitely many height-one primes, so the reciprocity sum below is a finite sum.
declarations.statement:
theorem localTameSymbol_ne_one_finite
    {A : Type u} {K : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (f g : Kˣ) :
    Set.Finite {q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1} |
      localTameSymbol q f g ≠ 1}
declarations.comment: finiteness of the set of contributing primes, which makes the sum finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sum_ord_localTameSymbol_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QJ.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain
with fraction field `K` and let `f, g` be units of `K`. The orders of vanishing of the tame
symbols `∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)` along `A / 𝔮`, summed over the height-one primes `𝔮` of `A`, give zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem sum_ord_localTameSymbol_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} {K : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [IsLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (f g : Kˣ) :
    ∃ (hquot : ∀ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
        Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (A ⧸ q.1)),
    (∑ᶠ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
        letI : q.1.IsPrime := q.2.1
        letI := hquot q
        let d := localTameSymbol q f g
        Multiplicative.toAdd (WithZero.unzero
          (x := Ring.ordFrac (A ⧸ q.1) (d : q.1.ResidueField))
          ((Units.isUnit d).map (Ring.ordFrac (A ⧸ q.1))).ne_zero)) = 0
declarations.comment: the reciprocity formula, second displayed form: all height-one primes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ChowSituation
declarations.doc:
The base situation of chapter 42: a locally Noetherian, universally catenary scheme equipped
with a dimension function on its underlying topological space.
declarations.statement: structure ChowSituation

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QM.** For a field `k`, the pair `(Spec k, δ)` with `δ(pt) = 0` at the unique point
is a base situation of chapter 42 (Situation 02QL): `Spec k` is Noetherian, it is universally
catenary (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_spec_of_field`), and the constant zero
is a dimension function on it (`Stacks.Chow.fieldDimensionFunction`). The base scheme is
`Spec k` by definition, and the dimension function vanishes by
`Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation_dimensionFunction`.

It is an `abbrev` so that its base scheme is reducibly `Spec k`: the cycle groups of the fibres
of a morphism are formed for this situation, and instance search on them has to see through to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Spec`.
declarations.statement: abbrev fieldChowSituation (k : Type u) [Field k] : ChowSituation.{u}
declarations.comment: the spectrum of a field with the zero dimension function is a Situation 02QL

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fieldBaseDimensionFunction
declarations.doc: The base dimension function on the spectrum of a field, taking every point to zero.
declarations.statement:
abbrev fieldBaseDimensionFunction (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k) → ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_chowSituation_spec_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of a Noetherian domain of Krull dimension one, with the dimension function
which is zero at its maximal ideals and one at its generic point, is a base situation for Chow
homology.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chowSituation_spec_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) :
    ∃ (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (hC : C.S = Spec (CommRingCat.of A)),
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, p.asIdeal.IsMaximal →
        (hC ▸ C.dimensionFunction) p = 0) ∧
      (hC ▸ C.dimensionFunction) (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum A) = 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.relativeDimension_nonneg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QO.** Over a Jacobson base whose dimension function vanishes at
closed points, the relative dimension of a scheme locally of finite type is nonnegative. Every
point specializes to a closed point of the closure of its singleton, where the relative
dimension vanishes, and a dimension function strictly decreases along specialization.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimension_nonneg {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    0 ≤ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f x

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topologicalKrullDim_eq_relativeDimension_toNat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QO.** The dimension of an integral closed subscheme of a scheme
locally of finite type over a Jacobson base is the relative dimension at its generic point. The
latter is converted to a natural number; its nonnegativity is
`Stacks.Chow.relativeDimension_nonneg`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_relativeDimension_toNat {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z] (ξ : Z)
    (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ (Set.univ : Set Z)) :
    topologicalKrullDim Z = (relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f (i ξ)).toNat
declarations.comment: relative dimension equals the dimension of the closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topologicalKrullDim_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QO.** The dimension of an integral closed subscheme of a scheme
locally of finite type over a Jacobson base equals the dimension of its local ring at every
closed point.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk_of_isClosed {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z] (z : Z)
    (hz : IsClosed ({z} : Set Z)) :
    topologicalKrullDim Z = ringKrullDim (Z.presheaf.stalk z)
declarations.comment: dimension of the local ring at a closed point

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.deltaDimension
declarations.doc:
The delta-dimension of an irreducible closed subset of a scheme locally of finite type over
the base is the value at its generic point of the dimension function propagated from the base.
declarations.statement:
def deltaDimension (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (Z : IrreducibleCloseds X) : ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension
declarations.doc:
The delta-dimension of a scheme locally of finite type over the base is the supremum of the
delta-dimensions of its irreducible components. In particular this defines the delta-dimension
of every closed subscheme of such a scheme.
declarations.statement:
def schemeDeltaDimension (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : EInt

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cyclesOfDimension
declarations.doc:
The subgroup `Z_k(X)` of cycles whose nonzero coefficients occur only at
integral closed subschemes of delta-dimension `k`.
declarations.statement:
def cyclesOfDimension (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) : AddSubgroup (AlgebraicCycle X ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.CycleGroup
declarations.doc: The abelian group `Z_k(X)` of cycles of delta-dimension `k`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev CycleGroup (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) : Type u

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isGenericPoint_component_of_relativeDimension_eq
declarations.doc:
A point of a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X` attaining an upper bound for the delta-dimension
of `Z` is the generic point of an irreducible component of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGenericPoint_component_of_relativeDimension_eq (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    {k : ℤ} (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) (ξ : Z)
    (hξ : relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f (i ξ) = k) :
    ∃ W : irreducibleComponents Z, IsGenericPoint ξ (W : Set Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLength_stalk_of_isGenericPoint_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02QT.** At the generic point of an irreducible component of a closed
subscheme, its local ring has finite length over the ambient local ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFiniteLength_stalk_of_isGenericPoint_component
    (C : Stacks.Chow.ChowSituation.{u}) {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (Z' : Set Z) (hZ' : Z' ∈ irreducibleComponents Z)
    (ξ : Z) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z') :
    letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk (i ξ)) (Z.presheaf.stalk ξ) :=
      Module.compHom (Z.presheaf.stalk ξ) (i.stalkMap ξ).hom
    IsFiniteLength (X.presheaf.stalk (i ξ)) (Z.presheaf.stalk ξ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.componentMultiplicity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QU.** The multiplicity of an irreducible component of a closed subscheme,
computed at its generic point as the length of the stalk of the subscheme over the stalk of the
ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
def componentMultiplicity {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (ξ : genericPoints Z) : ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QU.** The `k`-cycle `[Z]_k` associated to a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X`: the
coefficient of each irreducible component of delta-dimension `k` is its multiplicity.
declarations.statement:
def cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ) : CycleGroup C f k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QU.** At the image of the generic point of a component of delta-dimension `k`,
the associated cycle has that component's multiplicity as coefficient.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_apply (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ)
    (ξ : genericPoints Z)
    (hξ : relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f (i ξ.1) = k) :
    (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f i k).1 (i ξ.1) = componentMultiplicity i ξ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_apply_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QU.** A point that is not the image of the generic point of a component of
delta-dimension `k` has coefficient zero in the associated cycle.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_apply_eq_zero (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ) (x : X)
    (hx : ¬ ∃ ξ : genericPoints Z,
      i ξ.1 = x ∧ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f x = k) :
    (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f i k).1 x = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.locallyFinite_irreducibleComponents_supp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QW (1).** The irreducible components of the support of a coherent sheaf on a
locally Noetherian scheme form a locally finite family.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_irreducibleComponents_supp [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] :
    LocallyFinite fun Z : irreducibleComponents (SheafOfModules.supp F : Set X) ↦
      (Subtype.val '' Z.1 : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isFiniteLength_stalk_of_isGenericPoint_component_supp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QW (2).** At the generic point of an irreducible component of its support, the
stalk of a coherent sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme has finite length over the local ring
of the scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLength_stalk_of_isGenericPoint_component_supp [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (Z : irreducibleComponents (SheafOfModules.supp F : Set X)) (ξ : X)
    (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ (Subtype.val '' Z.1 : Set X)) :
    IsFiniteLength (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (F.presheaf.stalk ξ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isGenericPoint_component_supp_of_relativeDimension_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QW (3).** If the support of a coherent sheaf has delta-dimension at most `k`, then
a point of the support of delta-dimension `k` is the generic point of an irreducible component of
the support.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGenericPoint_component_supp_of_relativeDimension_eq (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ) (ξ : X)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hξ : ξ ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F)
    (hδ : relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f ξ = k) :
    ∃ Z : irreducibleComponents (SheafOfModules.supp F : Set X),
      IsGenericPoint ξ (Subtype.val '' Z.1 : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.sheafMultiplicity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QX.** The length of the stalk of a sheaf of modules at a point, as an integer. At
a generic point of an irreducible component of the support of a coherent sheaf this length is
finite and is the multiplicity of that component in the sheaf.
declarations.statement: def sheafMultiplicity (F : X.Modules) (x : X) : ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QX.** The `k`-cycle `[F]_k` associated to a coherent sheaf whose support has
delta-dimension at most `k`: the coefficient at a point of the support whose closure has
delta-dimension `k` is the length of the stalk there.
declarations.statement:
def cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    CycleGroup C f k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QX.** The coefficient formula for the cycle of a coherent sheaf does define a
`k`-cycle when the support of the sheaf has delta-dimension at most `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    ∃ c : CycleGroup C f k, ∀ x : X, (c : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) x =
      open Classical in
      if x ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F ∧ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f x = k then
        sheafMultiplicity F x
      else 0
declarations.comment: part (2): existence of the associated cycle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_eq_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QY.** For a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X` of delta-dimension at most `k`, the
`k`-cycle of `Z` is the `k`-cycle of its structure sheaf: `[Z]_k = [𝒪_Z]_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_eq_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f i k =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z)) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforwardStructureSheaf_le C f i hZ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02QZ.** The cycle of a coherent sheaf is additive along a short exact sequence of
coherent sheaves whose supports all have delta-dimension at most `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_add (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (E : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hE : E.ShortExact)
    [E.X₁.IsCoherent] [E.X₂.IsCoherent] [E.X₃.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hk₁ : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport E.X₁).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hk₂ : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport E.X₂).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hk₃ : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport E.X₃).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f E.X₂ k hk₂ =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f E.X₁ k hk₁ +
        cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f E.X₃ k hk₃

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_properClosedSubscheme_or_finiteDimensional_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02R1.** Let `X` and `Y` be integral schemes locally of finite type
over a Chow base `(S, δ)` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism over `S` with
`dim_δ X = dim_δ Y`. Then either `f(X)` is contained in a proper closed subscheme of `Y`, or
`f` is dominant and the extension of function fields `R(X)/R(Y)` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_properClosedSubscheme_or_finiteDimensional_functionField
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hdim : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = schemeDeltaDimension C sY) :
    (∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ Y), IsClosedImmersion i ∧
        Set.range f.base ⊆ Set.range i.base ∧ Set.range i.base ≠ Set.univ) ∨
      (∃ hdom : IsDominant f,
        letI : IsDominant f := hdom
        letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField :=
          (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
        FiniteDimensional Y.functionField X.functionField)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.locallyFinite_closure_image_of_isSpectralMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R2.** Under a spectral map to a prespectral space, the closures of the images of
a locally finite family of subsets form a locally finite family.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_closure_image_of_isSpectralMap {X : Type u} {Y : Type v}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [PrespectralSpace Y] (f : X → Y)
    (hf : IsSpectralMap f) {I : Type w} (Z : I → Set X) (hZ : LocallyFinite Z) :
    LocallyFinite fun i ↦ closure (f '' Z i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward
declarations.doc: Proper pushforward of cycles of delta-dimension `k`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_apply
declarations.doc:
The coefficient of the proper pushforward at a point is the locally finite sum of the
coefficients above it, weighted by their residue-field degrees when the delta-dimension is
preserved.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_apply (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) (c : CycleGroup C sX k) (y : Y) :
    (properPushforward C sX sY f hf k c).1 y =
      ∑ᶠ x ∈ f.base ⁻¹' {y}, c.1 x *
        (if relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x =
            relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sY (f.base x)
          then (f.residueDegree x : ℤ) else 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_single
declarations.doc:
An integral closed subscheme maps to its image with multiplicity the degree of the
function-field extension if its delta-dimension is preserved, and to zero otherwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_single (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) (x : X) (c : CycleGroup C sX k)
    (hc : c.1 = @Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single X _ ℤ (Classical.decEq X) _ x (1 : ℤ)) :
    (properPushforward C sX sY f hf k c).1 =
      if relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sY (f.base x) = k then
        @Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single Y _ ℤ (Classical.decEq Y) _
          (f.base x) (f.residueDegree x : ℤ)
      else 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R5.** Proper pushforward of `k`-cycles is functorial: pushing forward along
`f : X ⟶ Y` and then along `g : Y ⟶ Z` is pushing forward along the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_comp (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (sZ : Z ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsProper g]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (hg : g ≫ sZ = sY) (k : ℤ) :
    properPushforward C sY sZ g hg k ∘ properPushforward C sX sY f hf k =
      properPushforward C sX sZ (f ≫ g) (by rw [Category.assoc, hg, hf]) k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over the base `S` of
chapter 42, and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support has delta-dimension at most
`k`, with `f_* F` coherent. Then proper pushforward of `k`-cycles carries the cycle of `F` to the
cycle of the direct image: `f_* [F]_k = [f_* F]_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    [((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    properPushforward C sX sY f hf k (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sX F k hFk) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le C sX sY f hf F hFk)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over the base `S` of
chapter 42, and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed subscheme with `dim_δ(Z) ≤ k`, with `f_* (i_* 𝒪_Z)`
coherent. Then proper pushforward of `k`-cycles carries the cycle of `Z` to the cycle of the
direct image of its structure sheaf: `f_* [Z]_k = [f_* 𝒪_Z]_k`, where `𝒪_Z` is read as the
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `i_* 𝒪_Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ) (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    ∀ [((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))).IsCoherent],
    properPushforward C sX sY f hf k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX i k) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le C sX sY f hf
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))
          (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforwardStructureSheaf_le C sX i hZ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_eq_directImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R6, part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite
type over the base `S` of chapter 42, and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support has
delta-dimension at most `k`. Then `f_* [F]_k = [f_* F]_k`, where `f_* F` is coherent by
[Stacks, Tag 02O5] since `Y` is locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_eq_directImage (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsCoherent := properDirectImageIsCoherent f F
    properPushforward C sX sY f hf k (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sX F k hFk) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le C sX sY f hf F hFk)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_eq_directImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R6, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite
type over the base `S` of chapter 42, and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed subscheme with
`dim_δ(Z) ≤ k`. Then `f_* [Z]_k = [f_* 𝒪_Z]_k`, where `𝒪_Z` is the coherent `𝒪_X`-module
`i_* 𝒪_Z` and its direct image `f_* 𝒪_Z` is coherent by [Stacks, Tag 02O5] since `Y` is locally
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_eq_directImage (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ) (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))).IsCoherent :=
      properDirectImageIsCoherent f _
    properPushforward C sX sY f hf k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX i k) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le C sX sY f hf
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))
          (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforwardStructureSheaf_le C sX i hZ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02R6], part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over the base `S` of chapter 42, and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support
has delta-dimension at most `k`. Then proper pushforward of `k`-cycles carries the cycle of `F`
to the cycle of the direct image: `f_* [F]_k = [f_* F]_k`.

The coherence of `f_* F`, which is what lets the right-hand cycle be formed, is the proper
mapping theorem [Stacks, Tag 02O5] in the form `Stacks.Chow.properDirectImageIsCoherent`: `Y` is
locally Noetherian because it is locally of finite type over the locally Noetherian base. The
equation itself is
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_unconditional (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsProper f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsCoherent :=
      haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
      properDirectImageIsCoherent f F
    properPushforward C sX sY f hf k (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sX F k hFk) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le C sX sY f hf F hFk)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02R6], part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over the base `S` of chapter 42, and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed subscheme with
`dim_δ(Z) ≤ k`. Then proper pushforward of `k`-cycles carries the cycle of `Z` to the cycle of
the direct image of its structure sheaf: `f_* [Z]_k = [f_* 𝒪_Z]_k`.

Here `𝒪_Z` is read as the coherent `𝒪_X`-module `i_* 𝒪_Z`, and the coherence of its direct image
along `f` is again [Stacks, Tag 02O5]. The equation is
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_unconditional (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ) (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))).IsCoherent :=
      haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
      properDirectImageIsCoherent f ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))
    properPushforward C sX sY f hf k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX i k) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))) k
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le C sX sY f hf
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))
          (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforwardStructureSheaf_le C sX i hZ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dense_image_irreducibleComponent_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R8.** Every irreducible component of the scheme-theoretic inverse image of an
irreducible closed subscheme along a flat morphism dominates that subscheme: the inverse image
is flat over the subscheme by base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem dense_image_irreducibleComponent_pullback {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f]
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IrreducibleSpace Z]
    (W : irreducibleComponents (pullback f i : Scheme.{u})) :
    closure ((pullback.snd f i).base '' (W : Set (pullback f i : Scheme.{u}))) = Set.univ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R8.** The scheme-theoretic inverse image of a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ Y` along
a flat morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of relative dimension `r` has delta-dimension `dim_δ(Z) + r`, as
soon as its projection to `Z` meets every irreducible component of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (r : ℕ)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hmeets : ∀ V : irreducibleComponents Z,
      ∃ x : (pullback f i : Scheme.{u}), (pullback.snd f i).base x ∈ (V : Set Z)) :
    schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.snd f i ≫ i ≫ g) =
      schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ g) + ((r : ℤ) : EInt)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.deltaDimension_irreducibleComponent_pullback_snd_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R8.** Over an irreducible closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ Y`, every irreducible
component of the scheme-theoretic inverse image along a flat morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of relative
dimension `r` has delta-dimension `dim_δ(Z) + r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deltaDimension_irreducibleComponent_pullback_snd_comp (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IrreducibleSpace Z]
    (W : irreducibleComponents (pullback f i : Scheme.{u})) :
    deltaDimension C (pullback.snd f i ≫ i ≫ g)
        ⟨(W : Set (pullback f i : Scheme.{u})), W.2.1,
          isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents (W : Set (pullback f i : Scheme.{u})) W.2⟩ =
      deltaDimension C (i ≫ g)
          ⟨Set.univ, IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ Z, isClosed_univ⟩ + (r : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp_eq_iSup_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R8**, the dimension formula for the inverse image, at the source's hypotheses.
The source asserts `dim_δ(f⁻¹(Z)) = dim_δ(Z) + r` for a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ Y` and a flat
`f : X ⟶ Y` of relative dimension `r`, provided `f⁻¹(Z)` is nonempty; that is false
(`Stacks.Chow.not_forall_schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp_of_nonempty`), because a component
of `Z` missed by the image of `f` counts in `dim_δ(Z)` and in nothing upstairs. What the source's
proof does establish, with no hypothesis beyond flatness and relative dimension `r`, is this:
`dim_δ(f⁻¹(Z))` is `r` more than the supremum of `dim_δ(V)` over the irreducible components `V`
of `Z` that `f⁻¹(Z)` lies over. When every irreducible component of `Z` has nonempty inverse
image that supremum is `dim_δ(Z)`, which is
`Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp_eq_iSup_add (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.snd f i ≫ i ≫ g) =
      (⨆ V : {V : irreducibleComponents Z //
          ∃ x : (pullback f i : Scheme.{u}), (pullback.snd f i).base x ∈ (V.1 : Set Z)},
          (deltaDimension C (i ≫ g)
            ⟨(V.1 : Set Z), V.1.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents (V.1 : Set Z) V.1.2⟩ :
            EInt)) + ((r : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: corrected dimension formula: sup over the components of Z met by f⁻¹(Z)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.not_forall_schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp_of_nonempty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R8**: the first claim, `dim_δ(f⁻¹(Z)) = dim_δ(Z) + r` for a closed subscheme
`Z ⊂ Y` provided only that `f⁻¹(Z)` is nonempty, is false. The counterexample is
`Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_firstPointInclusion_ne`; the corrected formula is
`Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp_eq_iSup_add`, and under the additional
hypothesis that every irreducible component of `Z` has nonempty inverse image the source's
formula holds, `Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_snd_comp_of_nonempty :
    ¬ ∀ (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
      (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (r : ℕ)
      (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i],
      Nonempty (pullback f i : Scheme.{u}) →
        schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.snd f i ≫ i ≫ g) =
          schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ g) + ((r : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: the first claim is false as stated: f⁻¹(Z) nonempty does not suffice

registrations.name: LocallyFinite.preimage_continuous
registrations.comment: the inverse image of a locally finite collection of subsets along a continuous map is locally finite

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
The flat pullback of the cycle of an integral closed subscheme
`i : Z ⟶ X` of delta-dimension `k` is the cycle of delta-dimension `k + r` of its
scheme-theoretic inverse image `X' ×_X Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X' X Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX' : X' ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX']
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (f : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (hbase : f ≫ sX = sX') (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (k : ℤ)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z]
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sX) = (k : EInt)) :
    flatPullback C sX' sX f hbase r hf k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX i k) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX' (pullback.fst f i) (k + (r : ℤ))
declarations.comment: pullback of an integral closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RB.** Flat pullback of cycles along a flat morphism of relative dimension `r`, as
a homomorphism `Z_k(X) ⟶ Z_{k+r}(X')`.
declarations.statement:
def flatPullback (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (sX' : X' ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX'] (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (f : X' ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sX = sX') (r : ℕ)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (k : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup C sX k →+ CycleGroup C sX' (k + (r : ℤ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupRestrict_surjective
declarations.doc: Restriction of cycles along an open immersion is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleGroupRestrict_surjective (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X U : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sU : U ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sU]
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : j ≫ sX = sU) (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Surjective (cycleGroupRestrict C sX sU j hj k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupRestrict_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
A cycle restricts to zero on the open complement exactly when it is the proper pushforward of
a cycle on the closed complement.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleGroupRestrict_eq_zero_iff (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y U : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (sU : U ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sU] (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : i ≫ sX = sY) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : j ≫ sX = sU)
    (hcomplement : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) (k : ℤ) (c : CycleGroup C sX k) :
    cycleGroupRestrict C sX sU j hj k c = 0 ↔
      ∃ d : CycleGroup C sY k, properPushforward C sY sX i hi k d = c

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RD.** For flat morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` of relative dimensions `r`
and `s`, flat pullback of cycles satisfies `f^* ∘ g^* = (g ∘ f)^*` as maps
`Z_k(Z) ⟶ Z_{k+r+s}(X)`.

That `f ≫ g` is flat is `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.comp` and that it has relative dimension
`r + s` is Stacks 02NL, `AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension.comp_of_flat`; both are recorded
against this tag in this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_comp (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (sZ : Z ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [Flat g] (hfbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (hgbase : g ≫ sZ = sY)
    (r s : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (hg : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension g s) (k : ℤ)
    (hcast : k + (s : ℤ) + (r : ℤ) = k + ((r + s : ℕ) : ℤ)) (c : CycleGroup C sZ k) :
    (hcast ▸ flatPullback C sX sY f hfbase r hf (k + (s : ℤ))
          (flatPullback C sY sZ g hgbase s hg k c) :
        CycleGroup C sX (k + ((r + s : ℕ) : ℤ))) =
      flatPullback C sX sZ (f ≫ g) (by rw [Category.assoc, hgbase, hfbase]) (r + s)
        (AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension.comp_of_flat f g hf hg) k c

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_of_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RE, part (1), cycle identity.** For `q : X' ⟶ X` flat of relative dimension `r`
between schemes locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, and `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed
subscheme of delta-dimension at most `k`, the flat pullback of the cycle `[Z]_k` is the cycle
`[q^{-1}(Z)]_{k+r}` of the scheme-theoretic inverse image, here presented as `pullback.fst q i`:

`q^*[Z]_k = [X' ×_X Z]_{k+r}`.

No irreducibility is assumed of `Z` and only an inequality on its delta-dimension is required,
so this is the full generality of the source; the integral case is
`Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme`, which carries `@[stacks 02RB]`.
The companion dimension bound `dim_δ(q^{-1}(Z)) ≤ k + r`, in the same presentation of the
inverse image, is `Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_le`.

The source deduces part (1) from part (2), and so does this proof: `[Z]_k` is the cycle of the
coherent sheaf `i_* 𝒪_Z` by Stacks 02QY, flat pullback commutes with passing to the cycle of a
coherent sheaf by Stacks 02RE part (2),
`Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf`, and the inverse image of `i_* 𝒪_Z`
along `q` is the direct image of the structure sheaf of `X' ×_X Z` — the identity
`q^* 𝒪_Z = 𝒪_{q^{-1}(Z)}` of the source — because a closed immersion is affine and so its
direct image commutes with the flat base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_of_le (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X' X Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX' : X' ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX']
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (q : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [Flat q]
    (hbase : q ≫ sX = sX') (r : ℕ) (hq : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension q r)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sX) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    flatPullback C sX' sX q hbase r hq k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX i k) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX' (pullback.fst q i) (k + (r : ℤ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ Y` flat of relative dimension `r` between schemes locally of finite type over
the base of chapter 42, and `F` a coherent sheaf on `Y` whose support has delta-dimension at most
`k`, the flat pullback of the cycle of `F` is the cycle of the pullback of `F`:

`f^*[F]_k = [f^*F]_{k+r}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (F : Y.Modules) [hF : F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sY) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    flatPullback C sX sY f hbase r hf k (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY F k hFk) =
      @cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf X C sX inferInstance
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback X Y
          (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX) f F hF)
        (k + (r : ℤ))
        (schemeDeltaDimension_support_pullback_le C sX sY f hbase r hf F k hFk)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_closedSubscheme_cycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RE, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r` between schemes
locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, and let `i : Z ⟶ Y` be a closed subscheme
with `dim_δ(Z) ≤ k`. Then the inverse image `f⁻¹ Z = X ×_Y Z` satisfies
`dim_δ(f⁻¹ Z) ≤ k + r`, and `[f⁻¹ Z]_{k+r} = f^*[Z]_k` in `Z_{k+r}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_closedSubscheme_cycle (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sY) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.fst f i ≫ sX) ≤ ((k + (r : ℤ) : ℤ) : EInt) ∧
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX (pullback.fst f i) (k + (r : ℤ)) =
        flatPullback C sX sY f hbase r hf k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY i k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_coherentSheaf_cycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RE, part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r` between schemes
locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, and let `F` be a coherent sheaf on `Y` with
`dim_δ(Supp F) ≤ k`. Then `f^*F` is coherent, `dim_δ(Supp f^*F) ≤ k + r`, and
`f^*[F]_k = [f^*F]_{k+r}` in `Z_{k+r}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_coherentSheaf_cycle (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (F : Y.Modules) [hF : F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sY) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F).IsCoherent :=
      AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback f F
    ∃ hFk' : schemeDeltaDimension C
        ((reducedSupport ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)).subschemeι ≫ sX) ≤
          ((k + (r : ℤ) : ℤ) : EInt),
      flatPullback C sX sY f hbase r hf k (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sY F k hFk) =
        cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C sX ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)
          (k + (r : ℤ)) hFk'

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RE, part (1), dimension bound.** The scheme-theoretic inverse image of a closed
subscheme of delta-dimension at most `k` under a flat morphism of relative dimension `r` has
delta-dimension at most `k + r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_le
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ sY) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.fst f i ≫ sX) ≤ ((k + (r : ℤ) : ℤ) : EInt)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_support_pullback_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RE, part (2), dimension bound.** If a coherent sheaf on `Y` has support of
delta-dimension at most `k`, then the support of its pullback along a flat morphism of relative
dimension `r` has delta-dimension at most `k + r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_support_pullback_le
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (F : Y.Modules) [hF : F.IsCoherent] (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sY) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    schemeDeltaDimension C
        ((@reducedSupport X ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)
          (@AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback X Y
            (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX) f F hF)).subschemeι ≫ sX) ≤
      ((k + (r : ℤ) : ℤ) : EInt)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isProper_and_relativeDimension_and_flatPullback_properPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Proper pushforward and flat pullback across a fibre product square.** Let

      X' --g'--> X
      |          |
      f'         f
      v          v
      Y' --g-->  Y

be a fibre product diagram of schemes locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, with
`f` proper and `g` flat of relative dimension `r`. Then `f'` is proper, `g'` is flat of relative
dimension `r` (flat, locally of finite type, and of relative dimension `r` in the sense of
Stacks 02NJ), and for every `k` and every `α ∈ Z_k(X)`,

`g^* f_* α = f'_* (g')^* α`  in  `Z_{k+r}(Y')`.

The first assertion is stability of properness under base change, the second is Stacks 02NK and
stability of flatness and of local finite type under base change, and the third is
`Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_properPushforward_unconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_and_relativeDimension_and_flatPullback_properPushforward
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (sX' : X' ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX'] (sY' : Y' ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY']
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (g : Y' ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [Flat g]
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (hg : g ≫ sY = sY') (hg' : g' ≫ sX = sX')
    (r : ℕ) (hgr : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension g r) :
    IsProper f' ∧ Flat g' ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType g' ∧
      @AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension _ _ g'
        (MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip inferInstance) r ∧
      ∀ (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup C sX k),
        letI : IsProper f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq inferInstance
        letI : LocallyOfFiniteType g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip inferInstance
        letI : Flat g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip inferInstance
        flatPullback C sY' sY g hg r hgr k (properPushforward C sX sY f hf k α) =
          properPushforward C sX' sY' f'
            (comp_structureMorphism_of_isPullback sX sY sX' sY' f g g' f' hsq hf hg hg')
            (k + (r : ℤ))
            (flatPullback C sX' sX g' hg' r
              (AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension.of_isPullback hsq.flip hgr) k α)
declarations.comment: all three assertions, under the source's hypotheses: f' is proper, g' is flat of relative dimension r, and g^* f_* alpha = f'_* (g')^* alpha in Z_{k+r}(Y') for every k and every k-cycle alpha on X

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_flatPullback_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RH, the second assertion.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` finite locally free of degree `d` over
the base,

  `f_* f^* α = d α`   in `Z_k(Y)`.

The statement transports the left hand side along the equality `k + 0 = k` of delta-dimensions,
which is the degree that pullback and pushforward along `f` produce; that equality is taken as a
hypothesis so that the statement typechecks, exactly as in
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_flatPullback`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_flatPullback` with its fibre-degree hypothesis discharged
by `Stacks.Chow.fibreDegreeIsRank_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_flatPullback_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ)
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d] (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ)
    (hcast : k + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k) (α : CycleGroup C sY k) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f :=
      Stacks.Morphisms.locallyOfFiniteType_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d
    letI : Flat f := Stacks.Morphisms.flat_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d
    letI : IsProper f := Stacks.Morphisms.isProper_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d
    (hcast ▸ properPushforward C sX sY f hbase (k + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
          (flatPullback C sX sY f hbase 0
            (Stacks.Morphisms.relativeDimension_zero_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d) k α) :
        CycleGroup C sY k) = (d : ℤ) • α

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ord
registrations.comment: the definition, indexed by the generic point ξ of Z (coheight ξ = 1)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ord_eq_ordHom_of_coheight_eq_one
registrations.comment: at a codimension-one point the value is ord of the stalk (Tag 02MD)

registrations.name: irreducibleSetEquivPoints
registrations.comment: prime divisors Z correspond to their generic points ξ, codim Z = coheight ξ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_primeDivisor_iff_codimension_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RK.** An integral closed subscheme of `X` is a prime divisor exactly when the
closure of its generic point has codimension one in `X`. This is the definition of a prime
divisor, read through the presentation of an integral closed subscheme by its ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_primeDivisor_iff_codimension_one {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsIntegral I.subscheme) :
    (∃ D : Stacks.Divisors.PrimeDivisor X, D.idealSheaf = I) ↔
      codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton (genericPointOf I hI)) = 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.codimension_one_iff_schemeDeltaDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RK.** An integral closed subscheme of an integral scheme `X` locally of finite
type over the base has codimension one exactly when its delta-dimension is one less than that
of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimension_one_iff_schemeDeltaDimension (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsIntegral X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsIntegral I.subscheme) :
    codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton (genericPointOf I hI)) = 1 ↔
      schemeDeltaDimension C (I.subschemeι ≫ f) = schemeDeltaDimension C f + (-1 : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.deltaDimension_irreducibleComponent_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RK.** Every irreducible component of an effective Cartier divisor on an integral
scheme locally of finite type over the base has delta-dimension one less than the ambient
scheme.

The generic point of such a component has ambient local ring of Krull dimension one, hence
coheight one, which is exactly the hypothesis of
`Stacks.Chow.deltaDimension_irreducibleComponent_of_coheight_eq_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deltaDimension_irreducibleComponent_isEffectiveCartierDivisor (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsIntegral X]
    (D : X.IdealSheafData) (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    (Z : irreducibleComponents D.subscheme) :
    (deltaDimension C (D.subschemeι ≫ f)
        ⟨Z, Z.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents (Z : Set D.subscheme) Z.2⟩ : EInt) =
      schemeDeltaDimension C f + (-1 : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.locallyFinite_closure_notMem_range_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RL.** On a locally Noetherian integral scheme the prime divisors at whose generic
point `ξ` a rational function `f` does not lie in the local ring `O_{X,ξ}` form a locally finite
