collection of closed subsets of `X`. A prime divisor is indexed by its generic point, so the
collection is the family of closures of the codimension-one points `z` with `f ∉ O_{X,z}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_closure_notMem_range_algebraMap (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (f : X.functionField) :
    LocallyFinite fun z : {z : X // coheight z = 1 ∧
        f ∉ Set.range (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField)} ↦
      closure ({(z : X)} : Set X)
declarations.comment: the prime divisors with f ∉ O_{X,ξ}; no hypothesis f ≠ 0 needed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.locallyFiniteSupport_ord
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RL.** On a locally Noetherian integral scheme the prime divisors along which a
rational function `f` has nonzero order form a locally finite collection: the support of
`z ↦ ord_z(f)` meets a neighbourhood of every point in a finite set.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFiniteSupport_ord (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X.functionField) : LocallyFiniteSupport (X.ord f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_module_finite_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02RM.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and `ξ` a point of
`Y`. Assume that `X` and `Y` are integral, that `Y` is locally Noetherian, that `f` is proper and
dominant with `R(Y) ⊂ R(X)` finite, and that `dim (𝒪_{Y, ξ}) = 1`. Then there is an open
neighbourhood `V` of `ξ` such that the restriction `f⁻¹(V) → V` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_module_finite_functionField
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (ξ : Y) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] [IsDominant f]
    (hfin : letI := (functionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
      Module.Finite Y.functionField X.functionField)
    (hξ : ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, ξ ∈ V ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
The principal divisor `div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]` of a rational function on an integral
scheme `X` of delta-dimension `n` locally of finite type over the base, as an element of the
group `Z_{n-1}(X)` of cycles of delta-dimension `n - 1`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalCycle_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RP.** The principal divisor of a product of nonzero rational functions is the sum
of the principal divisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalCycle_mul (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {f g : X.functionField} (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    principalCycle X (f * g) = principalCycle X f + principalCycle X g

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.graphProjection_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of Stacks Project, Tag 02RQ.** The projection `p : Y ⟶ X` is proper. No
hypothesis on `X`, on `U` or on the section is needed: `Y` is closed in `X ×_S ℙ¹_S`, which is
proper over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem graphProjection_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ S) (U : X.Opens)
    (s : Γ(X, U)) : IsProper (graphProjection sX U s)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isIso_graphProjection_morphismRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks Project, Tag 02RQ.** The restriction `p|_{p⁻¹(U)} : p⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` of the
projection `p : Y ⟶ X` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_graphProjection_morphismRestrict (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
    IsIso (graphProjection sX U s ∣_ U)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isPullbackDefined_graphFibres
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of Stacks Project, Tag 02RQ.** The pullbacks `Y₀ = q⁻¹D₀` and `Y_∞ = q⁻¹D_∞` of
the zero and infinity divisors of `ℙ¹_S` along `q : Y ⟶ ℙ¹_S` are defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_graphFibres [IsIntegral X] (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U.toScheme]
    (g : (Γ(X, U))ˣ) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined (graphLineProjection sX U ↑g) (lineZeroDivisor C.S) ∧
      Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined (graphLineProjection sX U ↑g)
        (lineInfinityDivisor C.S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorCycle_graphClosure_eq_fibreCycles_sub
declarations.doc:
**Part (4) of Stacks Project, Tag 02RQ.** On `Y`, the principal divisor of the rational
function `f` is the difference `[Y₀]_{n-1} - [Y_∞]_{n-1}` of the cycles of the two fibres.

Here `f` on `Y` is the pullback of the invertible section `g` to the dense open `p⁻¹(U)`, carried
to the function field by `Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalDivisorCycle_graphClosure_eq_fibreCycles_sub [IsIntegral X] (n : ℤ)
    (dimX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt)) (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U.toScheme]
    (g : (Γ(X, U))ˣ) :
    principalDivisorCycle C (graphBaseMorphism sX U ↑g)
        (schemeDeltaDimension_graphClosure_of_chowSituation C sX n dimX U g)
        ((rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField (graphClosure sX U ↑g)).1
          ↑(graphRationalFunction sX U g (graphPreimageDense_of_chowSituation C sX U ↑g))) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (graphBaseMorphism sX U ↑g)
          (graphZeroFiber sX U ↑g).subschemeι (n - 1) -
        cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (graphBaseMorphism sX U ↑g)
          (graphInfinityFiber sX U ↑g).subschemeι (n - 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorCycle_eq_properPushforward_graphClosure
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of Stacks Project, Tag 02RQ.** The principal divisor of `f` on `X` is the proper
pushforward along `p : Y ⟶ X` of the principal divisor of `f` on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalDivisorCycle_eq_properPushforward_graphClosure [IsIntegral X] (n : ℤ)
    (dimX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt)) (f : (rationalFunctions X)ˣ) (U : X.Opens)
    [Nonempty U.toScheme] (g : (Γ(X, U))ˣ)
    (f_eq : ofSection X ⟨U, dense_opens_of_nonempty U⟩ ↑g = (f : rationalFunctions X)) :
    principalDivisorCycle C sX dimX ((rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField X).1 ↑f) =
      properPushforward C (graphBaseMorphism sX U ↑g) sX (graphProjection sX U ↑g) rfl (n - 1)
        (principalDivisorCycle C (graphBaseMorphism sX U ↑g)
          (schemeDeltaDimension_graphClosure_of_chowSituation C sX n dimX U g)
          ((rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField (graphClosure sX U ↑g)).1
            ↑(graphRationalFunction sX U g (graphPreimageDense_of_chowSituation C sX U ↑g))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorCycle_eq_imageFibreCycles_sub
declarations.doc:
**Part (6) of Stacks Project, Tag 02RQ.** Viewing `Y₀` and `Y_∞` as closed subschemes of `X`
through `p : Y ⟶ X`, the principal divisor of `f` on `X` is `[Y₀]_{n-1} - [Y_∞]_{n-1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalDivisorCycle_eq_imageFibreCycles_sub [IsIntegral X] (n : ℤ)
    (dimX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt)) (f : (rationalFunctions X)ˣ) (U : X.Opens)
    [Nonempty U.toScheme] (g : (Γ(X, U))ˣ)
    (f_eq : ofSection X ⟨U, dense_opens_of_nonempty U⟩ ↑g = (f : rationalFunctions X)) :
    principalDivisorCycle C sX dimX ((rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField X).1 ↑f) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX
          ((graphZeroFiber sX U ↑g).subschemeι ≫ graphProjection sX U ↑g) (n - 1) -
        cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX
          ((graphInfinityFiber sX U ↑g).subschemeι ≫ graphProjection sX U ↑g) (n - 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_principalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
Let `C = (S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X` and `Y` be integral and
locally of finite type over `S` with `n = dim_δ(Y)`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative
dimension `r`. For a nonzero rational function `g` on `Y`,

  `f^* div_Y(g) = div_X(g)`

in `Z_{n + r - 1}(X)`, where `g` is read on `X` through the extension `R(Y) ⊆ R(X)` of function
fields induced by `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_principalDivisorCycle (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) {n : ℤ}
    (hY : schemeDeltaDimension C sY = (n : EInt)) (g : Y.functionField) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    (flatPullback C sX sY f hbase r hf (n - 1) (principalDivisorCycle C sY hY g)).1 =
      (principalDivisorCycle C sX
        (schemeDeltaDimension_eq_add_of_flat C sX sY f hbase r hf hY)
        (dominantFunctionFieldMap f g)).1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RT.** For a dominant proper morphism `p : X ⟶ Y` of integral schemes locally of
finite type over the base with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, the proper pushforward of the principal
divisor of a nonzero rational function `f` on `X` is the principal divisor of the norm of `f` in
the extension `R(Y) ⊆ R(X)` of function fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] {n : ℤ}
    (hnX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : schemeDeltaDimension C sY = (n : EInt))
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper p] [IsDominant p] (hp : p ≫ sY = sX)
    (f : X.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := (dominantFunctionFieldMap p).toAlgebra
    properPushforward C sX sY p hp (n - 1) (principalDivisorCycle C sX hnX f) =
      principalDivisorCycle C sY hnY (Algebra.norm Y.functionField f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The degree of a principal divisor on a proper curve over a field vanishes.** For a Chow
situation whose base is the spectrum of a field with vanishing dimension function, a proper
integral `X` of delta-dimension one over that base, and an invertible rational function `f` on `X`,
the proper pushforward of `div(f)` to the base is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_zero
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (hS : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))
    (hδ : ∀ p : C.S, C.dimensionFunction p = 0)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (c : X ⟶ C.S) [IsProper c] [IsIntegral X]
    (hdim : schemeDeltaDimension C c = (1 : EInt))
    (f : (rationalFunctions X)ˣ) :
    properPushforward C c (𝟙 C.S) c (by simp) 0
      (principalDivisorCycle C c hdim ((rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField X).1 ↑f)) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorDegree_eq_zero_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RU in the displayed-sum form.** For a proper integral curve over a field the
weighted sum `∑_x ord_x(f) · [κ(x) : k]` of the orders of vanishing of an invertible rational
function vanishes. This is the other form of
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_zero`, the two being identified by
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_zero_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalDivisorDegree_eq_zero_of_isProper
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (hS : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))
    (hδ : ∀ p : C.S, C.dimensionFunction p = 0)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (c : X ⟶ C.S) [IsProper c] [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hdim : schemeDeltaDimension C c = (1 : EInt))
    (f : (rationalFunctions X)ˣ) :
    principalDivisorDegree c ((rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField X).1 ↑f) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorDegree_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02RU.** Let `X` be an integral scheme of dimension one, proper over a
field `k`. Then the degree of the principal divisor of a nonzero rational function `f` on `X`
vanishes:

  `∑_{x ∈ X} ord_x(f) · [κ(x) : k] = 0`.

The normalization `ν : X^ν ⟶ X` is a proper dominant birational morphism from a normal curve, so
the normal case applies to the image `F` of `f` in `R(X^ν)`, and the norm formula of Stacks 02RT
identifies `deg div_{X^ν}(F)` with `deg div_X(Nm(F)) = deg div_X(f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalDivisorDegree_eq_zero (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))]
    [IsCurve k (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))]
    [IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    principalDivisorDegree (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k)) f = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_zero_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02RU**, in its cycle form: the proper pushforward to `Spec k` of the
principal divisor of a nonzero rational function on a proper integral curve vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_zero_of_isCurve (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))]
    [IsCurve k (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))]
    [IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (c : X ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [IsProper c]
    (hc : c = X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k))
    (hdim : schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k) c = ((1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (f : X.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    properPushforward (fieldChowSituation k) c (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S) c
        (Category.comp_id c) 0
      (principalDivisorCycle (fieldChowSituation k) c hdim f) = 0
declarations.comment: the pushforward of the principal divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_principalDivisorFamilySum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RW.** A locally finite family of integral closed subschemes of `X` of
delta-dimension `k + 1`, each carrying a nonzero rational function, determines a cycle of
delta-dimension `k` on `X`, whose coefficients are the locally finite sums of the coefficients
of the pushed-forward principal divisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_principalDivisorFamilySum (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) {J : Type u} (W : J → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : ∀ j, IsIntegral (W j).subscheme)
    (hDim : ∀ j, schemeDeltaDimension C ((W j).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hLocal : LocallyFinite fun j ↦ ((W j).support : Set X))
    (g : ∀ j, (rationalFunctions (W j).subscheme)ˣ) :
    ∃ α : CycleGroup C p k,
      ∀ x : X, α.1 x = principalDivisorFamilyCoefficient C p W hW g x
declarations.comment: locally finite sums of principal divisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsRationallyEquivalentToZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RW.** A `k`-cycle is rationally equivalent to zero when its coefficients are the
locally finite sum of the pushforwards of the principal divisors of nonzero rational functions
on a locally finite family of integral closed subschemes of delta-dimension `k + 1`.
declarations.statement:
def IsRationallyEquivalentToZero (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup C p k) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalentToZero_zero
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02RW.** The zero cycle is rationally equivalent to zero, via the empty family.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalentToZero_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RW.** The sum of two cycles rationally equivalent to zero is rationally
equivalent to zero, via the disjoint union of the two families.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalentToZero_neg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RW.** The negative of a cycle rationally equivalent to zero is rationally
equivalent to zero, via the inverses of the same rational functions.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalences
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02RW.** The subgroup of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement:
def rationalEquivalences (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) : AddSubgroup (CycleGroup C p k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.RationallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RW.** Two `k`-cycles are rationally equivalent when their difference is a locally
finite sum of pushforwards of principal divisors.
declarations.statement:
abbrev RationallyEquivalent (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) (α β : CycleGroup C p k) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowGroup
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02RW.** The Chow group `A_k(X)` of `k`-cycles modulo rational equivalence.
declarations.statement:
abbrev chowGroup (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) : Type u

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_rationallyEquivalent_properPushforward_of_cycleGroupRestrict
declarations.doc:
Let `V ⊆ X` be an open subscheme and let `i : Y ⟶ X` be a closed immersion whose image is the
complement of `V`. If two `k`-cycles on `X` become rationally equivalent after restriction to `V`,
then they are rationally equivalent on `X` up to the pushforward of a `k`-cycle on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rationallyEquivalent_properPushforward_of_cycleGroupRestrict
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : i ≫ sX = sY)
    (V : X.Opens) (hcomplement : Set.range i.base = (Set.range V.ι.base)ᶜ)
    (k : ℤ) (α β : CycleGroup C sX k)
    (h : RationallyEquivalent C (V.ι ≫ sX) k
      (cycleGroupOpensRestrict C sX V k α) (cycleGroupOpensRestrict C sX V k β)) :
    ∃ γ : CycleGroup C sY k,
      RationallyEquivalent C sX k α (β + properPushforward C sY sX i hi k γ)
declarations.comment: lifting a rational equivalence from an open subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.surjective_chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
The localization sequence of Chow groups is exact at `A_k(V)`: restriction of `k`-cycle
classes to an open subscheme `V ⊆ X` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (V : X.Opens) (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Surjective (chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion C sX V k)
declarations.comment: surjectivity onto the Chow group of the open subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exact_chowPushforward_chowGroupOpensRestrict
declarations.doc:
The localization sequence of Chow groups is exact at `A_k(X)`: for an open subscheme `V ⊆ X`
and a closed immersion `i : Y ⟶ X` whose image is the complement of `V`, a `k`-cycle class on `X`
restricts to zero on `V` exactly when it is the pushforward of a `k`-cycle class on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_chowPushforward_chowGroupOpensRestrict (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : i ≫ sX = sY)
    (V : X.Opens) (hcomplement : Set.range i.base = (Set.range V.ι.base)ᶜ) (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Exact (chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C sY sX i hi k)
      (chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion C sX V k)
declarations.comment: exactness at the Chow group of the ambient scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalent_finsum_of_closedSupports
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02RZ, two-sided form.** Rational equivalences on a locally finite family of closed
subschemes of `X` may be summed: if cycles `a i` and `b i` on the closed subschemes `T i` are
rationally equivalent for each `i`, and the cycles `α`, `β` on `X` are coefficientwise the locally
finite sums of the pushforwards of the `a i` and of the `b i`, then `α` and `β` are rationally
equivalent on `X`.

Both locally finite sums have finite support at each point, because the pushforward of a cycle on
`T i` is supported on `(T i).support` and the family of those supports is locally finite. So they
may be subtracted termwise, which exhibits `α - β` as the locally finite sum of the pushforwards of
the `a i - b i`, each rationally equivalent to zero, and
`Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalentToZero_finsum_of_closedSupports` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalent_finsum_of_closedSupports (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) {I : Type u} (T : I → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hT : LocallyFinite fun i ↦ ((T i).support : Set X))
    (a b : ∀ i, CycleGroup C ((T i).subschemeι ≫ p) k)
    (hab : ∀ i, RationallyEquivalent C ((T i).subschemeι ≫ p) k (a i) (b i))
    {α β : CycleGroup C p k}
    (hα : ∀ x : X, α.1 x = ∑ᶠ i : I,
      (properPushforward C ((T i).subschemeι ≫ p) p (T i).subschemeι rfl k (a i)).1 x)
    (hβ : ∀ x : X, β.1 x = ∑ᶠ i : I,
      (properPushforward C ((T i).subschemeι ≫ p) p (T i).subschemeι rfl k (b i)).1 x) :
    RationallyEquivalent C p k α β

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S1 along an arbitrary open immersion.** Flat pullback along an open immersion over
the base carries cycles rationally equivalent to zero to cycles rationally equivalent to zero.

Flat pullback along an open immersion in relative dimension zero is restriction of cycles, by
`Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupRestrict_eq_flatPullback`, up to a transport of the degree from `k + 0` to
`k`; the statement for restriction is
`Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupRestrict_mem_rationalEquivalences`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isOpenImmersion :
    FlatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sU sX j hj 0
      (relativeDimension_of_isOpenImmersion j) k
declarations.comment: flat pullback along an arbitrary open immersion preserves rational equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S1.** Flat pullback of `k`-cycles along a morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of schemes locally
of finite type over the base which is flat and locally of finite type of relative dimension `r`
carries cycles rationally equivalent to zero to cycles rationally equivalent to zero.

A presentation `∑_j (i_j)_* div_{W_j}(g_j)` of a rational equivalence on `X` by a locally finite
family of integral closed subschemes `W_j ⊆ X` of delta-dimension `k + 1` is pulled back term by
term. The closed-immersion case of Stacks 02RG rewrites the pullback of each term as a pushforward
from the scheme-theoretic inverse image `f^{-1}(W_j)` of a cycle on `f^{-1}(W_j)`, which is
rationally equivalent to zero there by the case of Stacks 02S1 for a principal divisor on an
integral target. Those inverse images have as supports the preimages of the supports of the `W_j`,
so they form a locally finite family by Stacks 02R9, and Stacks 02RZ sums the pushforwards into a
single rational equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (sX' : X' ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX'] (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (f : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (hbase : f ≫ sX = sX') (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) (k : ℤ) :
    FlatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sX' sX f hbase r hf k
declarations.comment: the general case: an arbitrary flat morphism of relative dimension r

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_opensι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S1 along the inclusion of an open subscheme.** Flat pullback of `k`-cycles along
the inclusion of an open subscheme `V ⊆ X` carries cycles rationally equivalent to zero to cycles
rationally equivalent to zero.

A presentation `∑_j (i_j)_* div(g_j)` of a rational equivalence on `X`, by a locally finite family
of integral closed subschemes `W_j` of delta-dimension `k + 1`, restricts to the presentation by
the inverse images `W_j ×_X V` of those members whose generic point lies in `V`, carrying the
restrictions of the `g_j`. The members whose generic point misses `V` are supported off `V` and
contribute nothing there; the surviving inverse images are integral by
`Stacks.Chow.comap_integralComponentAt_of_isOpenImmersion`, keep their delta-dimension by
`Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_eq_of_isOpenImmersion`, form a locally finite family because
their supports are preimages, and their terms have the right coefficients by
`Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorPushforward_comap_opensι`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_opensι (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (V : X.Opens) (k : ℤ) :
    FlatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C (V.ι ≫ f) f V.ι rfl 0
      (relativeDimension_opensι V) k
declarations.comment: flat pullback along an open immersion preserves rational equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isRationallyEquivalentToZero_of_coe_eq_flatPullback_principalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S1 for a principal divisor on an integral target.** Let `X` and `Y` be locally of
finite type over the base of chapter 42 with `Y` integral of delta-dimension `k`, let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r`, and let `g` be a nonzero rational function on `Y`.
Then the flat pullback `f^* div_Y(g)` of the principal divisor of `g` is rationally equivalent to
zero, as a `(k + r - 1)`-cycle on `X`.

Stacks 0EPH writes that pullback as the locally finite sum `∑_j n_j (i_j)_* div_{X_j}(g)` over the
irreducible components `X_j` of `X` taken with their reduced structure. Each `X_j` is integral of
delta-dimension `k + r`, so `div_{X_j}(g)` is rationally equivalent to zero on `X_j` by Stacks
02RW, and the multiplicity `n_j` is absorbed by the subgroup. The components form a locally finite
family by Stacks 0BE1, so Stacks 02RZ sums the pushforwards into a single rational equivalence
on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRationallyEquivalentToZero_of_coe_eq_flatPullback_principalDivisorCycle
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [IsIntegral Y] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) {k j : ℤ}
    (hY : schemeDeltaDimension C sY = (k : EInt)) {g : Y.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (hj : j = k + (r : ℤ) - 1) (α : CycleGroup C sX j)
    (hα : ∀ x : X, α.1 x =
      (flatPullback C sX sY f hbase r hf (k - 1) (principalDivisorCycle C sY hY g)).1 x) :
    IsRationallyEquivalentToZero C sX j α
declarations.comment: the case of a principal divisor on an integral target

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Proper pushforward of `k`-cycles along a proper morphism over the base carries cycles
rationally equivalent to zero to cycles rationally equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper (k : ℤ) :
    ProperPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sX sY p hp k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_rationallyEquivalent_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Proper pushforward preserves rational equivalence of cycles: if `α` and `β` are rationally
equivalent `k`-cycles on `X` and `p : X ⟶ Y` is proper over the base, then `p_*α` and `p_*β` are
rationally equivalent `k`-cycles on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_rationallyEquivalent_of_isProper (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (p : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper p] (hp : p ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ)
    {α β : CycleGroup C sX k} (h : RationallyEquivalent C sX k α β) :
    RationallyEquivalent C sY k (properPushforward C sX sY p hp k α)
      (properPushforward C sX sY p hp k β)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroDivisor_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02S4, part (1), for the zero divisor.** If `W` is integral and is not
contained in the image of the zero section, then the zero divisor of `W` is an effective Cartier
divisor on `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroDivisor_isEffectiveCartierDivisor [IsIntegral W.subscheme]
    (h : ¬ Set.range W.subschemeι ⊆ Set.range (zeroSection f)) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (zeroDivisor f W)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.infinityDivisor_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02S4, part (1), for the infinity divisor.** If `W` is integral and is
not contained in the image of the infinity section, then the infinity divisor of `W` is an
effective Cartier divisor on `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem infinityDivisor_isEffectiveCartierDivisor [IsIntegral W.subscheme]
    (h : ¬ Set.range W.subschemeι ⊆ Set.range (infinitySection f)) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (infinityDivisor f W)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_familyFibreDifferences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02S4, part (4).** A `k`-cycle rationally equivalent to zero is the
total fibre difference of a locally finite family of integral closed subschemes of
`X ×_S 𝐏¹_S`, each of relative dimension `k + 1` at its generic points and contained in
neither distinguished section.

This is the converse of part (3): the family is produced from the family of integral closed
subschemes and rational functions witnessing rational equivalence, by replacing each member by
the closure of the graph of its rational function, read inside `X ×_S 𝐏¹_S`. The index type is
unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_familyFibreDifferences (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup C f k)
    (hα : IsRationallyEquivalentToZero C f k α) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (W : J → (projectiveLineProduct f).IdealSheafData),
      (∀ j, IsIntegral (W j).subscheme) ∧
      (∀ j, ∀ ξ : genericPoints (W j).subscheme,
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f (W j)) ξ.1 = k + 1) ∧
      (∀ j, ¬ Set.range (W j).subschemeι ⊆ Set.range (zeroSection f)) ∧
      (∀ j, ¬ Set.range (W j).subschemeι ⊆ Set.range (infinitySection f)) ∧
      LocallyFinite (fun j ↦ ((W j).support : Set (projectiveLineProduct f))) ∧
      (∀ x : X, α.1 x = familyFibreDifferenceCoefficient C f k W x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.fibreCycles_rationallyEquivalent
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02S4 part (2), in the two-cycle form the tag states.**
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreCycles_rationallyEquivalent
    (W : (projectiveLineProduct f).IdealSheafData) [IsIntegral W.subscheme]
    (hDim : ∀ ξ : genericPoints W.subscheme,
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f W) ξ.1 = k + 1)
    (h₀ : ¬ Set.range W.subschemeι ⊆ Set.range (zeroSection f))
    (hInf : ¬ Set.range W.subschemeι ⊆ Set.range (infinitySection f)) :
    RationallyEquivalent C f k
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (zeroFiber f W).subschemeι k)
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (infinityFiber f W).subschemeι k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.familyFibreDifferencesRationallyEquivalentToZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S4 part (3).** The family form, for a locally finite family of integral closed
subschemes of `X ×_S ℙ¹_S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem familyFibreDifferencesRationallyEquivalentToZero :
    FamilyFibreDifferencesRationallyEquivalentToZero C f k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToFibres_rationallyEquivalent_of_isEmbeddedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S5, with hypothesis (3) in the shape the source states it.** For a closed
subscheme `Z ⊆ X ×_S 𝐏¹_S` with `dim_δ(Z) ≤ k + 1` and `dim_δ(Z₀) ≤ k`, `dim_δ(Z_∞) ≤ k`, the
cycles of the two fibres are rationally equivalent on `X` as soon as

* `hEmbedded`, the source's hypothesis (3): every embedded point of `Z` either misses both
  distinguished sections or has relative dimension below `k`; and
* `hGeneric`, the clause the source omits: no irreducible component of `Z` of relative dimension
  exactly `k` has its generic point on a distinguished section.

`hGeneric` cannot be dropped — see the module documentation for an integral `Z` with no embedded
points at all for which the conclusion fails. Together the two clauses give the hypothesis of
`Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToFibres_rationallyEquivalent`, by
`Stacks.Chow.sectionAvoidance_of_isEmbeddedPoint_of_genericPoints`, and are given by it, by
`Stacks.Chow.mem_schemeAssociatedPoints_of_isEmbeddedPoint` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.mem_schemeAssociatedPoints_of_isGenericPoint_irreducibleComponent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToFibres_rationallyEquivalent_of_isEmbeddedPoint
    (hZ : ∀ ζ : Z.subscheme,
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f Z) ζ ≤ k + 1)
    (h₀ : schemeDeltaDimension C ((zeroFiber f Z).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hInf : schemeDeltaDimension C ((infinityFiber f Z).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hEmbedded : ∀ ζ : Z.subscheme, AlgebraicGeometry.IsEmbeddedPoint Z.subscheme ζ →
      ((Z.subschemeι ζ ∉ Set.range (zeroSection f) ∧
          Z.subschemeι ζ ∉ Set.range (infinitySection f)) ∨
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f Z) ζ < k))
    (hGeneric : ∀ ζ : Z.subscheme, ζ ∈ genericPoints Z.subscheme →
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f Z) ζ = k →
      (Z.subschemeι ζ ∉ Set.range (zeroSection f) ∧
        Z.subschemeι ζ ∉ Set.range (infinitySection f))) :
    RationallyEquivalent C f k
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (zeroFiber f Z).subschemeι k)
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (infinityFiber f Z).subschemeι k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToFibres_rationallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S5.** For a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X ×_S ℙ¹_S` whose relative dimension is at most
`k + 1`, whose two fibres have delta-dimension at most `k`, and each of whose associated points
either misses both distinguished sections or has relative dimension below `k`, the cycles of the
two fibres are rationally equivalent on `X`.

Both inputs are now theorems: the decomposition rule is
`Stacks.Chow.fibreCycleComponentDecompositionRule` and part (2) of Stacks 02S4 is
`Stacks.Chow.fibreCyclesRationallyEquivalentWithin`.

The source states its hypothesis (3) for the *embedded* points of `Z` rather than for all of
its associated points. That reading is strictly weaker and the lemma is false under it; the two
differ exactly at the generic points of the irreducible components of `Z` of relative dimension
`k`, which the source's proof silently assumes away when it reads `dim(A/I) = 1` off
`δ(ξ) = k`. `Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToFibres_rationallyEquivalent_of_isEmbeddedPoint`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Chow/FibreCycles/EmbeddedPointHypothesis.lean`) states the
hypothesis in the source's two-clause shape and documents the counterexample.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToFibres_rationallyEquivalent
    (Z : (projectiveLineProduct f).IdealSheafData)
    (hZ : ∀ ζ : Z.subscheme,
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f Z) ζ ≤ k + 1)
    (h₀ : schemeDeltaDimension C ((zeroFiber f Z).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hInf : schemeDeltaDimension C ((infinityFiber f Z).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hAssociated : ∀ ζ : Z.subscheme,
      ζ ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Z.subscheme →
      ((Z.subschemeι ζ ∉ Set.range (zeroSection f) ∧
          Z.subschemeι ζ ∉ Set.range (infinitySection f)) ∨
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase f Z) ζ < k)) :
    RationallyEquivalent C f k
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (zeroFiber f Z).subschemeι k)
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (infinityFiber f Z).subschemeι k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToCoherentFibres_rationallyEquivalent_of_decompositionRule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 02S6.** For a coherent sheaf `F` on `X ×_S 𝐏¹_S` whose support has relative
dimension at most `k + 1`, whose two fibres have delta-dimension at most `k`, and each of whose
associated points either misses both distinguished sections or has relative dimension below `k`,
the cycles `[F₀]_k` and `[F_∞]_k` of the two fibres are rationally equivalent.

The two inputs are `Stacks.Chow.coherentFibreCycleDecompositionRule`, the claim in the source's
proof, and `Stacks.Chow.familyFibreDifferencesRationallyEquivalentToZero`, Tag 02S4 part (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleAssociatedToCoherentFibres_rationallyEquivalent_of_decompositionRule
    [F.IsCoherent]
    (hSupp : ∀ ξ : projectiveLineProduct f, ξ ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F →
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (productBase f) ξ ≤ k + 1)
    (h₀ : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport (zeroFibreModule f F)).subschemeι ≫ f)
      ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hInf : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport (infinityFibreModule f F)).subschemeι ≫ f)
      ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hAssociated : ∀ ξ : projectiveLineProduct f, ξ ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F →
      ((ξ ∉ Set.range (zeroSection f) ∧ ξ ∉ Set.range (infinitySection f)) ∨
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (productBase f) ξ < k)) :
    RationallyEquivalent C f k
      (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f (zeroFibreModule f F) k h₀)
      (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f (infinityFibreModule f F) k hInf)
declarations.comment: all three hypotheses and the conclusion, with hypothesis (3) quantified over every associated point of F, as the source's own proof of this lemma uses it ('since ξ is not an associated point of F by assumption (3)'). The published statement of the tag quantifies (3) over the embedded associated points only; that reading is false, by the counterexample in the module documentation, so it is not what is registered here

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalent_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_fibres
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S6.** Let `F` be a coherent sheaf on `X ×_S 𝐏¹_S` with
`dim_δ(Supp(F)) ≤ k + 1`, with `dim_δ(Supp(F₀)) ≤ k` and `dim_δ(Supp(F_∞)) ≤ k`, and such that
every associated point `ξ` of `F` lies outside the union of the two distinguished sections or has
`δ(ξ) < k`. Then `[F₀]_k` and `[F_∞]_k` are rationally equivalent `k`-cycles on `X`.

The coherence of `F₀` and `F_∞`, needed to form their cycles, is Stacks 0EBF and is supplied in
the statement rather than assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalent_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_fibres
    (F : (projectiveLineProduct f).Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hSupp : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ productBase f) ≤
      ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (h₀ : haveI := isCoherent_zeroFibreModule C f F
      schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport (zeroFibreModule f F)).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤
        (k : EInt))
    (hInf : haveI := isCoherent_infinityFibreModule C f F
      schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport (infinityFibreModule f F)).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤
        (k : EInt))
    (hAssociated : ∀ ξ ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F,
      ξ ∉ Set.range (zeroSection f) ∪ Set.range (infinitySection f) ∨
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (productBase f) ξ < k) :
    haveI := isCoherent_zeroFibreModule C f F
    haveI := isCoherent_infinityFibreModule C f F
    RationallyEquivalent C f k
      (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f (zeroFibreModule f F) k h₀)
      (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f (infinityFibreModule f F) k hInf)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.coherentModulesDimLE_isSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S8.** Coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose support has delta-dimension at most `k` form a
Serre subcategory of the category of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance coherentModulesDimLE_isSerreClass (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) : (coherentModulesDimLE C f k).IsSerreClass

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom_integralComponentLayerClass
declarations.doc:
The cycle class homomorphism sends the class of `𝒪_Z` to the cycle `[Z]` of the integral closed
subscheme `Z` attached to a point of relative dimension `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerCycleHom_integralComponentLayerClass (x : X)
    (hx : relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f x = k) :
    dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k (integralComponentLayerClass C f k x) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (integralComponentAt x).subschemeι k
declarations.comment: the map `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})` on a prime cycle: the class of `𝒪_Z` has cycle `[Z]`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom_finsum_integralComponentLayerClass
declarations.doc:
The cycle of the class `∑ n_Z[𝒪_Z]` attached to a `k`-cycle `∑ n_Z[Z]` of finite support is
`∑ n_Z[Z]` again.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerCycleHom_finsum_integralComponentLayerClass (α : CycleGroup C f k)
    (hα : (Function.support (α.1 : X → ℤ)).Finite) :
    dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k
        (∑ᶠ x : X, α.1 x • integralComponentLayerClass C f k x) = α
declarations.comment: the inverse identity `[∑ n_Z 𝒪_Z]_k = ∑ n_Z[Z]`, for a `k`-cycle of finite support

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.mem_range_dimensionLayerCycleHom_of_finite_support
declarations.doc:
Every `k`-cycle with finite support is the cycle of a class in the Grothendieck group of the
dimension layer, namely of the weighted sum of the classes of the structure sheaves of the integral
closed subschemes it is supported on.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_range_dimensionLayerCycleHom_of_finite_support (α : CycleGroup C f k)
    (hα : (Function.support (α.1 : X → ℤ)).Finite) :
    α ∈ (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k).range
declarations.comment: every `k`-cycle of finite support is in the image of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) → Z_k(X)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerClassHom
declarations.doc:
The map `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` for `X` quasi-compact: a `k`-cycle `∑ n_Z[Z]`
is sent to `∑ n_Z[𝒪_Z]`, the coefficients weighting the classes of the structure sheaves of the
integral closed subschemes occurring in the cycle.
declarations.statement:
def dimensionLayerClassHom :
    CycleGroup C f k →+ GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C f (k - 1) k)
declarations.comment: the map `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})`, `∑ n_Z[Z] ↦ ∑ n_Z[𝒪_Z]`, for `X` quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom_comp_dimensionLayerClassHom
declarations.doc:
For `X` quasi-compact, the composite
`Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X)` is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerCycleHom_comp_dimensionLayerClassHom :
    (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k).comp (dimensionLayerClassHom C f k) = AddMonoidHom.id _
declarations.comment: the inverse identity `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) → Z_k(X) = id`, for `X` quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.surjective_dimensionLayerCycleHom
declarations.doc:
For `X` quasi-compact, every `k`-cycle is the cycle of a class in the Grothendieck group of the
dimension layer.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_dimensionLayerCycleHom :
    Function.Surjective (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9**, the map `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X)`, `F ↦ [F]_k`. The cycle
class of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module of support dimension at most `k` is additive along short exact
sequences and vanishes on support dimension at most `k - 1`, so it descends to the Grothendieck
group of the dimension layer.
declarations.statement:
def dimensionLayerCycleHom :
    GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C f (k - 1) k) →+ CycleGroup C f k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom_of
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9.** The homomorphism `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X)` sends the class of
the image of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` of support dimension at most `k` to the cycle
`[F]_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerCycleHom_of (F : CoherentModulesDimLE C f k) :
    dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k
        (GrothendieckGroup.of
          ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj F)) =
      dimensionLayerCycle C f k F
declarations.comment: the formula `F ↦ [F]_k` for the map out of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom_dimensionLayerCycleHom_mutuallyInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `(S, δ)`. The maps
`Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`,
`∑ n_Z[Z] ↦ [⨁_{n_Z > 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕n_Z}] - [⨁_{n_Z < 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕-n_Z}]`, and
`K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X)`, `F ↦ [F]_k`, are mutually inverse isomorphisms.

The first two conjuncts are the formulas defining the two maps (the direct sums are the locally
finite direct sums of `Stacks.Chow.cycleStructureSheafDimLE`), the last two the two composites
being the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerHom_dimensionLayerCycleHom_mutuallyInverse :
    (∀ c : CycleGroup C f k, cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k c =
      GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj
          (cycleStructureSheafDimLE C f k (cyclePositivePart C f k c))) -
        GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj
          (cycleStructureSheafDimLE C f k (cycleNegativePart C f k c)))) ∧
    (∀ F : CoherentModulesDimLE C f k, dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k
        (GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj F)) =
      dimensionLayerCycle C f k F) ∧
    (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k).comp (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k) = AddMonoidHom.id _ ∧
    (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k).comp (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k) = AddMonoidHom.id _
declarations.comment: the two maps, given by their formulas, are mutually inverse isomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupAddEquivDimensionLayer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9**, as an isomorphism: the group of `k`-cycles on `X` and the Grothendieck group
of the dimension layer `Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)`, identified by the two mutually inverse maps
`∑ n_Z[Z] ↦ [⨁_{n_Z > 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕n_Z}] - [⨁_{n_Z < 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕-n_Z}]` and `F ↦ [F]_k`.
declarations.statement:
def cycleGroupAddEquivDimensionLayer :
    CycleGroup C f k ≃+ GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C f (k - 1) k)
declarations.comment: `Z_k(X) ≃ K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})` by the two maps of the lemma

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9**, the map `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`. A `k`-cycle `∑ n_Z[Z]` is
sent to `[⨁_{n_Z > 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕n_Z}] - [⨁_{n_Z < 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕-n_Z}]`, the two locally finite direct
sums being coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose support has delta-dimension at most `k`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9.** The homomorphism `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` sends a `k`-cycle
`∑ n_Z[Z]` to the difference of the classes of the direct sums of the structure sheaves of the
integral closed subschemes occurring with positive, respectively negative, coefficient.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerHom_apply (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) (c : CycleGroup C f k) :
    cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k c =
      GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj
          (cycleStructureSheafDimLE C f k (cyclePositivePart C f k c))) -
        GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj
          (cycleStructureSheafDimLE C f k (cycleNegativePart C f k c)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom_comp_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9**, one of the two inverse identities: the composite
`Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X)` of the two maps of Tag 02S9 is the identity.

On a cycle `∑ n_Z[Z]` the two locally finite direct sums have cycles `∑_{n_Z > 0} n_Z[Z]` and
`∑_{n_Z < 0} (-n_Z)[Z]`, whose difference is the cycle one started with.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerCycleHom_comp_cycleDimensionLayerHom (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) :
    (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k).comp (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k) = AddMonoidHom.id _
declarations.comment: the composite `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) → Z_k(X)` is the identity

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerCycleHom_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9.** The cycle class of the element of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` attached
to a `k`-cycle is that cycle.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.injective_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9**, half of the bijectivity. The map
`Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` is injective, the cycle class homomorphism being a left
inverse of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_cycleDimensionLayerHom (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) : Function.Injective (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.surjective_dimensionLayerCycleHom_of_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02S9**, half of the bijectivity. The cycle class homomorphism
`K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X)` is surjective: every `k`-cycle is the cycle class of the
element attached to it.

The same conclusion is proved, for a quasi-compact `X`, as
`Stacks.Chow.surjective_dimensionLayerCycleHom` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Degrees.DimensionLayerClassOfCycle`, through the rival
construction of the map of Tag 02S9 recorded in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Chow/Degrees/DimensionLayerCycleClass.lean`. The version here
needs no quasi-compactness, the section it uses being `Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom`,
which is defined for every `X` locally of finite type over the base; hence the name, and hence
no quasi-compactness in the attribute below.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_dimensionLayerCycleHom_of_cycleDimensionLayerHom (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) : Function.Surjective (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) → Z_k(X)`, with no quasi-compactness

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom_dimensionLayerCycle
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian scheme, the class of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` of support dimension at most
`k` in `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` is the image of its cycle `[F]_k` under the map
`Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerHom_dimensionLayerCycle [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : CoherentModulesDimLE C f k) :
    cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k (dimensionLayerCycle C f k F) =
      GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C f (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom_comp_dimensionLayerCycleHom
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian scheme, the composite
`K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` of the cycle map and
the cycle class map is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerHom_comp_dimensionLayerCycleHom [IsNoetherian X] :
    (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k).comp (dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k) = AddMonoidHom.id _
declarations.comment: `K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) → Z_k(X) → K₀` is the identity, for `X` Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.surjective_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc: On a Noetherian scheme, the map `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_cycleDimensionLayerHom [IsNoetherian X] :
    Function.Surjective (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bijective_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian scheme, the map `Z_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` is bijective, the
cycle class homomorphism being a two-sided inverse.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_cycleDimensionLayerHom [IsNoetherian X] :
    Function.Bijective (cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerEquiv
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian scheme `X`, the group of `k`-cycles on `X` is the Grothendieck
group of the dimension layer `Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)`, by the two mutually inverse
homomorphisms `∑ n_Z[Z] ↦ [⨁_{n_Z > 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕n_Z}] - [⨁_{n_Z < 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕-n_Z}]` and
`F ↦ [F]_k`.
declarations.statement:
def cycleDimensionLayerEquiv [IsNoetherian X] :
    CycleGroup C f k ≃+ GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C f (k - 1) k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian scheme, the identification of the group of `k`-cycles with the Grothendieck
group of the dimension layer sends a cycle `∑ n_Z[Z]` to
`[⨁_{n_Z > 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕n_Z}] - [⨁_{n_Z < 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕-n_Z}]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerEquiv_apply [IsNoetherian X] (c : CycleGroup C f k) :
    cycleDimensionLayerEquiv C f k c = cycleDimensionLayerHom C f k c
declarations.comment: the formula for `Z_k(X) ≃ K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})`, for `X` Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
On a Noetherian scheme, the inverse of the identification of the group of `k`-cycles with the
Grothendieck group of the dimension layer sends the class of a coherent module `F` to the cycle
`[F]_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerEquiv_symm_apply [IsNoetherian X]
    (x : GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C f (k - 1) k)) :
    (cycleDimensionLayerEquiv C f k).symm x = dimensionLayerCycleHom C f k x
declarations.comment: the inverse formula for `Z_k(X) ≃ K₀`, for `X` Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalent_cycles_of_twoPeriodicComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SB.** Let `F` be a coherent sheaf on a scheme `X` locally of finite type over the
base, carrying a `(2, 1)`-periodic complex whose support has delta-dimension at most `k + 1` and
whose two cohomology sheaves are supported in delta-dimension at most `k`. Then the two cohomology
sheaves are coherent, their supports have delta-dimension at most `k`, and the associated
`k`-cycles `[H⁰]_k` and `[H¹]_k` are rationally equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalent_cycles_of_twoPeriodicComplex
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (K : CochainComplex X.Modules (ZMod 2))
    (e : ∀ i : ZMod 2, K.X i ≅ F) (k : ℤ)
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension C
      ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hHk : ∀ (i : ZMod 2) (x : X),
      x ∈ SheafOfModules.supp (K.homology i) →
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f x ≤ k) :
    ∃ (h₀ : (K.homology (0 : ZMod 2)).IsCoherent)
      (h₁ : (K.homology (1 : ZMod 2)).IsCoherent),
      letI := h₀
      letI := h₁
      ∃ (d₀ : schemeDeltaDimension C
          ((reducedSupport (K.homology 0)).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
        (d₁ : schemeDeltaDimension C
          ((reducedSupport (K.homology 1)).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)),
        RationallyEquivalent C f k
          (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f (K.homology 0) k d₀)
          (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f (K.homology 1) k d₁)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowToWideLayerHom_injective_and_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SC.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `(S, δ)`. The map
`CH_k(X) ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` of Tag 0FDS is injective, and its image is the image
`B_k(X)` of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`; that is, it
induces a bijection from `CH_k(X)` onto `B_k(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowToWideLayerHom_injective_and_range (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Injective (chowToWideLayerHom C sX k) ∧
      (chowToWideLayerHom C sX k).range = coherentDimensionLayerImage C sX k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.layerChowClass_eq_zero_of_layerWideningClass_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SC, the comparison.** An element of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X))` whose class in
`K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` vanishes has rationally trivial `k`-cycle.

This is the content of Stacks 02SC: by Stacks 02MX (1) the vanishing produces an object of
`Coh_{≤k-1}(X)` correcting the element to one that already dies in `K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X))`, by
Stacks 02MX (2) that corrected element is the difference of the classes of the two homology
objects of a `(2, 1)`-periodic complex of `Coh_{≤k+1}(X)`, and by Stacks 02SB the `k`-cycles of
those two homology objects are rationally equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem layerChowClass_eq_zero_of_layerWideningClass_eq_zero (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) (a : KZero (CoherentModulesDimLE C f k))
    (ha : layerWideningClass C f k a = 0) : layerChowClass C f k a = 0
declarations.comment: the comparison: a class killed in `K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}/Coh_{≤k-1})` has trivial cycle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SC.** The homomorphism `Bₖ(X) ⟶ CH_k(X)`. On the class of a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `A` with `dim_δ(Supp A) ≤ k` it is the class of the `k`-cycle `[A]_k`; this is
`Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom_apply` below. It exists because the `k`-cycle of
an element of `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X))` killed by the map to `K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` is
rationally trivial, which is
`Stacks.Chow.layerChowClass_eq_zero_of_layerWideningClass_eq_zero`.
declarations.comment: the homomorphism `Bₖ(X) → CH_k(X)` the bijection of the tag inverts

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom_coherentDimensionKZeroMk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SC.** The homomorphism `Bₖ(X) ⟶ CH_k(X)` sends the class of a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F` with `dim_δ(Supp F) ≤ k`, read in the layer `(k-1, k+1]`, to the class of the
`k`-cycle `[F]_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom_coherentDimensionKZeroMk (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (k : ℤ) (F : CoherentModulesDimLE C f k)
    (hF : coherentDimensionKZeroMk C f (k - 1) (k + 1) ((dimensionLayerInclusion C f k).obj F) ∈
      coherentDimensionLayerImage C f k) :
    coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom C f k
        ⟨coherentDimensionKZeroMk C f (k - 1) (k + 1) ((dimensionLayerInclusion C f k).obj F),
          hF⟩ =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C f k) (layerCycleOfLE C f k F F.property)
declarations.comment: the value of `Bₖ(X) → CH_k(X)` on the class of a coherent module

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionLayerImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SC, `Bₖ(X)`.** The image of the homomorphism of Grothendieck groups induced by the
inclusion of the dimension layer `(k - 1, k]` into the layer `(k - 1, k + 1]`.
declarations.statement:
def coherentDimensionLayerImage (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (k : ℤ) : AddSubgroup (coherentDimensionKZero C f (k - 1) (k + 1))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowToCoherentQuotientHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SD**, the canonical map `CH_k(X) → K₀(Coh(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` for `X` locally of
finite type over the base of a Chow situation: the canonical map
`CH_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` of Lemma 0FDS (`Stacks.Chow.chowToWideLayerHom`)
followed by the canonical map `K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → K₀(Coh(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`
(`Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionToQuotientHom`).
declarations.statement:
def chowToCoherentQuotientHom (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (k : ℤ) : chowGroup C f k →+ coherentQuotientKZero C f (k - 1)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `CH_k(X) → K₀(Coh(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`, built from Lemma 0FDS

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionToQuotientHom
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `K₀(Coh_{≤b}(X)/Coh_{≤a}(X)) → K₀(Coh(X)/Coh_{≤a}(X))`: the homomorphism of
Grothendieck groups induced by the exact functor that drops the upper dimension bound.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowToCoherentQuotientKZero
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `CH_k(X) → K₀(Coh(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`: the composite of a cycle class map
`φ : CH_k(X) → K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` with the canonical map that drops the upper
dimension bound.
declarations.statement:
def chowToCoherentQuotientKZero (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (k : ℤ) (φ : chowGroup C f k →+ coherentDimensionKZero C f (k - 1) (k + 1)) :
    chowGroup C f k →+ coherentQuotientKZero C f (k - 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.orderOfVanishingMeromorphic
declarations.doc:
**The order of vanishing of a regular meromorphic section along a prime divisor, Stacks
02SF.** The meromorphic section is a global section `s` of the sheaf `𝒦_X(L)` of meromorphic
sections of `L`; its order along `Z` is the order of vanishing, in the local ring at the generic
point of `Z`, of the rational function expressing the generic value of `s` in terms of a generator
of the stalk of `L` there.

`Stacks.Divisors.orderOfVanishingMeromorphic_eq` is the characterization, and it is what should be
used rather than this definition.
declarations.statement:
def orderOfVanishingMeromorphic (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (_hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) : ℤ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.orderOfVanishingMeromorphicData
declarations.doc:
A choice of the data provided by
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_orderOfVanishingMeromorphicData`: the quasi-coherence of `L`, the
order of vanishing of the regular meromorphic section `s` along the prime divisor `Z`, and its
characterization as the order of the coordinate of `s` with respect to any generator of `L` at
the generic point of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
def orderOfVanishingMeromorphicData
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (_hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) :
    { q : PSigma (fun _ : L.IsQuasicoherent => ℤ) //
      letI : L.IsQuasicoherent := q.1
      let ξ := Z.genericPoint
      let R := X.presheaf.stalk ξ
      let K := X.functionField
      letI : Module R (L.presheaf.stalk ξ) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) L.val ξ
      letI : Module K (L.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X)) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) L.val (genericPoint X)
      let isCoordinate := fun (m : L.presheaf.stalk ξ) (a : K) =>
        ((meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant X L).val.hom.val.app
          (op (⊤ : X.Opens))) (s.val (op ⊤)) =
          constantGenericStalkModuleSection X L ⊤
            (a • (L.presheaf.stalkSpecializes
              ((genericPoint_spec X).specializes trivial)) m)
      (∃ m : L.presheaf.stalk ξ,
        (Submodule.span R {m} = ⊤) ∧ (∃ a : K, isCoordinate m a)) ∧
      (∀ (m : L.presheaf.stalk ξ)
        (_ : Submodule.span R {m} = ⊤) (a : K),
        isCoordinate m a → q.2 = X.ord a ξ) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.orderOfVanishingMeromorphic
declarations.doc:
The order of vanishing along a prime divisor `Z` of a regular meromorphic section `s` of an
invertible module `L` on a locally Noetherian integral scheme: the order in `𝒪_{X, ξ}` of the
coordinate of `s` with respect to a generator of `L_ξ`, where `ξ` is the generic point of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
def orderOfVanishingMeromorphic
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor X) : ℤ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyFinite_primeDivisors_not_representedAt
declarations.doc:
The prime divisors at whose generic point a meromorphic section of a quasi-coherent module
on a locally Noetherian integral scheme is not an ordinary section form a locally finite
collection of closed subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_primeDivisors_not_representedAt [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [L.IsQuasicoherent] (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L) :
    LocallyFinite
      (fun Z : { Z : PrimeDivisor X // ¬ IsRepresentedAt L s Z.genericPoint } => Z.1.support)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyFinite_primeDivisors_orderOfVanishingMeromorphic_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
The prime divisors along which a regular meromorphic section of an invertible module on a
locally Noetherian integral scheme has nonzero order of vanishing form a locally finite
collection of closed subsets; equivalently, the orders are the coefficients of a Weil divisor.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_meromorphicSectionRatio
declarations.doc:
Two regular meromorphic sections of an invertible module on an integral scheme have a unique
ratio in the units of the ring of rational functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_meromorphicSectionRatio
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (hs' : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s') :
    ∃! f : (Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctions X)ˣ, IsMeromorphicSectionRatio X L s s' f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicWeilDivisor_eq_add_principalDivisor
declarations.doc:
The Weil divisors of two regular meromorphic sections of an invertible
module on a locally Noetherian integral scheme differ by the principal divisor of their ratio.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicWeilDivisor_eq_add_principalDivisor [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (hs' : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s') :
    weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection X L s hs =
      weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection X L s' hs' +
        principalDivisor X (meromorphicSectionRatio X L s s' hs hs')

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapFundamental
declarations.doc:
**The Weil divisor class of an invertible module, Stacks 02SJ (2).** On an integral scheme `X`
of delta-dimension `n`, locally of finite type over the base of a Chow situation, the class

  `c₁(L) ∩ [X] ∈ CH_{n-1}(X)`

of the divisor of zeros and poles of a nonzero meromorphic section of `L`.

An invertible module on an integral scheme has a regular meromorphic section with nonzero generic
value (`Stacks.ChernCap42.exists_isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_isIntegral`), and the class of its
divisor cycle does not depend on which one is taken; the characterizing equality is
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq`, which should be used in place of this
definition.
declarations.statement: def firstChernClassCapFundamental : chowGroup C p (n - 1)
declarations.comment: part (2): the Weil divisor class c₁(L) ∩ [X] in CH_{n-1}(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq
declarations.doc:
**The Weil divisor class is the class of `div_L(s)` for every nonzero section,
Stacks 02SJ (2).** In `CH_{n-1}(X)` the class `c₁(L) ∩ [X]` is represented by the divisor cycle
of *any* nonzero regular meromorphic section of `L`, not only by the one
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapFundamental` chose. This is the well-definedness the source asserts.

The source's nonvanishing of `s` is not assumed: on an integral scheme it follows from
regularity, by `Stacks.Divisors.genericValue_ne_zero_of_isRegularMeromorphicSection`. See the
implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.DivisorOfInvertibleSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq
    (s : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s) :
    firstChernClassCapFundamental C p n hn L =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk (divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle C p n hn L s hs)
declarations.comment:
part (2): c₁(L) ∩ [X] is the class of div_L(s) for every nonzero regular
meromorphic section s, so the definition does not depend on the chosen section

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.divisorOfMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**The divisor cycle of a regular meromorphic section, Stacks 02SJ (1).** The Weil divisor
`div_L(s)` of a regular meromorphic section of an invertible module on an integral scheme of
delta-dimension `n`, read as a cycle of delta-dimension `n - 1`, together with its coefficient
specification.

The coefficient at the generic point of a prime divisor `Z` is the order of vanishing
`ord_{Z, L}(s)` of Stacks 02SF, and the coefficient at a point which is no prime divisor's generic
point is zero; those are the two components of the subtype obligation, and they are available as
`Stacks.Chow.divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle_genericPoint` and
`Stacks.Chow.divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
def divisorOfMeromorphicSection (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [IsIntegral X] (n : ℤ)
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = (n : EInt)) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s) :
    { c : CycleGroup C p (n - 1) // IsDivisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle C p n L s hs c }
declarations.comment:
part (1): div_L(s) = ∑_Z ord_{Z, L}(s) [Z] as an element of Z_{n-1}(X), together
with its coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.ChernCap42.divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle_eq_cycleAssociatedToZeroScheme
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an integral scheme locally of finite type over the base of
chapter 42, of delta-dimension `n`, let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `s` be a nonzero
global section of `L`. Then the divisor of `s` is the cycle of its zero scheme:
`div_L(s) = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `Z_{n-1}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle_eq_cycleAssociatedToZeroScheme (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [IsIntegral X] (n : ℤ)
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = (n : EInt)) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle C p n hn L (meromorphicSectionOfSection L s)
        (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero X L s hs) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι (n - 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.ChernCap42.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_fundamentalCycle
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an integral scheme locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, of
delta-dimension `n`, let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `s` be a nonzero global section
of `L`. Then the first Chern class of `L` capped with the fundamental cycle `[X]` of `X`, in
degree `n - 1 + 1`, is the class of the cycle of the zero scheme of `s`:
`c₁(L) ∩ [X] = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `CH_{n-1}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_fundamentalCycle (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [IsIntegral X] (n : ℤ)
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = (n : EInt)) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p (n - 1) L
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (𝟙 X) (n - 1 + 1)) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι (n - 1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tensorMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SL: the tensor product of two meromorphic sections.** The meromorphic section of
`L ⊗_{𝒪_X} N` whose generic value is the pure tensor of the generic values of `s` and `t`. On an
integral scheme this determines it, by Tag 01X5 part (2);
`AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant_tensorMeromorphicSection` is the resulting
description on pure tensors of honest sections.
declarations.statement:
def tensorMeromorphicSection [L.IsQuasicoherent] [N.IsQuasicoherent]
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N).IsQuasicoherent]
    (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L) (t : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf N) :
    MeromorphicSection X.sheaf (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant_tensorMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SL: at the generic point the product is the pure tensor.** If the meromorphic
sections `s` and `t` are, at the generic point, the germs of honest sections `m` of `L` and `n`
of `N` over a neighbourhood `U` of it, then their product is the germ of the pure tensor
`m ⊗ n`. This fixes the product and not merely its divisor: a meromorphic section on an integral
scheme is determined by its generic germ.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant_tensorMeromorphicSection
    [L.IsQuasicoherent] [N.IsQuasicoherent] [(Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N).IsQuasicoherent]
    (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L) (t : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf N)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : genericPoint X ∈ U)
    (m : L.val.obj (op U)) (n : N.val.obj (op U))
    (hs : (meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant X L).val.hom.val.app (op (⊤ : X.Opens))
      (s.val (op ⊤)) =
        constantGenericStalkModuleSection X L ⊤ (L.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hU m))
    (ht : (meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant X N).val.hom.val.app (op (⊤ : X.Opens))
      (t.val (op ⊤)) =
        constantGenericStalkModuleSection X N ⊤ (N.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hU n)) :
    (meromorphicSectionSheafIsoConstant X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N)).val.hom.val.app
        (op (⊤ : X.Opens)) ((tensorMeromorphicSection X L N s t).val (op ⊤)) =
      constantGenericStalkModuleSection X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N) ⊤
        (PresheafOfModules.tensorSheafGerm X.sheaf L N (genericPoint X) U hU m n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularMeromorphicSection_tensorMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SL: a product of nonzero meromorphic sections is nonzero.** Regularity in the
sense of Tag 02OX is injectivity of multiplication by the generic value. Writing the generic
values of `s` and `t` as `a` and `b` times stalk bases of `L_η` and `N_η`, the generic value of
the product is `a * b` times the product of those bases, which is a stalk basis of
`(L ⊗_{𝒪_X} N)_η`; and `a * b` is nonzero in the function field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularMeromorphicSection_tensorMeromorphicSection
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L) (t : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf N)
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (ht : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf N t) :
    IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N)
      (tensorMeromorphicSection X L N s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection_tensorMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SL: the divisor of a product is the sum of the divisors.** The Weil divisor of
Tag 0BE6 part (1) is additive in the product of regular meromorphic sections of invertible
modules, coefficient by coefficient.
declarations.statement:
theorem weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection_tensorMeromorphicSection
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L) (t : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf N)
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (ht : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf N t) :
    weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N)
        (tensorMeromorphicSection X L N s t)
        (isRegularMeromorphicSection_tensorMeromorphicSection X L N s t hs ht) =
      weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection X L s hs + weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection X N t ht

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SL: the divisor class of a tensor product is the sum of the divisor classes.**
The Weil divisor class of Tag 0BE6 part (2) is additive in the tensor product of invertible
modules: a regular meromorphic section of each factor exists by Tag 02OZ part (1), their
product is a regular meromorphic section of the tensor product, and its divisor is the sum of
their divisors. This is the input Tag 0BE7 needs, and it is supplied to it in
`AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_tensorObj
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N] :
    weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N) =
      weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf X L + weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf X N

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.mk_flatPullback_meromorphicDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SM.** Let `C = (S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X` and `Y` be
integral and locally of finite type over `S` with `n = dim_δ(Y)`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of
relative dimension `r`. For an invertible module `L` on `Y`,

  `f^*(c₁(L) ∩ [Y]) = c₁(f^*L) ∩ [X]`

in `A_{n + r - 1}(X)`, where either side is the class of the divisor of a nonzero meromorphic
section, read on `Y` and pulled back on the left and read on `X` on the right.

The integrality of `X` is a hypothesis of the source, which assumes both `X` and `Y` integral;
the case of a general `X` is subsumed by Stacks 02SS.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_flatPullback_meromorphicDivisorCycle (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    (QuotientAddGroup.mk ((show (n : ℤ) - 1 + (r : ℤ) = n + (r : ℤ) - 1 by ring) ▸
          flatPullback C sX sY f hbase r hf (n - 1)
            (meromorphicDivisorCycleOfInvertible C sY hY L s).val) :
        chowGroup C sX (n + (r : ℤ) - 1)) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk (meromorphicDivisorCycleOfInvertible C sX
        (schemeDeltaDimension_eq_add_of_flat C sX sY f hbase r hf hY)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L) (genericStalkPullback f L s)).val
declarations.comment: the flat pullback read on the divisor of a nonzero meromorphic section

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The first Chern class cap product `Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(X)`, `α ↦ c₁(L) ∩ α`, of an invertible
module: `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCap` at the component rule of `L`.
declarations.statement: abbrev firstChernClassCapOfInvertible : CycleGroup C p (k + 1) →+ chowGroup C p k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_integral
declarations.doc:
On the fundamental cycle of a single integral closed subscheme `W ⊆ X` of delta-dimension
`k + 1`, the cap product of an invertible module is the proper Chow pushforward along `W ⟶ X` of
the first Chern class of `L|_W`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_integral_cycle` read through
`Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_mk`. The instance of Stacks 02S2 that
`Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward` requires is discharged, `W.subschemeι` being a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
