theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_integral (W : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      properChowPushforward C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) p W.subschemeι rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion W.subschemeι C
          (W.subschemeι ≫ p) p rfl k)
        (firstChernComponentClass C p k L W hW hDim)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_finsum
declarations.doc:
The locally finite component formula for the cap product of an invertible module: on a
presentation `α = ∑ n_j [W_j]` of a `(k+1)`-cycle, `c₁(L) ∩ α` is the class of
`∑ n_j c₁(L) ∩ [W_j]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_finsum {J : Type u} (W : J → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : ∀ j, IsIntegral (W j).subscheme)
    (hDim : ∀ j, schemeDeltaDimension C ((W j).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hLocal : LocallyFinite fun j ↦ ((W j).support : Set X)) (n : J → ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1))
    (hα : ∀ x : X, α.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (W j).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x) :
    ∃ β : CycleGroup C p k,
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L α = QuotientAddGroup.mk β ∧
      ∀ x : X, β.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
        (firstChernComponentCycle C p k (firstChernComponentCycleRule C p k L)
          (W j) (hW j) (hDim j)).1 x

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SP.** Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X` be locally of
finite type over `S` and let `L`, `N` be invertible `𝒪_X`-modules. Then

  `c₁(L) ∩ α + c₁(N) ∩ α = c₁(L ⊗_{𝒪_X} N) ∩ α`

in `A_k(X)` for every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`. The companion assertion of the same tag,
`c₁(𝒪_X) ∩ α = 0`, is `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_unit`, deduced from this one
through `𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X ≅ 𝒪_X`.

The cap product is the one of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ChernComponent.ClassRule`; see
the module documentation for why no `@[stacks 02SO]` attribute accompanies it.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_tensorObj (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L α + firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k N α =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj L N) α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SP.** `c₁(𝒪_X) ∩ α = 0` in `A_k(X)` for every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`.

Additivity applied to `L = N = 𝒪_X` together with `𝒪_X ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X ≅ 𝒪_X` gives
`c₁(𝒪_X) ∩ α + c₁(𝒪_X) ∩ α = c₁(𝒪_X) ∩ α`.

The companion assertion of the same tag is
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_tensorObj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_unit (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) α = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ChernCap42.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_closedSubscheme_eq_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SQ.** Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42 of the Stacks Project, let
`X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, let `Y ⊆ X` be a
closed subscheme and let `s` be a global section of `L|_Y`. Assume `dim_δ(Y) ≤ k + 1`, that
`dim_δ(Z(s)) ≤ k`, and that multiplication by `s` is injective on the local ring at the generic
point of every component of `Z(s)` of `δ`-dimension `k`. Then

`c₁(L) ∩ [Y]_{k + 1} = [Z(s)]_k`  in  `A_k(X)`.

The cycle `[Z(s)]_k` is read on `X` through the composite of the closed immersion of `Z(s)` into
`Y` with that of `Y` into `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_closedSubscheme_eq_zeroScheme
    (s : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L).sections)
    (hY : schemeDeltaDimension C (i ≫ p) ≤ (k + 1 : EInt))
    (hD : schemeDeltaDimension C
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L)
        (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ (i ≫ p)) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hs : ∀ ξ : genericPoints (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L) (s.eval (op ⊤))).subscheme,
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (i ≫ p)
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L)
          (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι ξ.1) = k →
      Function.Injective (ConcreteCategory.hom
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L)
            (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι ξ.1)).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y).map
            (((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L).unitHomEquiv.symm s))))) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p i (k + 1)) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L)
          (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ i) k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatNaturality_firstChernIdentityCapRule
declarations.doc:
**The flat-pullback identity on the test schemes.** For the canonical first Chern class cap
product and test morphisms `g : T ⟶ X` and `h : T' ⟶ T` with `h` flat of relative dimension `r`,

  `c₁((h ∘ g)^*ℒ) ∩ h^*α = h^*(c₁(g^*ℒ) ∩ α)`,

the two sides sitting in the degrees `(k + r) - 1` and `(k - 1) + r`. This is
`Stacks.Chow.IdentityCapRule.FlatNaturality` for `Stacks.Chow.firstChernIdentityCapRule` at the
canonical cap product.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatNaturality_firstChernIdentityCapRule :
    IdentityCapRule.FlatNaturality C sX 1
      (firstChernIdentityCapRule C sX (canonicalFirstChernCapRule C) L)
declarations.comment: the flat-pullback identity read for the identity cap rule of the canonical first Chern class cap product on the test schemes of X, i.e. the predicate `IdentityCapRule.FlatNaturality` that the bivariant class of Stacks 0B77 takes as its second naturality hypothesis, with no hypothesis of its own

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_firstChernCapOfInvertible_rationallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
Intersecting with the first Chern class of an invertible module commutes with flat pullback:
for `f : X' ⟶ X` flat of relative dimension `r`, an invertible module `L` on `X` and a
`(k+1)`-cycle `α` on `X`, the cycle representing `c₁(f^*L) ∩ f^*α` and the flat pullback of the
cycle representing `c₁(L) ∩ α` are rationally equivalent on `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_firstChernCapOfInvertible_rationallyEquivalent (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    RationallyEquivalent C (f ≫ p) (k + (r : ℤ))
      ((firstChernCapRule C (f ≫ p) (k + (r : ℤ))
          (firstChernComponentCycleRule C (f ≫ p) (k + (r : ℤ))
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L))).extendCycleGroup
        ((show k + 1 + (r : ℤ) = k + (r : ℤ) + 1 by omega) ▸
          flatPullback C (f ≫ p) p f rfl r hf (k + 1) α))
      (flatPullback C (f ≫ p) p f rfl r hf k
        ((firstChernCapRule C p k (firstChernComponentCycleRule C p k L)).extendCycleGroup α))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_fundamentalCycle
declarations.doc:
**The second displayed equation of Stacks 02ST.** Let `X` and `Y` be integral and locally of
finite type over the base with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be proper and dominant
over the base and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module. Then

`f_*(c₁(f^*L) ∩ [X]) = [R(X) : R(Y)] c₁(L) ∩ [Y] = c₁(L) ∩ f_*[X]`

in `CH_{n-1}(Y)`, the two equalities being the two conjuncts below.

The proper pushforward on Chow groups carries no hypothesis: Stacks 02S2 is
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence`. The invertibility of `f^*L` is
Stacks 0B8L, the instance `Stacks.Divisors.pullback_isInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properChowPushforward_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_fundamentalCycle
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] {n : ℤ}
    (hnX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : schemeDeltaDimension C sY = (n : EInt))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] [IsDominant f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (L : Y.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.sheaf.obj Y.ringCatSheaf.property L] :
    letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := (dominantFunctionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    properChowPushforward C sX sY f hf (n - 1)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sX sY f hf (n - 1))
          (firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sX (n - 1) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L)
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX (𝟙 X) (n - 1 + 1))) =
        (Module.finrank Y.functionField X.functionField : ℤ) •
          firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sY (n - 1) L
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY (𝟙 Y) (n - 1 + 1)) ∧
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sY (n - 1) L
          (properPushforward C sX sY f hf (n - 1 + 1)
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sX (𝟙 X) (n - 1 + 1))) =
        (Module.finrank Y.functionField X.functionField : ℤ) •
          firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sY (n - 1) L
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY (𝟙 Y) (n - 1 + 1))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_meromorphicDivisorCycleOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**The first displayed equation of Stacks 02ST.** For a proper dominant morphism `p : X ⟶ Y`
of integral schemes locally of finite type over the base with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, an
invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `L` and a nonzero meromorphic section `s` of `L`, the proper pushforward
of the divisor cycle of `p^*s` is `[R(X) : R(Y)]` times the divisor cycle of `s`, as cycles.

These are the hypotheses the source states the tag under; the rank-one hypothesis of
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_meromorphicDivisorCycle` is discharged here by
`Stacks.Divisors.isTrivializedNear_of_isInvertible`. The tag's second displayed equation, the
first Chern class consequence, is in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ChernClassDominantPushforward`, so the attribute names this
clause explicitly; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_meromorphicDivisorCycleOfInvertible (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] {n : ℤ}
    (hnX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : schemeDeltaDimension C sY = (n : EInt))
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper p] [IsDominant p] (hp : p ≫ sY = sX) (L : Y.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (s : L.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint Y)) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := (dominantFunctionFieldMap p).toAlgebra
    properPushforward C sX sY p hp (n - 1)
        (meromorphicDivisorCycle C sX hnX
          (fun x => (isTrivializedNear_of_isInvertible L (p.base x)).pullback)
          (genericStalkPullback p L s)).val =
      (Module.finrank Y.functionField X.functionField : ℤ) •
        (meromorphicDivisorCycle C sY hnY (isTrivializedNear_of_isInvertible L) s).val

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properNaturality_firstChernIdentityCapRule
declarations.doc:
**The projection formula on the test schemes.** For the canonical first Chern class cap product
and test morphisms `g : T ⟶ X` and `h : T' ⟶ T` with `h` proper,

  `c₁(g^*ℒ) ∩ h_*α = h_*(c₁((h ∘ g)^*ℒ) ∩ α)`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.IdentityCapRule.ProperNaturality` for
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernIdentityCapRule` at the canonical cap product.
declarations.statement:
theorem properNaturality_firstChernIdentityCapRule :
    IdentityCapRule.ProperNaturality C sX 1
      (firstChernIdentityCapRule C sX (canonicalFirstChernCapRule C) L)
declarations.comment: the projection formula read for the identity cap rule of the canonical first Chern class cap product on the test schemes of X, i.e. the predicate `IdentityCapRule.ProperNaturality` that the bivariant class of Stacks 0B77 takes as its first naturality hypothesis, with no hypothesis of its own

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_of_isProper'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SU.** Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over
the base scheme of chapter 42 and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module. Then for every
`(k+1)`-cycle `α` on `X`

  `p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α`  in  `A_k(Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properChowPushforward_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_of_isProper'
    (α : CycleGroup C sX (k + 1)) :
    letI := isInvertible_presheaf_modulePullback L p
    properChowPushforward C sX sY p hp k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sX sY p hp k)
        (firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sX k ((Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj L) α) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sY k L
        (properPushforward C sX sY p hp (k + 1) α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SU.** Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over
the base scheme of chapter 42, and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module. Then for every
`(k+1)`-cycle `α` on `X`

  `p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α`  in  `A_k(Y)`.

The invertibility of `p^*ℒ` is Stacks 0B8L (`Stacks.Divisors.pullback_isInvertible`), and proper
pushforward on Chow groups is defined by Stacks 02S2
(`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper`).
declarations.statement:
theorem properChowPushforward_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_of_isProper
    (α : CycleGroup C sX (k + 1)) :
    properChowPushforward C sX sY p hp k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C sX sY p hp k)
        (firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sX k ((Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj L) α) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sY k L (properPushforward C sX sY p hp (k + 1) α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.denominatorQuotients_shortExact_isCoherent_and_firstChernClassCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02SW.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 42.7.1, let `X` be locally of finite type
over `S`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let
`s ∈ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(ℒ))` be a meromorphic section of `ℒ`. Assume

1. `dim_δ(X) ≤ k + 1`,
2. `X` has no embedded points,
3. `ℱ` has no embedded associated points,
4. the support of `ℱ` is `X`, and
5. the section `s` is regular meromorphic.

Let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_X` be the ideal of denominators of `s`. Then we have the following:

1. there are short exact sequences

     `0 ⟶ ℐℱ ⟶^1 ℱ ⟶ 𝒬₁ ⟶ 0`,   `0 ⟶ ℐℱ ⟶^s ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℒ ⟶ 𝒬₂ ⟶ 0`;

2. the coherent sheaves `𝒬₁`, `𝒬₂` are supported in δ-dimension `≤ k`;
3. the section `s` restricts to a regular meromorphic section `sᵢ` on every irreducible
   component `Xᵢ` of `X` of δ-dimension `k + 1`; and
4. writing `[ℱ]_{k+1} = ∑ᵢ mᵢ[Xᵢ]` we have

     `[𝒬₂]_k - [𝒬₁]_k = ∑ᵢ mᵢ (Xᵢ ⟶ X)_* div_{ℒ|_{Xᵢ}}(sᵢ)`   in   `Z_k(X)`,

   in particular

     `[𝒬₂]_k - [𝒬₁]_k = c₁(ℒ) ∩ [ℱ]_{k+1}`   in   `CH_k(X)`.

This is the declaration carrying the tag; the results above and in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.DenominatorQuotients.Basic`,
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.DenominatorQuotients.ComponentDivisor` and
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.DenominatorQuotients.CycleIdentity` are its components.

An irreducible component of `X` is named by its generic point `η`, carrying the reduced induced
structure `Stacks.Chow.integralComponentAt η`; `sᵢ` is `Stacks.Chow.componentMeromorphicSection`,
the pullback of `s` along its closed immersion, and `(Xᵢ ⟶ X)_* div_{ℒ|_{Xᵢ}}(sᵢ)` is
`Stacks.Chow.componentDivisorCycle`.

The presentation `[ℱ]_{k+1} = ∑ᵢ mᵢ[Xᵢ]` is the first conjunct of part (4): its index is
`Stacks.Chow.topSupportPoints C f ℱ (k + 1)`, the points of the support of `ℱ` of
δ-dimension `k + 1`, and its coefficients `mᵢ` are the multiplicities
`Stacks.Chow.sheafMultiplicity ℱ ηᵢ`. The second conjunct — the equality in `Z_k(X)` — is read
coefficientwise, at an arbitrary point `x` of `X`, because the family of components of
δ-dimension `k + 1` is locally finite rather than finite, so both sides exist as locally finite
sums; a cycle is its coefficient function, so this is the asserted equality of cycles.
declarations.statement:
theorem denominatorQuotients_shortExact_isCoherent_and_firstChernClassCap
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (L F : X.Modules) (s : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L) [F.IsCoherent]
    {k : ℤ}
    (hdim : schemeDeltaDimension C f ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X)
    (hF : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F)
    (hSupp : (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleSheafOfModules F).supp = Set.univ)
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L)
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s) :
    -- (1) `0 ⟶ ℐℱ ⟶^1 ℱ ⟶ 𝒬₁ ⟶ 0` is short exact
    (denominatorQuotientShortComplex X L F s).ShortExact ∧
    -- (1) `0 ⟶ ℐℱ ⟶^s ℱ ⊗ ℒ ⟶ 𝒬₂ ⟶ 0` is short exact
    (@denominatorSectionQuotientShortComplex X L F s
        (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f) hL hs inferInstance hF hSupp).ShortExact ∧
    -- (2) `𝒬₁` and `𝒬₂` are coherent
    (denominatorQuotient X L F s).IsCoherent ∧
    (@denominatorSectionQuotient X L F s (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f) hL hs
        inferInstance hF hSupp).IsCoherent ∧
    -- (2) and are supported in δ-dimension `≤ k`
    schemeDeltaDimension C ((@reducedSupport X (denominatorQuotient X L F s)
        (isCoherent_denominatorQuotient C f L F s hdim hX hF hSupp hL hs)).subschemeι ≫ f)
      ≤ (k : EInt) ∧
    schemeDeltaDimension C ((@reducedSupport X
        (@denominatorSectionQuotient X L F s (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f) hL hs
          inferInstance hF hSupp)
        (isCoherent_denominatorSectionQuotient C f L F s hdim hX hF hSupp hL hs)).subschemeι ≫ f)
      ≤ (k : EInt) ∧
    -- (3) `s` restricts to a regular meromorphic section on every component of δ-dimension `k+1`
    (∀ (η : X) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints X),
        relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f η = k + 1 →
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection (integralComponentAt η).subscheme.sheaf
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (integralComponentAt η).subschemeι).obj L)
          (componentMeromorphicSection L s hη)) ∧
    -- (4) `[ℱ]_{k+1} = ∑ᵢ mᵢ[Xᵢ]`, over the components of δ-dimension `k + 1`
    (∀ x : X, (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f F (k + 1)
          (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_le_of_schemeDeltaDimension_le C f F hdim)).1 x =
        ∑ᶠ j : topSupportPoints C f F (k + 1), sheafMultiplicity F j.1 *
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (integralComponentAt j.1).subschemeι (k + 1)).1
            x) ∧
    -- (4) `[𝒬₂]_k - [𝒬₁]_k = ∑ᵢ mᵢ (Xᵢ ⟶ X)_* div_{ℒ|_{Xᵢ}}(sᵢ)` in `Z_k(X)`
    (∀ x : X,
        (denominatorSectionQuotientCycle C f L F s hdim hX hF hSupp hL hs).1 x -
            (denominatorQuotientCycle C f L F s hdim hX hF hSupp hL hs).1 x =
          ∑ᶠ j : topSupportPoints C f F (k + 1), sheafMultiplicity F j.1 *
            (componentDivisorCycle C f L s hL hs
              (mem_genericPoints_of_relativeDimension_eq C f hdim j.2.2) j.2.2).1 x) ∧
    -- (4) in particular `[𝒬₂]_k - [𝒬₁]_k = c₁(ℒ) ∩ [ℱ]_{k+1}` in `CH_k(X)`
    QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (denominatorSectionQuotientCycle C f L F s hdim hX hF hSupp hL hs -
          denominatorQuotientCycle C f L F s hdim hX hF hSupp hL hs) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C f k L (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f F (k + 1)
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_le_of_schemeDeltaDimension_le C f F hdim))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_mem_coherentDimensionLayerImage_layerMkTensor_sub
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02SX].** Let `(S, δ)` be a Chow situation, let `X` be locally of finite type
over `S`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module with
`dim_δ(Supp ℱ) ≤ k + 1`. Then the element

`[ℱ ⊗ ℒ] - [ℱ] ∈ K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))`

lies in the subgroup `Bₖ(X)` of [Stacks, Tag 02SC] and maps to `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [ℱ]_{k+1}` under the
homomorphism `Bₖ(X) ⟶ CH_k(X)` of that tag.

Both clauses are asserted: the membership is the existential witness, and the equation is the
statement about it. The membership is
`Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionKZeroMk_layerMkTensor_sub_mem` and the equation is
`Stacks.Chow.coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom_eq_firstChernClassCap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_coherentDimensionLayerImage_layerMkTensor_sub
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (L : X.Modules)
    [hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    {k : ℤ}
    (hdim : schemeDeltaDimension C ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    ∃ hmem : coherentDimensionKZeroMk C f (k - 1) (k + 1)
            (layerMkTensor C f (k + 1) F L hL hdim) -
          coherentDimensionKZeroMk C f (k - 1) (k + 1) (layerMk C f (k + 1) F hdim) ∈
        coherentDimensionLayerImage C f k,
      coherentDimensionLayerImageChowHom C f k ⟨_, hmem⟩ =
        firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C f k L
          (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C f F (k + 1) hdim)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The Gysin homomorphism of the zero scheme of a global section `s` of an invertible module:
`Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphism` at the first Chern class component rule of `L`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible : CycleGroup C p (k + 1) →+
    chowGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_of_not_le
declarations.doc:
The Gysin image of an integral closed subscheme not contained in the zero scheme is the class
of its scheme-theoretic intersection with that zero scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_of_not_le (W : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (h : ¬ Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s ≤ W) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
          ((W.comap (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).subschemeι) k)
declarations.comment: integral component not contained in the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_of_le
declarations.doc:
The Gysin image of an integral closed subscheme contained in the zero scheme of `s` is the
proper Chow pushforward into that zero scheme of the first Chern class of `L|_W`.

The instance of Stacks 02S2 that `Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward` requires is discharged, the
inclusion of `W` into the zero scheme being a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_of_le (W : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (h : Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s ≤ W) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      properChowPushforward C (W.subschemeι ≫ p)
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        (Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h) (by simp) k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h) C (W.subschemeι ≫ p)
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (by simp) k)
        (firstChernComponentClass C p k L W hW hDim)
declarations.comment: integral component contained in the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_finsum
declarations.doc: The locally finite component formula for the Gysin map of an invertible module.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_finsum {J : Type u} (W : J → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : ∀ j, IsIntegral (W j).subscheme)
    (hDim : ∀ j, schemeDeltaDimension C ((W j).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hLocal : LocallyFinite fun j ↦ ((W j).support : Set X)) (n : J → ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1))
    (hα : ∀ x : X, α.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (W j).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x) :
    ∃ β : CycleGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k,
      gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s α = QuotientAddGroup.mk β ∧
      ∀ x : (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme,
        β.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
          (gysinComponentCycle C p k L s (firstChernComponentClass C p k L)
            (W j) (hW j) (hDim j)).1 x

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
Intersection with the zero scheme of `s`, when that zero scheme is an effective Cartier
divisor, read as a class on the ambient scheme: the Gysin map of the zero scheme followed by
proper Chow pushforward along its closed immersion into `X`.
declarations.statement:
def effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s)) :
    CycleGroup C p (k + 1) →+ chowGroup C p k
declarations.comment: intersection with an effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02T9.** Pushing the Gysin class of the zero scheme `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X` forward to `X`
is capping with the first Chern class of `L`: `i_* i^* α = c₁(L) ∩ α` in `A_k(X)` for every
`α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`.

The vanishing of Stacks 02S2 that `Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward` requires is supplied, not
assumed, the zero scheme being a closed subscheme of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properChowPushforward_gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    properChowPushforward C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p rfl k)
        (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s α) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersection_divisorSheaf_eq_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02T9, the "in particular" clause for a given effective Cartier divisor.** For an
effective Cartier divisor `D` on `X`, intersection with `D` — taken through the canonical section
`1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)`, whose zero scheme is `D` — is capping with `c₁(𝒪_X(D))`.

The effective Cartier hypothesis of `Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersection` is carried but
unused by that construction, so transporting it along `Z(1_D) = D` (Stacks 01X0) costs nothing.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierIntersection_divisorSheaf_eq_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible
    (D : X.IdealSheafData) [hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D]
    (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible C p k (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf D)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection D)
        (isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_divisorSheaf D) α =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf D) α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.canonicalGysinSystem_isNaturalUnderInverseIso
declarations.doc:
**The canonical Gysin system is natural under inverse isomorphisms**: the inverse-isomorphism
case of the naturality of the Gysin operation.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalGysinSystem_isNaturalUnderInverseIso (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (canonicalGysinSystem C).IsNaturalUnderInverseIso
declarations.comment: the inverse-isomorphism case of the naturality of the Gysin operation, for the canonical Gysin system of Stacks 02TO, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.canonicalGysinSystem_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**The canonical Gysin system is natural under base-change isomorphisms**: the
base-change-isomorphism case of the naturality of the Gysin operation.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalGysinSystem_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (canonicalGysinSystem C).IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso
declarations.comment: the base-change-isomorphism case of the naturality of the Gysin operation, for the canonical Gysin system of Stacks 02TO, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
The Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module is natural under
pushforward along an isomorphism `u : A ⟶ B` of two schemes over a test scheme carrying the module,
the module on `A` and on `B` being its pullbacks from the test scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (gysinSystemOfInvertible C).IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso
declarations.comment: the isomorphism case of the naturality of the Gysin operation of a Gysin system, for an invertible module pulled back from a test scheme to both schemes -- the form the Gysin axiom of a bivariant class quantifies over -- with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpensRestriction
declarations.doc:
**The open-immersion case of Stacks 02TA for the Gysin operation of a Gysin system, with the
module on the ambient scheme.** The Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible
module is natural under restriction along an open immersion over the base, with no hypothesis.

Its Gysin operation is `Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOnChowOfInvertible`, so this is
`Stacks.Chow.chowGroupRestrict_gysinHomomorphismOnChowOfInvertible_of_eq`, the open-immersion case
of Stacks 0B71 at that map, after the quantified open immersion of the two zero schemes is
identified with the morphism of Remark 0B6Y by `Stacks.Chow.eq_zeroSchemePullbackHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpensRestriction (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (gysinSystemOfInvertible C).IsNaturalUnderOpensRestriction
declarations.comment: the open-immersion case of the naturality of the Gysin operation of a Gysin system, for an invertible module on the ambient scheme: restriction along an open immersion over the base carries the Gysin map of Z(s) to the Gysin map of Z(u^*s) across the square of Remark 0B6Y, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**The open-immersion case of Stacks 02TA for the Gysin operation of a Gysin system.** The
Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module is natural under restriction
along an open immersion `u : A ⟶ B` of schemes over a test scheme carrying the module, with no
hypothesis.

The module on `A` is the pullback of the module on the test scheme, not the pullback along `u` of
the module on `B`, so this is not the ambient-module form
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpensRestriction` but its composite with the
comparison of the two spellings,
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderPullbackComp`: the quantified open immersion of
the two zero schemes factors as the transport along
`Stacks.Chow.zeroScheme_pullback_pullback` followed by the morphism of Remark 0B6Y, uniquely
because the closed immersion of the zero scheme downstairs is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (gysinSystemOfInvertible C).IsNaturalUnderOpenImmersion
declarations.comment: the open-immersion case of the naturality of the Gysin operation of a Gysin system, for an invertible module pulled back from a test scheme to both schemes -- the form the Gysin axiom of a bivariant class quantifies over -- with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderInverseIso
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism case of Stacks 02TA for the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule**,
with the invertible module on the source of the isomorphism: for an isomorphism `u : A ⟶ B` over
the base with inverse `w`, an invertible module `L` on `A`, a section `s` of it and a morphism `j`
of zero schemes lying over `u`, the Gysin map of `(w^*L, w^*s)` on `B` applied to `u_*α` is
`j_*` of the Gysin map of `(L, s)` on `A` applied to `α`.

Stacks 02TA for the proper morphism `w` and the module `L` on `A` itself,
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderProperPushforward`, gives
`i^* w_* β = (j'')_* (i')^* β` for the morphism `j''` of Remark 0B6Y; at `β = u_* α` the left
side collapses since `u ≫ w = 𝟙`, and `j'' ≫ j = 𝟙` because `j` lies over `u` and a closed
immersion is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderInverseIso (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (gysinSystemOfInvertible C).IsNaturalUnderInverseIso
declarations.comment: the inverse-isomorphism case of the naturality of the Gysin operation of a Gysin system, for the system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderProperPushforward
declarations.doc:
The Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module is natural under
pushforward along an arbitrary proper morphism over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderProperPushforward (C : ChowSituation.{u}) :
    (gysinSystemOfInvertible C).IsNaturalUnderProperPushforward
declarations.comment: the naturality of the Gysin operation of a Gysin system under pushforward along a general proper morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_of_gysinCompatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TA.** Gysin pullback through the zero scheme of a global section of an invertible
module commutes with proper pushforward across the square of Remark 0B6Y:

  `i^* f_* α' = g_* (i')^* α'`  in  `A_k(Z(s))`,  for every `α' ∈ Z_{k+1}(X')`.

Both Gysin maps are `Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible`, functions of the invertible
module and the section alone; the morphism `g` of Remark 0B6Y is
`Stacks.Chow.zeroSchemePullbackHom`; and the instance of Stacks 02S2 that
`Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward` requires along `g` is supplied by
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence`. Nothing is assumed beyond the
properness of `f` and the commutativity of `f` over the base.

Both sides are classes of cycles on `Z(s)`, and the two cycles are rationally equivalent by
`Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalent_gysinRule_extendCycleGroup_properPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_of_gysinCompatible [IsProper f]
    (hf : f ≫ p = p') (α : CycleGroup C p' (k + 1)) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s (properPushforward C p' p f hf (k + 1) α) =
      properChowPushforward C ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).subschemeι ≫ p')
        ((zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s)
        (zeroSchemePullbackHom_comp f L s C p p' hf) k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
          ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).subschemeι ≫ p')
          ((zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s)
          (zeroSchemePullbackHom_comp f L s C p p' hf) k)
        (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p' k ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L)
          (AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackGlobalSections f L s) α)
declarations.comment: the identity i^* f_* α' = g_* (i')^* α' in A_k(Z(s)) over the square of Remark 0B6Y, for the Gysin map of an invertible module and a global section, with no hypothesis beyond properness of f and the commutativity of f over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
Intersecting a closed subscheme properly with a Cartier zero scheme computes
its Gysin class.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ)
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections) (Z : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (Z.subschemeι ≫ p) ≤
      ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hDZ : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).comap Z.subschemeι)) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L (s.eval (.op ⊤))
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p Z.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)
          ((Z.comap (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι).subschemeι)
            k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_support_le_of_mono_section
declarations.doc:
The support of a coherent sheaf on which a Cartier section is regular
loses at least one dimension upon restriction to the zero scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_support_le_of_mono_section
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ)
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hF : schemeDeltaDimension C
      ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ p) ≤
        ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hs : Mono (((Functor.uncurry.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩)).map
        (((𝟙 F), (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s)) : (_, _) ⟶ (_, _))))) :
    schemeDeltaDimension C
      ((@reducedSupport _
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι).obj F)
          (@AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subscheme X
            (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian
              ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p))
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι F
            inferInstance)).subschemeι ≫
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p) ≤ (k : EInt)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
Gysin pullback of the associated cycle of a coherent sheaf on which the
section is regular is the associated cycle of its restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ)
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hF : schemeDeltaDimension C
      ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ p) ≤
        ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hs : Mono (((Functor.uncurry.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩)).map
        (((𝟙 F), (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s)) : (_, _) ⟶ (_, _))))) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L (s.eval (.op ⊤))
        (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf C p F
          (k + 1) hF) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (@cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf _ C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p) inferInstance
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι).obj F)
          (@AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subscheme X
            (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian
              ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p))
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι F
            inferInstance) k
          (by
            exact schemeDeltaDimension_pullback_support_le_of_mono_section
              C p k L s F hF hs))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_comm_weilDivisorCycleN
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TH for the two canonical divisor cycles.** On an integral, locally Noetherian
scheme of delta-dimension `k + 2`,

`c₁(N) ∩ div_L(s) = c₁(L) ∩ div_N(t)`  in  `A_k(X)`,

where `div_L(s)` and `div_N(t)` are the divisor cycles of the two sections of the situation. No
parameter besides the situation remains: the two presentations by the family that
`Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_comm` asks for are
`Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation.weilDivisorAlgebraicCycle_weilDivisorN_apply`, read on `ℱ` for
`div_N(t)` and on `ℱ.swap` for `div_L(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_comm_weilDivisorCycleN
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = ((k + 2 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k N (ℱ.swap.weilDivisorCycleN C p hn) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L (ℱ.weilDivisorCycleN C p hn)
declarations.comment: the identity for two invertible modules with nonzero meromorphic sections on an integral, locally Noetherian scheme of delta-dimension `k + 2`, with no hypothesis: the key formula of Stacks 0AYC is discharged by `Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation.keyFormula_toKeyFormulaData` and the two divisor cycles of Stacks 02SJ are the canonical ones of the two sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_divisorOfMeromorphicSection_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TH.** Let `X` be integral and locally of finite type over the base scheme `S` of
chapter 42, with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `L` and `N` be invertible `𝒪_X`-modules, and let `s` and `t`
be nonzero (that is, regular) meromorphic sections of `L` and `N`. Writing `α = div_L(s)` and
`β = div_N(t)` for their divisor cycles of Stacks 02SJ (1),

  `c₁(N) ∩ α = c₁(L) ∩ β`  in  `CH_{n-2}(X)`.

The cycles of degree `n - 1` are read in degree `(n - 2) + 1`, the source of the cap product
`CH_{(n-2)+1} → CH_{n-2}`, by `Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupOfEq`. The proof is the key formula of
Stacks 0AYC, through `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_divisorCycle_comm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_divisorOfMeromorphicSection_comm (n : ℤ)
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = (n : EInt)) (L N : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    (s : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s)
    (t : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf N)
    (ht : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf N t) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p (n - 2) N
        (cycleGroupOfEq (by ring) (divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle C p n hn L s hs)) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p (n - 2) L
        (cycleGroupOfEq (by ring) (divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle C p n hn N t ht))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_divisorCycle_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TH.** Let `X` be integral and locally of finite type over the base scheme `S` of
chapter 42, of delta-dimension `k + 2`, let `L` and `N` be invertible modules on `X` and let `s`
and `t` be nonzero meromorphic sections of `L` and `N`. Writing `α = div_L(s)` and
`β = div_N(t)` for their divisor cycles of Stacks 02SJ (1),

  `c₁(N) ∩ α = c₁(L) ∩ β`  in  `A_k(X)`.

Nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses: the family of prime divisors and the local
generators of the situation of Stacks 0AYB are produced by
`Stacks.Chow.keyFormulaSituationOf`, the key formula of Stacks 0AYC for it is
`Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation.keyFormula_toKeyFormulaData`, the component rules of Stacks 02SO
are the canonical ones of `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible`, and the two divisor
cycles are presented by the family because a prime divisor outside it carries no order of
vanishing. The source states the conclusion in `CH_{n-2}(X)` for `dim_δ(X) = n`; here
`n = k + 2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_divisorCycle_comm
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = ((k + 2 : ℤ) : EInt)) (L N : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    {s : L.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X)} (hs : s ≠ 0)
    {t : N.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X)} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k N (divisorCycleOfInvertibleSection C p hn L s) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C p k L (divisorCycleOfInvertibleSection C p hn N t)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernCapFactorsEverywhere
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TI, with no hypothesis.** Intersecting with the first Chern class of an invertible
module kills every `(k+1)`-cycle rationally equivalent to zero, whatever the scheme locally of
finite type over the base and whatever the module.

This is the reduction of `Stacks.Chow.firstChernCapFactorsEverywhere_iff_killsPrincipalDivisor`
supplied with its integral case.
declarations.statement: theorem firstChernCapFactorsEverywhere : FirstChernCapFactorsEverywhere C k
declarations.comment: the factoring itself, with no hypothesis: capping with the first Chern class of an invertible module kills every cycle rationally equivalent to zero, for every scheme locally of finite type over the base and every module

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TI.** Intersection with the first Chern class of an invertible module, as an
operation `c₁(L) ∩ - : A_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(X)` on Chow groups.
declarations.statement: def firstChernClassCapChow : chowGroup C p (k + 1) →+ chowGroup C p k
declarations.comment: the descended operation c_1(L) cap - : A_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(X), agreeing with the cap product of 02SO on cycle representatives (firstChernClassCapChow_mk)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible_comm_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TJ.** For two invertible modules `ℒ` and `𝒩` on a scheme `X` locally of finite type
over the base, intersecting successively with the two first Chern classes is independent of the
order: `c₁(ℒ) ∩ c₁(𝒩) ∩ α = c₁(𝒩) ∩ c₁(ℒ) ∩ α` in `A_k(X)` for `α ∈ A_{k+1+1}(X)`.

The four descended operations are those of `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible`,
whose Stacks 02TI input is supplied by `Stacks.Chow.firstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor` in each of
the two degrees, and Stacks 02TH enters through
`Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.firstChernCapCommutesOnIntegralComponents`; see the implementation
notes of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ChernCapCommutativityInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible_comm_unconditional
    (α : chowGroup C p (k + 1 + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible C k (firstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor C k) p L
        (firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible C (k + 1)
          (firstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor C (k + 1)) p N α) =
      firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible C k (firstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor C k) p N
        (firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible C (k + 1)
          (firstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor C (k + 1)) p L α)
declarations.comment: the commutativity itself, with no hypotheses beyond the source's: it is `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible_comm` with both of its inputs supplied by the theorems named below, and it is the one registration of this tag. The four descended cap products are `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOnChowOfInvertible`, and the Stacks 02TI input each of them needs — the reduced form `Stacks.Chow.FirstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor`, the vanishing of the cap product on one principal divisor on an integral scheme, to which `Stacks.Chow.firstChernCapFactorsEverywhere_iff_killsPrincipalDivisor` shows Stacks 02TI is equivalent — is supplied in both degrees by `Stacks.Chow.firstChernCapKillsPrincipalDivisor`, which proves it outright. Stacks 02TH for the restrictions of the two modules to the integral closed subschemes of `X` of delta-dimension `k + 2`, as an equality of classes in `A_k(W)`, which is what the source reduces to, is `Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.firstChernCapCommutesOnIntegralComponents`, which proves it out of the key formula of Stacks 0AYC. The four cycle-level rules of Stacks 02SO and the four separate instances of Stacks 02TI that `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOnChow_comm` takes as inputs are all theorems here, and the passage from the integral subschemes to every class is proved too

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersection_eq_firstChernClassCap_of_keyFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TM, pushed forward to the ambient scheme.** Let `X` be integral of
delta-dimension `k + 2`, let `E` be an effective Cartier divisor on `X` and let `N` be an
invertible module with a nonzero meromorphic section `t`. Then intersecting `div_N(t)` with `E`
agrees with capping the fundamental cycle `[E]_{k+1}` with the first Chern class of `N`, in
`A_k(X)`.

This is the identity `i^* div_N(t) = c₁(N|_E) ∩ [E]_{k+1}` of the source after pushing forward
along the closed immersion `i : E ⟶ X`, the right hand side being read on `X` through Stacks 02SU;
see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Gysin42.ChernCapDivisor`.

Intersection with `E` is capping with `c₁(𝒪_X(E))` by Stacks 02T9, and the fundamental cycle
`[E]_{k+1}` is the divisor cycle of the canonical section `1_E` of `𝒪_X(E)`, presented by the
family `{Z_i}` of the key formula through `hfundamentalCycle`. So the identity is the
commutativity of Stacks 02TH for the pair `(𝒪_X(E), N)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierIntersection_eq_firstChernClassCap_of_keyFormula
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = ((k + 2 : ℤ) : EInt)) (E : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor E] (D : KeyFormulaData X)
    (hKey : D.KeyFormula C p) (chernN : FirstChernComponentCycleRule C p k)
    (hchernE : ∀ (i : D.Index) (hW : IsIntegral (D.component i).subscheme)
      (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C ((D.component i).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)),
      (firstChernComponentCycleRule C p k (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
        (D.component i) hW hDim).1 = D.restrictedDivisorL i)
    (hchernN : ∀ (i : D.Index) (hW : IsIntegral (D.component i).subscheme)
      (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C ((D.component i).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)),
      (chernN (D.component i) hW hDim).1 = D.restrictedDivisorN i)
    (fundamentalCycle divN : CycleGroup C p (k + 1))
    (hfundamentalCycle : ∀ x : X, fundamentalCycle.1 x = ∑ᶠ i, D.orderL i *
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (D.component i).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x)
    (hdivN : ∀ x : X, divN.1 x = ∑ᶠ i, D.orderN i *
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (D.component i).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x) :
    effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible C p k (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)
        (isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_divisorSheaf E) divN =
      firstChernClassCap C p k chernN fundamentalCycle
declarations.comment: after pushforward along E ⟶ X, granting the key formula 0AYC

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_eq_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_of_keyFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TM.** Let `X` be integral of delta-dimension `k + 2`, let `E` be an effective
Cartier divisor on `X` with closed immersion `i : E ⟶ X`, and let `N` be an invertible module on
`X` with a nonzero meromorphic section `t`. Then

`i^* div_N(t) = c₁(N|_E) ∩ [E]_{k+1}`  in  `A_k(E)`,

the identity of the source: the left hand side is the Gysin pullback of Stacks 02T8 along `i`,
which takes its values in the Chow group of `E`, and the right hand side is the cap product of
Stacks 02SO on `E` with the first Chern class of the restriction `N|_E`, applied to the
fundamental cycle of `E` read as a cycle on `E`.

The divisor cycle `div_N(t)` of Stacks 02SJ and the fundamental cycle `[E]_{k+1}` are explicit
parameters, each with the presentation the second step of the source's proof gives it: the first
by the family `{Z_i}` of prime divisors of the key formula data `D`, with the orders
`ord_{B_i}(g_i)`, and the second by a locally finite family `{V_j}` of integral closed subschemes
of `E` of delta-dimension `k + 1`, with multiplicities `m_j`. The remaining input is the rational
equivalence `Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaRationalEquivalenceOnDivisor` on `E`, which is the last step
of the source's proof; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Gysin42.ChernCapDivisor`.

Given these, the two sides are computed on their presentations by the locally finite component
formulas of Stacks 02T8 and 02SO, and the rational equivalence identifies the resulting two
classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_eq_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_of_keyFormula
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = ((k + 2 : ℤ) : EInt)) (E : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor E] (N : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    (D : KeyFormulaData X) {J : Type u}
    (V : J → (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
      (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subscheme.IdealSheafData)
    (hV : ∀ j, IsIntegral (V j).subscheme)
    (hVdim : ∀ j, schemeDeltaDimension C ((V j).subschemeι ≫
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
          (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι ≫ p) =
      ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hVlocal : LocallyFinite fun j ↦ ((V j).support :
      Set (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subscheme))
    (m : J → ℤ)
    (hKeyOnDivisor : KeyFormulaRationalEquivalenceOnDivisor C p hn E N D V hV hVdim m)
    (divN : CycleGroup C p (k + 1))
    (hdivN : ∀ x : X, divN.1 x = ∑ᶠ i, D.orderN i *
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (D.component i).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x)
    (fundamentalCycle : CycleGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X
      (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
      (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι ≫ p) (k + 1))
    (hfundamentalCycle : ∀ z : (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X
      (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
      (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subscheme,
      fundamentalCycle.1 z = ∑ᶠ j, m j *
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X
            (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
            (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι ≫ p)
          (V j).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 z) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E) divN =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X
          (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
          (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι ≫ p) k
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X
          (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf E)
          (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι).obj N)
        fundamentalCycle
declarations.comment: the identity i^* div_N(t) = c₁(N|_D) ∩ [D]_{n-1} in A_{n-2}(D), the conclusion of the source, granting the rational equivalence `KeyFormulaRationalEquivalenceOnDivisor` that the key formula 0AYC exhibits on D — the last step of the source's proof — together with the divisor cycle div_N(t) of 02SJ and the fundamental cycle [D]_{n-1} read on D, each with its presentation by a locally finite family of integral closed subschemes of delta-dimension n-1, which is the second step of the source's proof

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysin_divisorOfMeromorphicSection_eq_firstChernClassCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TM.** Let `X` be integral and locally of finite type over the base scheme `S` of
chapter 42, with `n = dim_δ(X)`, let `i : D ⟶ X` be an effective Cartier divisor, and let `N` be
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module with a nonzero (that is, regular) meromorphic section `t`. Then

  `i^* div_N(t) = c₁(N|_D) ∩ [D]_{n-1}`  in  `CH_{n-2}(D)`.

Here `i^*` is the Gysin homomorphism of Stacks 02T8 for the pair `(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)`, whose zero
scheme is `D` (`Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme_canonicalSection`), so it takes values in the Chow
group of `D`; `div_N(t)` is the divisor cycle of Stacks 02SJ (1); `N|_D` is the pullback of `N`
along `i`; and `[D]_{n-1}` is the fundamental cycle of `D`, the cycle of `D` as a closed
subscheme of itself. Cycles of degree `n - 1` are read in degree `(n - 2) + 1`, the source of
`i^*` and of the cap product into degree `n - 2`, by `Stacks.Chow.cycleGroupOfEq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysin_divisorOfMeromorphicSection_eq_firstChernClassCap (n : ℤ)
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C p = (n : EInt)) (E : X.IdealSheafData)
    [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor E] (N : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    (t : AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSection X.sheaf N)
    (ht : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf N t) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p (n - 2) (divisorSheaf E) (divisorSheafGlobalSection E)
        (cycleGroupOfEq (by ring) (divisorOfMeromorphicSectionCycle C p n hn N t ht)) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (divisorSheaf E)
          (divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι ≫ p) (n - 2)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (divisorSheaf E)
          (divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι).obj N)
        (cycleGroupOfEq (by ring) (fundamentalCycle C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (divisorSheaf E)
            (divisorSheafGlobalSection E)).subschemeι ≫ p) (n - 1)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinOfInvertibleDescends
declarations.doc:
For every scheme locally of finite type over the base, every invertible module on it, every
global section of that module and every degree, the Gysin map of the zero scheme of the section
kills the cycles rationally equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement: theorem gysinOfInvertibleDescends (C : ChowSituation.{u}) : GysinOfInvertibleDescends C
declarations.comment: the vanishing for every test datum at once, with no hypothesis: the bundled form of `gysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TO.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base `S` of chapter 42, let `L` be
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `s ∈ Γ(X, L)`, with zero scheme `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X` as in Stacks
02T8. The Gysin homomorphism `i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D)` kills every `(k+1)`-cycle rationally
equivalent to zero, so it factors through rational equivalence; the map it induces on Chow groups
is `Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible`.

The proof follows the source: the reduction to one integral `V` and one rational function on it
is `Stacks.Chow.gysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_components`, and that case
is `Stacks.Chow.gysinOfInvertibleKillsPrincipalDivisorOnComponent`, from the key formula 0AYC.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence :
    GysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C p k L s
declarations.comment: the Gysin homomorphism i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D) of the zero scheme of a section of an invertible module factors through rational equivalence; the induced map i^* : A_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D) is `gysinChowOfInvertible`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TO.** The Gysin homomorphism of the zero scheme `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X` of a global
section of an invertible module factors through rational equivalence to give the map

  `i^* : A_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D)`.

Its value on the class of a cycle is the Gysin homomorphism of Stacks 02T8 on that cycle
(`Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_mk`), and `Stacks.Chow.eq_gysinHomomorphismOnChowOfInvertible`
says it is the only homomorphism of Chow groups agreeing with the Gysin map of Stacks 02T8 on
cycle representatives.
declarations.statement:
def gysinChowOfInvertible : chowGroup C p (k + 1) →+
    chowGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
declarations.comment: the map i^* : A_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D) induced by the Gysin homomorphism of the zero scheme of a section of an invertible module, which factors through rational equivalence by `gysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_canonicalSection_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR, first equality.** Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r + 1`
between schemes locally of finite type over the base, let `i : D ⟶ X` be a relative effective
Cartier divisor on `X/Y` and let `i^*` be the Gysin map of the canonical section of `𝒪_X(D)`,
whose zero scheme is `D` (Stacks 01X0). Then `p|_D` is flat of relative dimension `r` and

  `i^* p^* α = (p|_D)^* α`  in  `CH_{k+1+r}(D)`  for every  `α ∈ CH_{k+1}(Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_canonicalSection_flatPullbackChow (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    haveI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D := hD.1
    haveI : Flat (D.subschemeι ≫ p) := hD.2
    zeroScheme_divisorSheafGlobalSection D ▸
      gysinChowOfInvertible C sX (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf D)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection D)
        (chowGroupCast C sX (degree_flatPullback_succ k r)
          (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1) α)) =
      flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C (D.subschemeι ≫ sX) sY (D.subschemeι ≫ p)
        (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r
        (Stacks.Divisors.relativeDimension_subschemeι_comp_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
          p r hp D hD) (k + 1) α
declarations.comment: first equality i^* p^* α = (p|_D)^* α, for p of relative dimension r + 1 (relative dimension 0 is `gysinChowOfInvertible_canonicalSection_flatPullbackChow_of_relativeDimension_zero`)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapChow_divisorSheaf_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR, second equality.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_canonicalSection_flatPullbackChow`, with `ℒ = 𝒪_X(D)`,

  `c₁(ℒ) ∩ p^* α = i_*((p|_D)^* α)`  in  `CH_{k+1+r}(X)`  for every  `α ∈ CH_{k+1}(Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapChow_divisorSheaf_flatPullbackChow (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    haveI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D := hD.1
    haveI : Flat (D.subschemeι ≫ p) := hD.2
    firstChernClassCapChow C (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) sX (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf D)
        (chowGroupCast C sX (degree_flatPullback_succ k r)
          (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1) α)) =
      properChowPushforward C (D.subschemeι ≫ sX) sX D.subschemeι rfl (k + 1 + (r : ℤ))
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C _ sX _ rfl _)
        (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C (D.subschemeι ≫ sX) sY (D.subschemeι ≫ p)
          (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r
          (Stacks.Divisors.relativeDimension_subschemeι_comp_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
            p r hp D hD) (k + 1) α)
declarations.comment: second equality c_1(O_X(D)) ∩ p^* α = i_*((p|_D)^* α), for p of relative dimension r + 1 (relative dimension 0 is `firstChernClassCapChow_divisorSheaf_flatPullbackChow_of_relativeDimension_zero`)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_canonicalSection_flatPullbackChow_of_relativeDimension_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR in relative dimension zero, first equality.** If `p` has relative dimension `0`
then a relative effective Cartier divisor `D` on `X/Y` is empty, so `CH_k(D) = 0` and
`i^* p^* α = 0` for every `α ∈ CH_{k+1}(Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_canonicalSection_flatPullbackChow_of_relativeDimension_zero
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p 0) (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    haveI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D := hD.1
    (zeroScheme_divisorSheafGlobalSection D ▸
      gysinChowOfInvertible C sX k (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf D)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection D)
        (chowGroupCast C sX (show k + 1 + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 by simp)
          (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C sX sY p hbase 0 hp (k + 1) α)) :
        chowGroup C (D.subschemeι ≫ sX) k) = 0
declarations.comment: first equality, for p of relative dimension 0: D is empty, so CH_k(D) = 0 and i^* p^* α = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapChow_divisorSheaf_flatPullbackChow_of_relativeDimension_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR in relative dimension zero, second equality.** If `p` has relative dimension `0`
then a relative effective Cartier divisor `D` on `X/Y` is empty, so `i_*((p|_D)^* α) = 0` and
`c₁(𝒪_X(D)) ∩ p^* α = 0` for every `α ∈ CH_{k+1}(Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapChow_divisorSheaf_flatPullbackChow_of_relativeDimension_zero
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p 0) (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    haveI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D := hD.1
    firstChernClassCapChow C k sX (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf D)
        (chowGroupCast C sX (show k + 1 + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 by simp)
          (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C sX sY p hbase 0 hp (k + 1) α)) = 0
declarations.comment: second equality, for p of relative dimension 0: D is empty, so c_1(O_X(D)) ∩ p^* α = i_*(0) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR, first equality, on an integral component.** Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be flat of
relative dimension `r + 1` over the base scheme of chapter 42, let `i : D ⟶ X` be a relative
effective Cartier divisor on `X/Y` presented as the zero scheme of a section `s` of an invertible
module `L`, and let `W ⊆ Y` be an integral closed subscheme of delta-dimension `k + 1`. Then

  `i^* p^* [W]_{k+1} = (p|_D)^* [W]_{k+1}`  in  `A_{k+1+r}(D)`.

The relative dimension `hq` of `D ⟶ Y` is a parameter; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.RelativeEffectiveCartierFlatPullback`. The flatness of
`D ⟶ Y` is both the second conjunct of `hD` and an instance binder, because stating
`(p|_D)^*` needs it before `hD` is available.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [Flat p] (hbase : p ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (k : ℤ) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections)
    [Flat ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)]
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))))
    (hq : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p) r)
    (W : Y.IdealSheafData) (hWint : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hWdim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ sY) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hcast : k + 1 + ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 + (r : ℤ) + 1) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C sX (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) L (s.eval (.op ⊤))
        (hcast ▸ flatPullback C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1)
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY W.subschemeι (k + 1))) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (flatPullback C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sY
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)
          (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r hq (k + 1)
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY W.subschemeι (k + 1)))
declarations.comment: first equality, on the fundamental cycle of an integral closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR, second equality, on an integral component, as intersection with `D`.** In the
situation of `Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle`,

  `D · p^* [W]_{k+1} = i_* ((p|_D)^* [W]_{k+1})`  in  `A_{k+1+r}(X)`,

where `D · −` is intersection with the effective Cartier divisor `D` (Stacks 02T8). The source
writes the left side as `c₁(ℒ) ∩ p^* α`; that form is
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle` below, one rewrite of this
through Stacks 02T9.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [Flat p] (hbase : p ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (k : ℤ) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections)
    [Flat ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)]
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))))
    (hq : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p) r)
    (W : Y.IdealSheafData) (hWint : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hWdim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ sY) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hcast : k + 1 + ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 + (r : ℤ) + 1) :
    effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible C sX (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) L (s.eval (.op ⊤)) hD.1
        (hcast ▸ flatPullback C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1)
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY W.subschemeι (k + 1))) =
      properChowPushforward C
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sX
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι rfl (k + 1 + (r : ℤ))
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sX rfl
          (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)))
        (QuotientAddGroup.mk
          (flatPullback C
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sY
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)
            (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r hq (k + 1)
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY W.subschemeι (k + 1))))
declarations.comment: second equality, as intersection with D, on a fundamental cycle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02TR, second equality, on an integral component.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle`,

  `c₁(L) ∩ p^* [W]_{k+1} = i_* ((p|_D)^* [W]_{k+1})`  in  `A_{k+1+r}(X)`,

the source's second equality: the left side is the cap product of Stacks 02SO and `L` is
canonically `𝒪_X(D)`, the divisor being the zero scheme of `s`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle` read
through Stacks 02T9, in the form
`Stacks.Chow.effectiveCartierIntersectionOfInvertible_eq_firstChernClassCapOfInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapOfInvertible_flatPullback_primeCycle
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [Flat p] (hbase : p ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (k : ℤ) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections)
    [Flat ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)]
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))))
    (hq : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p) r)
    (W : Y.IdealSheafData) (hWint : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hWdim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ sY) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hcast : k + 1 + ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 + (r : ℤ) + 1) :
    firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sX (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) L
        (hcast ▸ flatPullback C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1)
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY W.subschemeι (k + 1))) =
      properChowPushforward C
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sX
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι rfl (k + 1 + (r : ℤ))
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sX rfl
          (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)))
        (QuotientAddGroup.mk
          (flatPullback C
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sY
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)
            (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r hq (k + 1)
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C sY W.subschemeι (k + 1))))
declarations.comment: second equality, in the c₁(L) ∩ − form, on a fundamental cycle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r + 1` over
the base scheme of chapter 42 and let `i : D ⟶ X` be a relative effective Cartier divisor on
`X/Y`, presented as the zero scheme of a section `s` of an invertible module `L`. Then for every
class `α ∈ A_{k+1}(Y)`

  `i^* p^* α = (p|_D)^* α`  in  `A_{k+r}(D)`,

for the Gysin pullback of Stacks 02TO and the flat pullbacks of Stacks 02S1 on Chow groups, `p|_D`
having relative dimension `r` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.relativeDimension_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_flatPullbackChow (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [Flat p] (hbase : p ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (k : ℤ) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections)
    [Flat ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)]
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))))
    (hcast : k + 1 + ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 + (r : ℤ) + 1)
    (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    gysinChowOfInvertible C sX (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) L (s.eval (.op ⊤))
        (hcast ▸ flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1) α) =
      flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sY
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)
        (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r
        (AlgebraicGeometry.relativeDimension_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p r hp
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))) hD) (k + 1) α
declarations.comment: first equality, for an arbitrary class in A_{k+1}(Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapChow_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
In the situation of
`Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_flatPullbackChow`, for every class `α ∈ A_{k+1}(Y)`

  `c₁(L) ∩ p^* α = i_* ((p|_D)^* α)`  in  `A_{k+r}(X)`,

the cap product being the descended operation of Stacks 02TI, with `D` the zero scheme of `s`, so
that `L` is `𝒪_X(D)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapChow_flatPullbackChow (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [Flat p] (hbase : p ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hp : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension p (r + 1)) (k : ℤ) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections)
    [Flat ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)]
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))))
    (hcast : k + 1 + ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 + (r : ℤ) + 1)
    (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCapChow C (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)) sX L
        (hcast ▸ flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C sX sY p hbase (r + 1) hp (k + 1) α) =
      properChowPushforward C
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sX
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι rfl (k + 1 + (r : ℤ))
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sX rfl
          (k + 1 + (r : ℤ)))
        (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ sX) sY
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))).subschemeι ≫ p)
          (by rw [Category.assoc, hbase]) r
          (AlgebraicGeometry.relativeDimension_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor p r hp
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (.op ⊤))) hD) (k + 1) α)
declarations.comment: second equality, for an arbitrary class in A_{k+1}(Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackChow_surjective_isAffineSpaceBundle
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X` and `Y` be locally of finite type
over `S` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r` such that every point of `Y` has
an open neighbourhood `U` over which `f` is the projection `𝔸^r_U ⟶ U`. Then
