theorem exists_splittingMorphism_basechange_uniform (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (I : Type) [Fintype I] (E : I → X.Modules)
    (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ T : SplittingMorphism C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
      BaseChangeInjective C sX T.π (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) ∧
        ∀ i, Stacks.WeilCohomology.HasInvertibleFiltration T.P
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.π).obj (E i)) (r i)
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (2) for a finite collection of finite locally free modules of constant ranks r_i, with relative dimension d = sum of binom(r_i, 2), and with clause (1) in the form the source states it: ONE morphism pi : P -> X, and for EVERY f : Y -> X injectivity in every degree of the flat pullback along the base change of that pi, which is Stacks.Chow.BaseChangeInjective quantified over every cartesian square over pi and f. The only hypotheses are the source's: each module finite locally free of constant rank r_i. Clause (1) is proved through the iteration -- base case the identity of X, whose base change is an isomorphism; inductive step the splitting of the base change of a composite by CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_bot together with Stacks 02RD for a composite pullback, the base-changed layer being the projective bundle of the pulled-back module by Stacks.ProjectiveBundle.isPullback_baseChangeHom and its pullback injective by the injectivity half of Stacks 02TX. The single word of the tag delivered more weakly is projective, delivered as proper: IsProjectiveMorphism of the identity of X needs the identification of P^0_X with X, which this repository lacks

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_splittingMorphism_isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02UL (the splitting principle).** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, `X` locally
of finite type over `S` and `ℰ_i` (`i ∈ I`, `I` finite) finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules of
ranks `r_i`. There is a morphism `π : P ⟶ X` which is

* projective (Stacks 01W8), flat, and of relative dimension `d = ∑_i binom(r_i, 2)`,

such that

1. for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` locally of finite type over `S`, the flat pullback
   `π_Y^* : CH_k(Y) ⟶ CH_{k+d}(Y ×_X P)` along the base change of `π` is injective for every
   `k` (`Stacks.Chow.UniversallyChowInjective`), and
2. each `π^*ℰ_i` has a filtration whose successive quotients `ℒ_{i,1}, …, ℒ_{i,r_i}` are
   invertible `𝒪_P`-modules;

moreover the restriction map `A^*(X) ⟶ A^*(P)` of Stacks 0B7F is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_splittingMorphism_isProjective (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (I : Type) [Fintype I] (E : I → X.Modules)
    (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ T : SplittingMorphism C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
      IsProjective T.π ∧ Flat T.π ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension T.π (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) ∧
      UniversallyChowInjective C T.π (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) T.relDim ∧
      (∀ i, Stacks.WeilCohomology.HasInvertibleFiltration T.P
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.π).obj (E i)) (r i)) ∧
      ∀ (G : GysinSystem C) (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso),
        Function.Injective (chowCohomologyTotalRestriction C G sX T.π hgys)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_splittingMorphism_isProjective_ofInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02UL (the splitting principle).** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, `X` locally
of finite type over `S` and `ℰ_i` (`i ∈ I`, `I` finite) finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules of
ranks `r_i`. There is a morphism `π : P ⟶ X` which is

* projective (Stacks 01W8), flat, and of relative dimension `d = ∑_i binom(r_i, 2)`,

such that

1. for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` locally of finite type over `S`, the flat pullback
   `π_Y^* : CH_k(Y) ⟶ CH_{k+d}(Y ×_X P)` along the base change of `π` is injective for every
   `k` (`Stacks.Chow.UniversallyChowInjective`), and
2. each `π^*ℰ_i` has a filtration whose successive quotients `ℒ_{i,1}, …, ℒ_{i,r_i}` are
   invertible `𝒪_P`-modules;

moreover the restriction map `res : A^*(X) ⟶ A^*(P)` of Stacks 0B7F,
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible`, is injective. Nothing is assumed
beyond the hypotheses of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_splittingMorphism_isProjective_ofInvertible (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (I : Type) [Fintype I]
    (E : I → X.Modules) (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ T : SplittingMorphism C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
      IsProjective T.π ∧ Flat T.π ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension T.π (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) ∧
      UniversallyChowInjective C T.π (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) T.relDim ∧
      (∀ i, Stacks.WeilCohomology.HasInvertibleFiltration T.P
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.π).obj (E i)) (r i)) ∧
      Function.Injective (chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible C sX T.π)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_splittingMorphism_universal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02UL, the splitting principle.** Let `(S, δ)` be the situation of Stacks 02QL, let
`X` be locally of finite type over `S` and let `ℰ_i`, `i ∈ I` finite, be finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules of ranks `r_i`. There is a flat proper morphism `π : P ⟶ X` of relative dimension
`d = ∑_i binom(r_i, 2)`, along which flat pullback on Chow groups is injective in every degree,
such that

1. for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` locally of finite type over `S` the flat pullback
   `π_Y^* : A_k(Y) ⟶ A_{k+d}(Y ×_X P)` along the base change `π_Y : Y ×_X P ⟶ Y` is injective in
   every degree, and
2. each `π^*ℰ_i` has a filtration of length `r_i` whose successive quotients are invertible
   `𝒪_P`-modules.

The morphism is the iterated projective bundle
(`Stacks.Chow.BundleStep.ofProjectiveBundle`); clause (1) is carried through the iteration as
`Stacks.Chow.UniversallyInjectiveFlatPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_splittingMorphism_universal (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (I : Type) [Fintype I] (E : I → X.Modules)
    (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ T : SplittingMorphism C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
      (∀ {Y : Scheme.{u}} (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : Y ⟶ X) (k : ℤ),
        Function.Injective (flatPullbackChow C (pullback.fst f T.π ≫ sY) sY (pullback.fst f T.π)
          rfl (∑ i, (r i).choose 2)
          (AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension.of_isPullback
            (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f T.π).flip T.relDim) k
          (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general C _ _ _ _ _ _ _))) ∧
      ∀ i, Stacks.WeilCohomology.HasInvertibleFiltration T.P
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.π).obj (E i)) (r i)
declarations.comment: both clauses, clause (1) in the source's form: for every f : Y -> X, with Y locally of finite type over S by an arbitrary structure morphism, flat pullback along the base change Y x_X P -> Y is injective in every degree. Relative dimension d = sum of binom(r_i, 2). The source says projective; the morphism delivered is flat and proper (each layer is a projective bundle, proper by Stacks 0800), but H-projectivity of the tower is not proved

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_iff_isSmoothAt_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness at a prime is insensitive to base field extension** (Stacks 02UQ). Let `k` be a
field, `S` a finite type `k`-algebra, `K` a `k`-algebra and `S'` the base change `K ⊗_k S`. Let
`q'` be a prime of `S'` lying over the prime `q` of `S`. Then `S` is smooth over `k` at `q` if and
only if `S'` is smooth over `K` at `q'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSmoothAt_iff_isSmoothAt_of_isPushout {k S K S' : Type*} [Field k]
    [CommRing S] [CommRing K] [CommRing S'] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k K] [Algebra S S']
    [Algebra K S'] [Algebra k S'] [IsScalarTower k K S'] [IsScalarTower k S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout k S K S'] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (q : Ideal S) (q' : Ideal S')
    [q.IsPrime] [q'.IsPrime] [q'.LiesOver q] :
    Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q ↔ Algebra.IsSmoothAt K q'
declarations.comment:
The source takes `K/k` a field extension; `K` is here an arbitrary commutative
`k`-algebra, since only flatness of `k → K` is used and that is automatic over a field. The base
change is the abstract one, `Algebra.IsPushout k S K S'`, the prime correspondence is
`Ideal.LiesOver`, and smoothness at a prime is Mathlib's `Algebra.IsSmoothAt`, which for a finite
type algebra over a field is the source's Definition 00TB. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_singleton_fiber_of_isUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02UR.** Let `S` be an `R`-algebra of finite type and let `q` be a prime of `S`. If
`R → S` is unramified at `q` then it is quasi-finite at `q`: the point `q` is isolated in the
fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` through it. In particular an unramified ring map is quasi-finite: for
`[Algebra.Unramified R S]`, `Algebra.QuasiFinite R S` is found by instance resolution.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isOpen_singleton_fiber_of_isUnramifiedAt {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    [Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt R q.asIdeal] :
    IsOpen (X := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {q.comap (algebraMap R S)}) {⟨q, rfl⟩}
declarations.comment:
Unramified at `q` is `Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt R q` (Definition 00UT (3), via
`Algebra.exists_unramified_of_isUnramifiedAt`). Quasi-finite at `q` is Definition 00PL, the
equivalent conditions of Lemma 00PK, and the conclusion is condition (1), `q` isolated in its
fibre; condition (2), `Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q`, is instead Mathlib's instance
`Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt.instQuasiFiniteOfEssFiniteTypeOfFormallyUnramified`, which holds under
weaker hypotheses than the source's. The second sentence needs no declaration:
`Algebra.QuasiFinite R S` for `[Algebra.Unramified R S]` is `inferInstance`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaf.canonicalComplementSequence_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02UT.** The canonical sequence associated to an open subset and its
closed complement is short exact for every sheaf of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalComplementSequence_shortExact
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X) :
    ((canonicalComplementSequence U).obj F).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.hasCohomologyPushforwardIso_of_isClosedEmbedding
declarations.doc:
Closed embeddings have exact pushforward, and the derived global-sections
comparison is an isomorphism in every degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasCohomologyPushforwardIso_of_isClosedEmbedding
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i) :
    HasCohomologyPushforwardIso (hExtZ := hExtZ) (hExtX := hExtX) i

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.cohomologyPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
For a closed embedding `i : Z ⟶ X`, cohomology of an abelian sheaf on `Z` is
canonically isomorphic, naturally in the sheaf, to the cohomology of its pushforward to `X`.
This is [Stacks Project, Tag 02UV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02UV).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cohomologyPushforwardIso
    [hExtZ : HasExt.{w'} (Z.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    [hExtX : HasExt.{w'} (X.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i) (p : ℕ) :
    (@CategoryTheory.Sheaf.functorH _ _ (Opens.grothendieckTopology Z)
      hSheafZ hExtZ p :
      Z.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{w} ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w'}) ≅
      TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward AddCommGrpCat.{w} i ⋙
        (@CategoryTheory.Sheaf.functorH _ _ (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          hSheafX hExtX p :
          X.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{w} ⥤
            AddCommGrpCat.{w'})

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafH_constantSheaf_of_irreducibleSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02UW.** Let `X` be an irreducible topological space and `A` an abelian group. Then
`H^p(X, A) = 0` for every `p > 0`, where `A` also denotes the constant sheaf with value `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_constantSheaf_of_irreducibleSpace (A : AddCommGrpCat.{v}) (p : ℕ)
    (hp : 0 < p) :
    Subsingleton
      (Sheaf.H
        ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj A) p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafH_of_subsingleton_sheafH_integerExtensionByZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02UX]** (a special case of [Tohoku, Proposition 3.6.1]). Let `X` be a
topological space and let `d ≥ 0` be an integer. Assume

1. `X` is quasi-compact,
2. the quasi-compact opens form a basis for `X`,
3. the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, and
4. `Hᵖ(X, j_!ℤ_U) = 0` for all `p > d` and any quasi-compact open `j : U → X`.

Then `Hᵖ(X, ℱ) = 0` for all `p > d` and any abelian sheaf `ℱ` on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_of_subsingleton_sheafH_integerExtensionByZero (d : ℕ)
    (hX : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set X))
    (hBasis : PrespectralSpace (X : Type u))
    (hInter : QuasiSeparatedSpace (X : Type u))
    (hvanish : ∀ U : Opens X, IsCompact (U : Set X) → ∀ p : ℕ, d < p →
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} (integerExtensionByZero X U) p))
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X) (p : ℕ) (hp : d < p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} F p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ConstantIntegerSubsheaves.exists_open_restrict_iso_constant_zmultiples
declarations.doc:
An abelian subsheaf of the constant integer sheaf is, on some nonempty open of an
irreducible space, the constant sheaf of `dℤ`, compatibly with its inclusion into the
constant integer sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_restrict_iso_constant_zmultiples
    (X : TopCat.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X]
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [∀ (U : Opens X), HasSheafify
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U)) AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    (H : Subobject ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{v} ℤ)))) :
    ∃ (U : Opens X), (U : Set X).Nonempty ∧
      ∃ (d : ULift.{v} ℤ)
        (eH : ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))
          AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (AddSubgroup.zmultiples d))).obj ≅
          restrictPresheaf (Subobject.underlying.obj H).obj U)
        (eZ : ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))
          AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{v} ℤ))).obj ≅
          restrictPresheaf
            ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj
              (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{v} ℤ))).obj U),
        (∀ (V : (Opens ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))ᵒᵖ),
          ((toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))
            ((Functor.const (Opens ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))ᵒᵖ).obj
              (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{v} ℤ)))).app V) ≫ eZ.hom.app V =
          (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            ((Functor.const (Opens X)ᵒᵖ).obj
              (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{v} ℤ)))).app
                (op (U.isOpenEmbedding.functor.obj V.unop))) ∧
        (∀ (V : (Opens ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))ᵒᵖ),
          ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))
          AddCommGrpCat.{v}).map
            (AddCommGrpCat.ofHom
              (AddSubgroup.zmultiples d).subtype)).hom.app V ≫
              eZ.hom.app V = eH.hom.app V ≫
              H.arrow.hom.app (op (U.isOpenEmbedding.functor.obj V.unop)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomologyOverField_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02UZ.** For `f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper and `X` of topological Krull
dimension at most `d`, the cohomology `Hⁱ(X, ℱ)` of every `𝒪_X`-module vanishes for `i > d`.

Properness makes `X` a Noetherian scheme, hence a Noetherian space, where Grothendieck's theorem
is `Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_le`; the
three comparisons listed in the module documentation read that vanishing in the
`AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverField` spelling.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cohomologyOverField_of_topologicalKrullDim_le (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules) {d i : ℕ}
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hi : d < i) :
    IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f F i)
declarations.comment: the vanishing Hⁱ(X, ℱ) = 0 for i above the dimension, for the modules on a scheme proper over a field, read through the comparison of Tag 01F1 (1) with the cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf

declarations.doc:

one-dimensional proper scheme `X`.

declarations.comment: degree two on a one-dimensional proper scheme over a field, which is what Situation 0B5D consumes

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `X` is a Noetherian topological space of topological Krull dimension `0` and `F` is an
abelian sheaf on `X`, then `H^p(X, F) = 0` for every `p > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_eq_zero
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [NoetherianSpace X]
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [HasExt.{w'} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = ((0 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w}) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w', w, u, u} F p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_le
declarations.doc:
Grothendieck's vanishing theorem. Let `X` be a Noetherian topological space of topological
Krull dimension at most `d` and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X`. Then `H^p(X, F) = 0` for every
`p > d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_le
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [NoetherianSpace X]
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    {d p : ℕ} (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hp : d < p)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} F p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_le_of_coefficients
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02UZ], Grothendieck's vanishing theorem, with the coefficient universe free of
the space's.**  Let `X : Type u` be a Noetherian topological space of topological Krull dimension
at most `d` and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X` with values in `AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}`.  Then
`H^p(X, F) = 0` for every `p > d`.

This is `Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace` with its
`hspectral` hypothesis discharged.  That reduction was already stated at a free coefficient
universe — it passes to the soberification, whose lattice of opens is that of `X` — so the only
thing it was waiting for was clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0A3G] there, which is
`subsingleton_sheafH_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_of_coefficients`.
`Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_le` is this
statement with `w := u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafCohomology_of_noetherianSpace_of_dim_le_of_coefficients
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [NoetherianSpace X]
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}]
    [HasExt.{w'} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u w})]
    {d p : ℕ} (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hp : d < p)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w', max u w, u, u} F p)
declarations.comment: with the coefficient universe free of the universe of the space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomicLocus_eq_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02V3.**  For a flat morphism locally of finite presentation, the
syntomic locus commutes with arbitrary base change: if the square `g'`, `f'`, `f`, `g` is
cartesian then the set of points where `f'` is syntomic is the `g'`-preimage of the set of points
where `f` is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomicLocus_eq_preimage
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    {x' : X' | IsSyntomicAt f' x'} = g' ⁻¹' {x : X | IsSyntomicAt f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.smoothLocus_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**The smooth locus of a base change is the inverse image of the smooth locus.** Let
```
X' → X
↓    ↓
S' → S
```
be a cartesian diagram of schemes, with `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite presentation. Assume that
`f` is flat, or that `g : S' ⟶ S` is flat. Then the open subscheme of `X'` where the base-changed
morphism `f' : X' ⟶ S'` is smooth is the inverse image under `g' : X' ⟶ X` of the open subscheme
of `X` where `f` is smooth.

**Stacks Project, Tag 02V4.** Both of its cases are covered, the first by flatness of `f` and
the second by flatness of `g`. The instance `LocallyOfFinitePresentation f'` imposes no condition:
it follows from that of `f` by stability under base change, and it is what makes the smooth locus
`f'.smoothLocus` of the base-changed morphism defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.smoothLocus_eq_preimage_of_isPullback {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f']
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hflat : Flat f ∨ Flat g) :
    f'.smoothLocus = g' ⁻¹ᵁ f.smoothLocus

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FibreDimension.isZero_stalk_rightDerivedPlus_of_fiber_dimension_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02V7].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and let `y ∈ Y`. Assume
`Y` locally Noetherian, `f` proper and `dim(X_y) = d`. Then for every coherent sheaf `ℱ` on `X`
we have `(Rᵖ f_* ℱ)_y = 0` for all `p > d`.

The fibre dimension is taken as the upper bound `dim(X_y) ≤ d`, which is what the proof uses.
A neighbourhood `V` of `y` over which every fibre is bounded by `d` is produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_forall_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le`; the stalk at `y` of
the higher direct image along `f` is the one along `f ∣_ V`; over the affine base `V` the higher
direct image vanishes as soon as the cohomology of `f ⁻¹ V` does; and that vanishing is
`isZero_rightDerived_moduleGlobalSections_of_affine_base`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_stalk_rightDerivedPlus_of_fiber_dimension_le
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (y : Y) (d : ℕ)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (p : ℤ) (hp : (d : ℤ) < p) :
    IsZero ((((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedPlus p).obj F).presheaf.stalk y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrictGroupoid_isRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 02VB.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme over `S` and
`g : U' ⟶ U` a morphism.  With `R' = (U' ×_{g, U, t} R) ×_R (R ×_{s, U, g} U')` the iterated
fibre product of the displayed diagram, `s' : R' ⟶ R ×_{s, U, g} U' ⟶ U'` and
`t' : R' ⟶ U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ U'`, the groupoid scheme `restrictGroupoid G g` is
`(U', R', s', t', c')` for the canonical composition law
`c' = Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.restrictionComposition`, which is characterized as the
morphism on composable pairs whose source, target and underlying arrow of `R` are those of the
second factor, of the first factor, and the composite in `R`.  The morphism of groupoid schemes
`restrictGroupoidHom G g` is `g` on objects and the projection `R' ⟶ R` on arrows.  Finally, on
every scheme `T` over `S`, the functor of groupoids
`(U'(T), R'(T), s', t', c') ⟶ (U(T), R(T), s, t, c)` is the restriction of
`(U(T), R(T), s, t, c)` via `U'(T) ⟶ U(T)`: there is an isomorphism of categories to the
induced groupoid `InducedCategory (U(T), R(T), s, t, c) (· ≫ g)`, the identity on objects,
carrying the functor to the canonical functor `inducedFunctor` of the restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictGroupoid_isRestriction :
    (restrictGroupoid G g).objects = U' ∧
    (restrictGroupoid G g).arrows =
      pullback (pullback.snd g G.target) (pullback.fst G.source g) ∧
    (restrictGroupoid G g).source =
      pullback.snd (pullback.snd g G.target) (pullback.fst G.source g) ≫
        pullback.snd G.source g ∧
    (restrictGroupoid G g).target =
      pullback.fst (pullback.snd g G.target) (pullback.fst G.source g) ≫
        pullback.fst g G.target ∧
    (restrictGroupoid G g).comp = G.restrictionComposition g ∧
    (∀ {T : Over S} (a b : T ⟶ (restrictGroupoid G g).arrows)
        (w : a ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).source = b ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).target),
      (pullback.lift a b w ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).comp) ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).source =
          b ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).source ∧
        (pullback.lift a b w ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).comp) ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).target =
          a ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).target ∧
        (pullback.lift a b w ≫ (restrictGroupoid G g).comp) ≫
            (restrictGroupoidHom G g).mapArrows =
          G.compose (a ≫ (restrictGroupoidHom G g).mapArrows)
            (b ≫ (restrictGroupoidHom G g).mapArrows)
            (G.restriction_compose_condition g a b w)) ∧
    (restrictGroupoidHom G g).mapObjects = g ∧
    (restrictGroupoidHom G g).mapArrows =
      pullback.fst (pullback.snd g G.target) (pullback.fst G.source g) ≫
        pullback.snd g G.target ∧
    ∀ T : Over S,
      (∀ x, (restrictGroupoidEvaluationFunctor G g T).obj x = x) ∧
      restrictGroupoidEvaluationFunctor G g T ⋙ restrictGroupoidEvaluationInverse G g T =
        𝟭 _ ∧
      restrictGroupoidEvaluationInverse G g T ⋙ restrictGroupoidEvaluationFunctor G g T =
        𝟭 _ ∧
      restrictGroupoidEvaluationFunctor G g T ⋙
          inducedFunctor (restrictGroupoidEvaluationObj G g T) =
        (restrictGroupoidHom G g).evaluation T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restriction_groupoidScheme_agrees_restriction_preRelation
declarations.doc:
Restricting groupoid schemes and restricting (pre-)equivalence relations
agree via the constructions of Tags 0232 and 0233.

1. For a groupoid scheme `G` and `g : U' ⟶ G.objects`, the pre-relation of the restriction
   `G|_{U'}` (Tag 02VC) agrees with the restriction (Tag 02V9) of the pre-relation of `G`
   (Tag 0232): there is a unique isomorphism of their schemes of arrows compatible with the
   maps to `U' ×_S U'` and to the arrows of `G`.
2. For an equivalence relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_S U` and `g : U' ⟶ U`, the groupoid scheme of the
   restricted relation `j|_{U'}` (Tag 0233) agrees with the restriction to `U'` of the groupoid
   scheme of `j`: there is a unique isomorphism of groupoid schemes between them which is the
   identity of `U'` on objects and commutes with the maps of arrows to `R`. Being a pair of
   mutually inverse morphisms of groupoid schemes, it identifies the compositions, identities
   and inverses of the two groupoid structures.
declarations.statement:
theorem restriction_groupoidScheme_agrees_restriction_preRelation {S : Scheme.{u}} :
    (∀ (G : GroupoidScheme S) {U' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects),
      ∃! e : (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).groupoid.arrows ≅
          PreRelation.restriction (groupoidPreRelation G) g,
        e.hom ≫ PreRelation.restrict (groupoidPreRelation G) g =
            groupoidPreRelation (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).groupoid ≫
              prod.map (eqToHom (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).objects_eq)
                (eqToHom (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).objects_eq) ∧
          e.hom ≫ pullback.snd (prod.map g g) (groupoidPreRelation G) =
            (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).hom.mapArrows) ∧
    (∀ {R U U' : Over S} (j : PreRelation R U) [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source]
        (g : U' ⟶ U),
      ∃! e : GroupoidScheme.Isomorphism
          (groupoidSchemeOfIsEquivalenceRelation (PreRelation.restrict j g))
          (GroupoidScheme.restrict (groupoidSchemeOfIsEquivalenceRelation j)
            (g ≫ eqToHom
              (groupoidSchemeOfIsEquivalenceRelation_extendsRelation j).objects_eq.symm)).groupoid,
        e.hom.mapObjects = eqToHom
            ((groupoidSchemeOfIsEquivalenceRelation_extendsRelation
                (PreRelation.restrict j g)).objects_eq.trans
              (GroupoidScheme.restrict _ _).objects_eq.symm) ∧
          e.hom.mapArrows ≫ (GroupoidScheme.restrict _ _).hom.mapArrows ≫
              eqToHom (groupoidSchemeOfIsEquivalenceRelation_extendsRelation j).arrows_eq =
            eqToHom (groupoidSchemeOfIsEquivalenceRelation_extendsRelation
                (PreRelation.restrict j g)).arrows_eq ≫ pullback.snd (prod.map g g) j)

morphism is finite locally free, then so is `g`.

factor descends: the first is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_descendsAlong_surjective_inf_flat_inf_quasiCompact`, which is
the descent step of Tag 02LA, and the other two are Mathlib's.

    MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong
      (@IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      ((@Surjective.{u} ⊓ @Flat.{u} ⊓ @QuasiCompact.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_descendsAlong
declarations.doc:
**The second assertion of Stacks Project, Tag 02VO**, the descent step. Morphisms which are
finite locally free of a fixed degree `r` satisfy fpqc descent: if the base change of `g` along
a surjective flat quasi-compact morphism is finite locally free of degree `r`, then so is `g`.

The degree-free case makes `g` finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, so the rank
criterion `Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff_forall_finrank_eq` applies to both `g`
and its base change and turns the statement into one about the rank function
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank`. That function is compatible with base change by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank_of_isPullback`, and the covering morphism is surjective
on points, so the rank of `g` at an arbitrary point of its target is the rank of the base
change at a point above it, which is `r`.

    MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong (IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.property.{u} r)
      ((@Surjective.{u} ⊓ @Flat.{u} ⊓ @QuasiCompact.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))

declarations.doc: Descent data for schemes relative to a family of morphisms with common target.
declarations.statement: structure DescentData
declarations.comment: the gluing isomorphisms read over the pairwise fibre product, with the cocycle

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.pullbackFunctor
declarations.doc:
Pullback of descent data along a commutative square of schemes. On underlying schemes this
is base change along `f`; the gluing isomorphism is pulled back along the induced map of
self-fibre products.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackFunctor
    {S S' X X' : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (a' : X' ⟶ S') (h : S' ⟶ S)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (comm : f ≫ a = a' ≫ h) :
    PullbackFunctor a a' h f comm
declarations.comment: the pullback functor on descent data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullbackFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02VS, part (3).** Two morphisms of families of morphisms with fixed
target which have the same morphism `h` of base schemes induce canonically isomorphic pullback
functors on descent data, whatever their index maps and component morphisms are.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullbackCompatibility
declarations.doc:
Pullback of descent data commutes canonically with the equivalence between
a family and its coproduct morphism.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pullbackCompatibility
    (F : MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.{u}) : PullbackCompatibility F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullback_descentData_homOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02VS.** Let `𝒰 = {Uᵢ ⟶ S'}` and `𝒱 = {Vⱼ ⟶ S}` be families of
morphisms with fixed target and `h : S' ⟶ S`.

1. For every morphism of families `φ` over `h` and every descent datum `D` relative to `𝒱`, the
   system `pulledBackDatum` is a descent datum relative to `𝒰` whose component at `i` is
   `gᵢ^* Y_(α i)` and whose gluing isomorphism at `(i, i')` is the pullback of the gluing
   isomorphism of `D` at `(α i, α i')` along `gᵢ × gᵢ'`.
2. There is, for every such `φ`, a functor from descent data relative to `𝒱` to descent data
   relative to `𝒰` sending `D` to this pulled-back datum and acting on morphisms by
   componentwise base change;
3. for two morphisms of families `φ, ψ` over the same `h` these functors are isomorphic; and
4. after composing with the equivalences of Tag 023X between descent data for a family and
   descent data for its coproduct morphism, each of them is isomorphic to every pullback functor
   of Tag 023Y along the induced morphism of coproducts `∐ Uᵢ ⟶ ∐ Vⱼ` over `h`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullback_descentData_homOver {S S' : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S')
    (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S) (h : S' ⟶ S) :
    (∀ (φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h) (D : DescentData 𝒱.f) (i : 𝒰.I₀),
      (pulledBackDatum (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) D).obj i =
          (Over.pullback (φ.h₀ i)).obj (D.obj (φ.s₀ i)) ∧
        ∀ i' : 𝒰.I₀,
          ((pulledBackDatum (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) D).gluingPullbackIso i i').hom ≫
              pulledBackDatumTargetMap (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) D i i' =
            pulledBackDatumSourceMap (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) D i i' ≫
              (D.gluingPullbackIso (φ.s₀ i) (φ.s₀ i')).hom) ∧
    ∃ G : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h → (DescentData 𝒱.f ⥤ DescentData 𝒰.f),
      (∀ φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h,
        ∃ hG : ∀ D : DescentData 𝒱.f, (G φ).obj D = pulledBackDatum (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) D,
          ∀ (D E : DescentData 𝒱.f) (α : D ⟶ E) (i : 𝒰.I₀),
            (eqToHom (hG D)).hom i ≫
                (pulledBackDatumObjIso (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) D i).hom ≫
                (Over.pullback (φ.h₀ i)).map (α.hom (φ.s₀ i)) =
              ((G φ).map α).hom i ≫ (eqToHom (hG E)).hom i ≫
                (pulledBackDatumObjIso (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ) E i).hom) ∧
      (∀ φ ψ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h, Nonempty (G φ ≅ G ψ)) ∧
      ∀ (φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h)
        (P : DescentData.PullbackFunctor (Sigma.desc 𝒱.f) (Sigma.desc 𝒰.f) h
          (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ).coproductHom (ofHomOver 𝒰 𝒱 h φ).coproductHom_comp),
        Nonempty ((DescentData.familyCoproductEquivalence 𝒱.f).equivalence.functor ⋙
            P.functor ≅
          G φ ⋙ (DescentData.familyCoproductEquivalence 𝒰.f).equivalence.functor)
declarations.comment: all four parts, for morphisms of families over a fixed base morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullbackFunctor
declarations.doc: The pullback of descent data along a morphism of families is functorial.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pullbackFunctor (F : MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.{u}) :
    PullbackFunctor F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pulledBackDatum
declarations.doc:
Pull a descent datum back componentwise along a morphism of families.  If the morphism has
index map `α` and component maps `gᵢ`, its objects are `gᵢ * Y_(α i)` and its gluing
isomorphisms are the pullbacks of the original gluing isomorphisms along `gᵢ × gᵢ'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pulledBackDatum (F : MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.{u})
    (D : DescentData F.targetFamily.f) :
    DescentData F.sourceFamily.f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pulledBackDatum_obj
declarations.doc:
The component of the pulled-back datum at `i` is the pullback of the component at
`F.familyHom.s₀ i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pulledBackDatum_obj (F : MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.{u})
    (D : DescentData F.targetFamily.f) (i : F.sourceFamily.I₀) :
    (pulledBackDatum F D).obj i =
      (Over.pullback (F.familyHom.h₀ i)).obj (D.obj (F.familyHom.s₀ i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pulledBackDatum_gluing
declarations.doc:
On each pair of indices, the gluing isomorphism of the pulled-back datum is the
pullback of the original gluing isomorphism along the two component morphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma pulledBackDatum_gluing (F : MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.{u})
    (D : DescentData F.targetFamily.f) (i i' : F.sourceFamily.I₀) :
    ((pulledBackDatum F D).gluingPullbackIso i i').hom ≫
        pulledBackDatumTargetMap F D i i' =
      pulledBackDatumSourceMap F D i i' ≫
        (D.gluingPullbackIso (F.familyHom.s₀ i) (F.familyHom.s₀ i')).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.canonicalFamilyFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The canonical descent datum relative to a family.** The functor sending a scheme `U` over
`S` to the descent datum relative to `{X i ⟶ S}` whose member over `X i` is the base change of
`U` along `X i ⟶ S`, obtained by pulling back the trivial descent datum of `U`.
declarations.statement: def canonicalFamilyFunctor (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S) : Over S ⥤ DescentData f
declarations.comment: (1) canonical descent datum on the family X i ×_S U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.IsEffectiveFamily
declarations.doc:
**Effectivity of a descent datum relative to a family.** A descent datum relative to
`{X i ⟶ S}` is effective if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over
`S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEffectiveFamily {f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S} (D : DescentData f) : Prop
declarations.comment: (2) effective descent datum relative to a family

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalFamilyDescentFunctor
declarations.doc:
The canonical descent datum functor for an arbitrarily indexed family of schemes over `S`:
it sends a scheme `U` over `S` to the descent datum whose components are the fibre products of
`U` with the members of the family, with the gluing isomorphisms that preserve the projection to
`U`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.doc:
A descent datum relative to a family is effective if it is isomorphic to the canonical
descent datum of some scheme over the common base.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFamilyEffective (D : DescentData f) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.faithful_overPullback_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02VX.** Base change along a surjective flat morphism of schemes is a
faithful functor on the category of schemes over the base.
declarations.statement:
instance Flat.faithful_overPullback_of_surjective {S' S : Scheme.{u}} (h : S' ⟶ S)
    [Flat h] [Surjective h] : (Over.pullback h).Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_isEquivalence_of_zariskiRefinement
declarations.doc: A fibrewise Zariski refinement induces an equivalence on descent data.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pullbackFunctor_isEquivalence_of_zariskiRefinement
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (U V : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (α : U.HomOver V (𝟙 S))
    (hZar : ∀ j : V.I₀,
      Presieve.ofArrows
        (fun i : {i : U.I₀ // α.s₀ i = j} ↦ U.X i)
        (fun i ↦ α.h₀ i.val ≫ eqToHom (congrArg V.X i.property)) ∈
          Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage (V.X j)) :
    Nonempty ((MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullbackFunctor
      { sourceBase := S, targetBase := S,
        sourceFamily := U, targetFamily := V,
        baseHom := 𝟙 S, familyHom := α }).functor.IsEquivalence)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.descentData_equivalence_of_zariskiCovering
declarations.doc: Schemes over a base are equivalent to descent data for any Zariski cover.
declarations.statement:
public theorem descentData_equivalence_of_zariskiCovering
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (U : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (hZar : Presieve.ofArrows U.X U.f ∈ Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage S) :
    Nonempty (Over S ≌ DescentData U.f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_fpqcRefinement
declarations.doc:
An fpqc refinement of each member of a family induces a fully faithful
pullback functor on descent data.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_fpqcRefinement
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (U V : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (α : U.HomOver V (𝟙 S))
    (hfpqc : ∀ j : V.I₀,
      Presieve.ofArrows
        (fun i : {i : U.I₀ // α.s₀ i = j} ↦ U.X i)
        (fun i ↦ α.h₀ i.val ≫ eqToHom (congrArg V.X i.property)) ∈
          Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage (V.X j)) :
    Nonempty ((MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullbackFunctor
      { sourceBase := S, targetBase := S,
        sourceFamily := U, targetFamily := V,
        baseHom := 𝟙 S, familyHom := α }).functor.FullyFaithful)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.canonicalFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_fpqc
declarations.doc:
If the single morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is an fpqc covering of `S`, then the canonical descent
datum functor `Over S ⥤ DescentDatum f` is fully faithful, so schemes over `S` form a full
subcategory of the descent data relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_fpqc (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hcover : Presieve.singleton f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.coverings S) :
    Nonempty (canonicalFunctor f).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: in particular, for a covering by a single morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W0.** Let `U` and `V` be families of schemes over `S` and let `α` exhibit `U` as
a refinement of `V` over the identity of `S`. If `U` is an fpqc covering of `S`, then the
pullback functor from descent data relative to `V` to descent data relative to `U` is fully
faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_refinement
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (U V : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (α : U.HomOver V (𝟙 S))
    (hU : Presieve.ofArrows U.X U.f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S) :
    Nonempty ((MorphismOfSchemeFamilies.pullbackFunctor
      { sourceBase := S, targetBase := S,
        sourceFamily := U, targetFamily := V,
        baseHom := 𝟙 S, familyHom := α }).functor.FullyFaithful)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_canonicalFunctor_comp_familyCoproduct_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W0**, final sentence: the schemes over `S` form a full subcategory of the
category of descent data relative to an fpqc covering `U` of `S`. The embedding is the
canonical descent datum of the coproduct morphism of `U`, read as a descent datum for the
family through the family–coproduct equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_canonicalFunctor_comp_familyCoproduct_inverse
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (U : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (hU : Presieve.ofArrows U.X U.f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S) :
    Nonempty ((DescentData.canonicalFunctor (Sigma.desc U.f) ⋙
      (DescentData.familyCoproductEquivalence U.f).equivalence.inverse).FullyFaithful)
declarations.comment: the schemes over the base as a full subcategory of the descent data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SatisfiesDescent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W2.** Morphisms with property `P` satisfy descent for the coverings
of a precoverage `K` if every descent datum relative to a `K`-covering whose components are
`P`-morphisms is effective.
declarations.statement: abbrev SatisfiesDescent (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (K : Precoverage Scheme.{u}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_affineBase_of_affineSingleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W3, the case of an affine base, for the fppf, étale, smooth and
syntomic coverings.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base which is stable
under any base change and such that a nonempty finite disjoint union of morphisms with `P` again
has `P`. Let `τ` be one of fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic, and suppose that for every
surjective morphism of affine schemes which is flat of finite presentation, étale, smooth or
syntomic according to `τ`, every descent datum relative to it whose member has `P` is effective.
Then every descent datum relative to a `τ`-covering of an affine scheme whose members have `P`
is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_affineBase_of_affineSingleton
    {P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}} [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (τ : CoveringTopology) (hτ : τ ≠ .zariski)
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (g : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (g j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map g))
    (haffine : ∀ {A T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine T] (a : A ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → coveringMorphismProperty τ a →
      ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (h𝒰 : 𝒰.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.precoverage (coveringMorphismProperty τ) S)
    (D : DescentData 𝒰.f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: the case of an affine base, for τ = fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_affineBase_fpqc_of_affineSingleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W3, the case of an affine base, for the fpqc coverings.** Let `P` be
a property of morphisms of schemes over a base which is stable under any base change and such
that a nonempty finite disjoint union of morphisms with `P` again has `P`. Suppose that for
every surjective flat morphism of affine schemes, every descent datum relative to it whose
member has `P` is effective. Then every descent datum relative to an fpqc covering of an affine
scheme whose members have `P` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_affineBase_fpqc_of_affineSingleton
    {P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}} [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (g : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (g j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map g))
    (haffine : ∀ {A T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine T] (a : A ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → Flat a → ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (h𝒰 : 𝒰.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData 𝒰.f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: the case of an affine base, for τ = fpqc

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_affineSingleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W3, for the fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic coverings.** Let `P` be
a property of morphisms of schemes over a base which is stable under any base change and such
that a nonempty finite disjoint union of morphisms with `P` again has `P`. Let `τ` be one of
fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic, and suppose that for every surjective morphism of affine
schemes which is flat of finite presentation, étale, smooth or syntomic according to `τ`, every
descent datum relative to it whose member has `P` is effective. Then every descent datum
relative to a `τ`-covering of an arbitrary scheme whose members have `P` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_affineSingleton [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (τ : CoveringTopology) (hτ : τ ≠ .zariski)
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (g : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (g j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map g))
    (haffine : ∀ {A T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine T] (a : A ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → coveringMorphismProperty τ a →
      ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (h𝒰 : 𝒰.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.precoverage (coveringMorphismProperty τ) S)
    (D : DescentData 𝒰.f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: for τ = fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic, over an arbitrary base, for a covering family indexed in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_fpqc_of_affineSingleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W3, for the fpqc coverings.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of
schemes over a base which is stable under any base change and such that a nonempty finite
disjoint union of morphisms with `P` again has `P`. Suppose that for every surjective flat
morphism of affine schemes, every descent datum relative to it whose member has `P` is
effective. Then every descent datum relative to an fpqc covering of an arbitrary scheme whose
members have `P` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_fpqc_of_affineSingleton [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (g : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (g j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map g))
    (haffine : ∀ {A T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine T] (a : A ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → Flat a → ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} S)
    (h𝒰 : 𝒰.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData 𝒰.f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: for τ = fpqc, over an arbitrary base, for a covering family indexed in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_affineSingleton_of_anyIndex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W3, for the fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic coverings, with no
restriction on the index type of the covering family.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of
schemes over a base which is stable under any base change and such that a nonempty finite
disjoint union of morphisms with `P` again has `P`. Let `τ` be one of fppf, étale, smooth and
syntomic, and suppose that for every surjective morphism of affine schemes which is flat of
finite presentation, étale, smooth or syntomic according to `τ`, every descent datum relative to
it whose member has `P` is effective. Then every descent datum relative to a `τ`-covering of an
arbitrary scheme, indexed by a type in an arbitrary universe, whose members have `P` is
effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_affineSingleton_of_anyIndex [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (τ : CoveringTopology) (hτ : τ ≠ .zariski)
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (g : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (g j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map g))
    (haffine : ∀ {A T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine T] (a : A ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → coveringMorphismProperty τ a →
      ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.precoverage (coveringMorphismProperty τ) S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: for τ = fppf, étale, smooth and syntomic, over an arbitrary base, for a covering family indexed in an arbitrary universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_fpqc_of_affineSingleton_of_anyIndex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02W3, for the fpqc coverings, with no restriction on the index type of
the covering family.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base which is stable
under any base change and such that a nonempty finite disjoint union of morphisms with `P` again
has `P`. Suppose that for every surjective flat morphism of affine schemes, every descent datum
relative to it whose member has `P` is effective. Then every descent datum relative to an fpqc
covering of an arbitrary scheme, indexed by a type in an arbitrary universe, whose members have
`P` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_fpqc_of_affineSingleton_of_anyIndex [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (g : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (g j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map g))
    (haffine : ∀ {A T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine T] (a : A ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → Flat a → ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: for τ = fpqc, over an arbitrary base, for a covering family indexed in an arbitrary universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
Let `P` be stable under base change and closed under finite disjoint unions, and let every
descent datum relative to a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes whose component has `P` be
effective.  Then over an affine base every descent datum relative to an fpqc covering whose
components have `P` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_isAffine
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hcoprod : ∀ {J : Type u} [Finite J] [Nonempty J] {Y Z : J → Scheme.{u}}
      (a : ∀ j, Y j ⟶ Z j), (∀ j, P (a j)) → P (Limits.Sigma.map a))
    (haffine : ∀ {T Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsAffine Z] (a : Z ⟶ T),
      Surjective a → Flat a → ∀ E : DescentDatum a, P (E.obj ()).hom → E.IsEffective)
    [IsAffine S] (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hP : ∀ i, P (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: the fpqc case over an affine base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.sheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W5.** Let `J` be a subcanonical topology on the category of schemes (for instance
the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology), let `S` be a scheme and let
`{f i : X i ⟶ S}` be a `J`-covering of `S`. Then descent data `(V_i, φ_ij)` of schemes relative to
`{f i}` are equivalent to sheaves `F` on `(Sch/S)_J` such that every product `h_{X i} × F` is
representable. The functor sends `D` to the sheaf `T ↦ Hom(can T, D)` of morphisms of descent
data out of the canonical descent datum of `T`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafEquivalence :
    DescentData f ≌ (sheavesLocallyRepresentable J f).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.representableBy_sheafEquivalence_functor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W5, part (1)**, from left to right: for a descent datum `(V_i, φ_ij)`, the product
`h_{X i} × F` with the corresponding sheaf `F` is represented by `V_i`, viewed as a scheme over
`S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableBy_sheafEquivalence_functor (D : DescentData f) (i : ι) :
    (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (f i)) ⨯ ((sheafEquivalence hf).functor.obj D).obj.obj).RepresentableBy
      ((Over.map (f i)).obj (D.obj i))
declarations.comment: part (1): the objects representing `h_{S_i} × F` are the schemes `X_i`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.representableBy_sheafEquivalence_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W5, part (1)**, from right to left: for a sheaf `F` on `(Sch/S)_J` with every
`h_{X i} × F` representable, the product `h_{X i} × F` is represented by the `i`-th component of
the corresponding descent datum, viewed as a scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableBy_sheafEquivalence_inverse
    (F : (sheavesLocallyRepresentable J f).FullSubcategory) (i : ι) :
    (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (f i)) ⨯ F.obj.obj).RepresentableBy
      ((Over.map (f i)).obj (((sheafEquivalence hf).inverse.obj F).obj i))
declarations.comment: part (1), from sheaves to descent data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isRepresentable_sheafEquivalence_functor_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W5, part (2)**: the sheaf corresponding to a descent datum is representable if and
only if the descent datum is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_sheafEquivalence_functor_iff (D : DescentData f) :
    ((sheafEquivalence hf).functor.obj D).obj.obj.IsRepresentable ↔ D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: part (2): `F` is representable if and only if the descent datum is effective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isRepresentable_iff_isFamilyEffective_sheafEquivalence_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02W5, part (2)**, from the side of sheaves: a sheaf `F` on `(Sch/S)_J` with every
`h_{X i} × F` representable is representable if and only if the corresponding descent datum is
effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_iff_isFamilyEffective_sheafEquivalence_inverse
    (F : (sheavesLocallyRepresentable J f).FullSubcategory) :
    F.obj.obj.IsRepresentable ↔ ((sheafEquivalence hf).inverse.obj F).IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: part (2), from sheaves to descent data

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isRepresentable_overMap_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be an object of a category `C`, let `T` be an object over `S` and let `F` be a presheaf
of types on `C/S`. Then the product `h_T ⨯ F` is representable if and only if the restriction of
`F` to `C/T.left` is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_overMap_iff {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} (T : Over S)
    (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :
    ((Over.map T.hom).op ⋙ F).IsRepresentable ↔ (yoneda.obj T ⨯ F).IsRepresentable

        MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft
declarations.doc:
**Effective descent along the covering sieves of the big fppf site of `S` at the
monomorphisms locally of finite type**, unconditionally. This is
`isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft_of_isQuasiAffineHom`
with its hypothesis discharged, and it is the descent hypothesis which the diagonal of a quotient
sheaf consumes. (The name of that conditional statement is too long to cite on one line here;
it lives in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Descent.CoveringSieveQuasiAffineDescent`.)

No cardinal hypothesis and no hypothesis on the site's cutoff is used: the passage from affine to
arbitrary base objects is paid for by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_le_of_mono`, available
because the property lies below the monomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft :
    IsEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve B S hS
      (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms Scheme.{u} ⊓ @LocallyOfFiniteType)
declarations.comment: effective descent along the covering sieves of the site, at the monomorphisms locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02W8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02W8) in the scheme-descent-datum
form, for a single quasi-compact chart.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a surjective, flat, quasi-compact
morphism of schemes and let `(V, φ)` be a descent datum relative to `X/S` whose structure
morphism `V ⟶ X` is separated, locally quasi-finite and locally of finite type. Then `(V, φ)` is
effective: it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.

Such a structure morphism is ind-quasi-affine by Stacks 0AP9, so this is Gabber's effectivity
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_quasiCompact`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_of_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite {S X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    [Surjective f] [Flat f] [QuasiCompact f] (D : DescentDatum f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated D.over.hom) (hqf : LocallyQuasiFinite D.over.hom)
    (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType D.over.hom) : DescentData.IsEffective D
declarations.comment: the scheme-descent-datum form, for a single quasi-compact chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 02W8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02W8).** Let `S` be a scheme, let
`{X i ⟶ S}` be an fppf covering family and let `D = (V i / X i, φ i j)` be a descent datum
relative to that family. If each morphism `V i ⟶ X i` is separated and locally quasi-finite, then
the descent datum is effective: it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over
`S`.

Quasi-finiteness is Stacks 02NG — `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`, as in the formalization of Stacks 01TD, of Stacks 02LR
and of Stacks 0AP9, Mathlib's `LocallyQuasiFinite` not itself asking for local finite type.

Such a structure morphism is ind-quasi-affine by Stacks 0AP9,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite`, and an fppf
covering family is an fpqc covering family, so this is Gabber's effectivity
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_anyIndex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite {ι : Type v}
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage S) (D : DescentData f)
    (hsep : ∀ i, IsSeparated (D.obj i).hom)
    (hqf : ∀ i, LocallyQuasiFinite (D.obj i).hom)
    (hft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveFlat_isSeparated_inf_locallyQuasiFinite_inf_lft
declarations.doc:
**Effective descent along a single surjective flat morphism of the site locally of finite
presentation, for the separated locally quasi-finite morphisms locally of finite type**, over an
arbitrary base object, unconditionally.

This is the property of Stacks 02W8 descended along the one-element fppf coverings, which is the
shape Stacks 046J consumes: that tag reduces to a covering `{F → G}` by a single surjective, flat
morphism locally of finite presentation, not to a general covering sieve.

All five steps of Stacks 02W8 are discharged. Steps 1, 2 and 5 over an affine base, together with
steps 3 and 4, are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coveringSieveBody_affineBase_isSeparated_inf_locallyQuasiFinite_inf_lft`;
the passage from an affine base object to an arbitrary one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveFlat_of_affineBase`, whose glueing is
paid for by the size bound of the single flat covering morphism.

Compare
`isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_isSeparated_inf_lqf_inf_lft_of_isRegular` in this namespace,
the same property in the covering-sieve shape, which carries a regularity hypothesis on the
site's cutoff. That hypothesis is not an artefact: a covering sieve supplies no single surjective
morphism whose size bounds the glueing, and the property of Stacks 02W8 admits no size bound of
its own, `∐_{i < κ} Spec A ⟶ Spec A` having it for every `κ`. Restricting to one-element
coverings is exactly what removes the hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveFlat_isSeparated_inf_locallyQuasiFinite_inf_lft
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    IsEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveFlat B S hS
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.{u} ⊓ @LocallyQuasiFinite ⊓ @LocallyOfFiniteType :
        MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: effective descent along a single surjective flat chart of the site

     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@UniversallyOpen : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (15): flat
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@Flat : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Flat : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Flat : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (16): syntomic
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (17): smooth
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@Smooth : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Smooth : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Smooth : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (18): unramified, and G-unramified
    ((MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@Unramified : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@Unramified : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@Unramified : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@GUnramified : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@GUnramified : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@GUnramified : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage)) ∧
    -- entry (19): étale
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (20): proper
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@IsProper : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@IsProper : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@IsProper : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (21): finite, and integral
    ((MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@IsFinite : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@IsFinite : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@IsFinite : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@IsIntegralHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@IsIntegralHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@IsIntegralHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage)) ∧
    -- entry (22): finite locally free, of unconstrained and of fixed rank
    ((MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
           (@Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
           Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
       MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
           (@Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
           Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
      (∀ d : ℕ,
        MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
            (Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.property.{u} d) ∧
        MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
            (Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.property.{u} d) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
        MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
            (Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.property.{u} d) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage)) ∧
    -- entry (23): universally submersive
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
         ((topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).universally) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         ((topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).universally)
         Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         ((topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).universally)
         Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- entry (24): universal homeomorphism
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
         (@UniversalHomeomorphism : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@UniversalHomeomorphism : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ∧
     MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
         (@UniversalHomeomorphism : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) ∧
    -- the last sentence (02YM): immersions in general are fppf local on the base, and no fpqc
    -- locality is claimed of them
    (MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@IsImmersion : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ∧
      MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@IsImmersion : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        Scheme.fppfPrecoverage)
declarations.comment: The remark in full, as one conjunction in the source's order: entry (n) is the n-th conjunct, and each conjunct states that the property that entry names is stable under arbitrary base change, local on the base for the fpqc precoverage, and a fortiori local on the base for the fppf precoverage. Entry (1) is the conjunction of its three cases, (a) closed, (b) open and (c) quasi-compact immersions; each entry with two readings, namely (4), (10), (11), (12), (18), (21) and (22), is the conjunction of both readings; and entries (13) and (22) are quantified over their numerical parameter. The twenty-fifth and last conjunct is the remark's closing sentence: being an immersion is stable under arbitrary base change and local on the base for the fppf precoverage, which is Descent, Lemma 02YM.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasSchemeProperty_prod_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WM.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of schemes which is stable under
composition. If two representable morphisms of presheaves `a₁ : F₁ ⟶ G₁` and `a₂ : F₂ ⟶ G₂`
on the big fppf site of `S` both have `P` in the sense of Stacks 025V, then so does their
product `a₁ × a₂ : F₁ × F₂ ⟶ G₁ × G₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSchemeProperty_prod_map (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsStableUnderComposition] {F₁ F₂ G₁ G₂ : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a₁ : F₁ ⟶ G₁) (a₂ : F₂ ⟶ G₂)
    (h₁ : HasSchemeProperty B S hS P a₁) (h₂ : HasSchemeProperty B S hS P a₂) :
    HasSchemeProperty B S hS P (prod.map a₁ a₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_clopen_scheme_coproduct
declarations.doc:
A sheaf coproduct represented by a scheme comes from an open-and-closed
coproduct decomposition of that scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_clopen_scheme_coproduct
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (I : Type v)
    (Fᵢ : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (F : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (ι : ∀ i, Fᵢ i ⟶ F)
    (hcoprod : IsColimit (Cofan.mk F ι))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : F.obj ≅ yoneda.obj U) :
    ∃ (Uᵢ : I → BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (j : ∀ i, Uᵢ i ⟶ U)
      (eᵢ : ∀ i, (Fᵢ i).obj ≅ yoneda.obj (Uᵢ i)),
      (∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (j i))) ∧
      (∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (j i))) ∧
      (∀ i, (eᵢ i).hom ≫ yoneda.map (j i) = (ι i).hom ≫ e.hom) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
        (fun i => (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (j i))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan_ulift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WO and Stacks 0F15 for sheaves with values in a universe `max w u` independent of
the universe `u` of the schemes.** A section `x` of a coproduct `P = ∐ᵢ Fᵢ` of pointwise
`u`-small sheaves over an object `W` of the big fppf site of `S`, the index type being
`u`-small, decomposes `W` into a family of pairwise disjoint open subobjects `W' i`, covering
`W`, such that `x` restricted to `W' i` comes from `Fᵢ`; and each `W' i` is universal with that
property.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan` with the value
universe of the sheaves decoupled from the universe of the morphisms of the site. The
decomposition machinery is not rebuilt: the sheaves are universe lifts of sheaves of `Type u`,
the coproduct cocone descends to those by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_shrink_isColimit_cofan_of_small`, and the conclusion, which speaks
of objects of the site and of sections, transports back along the lift.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan_ulift {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    {F : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))}
    (hF : ∀ i, FunctorToTypes.Small.{u} (F i).obj)
    {P : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))} (ι : ∀ i, F i ⟶ P)
    (hP : IsColimit (Cofan.mk P ι)) (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : P.obj.obj (op W)) :
    ∃ (W' : I → BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : ∀ i, W' i ⟶ W),
      (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i))) ∧
      (∀ i, ∃ z : (F i).obj.obj (op (W' i)),
        (ι i).hom.app (op (W' i)) z = P.obj.map (p i).op x) ∧
      (∀ i i', i ≠ i' → ∀ (y : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (W' i))
        (y' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (W' i')),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i) y ≠
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i') y') ∧
      (∀ w : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W,
        ∃ i, w ∈ Set.range ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i))) ∧
      (∀ (i : I) (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (t : T ⟶ W),
        (∃ z : (F i).obj.obj (op T), (ι i).hom.app (op T) z = P.obj.map t.op x) →
        ∃ t' : T ⟶ W' i, t' ≫ p i = t)
declarations.comment: in an arbitrary value universe, for pointwise `u`-small sheaves and a `u`-small index type; the smallness hypotheses are absent from `AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan`, which is the same statement in the value universe of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.isEmpty_toScheme_of_eq_of_ne_ulift
declarations.doc:
**Distinct legs of a coproduct cocone of pointwise `u`-small sheaves on the big fppf site of
`S` have disjoint images**, for a value universe independent of the universe of the objects of
the site: an object of the site carrying sections of two different members of the family with the
same image in the coproduct has no points.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.isEmpty_toScheme_of_eq_of_ne` with the value universe of the
sheaves decoupled from the universe of the morphisms of the site, and is the disjointness half
of Stacks 02WO there.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sheaf.isEmpty_toScheme_of_eq_of_ne_ulift {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    {F : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))}
    (hF : ∀ i, FunctorToTypes.Small.{u} (F i).obj)
    {P : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))} (ι : ∀ i, F i ⟶ P)
    (hP : IsColimit (Cofan.mk P ι)) {i j : I} (hij : i ≠ j) {W : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (x : (F i).obj.obj (op W)) (y : (F j).obj.obj (op W))
    (h : (ι i).hom.app (op W) x = (ι j).hom.app (op W) y) :
    IsEmpty ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W)
declarations.comment: disjointness of the legs, in an arbitrary value universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WP.** Every summand of a sheaf coproduct that is an algebraic space is an
algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_coproduct
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (I : Type v)
    (Fᵢ : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (F : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (ι : ∀ i, Fᵢ i ⟶ F)
    (hcoprod : IsColimit (Cofan.mk F ι))
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F.obj)
    (i : I) : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Fᵢ i).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WQ.** A coproduct of algebraic spaces over `S` is an algebraic space over `S`,
provided the chosen surjective étale scheme atlases of the members have a coproduct inside the
big fppf site over `S`.

The sheaf condition is part of the data. The diagonal is representable by
`AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_isColimit_cofan`, and the coproduct `V` of
the atlases, with the morphism to the coproduct sheaf glued by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_hom_yoneda_of_isColimit_cofan`, is a surjective étale atlas by
`AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_inverseImage_of_isColimit_cofan`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_coproduct
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v}
    (F : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (F i))
    (G : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (ι : ∀ i, (⟨F i, (hF i).isSheaf⟩ :
      Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ G)
    (hG : IsColimit (Cofan.mk G ι))
    (U : I → BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (U i) ⟶ F i)
    (hsurj : ∀ i, (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (f i))
    (hetale : ∀ i, (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (f i))
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (j : ∀ i, U i ⟶ V)
    (hV : IsColimit (Cofan.mk V j)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isColimit_of_contains
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WQ.** Let `G` be the coproduct, in fppf sheaves over `S`, of algebraic spaces
`Fᵢ`, and let `aᵢ : Uᵢ → Fᵢ` be surjective étale charts whose coproduct `∐ Uᵢ` of underlying
schemes is an object of the site. Then `G` is an algebraic space over `S`.

No bound on the index type and no hypothesis on the diagonal is assumed. The disjoint union
`∐ Uᵢ` becomes a coproduct inside the site by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.exists_isColimit_cofan_of_size_sigma_lt`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_coproduct` concludes; there the diagonal of `G` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_isColimit_cofan`, proved for an index type
of any size by splitting `V ×_G W` into the pieces `Vᵢ ×_{Fᵢ} Wᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_isColimit_of_contains
    {I : Type u} {Fᵢ : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)}
    (hFᵢ : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Fᵢ i).obj)
    {G : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)}
    (jj : ∀ i, Fᵢ i ⟶ G) (hcoprod : IsColimit (Cofan.mk G jj))
    (Uᵢ : I → BigFppfOver B S hS) (aᵢ : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (Uᵢ i) ⟶ (Fᵢ i).obj)
    (hsurjᵢ : ∀ i, (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (aᵢ i))
    (hetᵢ : ∀ i, (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (aᵢ i))
    (hsum : B.Contains (∐ fun i => (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (Uᵢ i))) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.obj
declarations.comment: the precise hypothesis of the source: the coproduct of a choice of surjective étale charts of the members is an object of the site; no bound on the index type
