declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpaceULift_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WQ** for presheaves with values in a universe `max w u` independent of the
universe `u` of the schemes. A coproduct of algebraic spaces over `S`, indexed by a `u`-small
type and with values in `Type (max w u)`, is an algebraic space over `S`, provided the chosen
surjective étale scheme atlases of the members have a coproduct inside the big fppf site
over `S`.

The presheaves involved are pointwise `u`-small, so they are universe lifts of presheaves of
`Type u` and the algebraic-space condition transports along the lift; the universal property of
the coproduct transports along it too, by fullness, so no coproduct of sheaves of `Type u` is
formed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpaceULift_coproduct {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    {Fᵢ : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))}
    (hFᵢ : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{w} B S hS (Fᵢ i).obj)
    {G : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))} (ι : ∀ i, Fᵢ i ⟶ G)
    (hG : IsColimit (Cofan.mk G ι))
    (U : I → BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (a : ∀ i, (uliftYoneda.{w}).obj (U i) ⟶ (Fᵢ i).obj)
    (hsurj : ∀ i, (surjectiveOnSite B S hS).relative (uliftYoneda.{w}) (a i))
    (hetale : ∀ i, (etaleOnSite B S hS).relative (uliftYoneda.{w}) (a i))
    {V : BigFppfOver B S hS} {j : ∀ i, U i ⟶ V} (hV : IsColimit (Cofan.mk V j)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{w} B S hS G.obj
declarations.comment: in an arbitrary value universe, for a `u`-small index type; the index is unrestricted in `AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_coproduct`, which is the same statement in the value universe of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_open_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WR.** An fppf sheaf with a jointly surjective family of representable open
algebraic-space subfunctors is an algebraic space, when the coproduct of the family is itself
an algebraic space.

The index type `I` is arbitrary, in any universe `v`, with no bound on its cardinality: the
existence of the coproduct `G` in the sheaf category and its being an algebraic space are
hypothesis (2)(e) of the source, given here as `hcoprod` and `hG`. The members are sheaves with
maps `ι i ≫ g` to `F` rather than subfunctors of `F`; these maps are open immersions, hence
monomorphisms, so this covers the source's subfunctors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_open_cover
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (I : Type v)
    (Fᵢ : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (hFᵢ : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Fᵢ i).obj)
    (G : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (ι : ∀ i, Fᵢ i ⟶ G)
    (hcoprod : IsColimit (Cofan.mk G ι))
    (g : G.obj ⟶ F)
    (hopen : ∀ i, (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@IsOpenImmersion.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) ((ι i).hom ≫ g))
    (hsurj : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) g)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.obj) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WS.** An equivalence relation over `S` is *étale* when its source and
target maps are étale morphisms of schemes.
declarations.statement: class IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation {R U : Over S} (j : PreRelation R U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_restrict
declarations.doc:
Restricting an étale equivalence relation along an étale morphism again gives an étale
equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
instance isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_restrict (j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation R U)
    (g : U' ⟶ U) [Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation j] [Etale g.left] :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (AlgebraicGeometry.PreRelation.restrict j g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_restrictedQuotientMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WU.** Let `j = (t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_S U` be an equivalence relation of schemes over
`S` whose source and target maps are surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and
let `g : U' ⟶ U` be flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `R' = R|_{U'}` be the
restriction of `j` along `g`. The induced map `U'/R' ⟶ U/R` of quotient sheaves on the big fppf
site over `S` is representable and an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_restrictedQuotientMap (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (j : PreRelation R U) (g : U' ⟶ U) [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source]
    (hs_surj : Surjective j.source.left) (ht_surj : Surjective j.target.left)
    (hs_flat : Flat j.source.left) (ht_flat : Flat j.target.left)
    (hs_lfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.source.left)
    (ht_lfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.target.left)
    (hg_flat : Flat g.left) (hg_lfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left) :
    Space.IsOpenImmersion B S hS
      (restrictQuotientSheafMap (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (CategoryTheory.Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion) j g).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_restrictedQuotientMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WU.** Let `j` be an equivalence relation on `U` over `S` whose source and
target maps are surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `g : U' ⟶ U` be
flat and locally of finite presentation. Let `R' = R|_{U'}` be the restriction of `j` along
`g` (`AlgebraicGeometry.PreRelation.restrict`). Then the induced map of fppf quotient sheaves
`U'/R' ⟶ U/R` is representable and an open immersion (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenImmersion`
asks for representability). No hypothesis beyond the source's is assumed: the saturation
`t(s⁻¹(g(U')))` is shown to be open and covered fppf by the reach map from flatness and local
finite presentation alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_restrictedQuotientMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (j : PreRelation R U) (g : U' ⟶ U)
    [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source]
    (hs_surj : Surjective j.source.left)
    (ht_surj : Surjective j.target.left)
    (hs_flat : Flat j.source.left)
    (ht_flat : Flat j.target.left)
    (hs_lfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.source.left)
    (ht_lfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.target.left)
    (hg_flat : Flat g.left)
    (hg_lfp : LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS
      (restrictQuotientSheafMap (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion) j g).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_isPullback
declarations.doc: The relation is the fibre product `U ×_{U/R} U`. Nothing is assumed about the quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_isPullback
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)] :
    IsPullback (yoneda.map t) (yoneda.map s)
      (quotientMap B S hS s t) (quotientMap B S hS s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
The quotient map of an étale equivalence relation is surjective after every representable
base change, as soon as it is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_surjective
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)]
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (quotientMap B S hS s t)) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (quotientMap B S hS s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_etale
declarations.doc:
The quotient map of an étale equivalence relation is étale after every representable base
change, as soon as it is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_etale
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)]
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (quotientMap B S hS s t)) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (quotientMap B S hS s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientPresentation
declarations.doc:
An étale equivalence relation whose quotient sheaf is an algebraic space presents that
algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientPresentation
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)]
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (quotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (Over.post B.inclusion) (relation B S hS s t)).obj) :
    Presentation B S hS _ hQ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.uliftQuotientMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the lifted functor of points of the presenting
scheme to the lifted quotient sheaf of its relation.
declarations.statement:
def uliftQuotientMap [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max u v))] :
    uliftYoneda.{v}.obj U ⟶ (uliftQuotientSheaf.{u, v} B S hS s t).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap
declarations.doc: The canonical map from the presenting scheme to the quotient sheaf of its relation.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quotientMap :
    yoneda.obj U ⟶
      (quotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (Over.post B.inclusion) (relation B S hS s t)).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotient_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WW, the algebraic-space property.** The quotient sheaf of an étale equivalence
relation on an object of the big fppf site of `S` is an algebraic space over `S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_relation_of_diagDescent` with
its descent hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_quotient_unconditional
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)] :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (quotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (Over.post B.inclusion) (relation B S hS s t)).obj
declarations.comment: the quotient sheaf is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_surjective_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WW, surjectivity of the quotient map.** The canonical map `U ⟶ U/R` is
surjective after every representable base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_surjective_unconditional
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)] :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (quotientMap B S hS s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_etale_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WW, étaleness of the quotient map.** The canonical map `U ⟶ U/R` is étale after
every representable base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_etale_unconditional
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)] :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (quotientMap B S hS s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientPresentation_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WW, the presentation.** An étale equivalence relation presents its quotient
sheaf: `(U, R, U ⟶ U/R)` is a presentation of the algebraic space `U/R`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientPresentation_unconditional
    [IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relation B S hS s t)] :
    Presentation B S hS _ (isAlgebraicSpace_quotient_unconditional B S hS s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
A representable transformation to an algebraic space over `S` has an
algebraic space over `S` as its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_relativelyRepresentable
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : G ⟶ F) (ha : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable a)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_inverseImage_iff_atlas_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WZ.** A representable transformation of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
has a base-change stable, fppf local relative property exactly when its base change along one
surjective étale representable transformation to the target has it. The presheaves are
arbitrary: no algebraic space condition on `F` or `G` enters the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_inverseImage_iff_atlas_snd
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [P.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.fppfPrecoverage]
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : G ⟶ F) (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
    (hq_surj : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) q)
    (hq_etale : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) q) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf
      (P.inverseImage (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f ↔
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (hf.snd q))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_prod
declarations.doc: The presheaf product of two algebraic spaces over `S` is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_prod (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (F ⨯ G)
declarations.comment: the product is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces.isLimitBinaryFanProduct
declarations.doc:
The presheaf product of two algebraic spaces over `S`, with the two presheaf projections, is
a product in the category of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isLimitBinaryFanProduct (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (prod.fst : F.obj ⨯ G.obj ⟶ F.obj) : product B S hS F G ⟶ F)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (prod.snd : F.obj ⨯ G.obj ⟶ G.obj) :
        product B S hS F G ⟶ G))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_etale_chart_lift
declarations.doc:
Let `a : F ⟶ G` be a morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` with `F` an
algebraic space over `S`. Every surjective étale scheme chart `q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G` is
dominated by a surjective étale scheme chart of `F`: there are an object `U` of the site, a
surjective étale chart `p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F` and a morphism `α : U ⟶ V` making the square
commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_surjective_etale_chart_lift {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (a : F ⟶ G) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G)
    (hq_surjective : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q)
    (hq_etale : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F) (α : U ⟶ V),
      p ≫ a = yoneda.map α ≫ q ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf p ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X2.** The category of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site:
the full subcategory of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` whose objects are algebraic
spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev AlgebraicSpaces (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the category of algebraic spaces over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X2.** The presheaf fibre product of two algebraic spaces over an algebraic
space is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_pullback {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : F ⟶ H) (g : G ⟶ H) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hH : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS H) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (pullback f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X2.** The presheaf fibre product of two algebraic spaces is a fibre product
in the category of algebraic spaces over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_fiberProduct {F G H : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : F ⟶ H) (g : G ⟶ H) :
    IsPullback (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom g.hom) : fiberProduct B S hS f g ⟶ F)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom g.hom) : fiberProduct B S hS f g ⟶ G) f g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X3.** An algebraic space separated over `S` is quasi-separated over `S`: a
diagonal which is a closed immersion is in particular quasi-compact. Together with the
definition of quasi-separatedness this is the parenthetical remark of Section 65.13, that the
diagonal is quasi-compact as soon as `F` is separated or quasi-separated over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isSeparatedOver (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsSeparatedOver B S hS F) : IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_isSeparated_inf_quasiFinite_diag_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X3.** Let `F` be an algebraic space over `S` whose diagonal is quasi-compact,
that is, which is quasi-separated over `S`. Then the diagonal is separated and quasi-finite:
every represented base change of it is a separated, locally quasi-finite, locally of finite
type and quasi-compact morphism of schemes.

Separatedness is Stacks 02X4, part (3); locally quasi-finite and locally of finite type are
Stacks 02X4, part (4); quasi-compactness is the hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_isSeparated_inf_quasiFinite_diag_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hΔ : IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.{u} ⊓ @AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite.{u} ⊓
          @AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} ⊓ @AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact.{u} :
        MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag F)
declarations.comment: a quasi-compact diagonal is quasi-finite and separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_isQuasiAffineHom_diag_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X3.** Let `F` be an algebraic space over `S` whose diagonal is quasi-compact,
that is, which is quasi-separated over `S`. Then the diagonal is quasi-affine: every
represented base change of it is a quasi-affine morphism of schemes.

The diagonal is separated and quasi-finite, and a separated quasi-finite morphism of schemes
is quasi-affine by Stacks 02LR.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_isQuasiAffineHom_diag_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hΔ : IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_locallyOfFiniteType_diag
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X4, part (1).** The diagonal of an algebraic space over `S` is locally of
finite type: every represented base change of it is a morphism of schemes locally of finite
type.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_locallyOfFiniteType_diag (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_monomorphisms_diag
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X4, part (2).** The diagonal of an algebraic space over `S` is a monomorphism:
every represented base change of it is a monomorphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_monomorphisms_diag (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_isSeparated_diag
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X4, part (3).** The diagonal of an algebraic space over `S` is separated: every
represented base change of it is a separated morphism of schemes. This follows from part (2),
a monomorphism of schemes being separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_isSeparated_diag (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@IsSeparated.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_locallyQuasiFinite_diag
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X4, part (4).** The diagonal of an algebraic space over `S` is locally
quasi-finite: every represented base change of it is a morphism of schemes which is locally of
finite type and has discrete fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_locallyQuasiFinite_diag (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      ((@LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊓
        (@LocallyQuasiFinite.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space over `S` is *separated over `S`* when its diagonal is a closed immersion
of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSeparatedOver (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallySeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space over `S` is *locally separated over `S`* when its diagonal is an
immersion of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallySeparatedOver (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space over `S` is *quasi-separated over `S`* when its diagonal is
quasi-compact after every representable base change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiSeparatedOver (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space over `S` is *Zariski locally quasi-separated over `S`* when it admits a
Zariski covering by open subspaces which are quasi-separated over `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor
registrations.comment: A presheaf of sets is just a functor `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Cat.isFinalTwoCommSq_categoricalPullbackSq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02X9.** The explicit 2-fibre product of two functors is a 2-fibre product of them in
the 2-category of categories in the sense of Stacks 003Q: a final object of the 2-category of
2-commutative diagrams over the cospan, so any two 1-morphisms into it from a 2-commutative
square are isomorphic by a *unique* 2-morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isFinalTwoCommSq_categoricalPullbackSq (F : A ⟶ C) (G : B ⟶ C) :
    IsFinalTwoCommSq (categoricalPullbackSq F G)
declarations.comment: the explicit construction is a 2-fibre product in the sense of Stacks 003Q, with the uniqueness of the 2-isomorphism of Stacks 003P (2)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.map
declarations.doc:
The functor `𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒜 ×_𝒞 ℬ` induced by a 2-commutative diagram between the two cospans: on
objects it sends `(x, y, φ)` to `(L x, K y, α_y⁻¹ ∘ M(φ) ∘ β_x⁻¹)`, and on morphisms it applies `L`
and `K` componentwise.
declarations.statement:
def CategoricalPullback.map (H : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒵) (I : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒵)
    (L : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒜) (K : 𝒴 ⥤ ℬ) (M : 𝒵 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒞) (G : ℬ ⥤ 𝒞)
    (α : K ⋙ G ≅ I ⋙ M) (β : H ⋙ M ≅ L ⋙ F) :
    CategoricalPullback H I ⥤ CategoricalPullback F G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.induced_faithful_of_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XB (1)** — If `K` and `L` are faithful, then the induced functor
`𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒜 ×_𝒞 ℬ` is faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem induced_faithful_of_faithful [K.Faithful] [L.Faithful] :
    (CategoricalPullback.map H I L K M F G α β).Faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.induced_fullyFaithful_of_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XB (2)** — If `K` and `L` are fully faithful and `M` is faithful,
then the induced functor `𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒜 ×_𝒞 ℬ` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem induced_fullyFaithful_of_fullyFaithful
    [K.Faithful] [K.Full] [L.Faithful] [L.Full] [M.Faithful] :
    (CategoricalPullback.map H I L K M F G α β).Faithful ∧
      (CategoricalPullback.map H I L K M F G α β).Full

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.induced_isEquivalence_of_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XB (3)** — If `K` and `L` are equivalences and `M` is fully
faithful, then the induced functor `𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒜 ×_𝒞 ℬ` is an equivalence
of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem induced_isEquivalence_of_isEquivalence
    [K.IsEquivalence] [L.IsEquivalence] [M.Faithful] [M.Full] :
    (CategoricalPullback.map H I L K M F G α β).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.assocFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XC.** The canonical comparison functor
`(𝒜 ×_ℬ 𝒞) ×_𝒟 ℰ ⥤ 𝒜 ×_ℬ (𝒞 ×_𝒟 ℰ)`, rebracketing `((A, C, φ), E, ψ) ↦ (A, (C, E, ψ), φ)`.
declarations.statement:
def CategoricalPullback.assocFunctor
    (H : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) (K : 𝒞 ⥤ ℬ) (L : 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒟) (M : ℰ ⥤ 𝒟) :
    CategoricalPullback (CategoricalPullback.π₂ H K ⋙ L) M ⥤
      CategoricalPullback H (CategoricalPullback.π₁ L M ⋙ K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XC.** Associativity of 2-fibre products of categories: for
`H : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ`, `K : 𝒞 ⥤ ℬ`, `L : 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒟` and `M : ℰ ⥤ 𝒟` the two iterated 2-fibre products
are canonically equivalent, `(𝒜 ×_ℬ 𝒞) ×_𝒟 ℰ ≌ 𝒜 ×_ℬ (𝒞 ×_𝒟 ℰ)`, via
`CategoricalPullback.assocFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def CategoricalPullback.assoc
    (H : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) (K : 𝒞 ⥤ ℬ) (L : 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒟) (M : ℰ ⥤ 𝒟) :
    CategoricalPullback (CategoricalPullback.π₂ H K ⋙ L) M ≌
      CategoricalPullback H (CategoricalPullback.π₁ L M ⋙ K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.assocComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XD.** The canonical equivalence of categories `(A ×_B C) ×_C D ≌ A ×_B D`
for `A --F--> B <--G-- C <--H-- D`, i.e.
`CategoricalPullback (π₂ F G) H ≌ CategoricalPullback F (H ⋙ G)`, given by
`assocCompFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def assocComp :
    CategoricalPullback (π₂ F G) H ≌ CategoricalPullback F (H ⋙ G)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.prodDiagFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XE.** The canonical comparison functor
`CategoricalPullback (G₁.prod G₂) (Functor.diag S) ⥤ CategoricalPullback G₁ G₂`. On objects it
sends `((X₁, X₂), Y, φ)` to `(X₁, X₂, φ₁ ≪≫ φ₂⁻¹)`, where `φ = (φ₁, φ₂)`; on morphisms it acts as
the identity on the underlying pair of component morphisms.
declarations.statement:
def prodDiagFunctor (G₁ : C₁ ⥤ S) (G₂ : C₂ ⥤ S) :
    CategoricalPullback (G₁.prod G₂) (Functor.diag S) ⥤ CategoricalPullback G₁ G₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.isEquivalence_prodDiagFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XE.** The canonical comparison functor `prodDiagFunctor` is an equivalence of
categories: the 2-fibre product of `G₁ × G₂ : C₁ × C₂ ⥤ S × S` and the diagonal `Δ : S ⥤ S × S`
is canonically equivalent to `C₁ ×_S C₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_prodDiagFunctor (G₁ : C₁ ⥤ S) (G₂ : C₂ ⥤ S) :
    (prodDiagFunctor G₁ G₂).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.prodDiagEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XE.** The canonical equivalence of categories
`CategoricalPullback (G₁.prod G₂) (Functor.diag S) ≌ CategoricalPullback G₁ G₂`, induced by
`prodDiagFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def prodDiagEquiv (G₁ : C₁ ⥤ S) (G₂ : C₂ ⥤ S) :
    CategoricalPullback (G₁.prod G₂) (Functor.diag S) ≌ CategoricalPullback G₁ G₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.diagComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XF.** The comparison functor `(𝒞 ×_𝒮 𝒞) ×_{𝒞 × 𝒞} 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒞 ×_{𝒮 × 𝒮} 𝒮`. On objects
it sends `((c₁, c₂, φ), c₃, ψ)` to `(c₃, G₁ c₁, (G₁ ψ₁⁻¹, φ⁻¹ ∘ G₂ ψ₂⁻¹))`, and on morphisms
`((α₁, α₂), α₃)` to `(α₃, G₁ α₁)`.
declarations.statement: def diagComparison : diagComparisonSource G₁ G₂ ⥤ diagComparisonTarget G₁ G₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.isEquivalence_diagComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XF.** The comparison functor `(𝒞 ×_𝒮 𝒞) ×_{𝒞 × 𝒞} 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒞 ×_{𝒮 × 𝒮} 𝒮` is an
equivalence of categories. (The source asserts an isomorphism of categories; that is corrected to
an equivalence per the Stacks comments #5394 and #5627, since the functor is in general not
bijective on objects.)
declarations.statement: theorem isEquivalence_diagComparison : (diagComparison G₁ G₂).IsEquivalence

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Fiber
registrations.comment: (1) objects of the fibre category, (2) lifts of an object

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullbackOver.toFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** The canonical functor `(X ×_S Y)_U ⥤ X_U ×_{S_U} Y_U`, sending
`(U, x, y, f)` to `(x, y, f)` and `(a, b)` to `(a, b)`.
declarations.statement:
def toFiberPullback (hf : F ⋙ pS = pX) (hg : G ⋙ pS = pY) (U : C) :
    (CategoricalPullbackOver.structureFunctor (pX := pX) (pY := pY) (pS := pS) (F := F)
      (G := G)).Fiber U ⥤
    CategoricalPullback (Functor.fiberMap pX pS F hf U) (Functor.fiberMap pY pS G hg U)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullbackOver.ofFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** The canonical functor `X_U ×_{S_U} Y_U ⥤ (X ×_S Y)_U` inverse to
`toFiberPullback`, sending `(x, y, f)` to `(U, x, y, f)` and `(a, b)` to `(a, b)`.
declarations.statement:
def ofFiberPullback (hf : F ⋙ pS = pX) (hg : G ⋙ pS = pY) (U : C) :
    CategoricalPullback (Functor.fiberMap pX pS F hf U) (Functor.fiberMap pY pS G hg U) ⥤
    (CategoricalPullbackOver.structureFunctor (pX := pX) (pY := pY) (pS := pS) (F := F)
      (G := G)).Fiber U

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullbackOver.toFiberPullback_comp_ofFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** Composing the comparison functor with its inverse gives the identity on the
fibre `(X ×_S Y)_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toFiberPullback_comp_ofFiberPullback (hf : F ⋙ pS = pX) (hg : G ⋙ pS = pY) (U : C) :
    toFiberPullback pX pY pS F G hf hg U ⋙ ofFiberPullback pX pY pS F G hf hg U = 𝟭 _

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullbackOver.ofFiberPullback_comp_toFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** Composing the inverse comparison functor with the comparison functor gives
the identity on `X_U ×_{S_U} Y_U`. Together with
`toFiberPullback_comp_ofFiberPullback` this says the fibre of the 2-fibre product over `C` at `U`
is *isomorphic*, not merely equivalent, to the 2-fibre product of the fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem ofFiberPullback_comp_toFiberPullback (hf : F ⋙ pS = pX) (hg : G ⋙ pS = pY) (U : C) :
    ofFiberPullback pX pY pS F G hf hg U ⋙ toFiberPullback pX pY pS F G hf hg U = 𝟭 _

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.toFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** The canonical functor `(𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴)_U ⥤ 𝒳_U ×_{𝒮_U} 𝒴_U`, sending
`(U, x, y, φ)` to `(x, y, φ)` and `(a, b)` to `(a, b)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.ofFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** The canonical functor `𝒳_U ×_{𝒮_U} 𝒴_U ⥤ (𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴)_U` inverse to
`toFiberPullback`, sending `(x, y, φ)` to `(U, x, y, φ)` and `(a, b)` to `(a, b)` over `𝟙 U`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.toFiberPullback_comp_ofFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** Composing the comparison functor with its inverse gives the identity on the
fibre `(𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴)_U`: the round trip forgets the base object and reinstates it as the literal
`U`, which is the same object because it lies over `U`, and both functors are the identity on the
underlying pair of components.
declarations.statement:
theorem toFiberPullback_comp_ofFiberPullback (hF : F ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒳) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒴) (U : 𝒞) :
    toFiberPullback p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G hF hG U ⋙ ofFiberPullback p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G hF hG U = 𝟭 _

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.ofFiberPullback_comp_toFiberPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI.** Composing the inverse comparison functor with the comparison functor gives
the identity on `𝒳_U ×_{𝒮_U} 𝒴_U`: the base coordinate `U` is added and then forgotten, so the
triple `(x, y, φ)` is rebuilt unchanged. Together with `toFiberPullback_comp_ofFiberPullback`
this says the fibre of the 2-fibre product over `𝒞` at `U` is *isomorphic*, not merely
equivalent, to the 2-fibre product of the fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem ofFiberPullback_comp_toFiberPullback (hF : F ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒳) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒴) (U : 𝒞) :
    ofFiberPullback p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G hF hG U ⋙ toFiberPullback p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G hF hG U = 𝟭 _

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fiberEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XI**, as an equivalence of categories: the fibre of the 2-fibre product over `𝒞`
at `U` is the 2-fibre product of the fibre categories. Both unit and counit are identities, the
two functors being strictly mutually inverse.

declarations.name: Stacks.StronglyCartesian.isStronglyCartesian_conditions_hold
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XL.** All three claims of `StronglyCartesianStability` hold for every `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞`,
each supplied by Mathlib: `Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.comp`, `.of_isIso` and
`.isIso_of_base_isIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStronglyCartesian_conditions_hold {𝒞 : Type*} [Category 𝒞] {𝒮 : Type*} [Category 𝒮]
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) : StronglyCartesianStability p

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XM.** A functor `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` is a *fibred category over `𝒮`* when for every object
`x` of `𝒳` lying over an object `U` of `𝒮` and every morphism `f : V ⟶ U` of `𝒮` there exists a
strongly cartesian morphism `f^* x ⟶ x` lying over `f`.

That `φ` lies over `f` is part of `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian`, which extends
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsHomLift`. See the implementation notes for why this is Mathlib's
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered` and not its `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsPreFibered`.
declarations.statement: def IsFibredCategory (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFibredCategory_iff_isFibered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XM is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered`.** Forward, a strongly
cartesian lift of every base morphism makes `p` fibred by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.of_exists_isStronglyCartesian`. Backward, a fibred category has
a cartesian lift of every base morphism by `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsPreFibered.exists_isCartesian`
and every cartesian morphism of a fibred category is strongly cartesian by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.isStronglyCartesian_of_isCartesian`.
declarations.statement: theorem isFibredCategory_iff_isFibered (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) : p.IsFibredCategory ↔ p.IsFibered

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered
registrations.comment: Mathlib's SGA 1 VI.6.1 form of the definition, identified with the Stacks form by `CategoryTheory.Functor.isFibredCategory_iff_isFibered`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XN (1).**
A *choice of pullbacks* for `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` is a choice, for every morphism `f : V ⟶ U` of `𝒮` and
every object `x` of the fibre of `p` over `U`, of an object `f^* x` of the fibre over `V` together
with a strongly cartesian morphism `f^* x ⟶ x` lying over `f`.
declarations.statement: structure ChoiceOfPullbacks (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.pullbackFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XN (2).**
The *pullback functor* `f^* : 𝒳_U ⥤ 𝒳_V` between the fibres of `p` attached to a morphism
`f : V ⟶ U` of `𝒮` by a choice of pullbacks.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pullbackFunctor {V U : 𝒮} (f : V ⟶ U) : p.Fiber U ⥤ p.Fiber V

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XO (3)**, for an arbitrary choice of pullbacks. The pseudofunctor
`𝒮ᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat` attached to a choice of pullbacks `c` of a fibred category: `U ↦ 𝒳_U`,
`f ↦ f^*` (the pullback functor of `c`), with unitor `α_U` and compositor `α_{g,f}` the canonical
isomorphisms of Stacks 02XO (1), (2).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pseudofunctor : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete 𝒮ᵒᵖ) Cat
declarations.comment: (3), for an arbitrary choice of pullbacks

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_mapId_hom_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XO (2).** The component at `x` of the unitor of `c.pseudofunctor` is, in `𝒳`, the
chosen lift of the identity at `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pseudofunctor_mapId_hom_app (U : LocallyDiscrete 𝒮ᵒᵖ) (x : p.Fiber U.as.unop) :
    Fiber.fiberInclusion.map ((c.pseudofunctor.mapId U).hom.toNatTrans.app x) =
      c.map (𝟙 U.as.unop) x
declarations.comment: (2), for an arbitrary choice of pullbacks

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_fac
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XO (1).** The component at `x` of the compositor of `c.pseudofunctor` at `(φ, γ)`
makes the triangle with the chosen lifts commute: followed by the chosen lifts of `γ` and of `φ`,
it is the chosen lift of the composite.
declarations.statement:
lemma pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_fac {U V W : LocallyDiscrete 𝒮ᵒᵖ} (φ : U ⟶ V) (γ : V ⟶ W)
    (x : p.Fiber U.as.unop) :
    Fiber.fiberInclusion.map ((c.pseudofunctor.mapComp φ γ).hom.toNatTrans.app x) ≫
        c.map γ.as.unop (c.obj φ.as.unop x) ≫ c.map φ.as.unop x =
      c.map (φ ≫ γ).as.unop x
declarations.comment: (1), for an arbitrary choice of pullbacks

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XO (1), uniqueness.** The component at `x` of the compositor of `c.pseudofunctor` at
`(φ, γ)` is the unique morphism of the fibre making the triangle with the chosen lifts commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_unique {U V W : LocallyDiscrete 𝒮ᵒᵖ} (φ : U ⟶ V)
    (γ : V ⟶ W) (x : p.Fiber U.as.unop)
    (θ : c.obj (φ ≫ γ).as.unop x ⟶ c.obj γ.as.unop (c.obj φ.as.unop x))
    (hθ : Fiber.fiberInclusion.map θ ≫ c.map γ.as.unop (c.obj φ.as.unop x) ≫
        c.map φ.as.unop x = c.map (φ ≫ γ).as.unop x) :
    θ = (c.pseudofunctor.mapComp φ γ).hom.toNatTrans.app x
declarations.comment: (1), uniqueness, for an arbitrary choice of pullbacks

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.existsUnique_compIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XO (1)**, as stated in the source. For composable `f : V ⟶ U` and `g : W ⟶ V`
there is a unique isomorphism `α_{g,f} : (f ∘ g)^* ≅ g^* ∘ f^*` of functors from the fibre over
`U` to the fibre over `W` such that, for every `y`, the chosen lift `(f ∘ g)^* y ⟶ y` is
`(α_{g,f})_y` followed by the chosen lifts `g^* f^* y ⟶ f^* y ⟶ y`. The compositor of
`c.pseudofunctor` satisfies this triangle (`pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_fac`), so it is this
`α_{g,f}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_compIso {W V U : 𝒮} (g : W ⟶ V) (f : V ⟶ U) :
    ∃! α : c.pullbackFunctor (g ≫ f) ≅ c.pullbackFunctor f ⋙ c.pullbackFunctor g,
      ∀ y : p.Fiber U, Fiber.fiberInclusion.map (α.hom.app y) ≫ c.map g (c.obj f y) ≫
        c.map f y = c.map (g ≫ f) y
declarations.comment: (1), existence and uniqueness of the isomorphism, for an arbitrary choice of pullbacks

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFibered
declarations.doc:
The 2-category of fibred categories over `𝒮`: the sub-2-category of the 2-category
`BasedCategory 𝒮` of categories over `𝒮` (Stacks 003Y) whose

1. objects are the categories `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` over `𝒮` that are fibred categories;
2. 1-morphisms `(𝒳, p) ⟶ (𝒴, p')` are the functors `G : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` with `p' ∘ G = p` carrying
   strongly cartesian morphisms to strongly cartesian morphisms;
3. 2-morphisms `t : G ⟶ H` are the morphisms of functors with `p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every
   object `x` of `𝒳`.

The hom-category `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is the source's `Mor_{Fib/𝒮}(𝒳, 𝒴)`.
declarations.statement: structure CatFibered (𝒮 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒮]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isFibered_structureFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XQ, fibredness.** If `p𝒳`, `p𝒴`, `p𝒮` are fibred categories over `𝒞` and
`F`, `G` are 1-morphisms of fibred categories over `𝒞`, then the structure functor of the
2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴` exhibits it as a fibred category over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem TwoFibreProductOver.isFibered_structureFunctor
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮)
    [p𝒳.IsFibered] [p𝒴.IsFibered] [p𝒮.IsFibered]
    (hF : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒳 p𝒮 F)
    (hG : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒴 p𝒮 G) :
    (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).IsFibered

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fst_isFibredOneMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XQ, first projection.** Under the hypotheses of
`TwoFibreProductOver.isFibered_structureFunctor`, the first projection `π₁` is a 1-morphism
of fibred categories over `𝒞`: it is strictly over `𝒞` and preserves strongly cartesian
morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem TwoFibreProductOver.fst_isFibredOneMorphism
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮)
    [p𝒳.IsFibered] [p𝒴.IsFibered] [p𝒮.IsFibered]
    (hF : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒳 p𝒮 F)
    (hG : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒴 p𝒮 G) :
    Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) p𝒳
      (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.snd_isFibredOneMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XQ, second projection.** Under the hypotheses of
`TwoFibreProductOver.isFibered_structureFunctor`, the second projection `π₂` is a 1-morphism
of fibred categories over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem TwoFibreProductOver.snd_isFibredOneMorphism
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮)
    [p𝒳.IsFibered] [p𝒴.IsFibered] [p𝒮.IsFibered]
    (hF : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒳 p𝒮 F)
    (hG : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒴 p𝒮 G) :
    Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) p𝒴
      (TwoFibreProductOver.snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.lift_isFibredOneMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XQ, universal property in `Fib/𝒞`.** Let `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` and `G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮` be
1-morphisms of fibred categories over `𝒞`, and let `(W, pW)` be a category over `𝒞` with
1-morphisms of fibred categories `H : W ⥤ 𝒳`, `K : W ⥤ 𝒴` and a vertical isomorphism
`t : H ⋙ F ≅ K ⋙ G`. Then the mediating 1-morphism `lift : W ⥤ 𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴` of Stacks 0040 is a
1-morphism of fibred categories: it is strictly over `𝒞` and preserves strongly cartesian
morphisms. The image of a strongly cartesian `φ` has the strongly cartesian components `H φ` and
`K φ`, so it is strongly cartesian by `isStronglyCartesian_of_components`.

Fibredness of `p𝒳`, `p𝒴`, `p𝒮` and `pW` is not used, so the statement is made without it.
declarations.statement:
theorem lift_isFibredOneMorphism
    (hF : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒳 p𝒮 F) (hG : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒴 p𝒮 G)
    {W : Type u₅} [Category.{v₅} W] {pW : W ⥤ 𝒞} {H : W ⥤ 𝒳} {K : W ⥤ 𝒴}
    (hH : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism pW p𝒳 H) (hK : Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism pW p𝒴 K)
    (t : H ⋙ F ≅ K ⋙ G) (ht : ∀ w, p𝒮.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (t.hom.app w)) :
    Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism pW (structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G)
      (lift p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH.comp_eq hK.comp_eq t ht)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.liftIso_hom_app_isHomLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XQ, uniqueness in `Fib/𝒞`.** The 2-isomorphism `liftIso` between another
factorisation `γ` of the test cone and the mediating 1-morphism `lift` is a 2-morphism over `𝒞`:
each of its components lies over an identity of `𝒞` for the structure functor. Together with
`natTrans_ext` this makes the factorisation unique up to a unique 2-isomorphism of `Fib/𝒞`,
whose 2-morphisms are those of the 2-category of categories over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem liftIso_hom_app_isHomLift
    {W : Type u₅} [Category.{v₅} W] {pW : W ⥤ 𝒞} {H : W ⥤ 𝒳} {K : W ⥤ 𝒴}
    {t : H ⋙ F ≅ K ⋙ G} (γ : W ⥤ TwoFibreProductOver p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G)
    (a : γ ⋙ fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ≅ H) (b : γ ⋙ snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ≅ K)
    (ha : ∀ w, p𝒳.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (a.hom.app w))
    (hb : ∀ w, p𝒴.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (b.hom.app w))
    (hab : Functor.whiskerRight a.hom F ≫ t.hom =
      Functor.whiskerLeft γ (psiIso p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight b.hom G)
    (hH : H ⋙ p𝒳 = pW) (hK : K ⋙ p𝒴 = pW)
    (ht : ∀ w, p𝒮.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (t.hom.app w)) (w : W) :
    (structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w))
      ((liftIso γ a b ha hb hab hH hK ht).hom.app w)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.of_comp_over
declarations.doc:
If a fibred category `p : S ⥤ C` factors as `p' ⋙ Over.forget U` through the slice
category `Over U`, then `p' : S ⥤ Over U` is a fibred category.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFibered.of_comp_over (p : S ⥤ C)
    [p.IsFibered] (h : p' ⋙ Over.forget U = p) :
    p'.IsFibered

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
The 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`: the full sub-2-category of the
2-category `BasedCategory 𝒞` of categories over `𝒞` (Stacks 003Y) spanned by the categories fibred
in groupoids. Explicitly:

1. its objects are the categories `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` over `𝒞` that are fibred in groupoids;
2. its 1-morphisms `(𝒮, p) ⟶ (𝒮', p')` are the functors `G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'` with `p' ∘ G = p`
   (no condition on strongly cartesian morphisms is needed: see
   `CatFiberedInGroupoids.isStronglyCartesian_map`);
3. its 2-morphisms `t : G ⟶ H` are the morphisms of functors with `p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every
   object `x` of `𝒮`.
declarations.statement: abbrev CatFiberedInGroupoids (𝒞 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒞]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.of_comp_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XT.** If `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` is fibred in groupoids and factors through the slice
category `Over U` as `p' ⋙ Over.forget U = p`, then `p' : 𝒮 ⥤ Over U` is fibred in
groupoids: lifts of morphisms of `Over U` and unique fill-ins for `p'` are obtained from those
for `p`, because the structure morphism of a lifted object is forced and `Over.forget U` is
faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.of_comp_over
    {𝒮 𝒞 : Type*} [Category 𝒮] [Category 𝒞] (U : 𝒞)
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (p' : 𝒮 ⥤ Over U)
    (h : p' ⋙ Over.forget U = p) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.presheafOfCategories
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XV.**
The category `𝒮_F` attached to a presheaf of categories `F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat`, together with its
projection `p_F : 𝒮_F ⥤ 𝒞`, as an object of the 2-category of categories over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement: abbrev presheafOfCategories (F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat.{v₂, u₂}) : BasedCategory 𝒞

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PresheafOfCategories.objEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XV.**
`Ob(𝒮_F) = {(U, x) | U ∈ Ob(𝒞), x ∈ Ob(F(U))}`.
declarations.statement: def objEquiv : ∫ᶜ F.toPseudofunctor' ≃ Σ U : 𝒞, F.obj (op U)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PresheafOfCategories.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XV.**
`Mor_{𝒮_F}((V, y), (U, x))` is the disjoint union over `f : V ⟶ U` of `Mor_{F(V)}(y, f^* x)`.
declarations.statement:
def homEquiv (X Y : ∫ᶜ F.toPseudofunctor') :
    (X ⟶ Y) ≃ Σ f : X.base ⟶ Y.base, (X.fiber ⟶ (F.map f.op).toFunctor.obj Y.fiber)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PresheafOfCategories.comp_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XV.**
The composition of `𝒮_F` is the source's: the composite of `ψ : z ⟶ g^* y` with `φ : y ⟶ f^* x` is
`g^*(φ) ∘ ψ`, read as a morphism `z ⟶ (f ∘ g)^* x` through `pullback_comp_obj`.
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_fiber {X Y Z : ∫ᶜ F.toPseudofunctor'} (u : X ⟶ Y) (v : Y ⟶ Z) :
    (u ≫ v).fiber = u.fiber ≫ (F.map u.base.op).toFunctor.map v.fiber ≫
      eqToHom (pullback_comp_obj F u.base v.base Z.fiber)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PresheafOfCategories.isFibered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XV.**
The projection `p_F : 𝒮_F ⥤ 𝒞` is a fibred category.

This bridge is load-bearing: instance resolution does not see Mathlib's
`CoGrothendieck.instIsFiberedForget` through `BasedCategory.ofFunctor`'s projection, so
`infer_instance` fails on this goal without it.
declarations.statement: instance isFibered : (presheafOfCategories F).p.IsFibered

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsSplitFibered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XW.**
A *split fibred category* over `𝒞` is a fibred category `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` that is isomorphic over `𝒞`
to the fibred category `𝒮_F` attached to some presheaf of categories `F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat`
(Stacks 02XV). The source is explicit that isomorphism over `𝒞`, and not merely equivalence over
`𝒞`, is meant.
declarations.statement: def Functor.IsSplitFibered (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isSplitFibered_iff_exists_isSplitCleavage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XX**, with the source's condition on a choice of pullbacks replaced by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.ChoiceOfPullbacks.IsSplitCleavage`: a fibred category is split
(Stacks 02XW) if and only if some choice of pullbacks (Stacks 02XN) has its two canonical
comparisons of Stacks 02XN equal to identities, i.e. has *chosen cartesian lifts* strictly
compatible with identities and composition.

The source states the condition on the pullback *functors*, as `(f ∘ g)^* = g^* ∘ f^*`, and that
biconditional is false: see the module docstring, and the two counterexamples
`CategoryTheory.SplittingCounterexample.compatibleWithComp_not_isSplitting` and
`CategoryTheory.SplitCleavageCounterexample.isSplitting_not_isSplitFibered` in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/FiberedCategory/SplittingCounterexample.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isSplitFibered_iff_exists_isSplitCleavage {p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮} :
    p.IsSplitFibered ↔ ∃ c : p.ChoiceOfPullbacks, c.IsSplitCleavage

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isFibredEquivalenceOver_presheafOfGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XY.**
Every category fibred in groupoids `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` is equivalent, in the 2-category of fibred
categories over `𝒞`, to the category `𝒮_F` (Stacks 0049,
`CategoryTheory.presheafOfGroupoids`) attached to a contravariant functor
`F : 𝒞 ⥤ Groupoids`; in other words, every category fibred in groupoids is equivalent to a split
one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFibredEquivalenceOver_presheafOfGroupoids (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    ∃ (F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grpd.{v₂, max u₁ u₂ v₁}) (Φ : 𝒳 ⥤ (presheafOfGroupoids F).obj),
      IsFibredEquivalenceOver p (presheafOfGroupoids F).p Φ

declarations.name: IsSetoidCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02XZ.** A category `C` is a *setoid* when every morphism of `C` is an
isomorphism and every endomorphism `f : X ⟶ X` is `𝟙 X`; equivalently `C` is a thin groupoid,
so a setoid is a set together with an equivalence relation on it.
declarations.statement: def IsSetoidCategory (C : Type*) [Category C] : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSetoids
declarations.doc:
The 2-category of categories fibred in setoids over `𝒞`: the full sub-2-category of the
2-category `BasedCategory 𝒞` of categories over `𝒞` spanned by the categories fibred in setoids.
Explicitly:

1. its objects are the categories `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` over `𝒞` that are fibred in setoids;
2. its 1-morphisms `(𝒮, p) ⟶ (𝒮', p')` are the functors `G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'` with `p' ∘ G = p`;
3. its 2-morphisms `t : G ⟶ H` are the morphisms of functors with `p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every
   object `x` of `𝒮`.
declarations.statement: abbrev CatFiberedInSetoids (𝒞 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒞]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets.exists_eq_eqToHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y2**, first assertion. The only 2-morphisms between categories fibred in sets are
identities: a 2-morphism `t : G ⟶ H` of the 2-category of categories fibred in sets over `𝒞`
forces `G = H`, and `t` is then the identity 2-morphism of `G` (written `eqToHom`). In other words,
the 2-category of categories fibred in sets is a category.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eq_eqToHom {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInSets.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞} {G H : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (t : G ⟶ H) : ∃ h : G = H, t = eqToHom h
declarations.comment: 2-morphisms between categories fibred in sets are identities

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets.presheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y2**, the equivalence. Let `C` be a category. There is an equivalence of categories
between the category of presheaves of sets on `C` and the category of categories fibred in sets
over `C`. The functor from left to right is the construction `F ↦ 𝒮_F` of Stacks 04TM
(`CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets.ofPresheaf`), and the functor from right to left sends
`p : 𝒮 ⥤ C` to its presheaf of objects `U ↦ Ob(𝒮_U)`
(`CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets.objPresheafFunctor`); see
`CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets.presheafEquivalence_functor` and
`CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets.presheafEquivalence_inverse`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheafEquivalence :
    (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u w)) ≌ CatFiberedInSets.{v, v, u, max u w} C
declarations.comment: presheaves of sets ≌ categories fibred in sets: F ↦ S_F, p ↦ (U ↦ Ob(S_U))

declarations.name: StacksRepresentableCFG.representable_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y3** (part 1). A category fibred in groupoids `p : S ⥤ C` is representable
if and only if `S` is fibred in setoids and its presheaf of isomorphism classes
`\overline{S}` is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem representable_iff (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) :
    IsRepresentable p ↔ (p.IsFiberedInSetoids ∧ IsoClassRepresentable p)

declarations.name: StacksRepresentableCFG.representing_pair_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y3** (part 2). If a category `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` is representable, the pair `(X, j)`,
with `j : 𝒮 → 𝒞/X` an equivalence over `𝒞`, is uniquely determined up to isomorphism: for
two such pairs `(X, j)` and `(X', j')` there is an isomorphism `φ : X' ≅ X` in `𝒞` and a
2-isomorphism `α : (𝒞/φ) ∘ j' ≅ j` over `𝒞`, where `𝒞/φ = Over.map φ.hom : 𝒞/X' ⥤ 𝒞/X`;
"over `𝒞`" means that `α` whiskered with `Over.forget X` is the identity 2-cell.
declarations.statement:
theorem representing_pair_unique (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) {X X' : 𝒞} (j : RepresentableBy p X)
    (j' : RepresentableBy p X') :
    ∃ φ : X' ≅ X, ∃ α : j'.hom.functor ⋙ Over.map φ.hom ≅ j.hom.functor,
      Functor.whiskerRight α.hom (Over.forget X) =
        eqToHom (by rw [Functor.assoc, Over.mapForget_eq, j'.hom.w, j.hom.w])
declarations.comment: (2); stated for any category over C, Stacks' case is p fibred in groupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.FstFiber.objEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y5 (1).**
The objects of the fibre category of `(𝒞/U) ×_𝒴 𝒳` over an object `f : V ⟶ U` of `𝒞/U` are the
pairs `(x, φ)` consisting of an object `x` of the fibre `𝒳_V` and a morphism
`φ : G(f) ⟶ F(x)` of the fibre `𝒴_V`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.FstFiber.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y5 (2).**
The morphisms of the fibre category of `(𝒞/U) ×_𝒴 𝒳` over an object `f : V ⟶ U` of `𝒞/U` between
two objects `(x, φ)` and `(x', φ')` are exactly the morphisms `ψ : x ⟶ x'` of the fibre `𝒳_V`
with `F(ψ) = φ' ∘ φ⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fst_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y6.** Let `𝒳`, `𝒴` be categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`, let `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` and
`G : 𝒞/U ⥤ 𝒴` be 1-morphisms over `𝒞`. Then the first projection of the 2-fibre product
`(𝒞/U) ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒞/U` is a category fibred in groupoids over the slice `𝒞/U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem TwoFibreProductOver.fst_isFiberedInGroupoids (U : 𝒞) (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (G : Over U ⥤ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hF : F ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒴 = Over.forget U) :
    (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.forget U) p𝒳 p𝒴 G F).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y7.** `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` (a 1-morphism over `𝒞`) is *representable*, equivalently
`𝒳` is *relatively representable over* `𝒴`, when for every object `U` of `𝒞` and every
1-morphism `G : 𝒞/U ⥤ 𝒴` over `𝒞` (i.e. `G ⋙ q = Over.forget U`), the first projection
`(𝒞/U) ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞/U` of the 2-fibre product over `𝒞` is a representable category fibred in
groupoids.

The source states this for `𝒳`, `𝒴` fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`; the predicate here does
not assume that, so it is the same condition stated for an arbitrary 1-morphism and
specialises to the source's notion.
declarations.statement: def IsRepresentableMorphism (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.inducedFiberFunctor_faithful_of_isRepresentableMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Y8** (Lemma 4.42.4), the stated implication. If `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` is a representable
1-morphism over `𝒞` between categories fibred in groupoids, then for every object `U` of `𝒞` the
induced functor on fibre categories `F_U : 𝒳_U ⥤ 𝒴_U` is faithful. The converse is not proved
here.
declarations.statement:
theorem inducedFiberFunctor_faithful_of_isRepresentableMorphism
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞)
    (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hF : F ⋙ q = p)
    (hrep : IsRepresentableMorphism p q F) (U : 𝒞) :
    (inducedFiberFunctor p q F hF U).Faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isRepresentableMorphism_of_faithful_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳`, `𝒴` be categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`, let `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism
over `𝒞` and let `c` be a choice of pullbacks for `𝒴`. If every functor `F_U : 𝒳_U ⥤ 𝒴_U` on
fibre categories is faithful, and if for every `U` and every object `y` of `𝒴_U` the presheaf on
`𝒞/U` of isomorphism classes of pairs `(x, φ : f^* y ⟶ F(x))` is representable, then `F` is a
representable 1-morphism in the sense of Stacks 02Y7.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableMorphism_of_faithful_of_isRepresentable (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hF : F ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (c : p𝒴.ChoiceOfPullbacks)
    (hfaithful : ∀ U : 𝒞, (Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.inducedFiberFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 F hF U).Faithful)
    (hrepresentable : ∀ (U : 𝒞) (y : p𝒴.Fiber U),
      (PairIsoClass.presheaf F c y h𝒳 h𝒴 hF).IsRepresentable) :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p𝒳 p𝒴 F

declarations.name: Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.isRepresentableMorphism_diagonal_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YA.** Let `𝒞` be a category with products of pairs and fibre products, and let
`p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` be a category fibred in groupoids. The diagonal `𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮 × 𝒮` into the 2-fibre product
`𝒮 × 𝒮 = 𝒮 ×_𝒞 𝒮` over the final object `𝟭 𝒞` (Stacks 0040) is representable (Stacks 02Y7) if and
only if, for every object `U` of `𝒞`, every 1-morphism `G : 𝒞/U ⥤ 𝒮` is representable.

The morphisms of `𝒞` and of `𝒮` are taken in one universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableMorphism_diagonal_iff [HasBinaryProducts 𝒞] [HasPullbacks 𝒞]
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsRepresentableMorphism p (structureFunctor p p (𝟭 𝒞) p p) (diagonal (Functor.comp_id p)) ↔
      ∀ (U : 𝒞) (G : Over U ⥤ 𝒮), G ⋙ p = Over.forget U →
        IsRepresentableMorphism (Over.forget U) p G

declarations.name: Topology.IsCoinducing.isLocallyClosed_iff_preimage
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02YB** (part 4). An open coinducing map detects locally closed subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem Topology.IsCoinducing.isLocallyClosed_iff_preimage
    {f : X → Y} (hf : IsCoinducing f) (hopen : IsOpenMap f) (T : Set Y) :
    IsLocallyClosed T ↔ IsLocallyClosed (f ⁻¹' T)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.comp_source_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The square formed by composition, the second projection, and two copies of the source map
is a pullback square: a composable pair of arrows is determined by its first member together
with its composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_source_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback G.comp (pullback.snd G.source G.target) G.source G.source

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.target_comp_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The upper triangle in the composition diagram, viewed as a square with two copies of its
apex, is a pullback square: a pair of arrows with the same target is the same thing as a
composable pair together with its composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem target_comp_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback (pullback.fst G.source G.target) G.comp G.target G.target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_common_field_fiber_iso
declarations.doc:
If two arrows in a groupoid scheme have the same target, then the fibres of the source
map over their sources become isomorphic after extending both residue fields to a common
field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_common_field_fiber_iso {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) (r r' : G.arrows.left)
    (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K),
      Nonempty
        (Over.mk (pullback.snd
          (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K)))) ≅
        Over.mk (pullback.snd
          (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r'))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K)))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_common_field_fiber_iso_mapping_point
declarations.doc:
The common field and source-fibre isomorphism for two arrows with the same target can be
chosen so that the isomorphism carries a point above the first arrow to a point above the
second.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_common_field_fiber_iso_mapping_point {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) (r r' : G.arrows.left)
    (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K),
      let g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r))) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K))
      let g' : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r'))) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K))
      let P : Scheme.{u} :=
        pullback (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r)) g
      let _P' : Scheme.{u} :=
        pullback (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r')) g'
      let POver : Over (Spec (.of K)) := Over.mk
        (pullback.snd (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r)) g)
      let POver' : Over (Spec (.of K)) := Over.mk
        (pullback.snd (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r')) g')
      ∃ (x : P) (e : POver ≅ POver'),
        ((pullback.fst
            (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r)) g) ≫
              G.source.left.fiberι (G.source.left r)).base x = r ∧
          ((pullback.fst
            (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r')) g') ≫
              G.source.left.fiberι (G.source.left r')).base (e.hom.left.base x) = r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatIsoLocallyOnBase_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YF (3).** If the source and target maps of a groupoid scheme are flat, then for
two arrows with the same target the two germs of the source map, at the first arrow over its
source and at the second arrow over its source, are flat locally on the base isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatIsoLocallyOnBase_source {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (hs : Flat G.source.left) (ht : Flat G.target.left)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    FlatIsoLocallyOnBase G.source.left r G.source.left r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YF (4).** If the source and target maps of a groupoid scheme have a property `P`
of morphisms of schemes, then for two arrows with the same target the two germs of the source
map, at the first arrow over its source and at the second arrow over its source, are isomorphic
locally on the base in the topology belonging to `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocallyOnBase_source {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (hs : P G.source.left) (ht : P G.target.left)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    IsoLocallyOnBase P G.source.left r G.source.left r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_etale
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02YF (4), the étale case.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocallyOnBase_source_etale {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (hs : Etale G.source.left) (ht : Etale G.target.left)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    IsoLocallyOnBase @Etale G.source.left r G.source.left r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_smooth
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02YF (4), the smooth case.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocallyOnBase_source_smooth {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (hs : Smooth G.source.left) (ht : Smooth G.target.left)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    IsoLocallyOnBase @Smooth G.source.left r G.source.left r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_syntomic
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02YF (4), the syntomic case.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocallyOnBase_source_syntomic {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (hs : Syntomic G.source.left) (ht : Syntomic G.target.left)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    IsoLocallyOnBase @Syntomic G.source.left r G.source.left r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YF (4), the fppf case:** source and target flat and locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocallyOnBase_source_fppf {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (hs : Flat G.source.left) (hs' : LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left)
    (ht : Flat G.target.left) (ht' : LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    IsoLocallyOnBase (@Flat ⊓ @LocallyOfFinitePresentation) G.source.left r
      G.source.left r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.source_fiber_comparison_of_target_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YF.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid over a scheme `S` and let `r`, `r'` be
two arrows with the same target.  Writing `u = s r` and `u' = s r'`, and `F_u = s⁻¹(u)`,
`F_{u'} = s⁻¹(u')` for the scheme theoretic fibres of the source map:

1. there is a field `k` extending both `κ(u)` and `κ(u')` together with an isomorphism
   `(F_u)_k ≅ (F_{u'})_k`;
2. that isomorphism may be chosen so that a point lying over `r` maps to a point lying over
   `r'`;
3. if `s` and `t` are flat then the morphisms of germs `s : (R, r) ⟶ (U, u)` and
   `s : (R, r') ⟶ (U, u')` are flat locally on the base isomorphic;
4. if `s` and `t` are étale (resp. smooth, syntomic, or flat and locally of finite
   presentation) then those two morphisms of germs are locally on the base isomorphic in the
   étale (resp. smooth, syntomic, fppf) topology.

The four parts are `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_common_field_fiber_iso`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_common_field_fiber_iso_mapping_point`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.flatIsoLocallyOnBase_source` and the four cases
`AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_etale`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_smooth`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_syntomic`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isoLocallyOnBase_source_fppf`; the flatness, étaleness, smoothness,
syntomicity and finite presentation assumptions of parts (3) and (4) appear as hypotheses of
those parts, exactly as in the source, and not of the lemma.
declarations.statement:
theorem source_fiber_comparison_of_target_eq {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) (h : G.target.left r = G.target.left r') :
    (∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K),
      Nonempty
        (Over.mk (pullback.snd
          (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K)))) ≅
        Over.mk (pullback.snd
          (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r'))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K)))))) ∧
    (∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K),
      let g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r))) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r)) K))
      let g' : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r'))) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (G.objects.left.residueField (G.source.left r')) K))
      let P : Scheme.{u} :=
        pullback (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r)) g
      let _P' : Scheme.{u} :=
        pullback (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r')) g'
      let POver : Over (Spec (.of K)) := Over.mk
        (pullback.snd (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r)) g)
      let POver' : Over (Spec (.of K)) := Over.mk
        (pullback.snd (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r')) g')
      ∃ (x : P) (e : POver ≅ POver'),
        ((pullback.fst
            (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r)) g) ≫
              G.source.left.fiberι (G.source.left r)).base x = r ∧
          ((pullback.fst
            (G.source.left.fiberToSpecResidueField (G.source.left r')) g') ≫
              G.source.left.fiberι (G.source.left r')).base (e.hom.left.base x) = r') ∧
    (Flat G.source.left → Flat G.target.left →
      FlatIsoLocallyOnBase G.source.left r G.source.left r') ∧
    (Etale G.source.left → Etale G.target.left →
      IsoLocallyOnBase @Etale G.source.left r G.source.left r') ∧
    (Smooth G.source.left → Smooth G.target.left →
      IsoLocallyOnBase @Smooth G.source.left r G.source.left r') ∧
    (Syntomic G.source.left → Syntomic G.target.left →
      IsoLocallyOnBase @Syntomic G.source.left r G.source.left r') ∧
    (Flat G.source.left → LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left →
      Flat G.target.left → LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left →
      IsoLocallyOnBase (@Flat ⊓ @LocallyOfFinitePresentation) G.source.left r
        G.source.left r')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalDiagram_commutes
declarations.doc: The left-hand part of the displayed diagonal diagram commutes.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalDiagram_commutes {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    arrowDiagonal G ≫ bottomComparison G = topComparison G ≫ rightVertical G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topComparison_isIso
declarations.doc: The upper comparison morphism in the diagonal diagram is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma topComparison_isIso {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsIso (topComparison G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bottomComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
The lower comparison morphism in the diagonal diagram is an isomorphism, with inverse
`(f, h) ↦ (f, f ∘ h)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bottomComparison_isIso {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsIso (bottomComparison G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rightSquare_isPullback
declarations.doc: The right-hand square in the diagonal diagram is a pullback square.
declarations.statement:
lemma rightSquare_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback (pullback.snd G.source (𝟙 G.objects)) (rightVertical G)
      (identityStabilizer G) (pullback.snd G.source
        (pullback.snd (sourceTarget G) (diagonal G)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sourceTarget_quasiSeparated_iff_stabilizer_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
The source-target morphism is quasi-separated exactly when the stabilizer is
quasi-separated over the object scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem sourceTarget_quasiSeparated_iff_stabilizer_quasiSeparated
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    QuasiSeparated (sourceTarget G).left ↔ QuasiSeparated (stabilizer G).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stabilizer_quasiSeparated_iff_identity_quasiCompact
declarations.doc: The stabilizer is quasi-separated exactly when its identity section is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem stabilizer_quasiSeparated_iff_identity_quasiCompact
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    QuasiSeparated (stabilizer G).hom ↔ QuasiCompact (identityStabilizer G).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sourceTarget_isSeparated_iff_stabilizer_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
The source-target morphism is separated exactly when the stabilizer is separated over
the object scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem sourceTarget_isSeparated_iff_stabilizer_isSeparated
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsSeparated (sourceTarget G).left ↔ IsSeparated (stabilizer G).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stabilizer_isSeparated_iff_identity_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: The stabilizer is separated exactly when its identity section is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem stabilizer_isSeparated_iff_identity_isClosedImmersion
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsSeparated (stabilizer G).hom ↔ IsClosedImmersion (identityStabilizer G).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02YQ.** A morphism of presheaves is representable by algebraic
spaces if its pullback to every scheme over the base is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (a : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02YR.** A transformation representable by algebraic spaces has a
sheaf as its source if its target is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS a)
    (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) G) :
