declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpaceULift_of_isRepresentable_uliftYoneda
declarations.doc:
The source of a morphism of presheaves with values in `Type (max w u)` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and whose target is isomorphic to the universe-lifted Yoneda
presheaf of an object of the big fppf site of `S` is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpaceULift_of_isRepresentable_uliftYoneda
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)} {U : BigFppfOver B S hS} (a : F ⟶ G)
    (e : G ≅ (uliftYoneda.{w}).obj U)
    (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS a) :
    IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{w} B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YS.** A transformation representable by algebraic spaces to an algebraic space over
`S` has an algebraic space over `S` as its source.

The three clauses of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace` are verified as in Stacks 02WY. The
sheaf clause is Stacks 02YR. The diagonal clause is the composite
`Δ_F = Δ_{F/G} ≫ (F ×_G F ⟶ F × F)`, representable because `Δ_{F/G}` is — this is Stacks 05LA in
the strengthened form above — and because the second factor is a base change of `Δ_G`. For the
atlas clause, base-changing a scheme atlas of `G` along `a` gives a surjective étale morphism to
`F` from an *algebraic space*, and composing it with a scheme atlas of that algebraic space gives
a scheme atlas of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : F ⟶ G) (ha : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS a)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YU, part (1).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is an *open
immersion* when it is representable and every represented base change of it is an open
immersion of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsOpenImmersion {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YU, part (2).** A subfunctor of a presheaf on the big fppf site of `S` is
an *open subspace* when it is an algebraic space over `S` and its inclusion is an open
immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsOpenSubspace {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (G : Subfunctor F) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YU, part (3).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a *closed
immersion* when it is representable and every represented base change of it is a closed
immersion of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsClosedImmersion {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YU, part (4).** A subfunctor of a presheaf on the big fppf site of `S` is
a *closed subspace* when it is an algebraic space over `S` and its inclusion is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsClosedSubspace {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (G : Subfunctor F) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YU, part (5).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is an *immersion*
when it is representable and every represented base change of it is an immersion of
schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsImmersion {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YU, part (6).** A subfunctor of a presheaf on the big fppf site of `S` is
a *locally closed subspace* when it is an algebraic space over `S` and its inclusion is
an immersion.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLocallyClosedSubspace {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (G : Subfunctor F) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YV**, part (1): a composite of open immersions of algebraic spaces over `S` is
an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_comp {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ H)
    (hf : IsOpenImmersion B S hS f) (hg : IsOpenImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YV**, part (2): a composite of closed immersions of algebraic spaces over `S` is
a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_comp {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ H)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) (hg : IsClosedImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isImmersion_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02YV**, part (3): a composite of immersions of algebraic spaces over `S` is an
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_comp {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ H)
    (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f) (hg : IsImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsImmersion B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_involutionQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z1, quasi-separatedness.** Away from characteristic two, the quotient of the
affine line by the punctured graph of negation is a quasi-separated algebraic space.

The chart `𝔸¹_k ⟶ X` is surjective and étale by Stacks 0265, its source is affine and hence
quasi-separated, and the second projection of its kernel pair is a base change of the target
map of the relation, which is affine; Stacks 07S4 concludes.

Representability of the diagonal of `X`, from which surjectivity and étaleness of the chart
both follow, is supplied unconditionally by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativelyRepresentable_diag_quotientSheaf` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_involutionQuotient (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) :
    Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ
      (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z1.** Away from characteristic two, the involution relation on the affine
line is an étale equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEquivalenceRelation [NeZero (2 : k)] :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (involutionRelation k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z1.** Away from characteristic two, the quotient of the affine line by the
punctured graph of negation is an algebraic space over the ground field.

The chart `affineLineChart` is affine, so the two descent hypotheses of Stacks 0265 are
discharged unconditionally by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_affineBase_unconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.not_isImmersion_involutionRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z1.** The pre-relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_k U` of the involution quotient is not an
immersion.

On the graph summand `j` restricts to the inclusion of the puncture followed by the graph of
negation; on the diagonal summand it restricts to the diagonal. The generic point of the
punctured line specializes to the zero section, which negation fixes, so an immersion would
force a specialization between the images of the two summands that
`not_specializes_relationScheme` rules out upstairs.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isImmersion_involutionRelation :
    ¬ AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion ((involutionRelation k).left)
declarations.comment: the relation j is not an immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.not_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated_involutionQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z1, not locally separated.** Away from characteristic two, the quotient of the
affine line by the punctured graph of negation is not a locally separated algebraic space.

The contrapositive of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated` (Stacks 04ZI,
part 2) reduces this to the relative statement `not_isLocallySeparatedOver_quotientSpace`, using
the algebraicity of the quotient supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated_involutionQuotient (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) :
    ¬ Space.IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ
      (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_actionQuotient_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z2.** Let a group `G` act on an object `V` of the big fppf site of `S` so that
no nonidentity element fixes a point of `V` and acts trivially on its residue field. Then the
quotient `V/R` of `V` by the graph relation `R = ∐_{g ∈ G} V` of the action is an algebraic
space over `S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_actionQuotient` with its descent hypothesis
discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_actionQuotient_unconditional {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Type v) [Group G]
    [Small.{u} G] (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    (a : G →* Aut (underlyingOver B hS V))
    (ha : ActsNontriviallyOnFixedResidueFields (underlyingOver B hS V) G a) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (actionQuotient G B hS V a)
declarations.comment: the quotient is an algebraic space

The scheme of arrows of the graph relation of a group action: the disjoint union of one

declarations.statement: abbrev actionRelationScheme : Over S

The quotient of a scheme in a big fppf site by a group action: the quotient sheaf of the

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ActsNontriviallyOnFixedResidueFields
declarations.doc:
The action of a group on a scheme over `S` *acts nontrivially on fixed residue fields*

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.actionQuotient
declarations.doc:
The quotient of a scheme in a big fppf site by a group action: the quotient sheaf of the

abbrev actionQuotient (a : G →* Aut (underlyingOver B hS V))

declarations.comment: the quotient U/G of a scheme by a group action satisfying (*)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparatedOver_actionQuotient_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z4, part (2).** Let a finite group `G` act on an object `V` of the big fppf site
over `S` so that no nonidentity element fixes a point of `V` together with its residue field. If
`V` is separated over `S`, then the quotient `V/G` is separated over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_actionQuotient_unconditional (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G]

    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated (underlyingOver B hS V).hom] :
    IsSeparatedOver B S hS (actionQuotient G B hS V a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparatedOver_actionQuotient_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z4, part (1).** Let a finite group `G` act on an object `V` of the big fppf site
over `S` so that no nonidentity element fixes a point of `V` together with its residue field. If
`V` is quasi-separated over `S`, then the quotient `V/G` is quasi-separated over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedOver_actionQuotient_unconditional (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (a : G →* Aut (underlyingOver B hS V))
    (ha : ActsNontriviallyOnFixedResidueFields (underlyingOver B hS V) G a)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    [QuasiSeparated (underlyingOver B hS V).hom] :
    IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS (actionQuotient G B hS V a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientPoint_of_galois_equivariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z5, the converse descent.** Galois-equivariant field-valued data descend to a
point of the action quotient whose pullback is the image of the supplied point upstairs.

Let `L/K` be finite Galois with Galois group identified with a finite subgroup `H` of `G`,
and let `f : Spec L ⟶ V` be a point over the given point of the base which is equivariant for
that identification. Then the image of `f` in the quotient is invariant under the Galois
group, so it descends through the sheaf condition on the étale covering `Spec L ⟶ Spec K` to a
`K`-valued point of the quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientPoint_of_galois_equivariant (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] (H : Subgroup G) [Finite H]
    (e : H ≃* (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
    (f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ (underlyingOver B hS V).left)
    (hf : f ≫ (underlyingOver B hS V).hom =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) ≫ b)
    (he : ∀ h : H,
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (e h⁻¹).toRingHom) ≫ f = f ≫ (a h.1).asIso.hom.left) :
    ∃ ξ : (actionQuotient G B hS V a).obj (op (fieldObject (hS := hS) K hK b)),
      IsQuotientLift B hS V G a K hK b ξ L f hf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_galois_equivariant_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z5, the Galois-equivariant lift.** Let a group `G` act on an object `V` of the
big fppf site over `S` so that no nonidentity element fixes a point of `V` together with its
residue field. Then every `K`-valued point `ξ` of the quotient `V/G` is the image of an
equivariant point over a finite Galois extension of `K`: there are a finite Galois extension
`L/K`, a finite subgroup `H` of `G`, an isomorphism `H ≃* Gal(L/K)` and a morphism
`Spec L ⟶ V` over the given point of the base which is equivariant for that isomorphism and
whose image in the quotient is the pullback of `ξ`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_galois_equivariant_lift_of_descent` with its descent
hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongCoveringSieve_monomorphisms_inf_lft`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_galois_equivariant_lift
    (ha : ActsNontriviallyOnFixedResidueFields (underlyingOver B hS V) G a)
    (ξ : (actionQuotient G B hS V a).obj (op (fieldObject (hS := hS) K hK b))) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : FiniteDimensional K L)
      (_ : IsGalois K L) (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Finite H) (e : H ≃* (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
      (f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ (underlyingOver B hS V).left)
      (hf : f ≫ (underlyingOver B hS V).hom =
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) ≫ b),
      (∀ h : H,
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (e h⁻¹).toRingHom) ≫ f = f ≫ (a h.1).asIso.hom.left) ∧
      IsQuotientLift B hS V G a K hK b ξ L f hf
declarations.comment: the Galois-equivariant lift of a field-valued point of the quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_galois_equivariant_lift_and_existsUnique_quotientPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z5.** Let a group `G` act on an object `V` of the big fppf site over `S` so
that condition `(*)` of Stacks 02Z2 holds: no nonidentity element fixes a point of `V`
together with its residue field. Then for a field `K` with a point `Spec K ⟶ S` of the base:

* every `K`-valued point `ξ` of the quotient `V/G` comes from a finite Galois extension `L/K`,
  a finite subgroup `H ⊆ G`, an isomorphism `H ≃* Gal(L/K)` and an `H`-equivariant morphism
  `Spec L ⟶ V` over the base whose image in the quotient is the pullback of `ξ`;
* conversely, such data determine a `K`-valued point of `V/G`: there is exactly one whose
  pullback to `Spec L` is the image of the given morphism `Spec L ⟶ V`.

The two halves are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_galois_equivariant_lift` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_quotientPoint_of_galois_equivariant`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_galois_equivariant_lift_and_existsUnique_quotientPoint
    (ha : ActsNontriviallyOnFixedResidueFields (underlyingOver B hS V) G a) :
    (∀ ξ : (actionQuotient G B hS V a).obj (op (fieldObject (hS := hS) K hK b)),
      ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : FiniteDimensional K L)
        (_ : IsGalois K L) (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Finite H) (e : H ≃* (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
        (f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ (underlyingOver B hS V).left)
        (hf : f ≫ (underlyingOver B hS V).hom =
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) ≫ b),
        (∀ h : H,
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (e h⁻¹).toRingHom) ≫ f = f ≫ (a h.1).asIso.hom.left) ∧
        IsQuotientLift B hS V G a K hK b ξ L f hf) ∧
    (∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
      (H : Subgroup G) [Finite H] (e : H ≃* (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
      (f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ (underlyingOver B hS V).left)
      (hf : f ≫ (underlyingOver B hS V).hom =
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) ≫ b),
      (∀ h : H,
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (e h⁻¹).toRingHom) ≫ f = f ≫ (a h.1).asIso.hom.left) →
      ∃! ξ : (actionQuotient G B hS V a).obj (op (fieldObject (hS := hS) K hK b)),
        IsQuotientLift B hS V G a K hK b ξ L f hf)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.galoisAction_nontrivialOnFixedResidueFields
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z6.** Every nonidentity element of the absolute Galois group of `ℚ` acts
nontrivially on the residue field at the unique point of `Spec ℚ̄`.
declarations.statement:
theorem galoisAction_nontrivialOnFixedResidueFields :
    Space.ActsNontriviallyOnFixedResidueFields
      (Space.underlyingOver B hS (siteCover B hS hU)) galoisGroup (galoisAction B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.fieldPoint_algEquiv_algebraicClosure_or_real
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z6.** A field algebraic over `ℚ` carrying a point of the Galois quotient of
`Spec ℚ̄` is isomorphic over `ℚ` either to `ℚ̄` itself or to the field `algebraicClosure ℚ ℝ`
of real algebraic numbers.

The point lifts to a morphism `Spec L → Spec ℚ̄` for a finite extension `L` of the field, so
`L` is algebraic over `ℚ` and receives `ℚ̄`, hence is a copy of `ℚ̄` and is algebraically
closed; the Artin–Schreier degree bound in characteristic zero then leaves only degree one
and degree two, and the quadratic case is the real closure.
declarations.statement:
theorem fieldPoint_algEquiv_algebraicClosure_or_real
    (K : Type) [Field K] [Algebra ℚ K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ K]
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K))) (b : Spec (.of K) ⟶ base)
    (ξ : (galoisQuotient B hS hU).obj
      (op (Over.mk (ObjectProperty.homMk b : B.obj hK ⟶ B.obj hS)))) :
    Nonempty (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ∨
      Nonempty (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] algebraicClosure ℚ ℝ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.translationQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z7.** The fppf sheaf quotient of the affine line over `k` by integer

declarations.statement:
abbrev translationQuotient (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))

    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.genericQuotientMorphism
declarations.doc:
The generic point of the affine line over `k`, as a morphism `γ : Spec k(x) ⟶ X = 𝔸¹_k/ℤ`
of fppf sheaves over `Spec k`: the generic point of the line followed by the projection onto
the quotient.
declarations.statement:
def genericQuotientMorphism (hU : B.Contains (affineLine k).left) :
    points (siteOver k B hS) (genericPointOver k) ⟶ translationQuotient k B hS hU
declarations.comment: the generic point of the quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.isPullback_genericQuotientMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z7, the self-fibre-product of the generic point.** The fibre product
`Spec k(x) ×_{γ, X, γ} Spec k(x)` over `X = 𝔸¹_k/ℤ` is the disjoint union of one copy of
`Spec k(x)` for every integer: it is the graph relation of the translation action of `ℤ` on
`Spec k(x)`, whose two projections send the summand indexed by `n` to the translate of the
generic point by `n` and to the generic point itself.

The kernel pair of the projection `𝔸¹_k ⟶ 𝔸¹_k/ℤ` is the graph relation of the action on the
line — this is Stacks 0265 in the form
`Stacks.Groupoids.quotientChart_app_eq_iff_rel` — and that relation restricts along the
monomorphism `Spec k(x) ⟶ 𝔸¹_k` to the graph relation of the action on `Spec k(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_genericQuotientMorphism [CharZero k]
    (hU : B.Contains (affineLine k).left) :
    IsPullback
      ((siteOver k B hS).op.whiskerLeft (yoneda.map
        (Space.actionRelationTarget (genericPointOver k) (Multiplicative ℤ)
          (genericPointTranslationAction k))))
      ((siteOver k B hS).op.whiskerLeft (yoneda.map
        (Space.actionRelationSource (genericPointOver k) (Multiplicative ℤ))))
      (genericQuotientMorphism k B hS hU) (genericQuotientMorphism k B hS hU)
declarations.comment: the self-fibre-product of the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.not_mono_genericQuotientMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z7, part 1.** The generic point `γ : Spec k(x) ⟶ 𝔸¹_k/ℤ` is *not* a
monomorphism: translating the indeterminate by one is a nonidentity automorphism of
`Spec k(x)` which `γ` does not separate, because the translation is identified with the
identity in the quotient. It is the summand indexed by `1` of the self-fibre-product computed
in `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.isPullback_genericQuotientMorphism` on which the
two projections differ.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_mono_genericQuotientMorphism [CharZero k]
    (hU : B.Contains (affineLine k).left) (hG : B.Contains (Spec (.of (RatFunc k)))) :
    ¬ Mono (genericQuotientMorphism k B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.not_hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_genericQuotientPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z7, part 3.** The generic point of the quotient `X = 𝔸¹_k/ℤ` has *no*
monomorphic field-valued representative: no monomorphism `Spec L ⟶ X` from the spectrum of a
field presents it.

If `p` were one, with field `L`, then `p` would lift to the line over an extension `M` of `L`
of finite type, hence algebraic, and the coordinate `z` of that lift would agree, up to an
integer translation, with the indeterminate: so `z` is transcendental over `k`, and `L(z)` has
two embeddings into a single field differing by one on `z`. Monomorphy of `p` forces those two
embeddings to agree on `L`, which makes the minimal polynomial of `z` over `L` invariant under
translating the variable by one. In characteristic zero no nonconstant polynomial is.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_genericQuotientPoint (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [CharZero k] (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hG : B.Contains (Spec (.of (RatFunc k))))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    ¬ Space.HasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative B (Spec (.of k)) hS
      (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS))
      ((genericQuotientPoint k B hS hG).class B (Spec (.of k)) hS
        (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS)))
declarations.comment: no monomorphic field-valued representative of the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineTranslation.not_exists_mono_factorisation_genericQuotientPoint
declarations.doc:
The generic point `γ : Spec k(x) ⟶ X = 𝔸¹_k/ℤ` factors through no monomorphism from the
spectrum of a field: there is no field-valued point `p` of `X` whose presenting morphism
`Spec L ⟶ X` is a monomorphism and through which `γ` factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_exists_mono_factorisation_genericQuotientPoint (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hG : B.Contains (Spec (.of (RatFunc k))))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    ¬ ∃ (p : Space.FieldValuedPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hS
          (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS)))
        (f : (genericQuotientPoint k B hS hG).siteObject B (Spec (.of k)) hS
          (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS)) ⟶
            p.siteObject B (Spec (.of k)) hS
              (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS))),
        Mono (Space.fieldMorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hS
            (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS)) p) ∧
          yoneda.map f ≫ Space.fieldMorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hS
              (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS)) p =
            Space.fieldMorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hS
              (translationQuotient k B hS (contains_affineLine k B hS))
              (genericQuotientPoint k B hS hG)
declarations.comment: gamma factors through no monomorphism from a field spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.pow_card_eq_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** Every element of the product of copies of a finite field
satisfies `x ^ q = x`, where `q` is the number of elements of the field.
declarations.statement: theorem pow_card_eq_self (x : productRing K) : x ^ Nat.card K = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.nonempty_algEquiv_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The residue field at any prime of the product is
isomorphic to the factor field, compatibly with its diagonal `K`-algebra structure.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_algEquiv_residueField (p : PrimeSpectrum (productRing K)) :
    Nonempty (K ≃ₐ[K] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** Every point of the spectrum of the product of copies of a
finite field is closed.
declarations.statement: theorem isClosed_singleton (x : space K) : IsClosed ({x} : Set (space K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.dense_coordinatePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The points of the spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, k` determined by
the coordinate projections form a dense subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem dense_coordinatePoints (K : Type u) [Field K] :
    Dense (Set.range (fun n : ℕ ↦ (coordinate K n).base (default : base K)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.exists_unit_mul_idempotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** Every element of a product of copies of a field is a unit
times an idempotent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unit_mul_idempotent (x : productRing K) :
    ∃ (u : (productRing K)ˣ) (e : productRing K),
      IsIdempotentElem e ∧ x = (u : productRing K) * e

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isTopologicalBasis_isClopen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The clopen subsets of the spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, k` form a
topological basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTopologicalBasis_isClopen :
    TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis {s : Set (space K) | IsClopen s}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.instTotallyDisconnectedSpace
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, k` is totally disconnected.
declarations.statement: instance instTotallyDisconnectedSpace : TotallyDisconnectedSpace (space K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isOpen_singleton_iff_coordinate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The open points of the spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, k` are
precisely the points coming from the coordinate projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_singleton_iff_coordinate (x : space K) :
    IsOpen ({x} : Set (space K)) ↔
      ∃ n : ℕ, x = (coordinate K n).base (default : base K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.exists_noncoordinate_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, k` has a point not coming from any
coordinate projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_noncoordinate_point :
    ∃ x : space K, ∀ n : ℕ, x ≠ (coordinate K n).base (default : base K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.not_discreteTopology
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 02Z8.** The spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, k` is not discrete.
declarations.statement: theorem not_discreteTopology : ¬ DiscreteTopology (space K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The two charted projections form an étale equivalence relation on `U` in
the big fppf site over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_chart :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation
      (Space.relation B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR) (chartTarget k B hS hU hR))
declarations.comment: the charted relation is an étale equivalence relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isAlgebraicSpace_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The quotient `X = U/R` is an algebraic space over `S`. This is Stacks
02WW applied to the étale equivalence relation of the example.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_quotient :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B (base k) hS (quotient k B hS hU hR)
declarations.comment: the quotient X = U/R is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.quotientMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The quotient map `U ⟶ X` is surjective after every representable base
change: the morphism `|U| → |X|` of the source is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_surjective :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (base k) hS)))
      (Space.quotientMap B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR)
        (chartTarget k B hS hU hR))
declarations.comment: the quotient map U ⟶ X is surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.quotientMap_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The quotient map `U ⟶ X` is étale after every representable base
change.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_etale :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (base k) hS)))
      (Space.quotientMap B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR)
        (chartTarget k B hS hU hR))
declarations.comment: the quotient map U ⟶ X is étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The triple `(U, R, U ⟶ X)` is a presentation of the algebraic space
`X = U/R`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presentation :
    Space.Presentation B (base k) hS (quotient k B hS hU hR)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_quotient k B hS hU hR)
declarations.comment: the presentation of X by U and R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.quotientMap_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The relation `R` is the fibre product `U ×_X U`: the points of `U` that
become equal in `X` are exactly the ones related by `R`. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.quotientMap_comp_chartCoordinate_eq` this is the
assertion of the source that the coordinate points of `U` all map to one point of `X` and
that no other point of `U` gets identified with anything.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_isPullback :
    IsPullback (yoneda.map (chartTarget k B hS hU hR))
      (yoneda.map (chartSource k B hS hU hR))
      (Space.quotientMap B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR)
        (chartTarget k B hS hU hR))
      (Space.quotientMap B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR)
        (chartTarget k B hS hU hR))
declarations.comment: exactly the related points of U are identified in X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.quotientMap_comp_chartCoordinate_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** All the coordinate points of `U` have the same image in `X`: the
composites of the coordinate morphisms `S ⟶ U` with the quotient map agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientMap_comp_chartCoordinate_eq (n m : ℕ) :
    yoneda.map (chartCoordinate k B hS hU n) ≫
        Space.quotientMap B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR)
          (chartTarget k B hS hU hR) =
      yoneda.map (chartCoordinate k B hS hU m) ≫
        Space.quotientMap B (base k) hS (chartSource k B hS hU hR)
          (chartTarget k B hS hU hR)
declarations.comment: all the coordinate points of U map to one point of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.coordinatePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The point `x₀` of `X`: the common image of all the coordinate points of
`U`. It is a section of the structure morphism of `X`, the base `S` being a terminal object
of the site by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isTerminal_baseChart`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coordinatePoint :
    yoneda.obj (baseChart k B hS) ⟶ quotient k B hS hU hR
declarations.comment: x₀ is the image of a section S ⟶ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.surjective_pointsMap_quotientMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02Z8.** The map `|U| → |X|` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_pointsMap_quotientMap :
    Function.Surjective (pointsMap B (base K) hS (yoneda.obj (spaceChart K B hS hU))
      (Space.quotientMap B (base K) hS (chartSource K B hS hU hR)
        (chartTarget K B hS hU hR)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.continuous_pointsMap_quotientMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 02Z8.** The map `|U| → |X|` is continuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuous_pointsMap_quotientMap :
    Continuous (pointsMap B (base K) hS (yoneda.obj (spaceChart K B hS hU))
      (Space.quotientMap B (base K) hS (chartSource K B hS hU hR)
        (chartTarget K B hS hU hR)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.pointsMap_quotientMap_coordinatePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The point of `|U|` of the `n`-th coordinate maps to the point `x₀` of
`|X|`, for every `n`: all the coordinate points of `|U|` are identified in `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointsMap_quotientMap_coordinatePoint (n : ℕ) :
    pointsMap B (base K) hS (yoneda.obj (spaceChart K B hS hU))
        (Space.quotientMap B (base K) hS (chartSource K B hS hU hR)
          (chartTarget K B hS hU hR))
        ((schemePointsHomeomorph B (base K) hS (spaceChart K B hS hU)).symm
          ((coordinate K n).base (default : base K))) =
      pointsMap B (base K) hS (yoneda.obj (baseChart K B hS))
        (coordinatePoint K B hS hU hR) (basePoint K B hS)
declarations.comment: the coordinate points of |U| all map to x₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.dense_range_pointsMap_coordinatePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The image of the section `S ⟶ X` is dense in `|X|`: the point `x₀` has
closure all of `|X|`, so `|X|` is irreducible with generic point `x₀`.

The coordinate points are dense in `|U|` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.dense_coordinatePoints`, the map `|U| → |X|` is
continuous and surjective, and it carries every coordinate point to `x₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dense_range_pointsMap_coordinatePoint :
    Dense (Set.range (pointsMap B (base K) hS (yoneda.obj (baseChart K B hS))
      (coordinatePoint K B hS hU hR)))
declarations.comment: the closure of x₀ is all of |X|

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isOpenImmersion_coordinate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** Each coordinate projection of the product ring defines an open immersion
`S ⟶ U`: it is the localization of the product at the idempotent supported at `n`.
declarations.statement: instance isOpenImmersion_coordinate (n : ℕ) : IsOpenImmersion (coordinate k n)
declarations.comment: the coordinate morphisms are open immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isClosedImmersion_coordinate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** Each coordinate projection of the product ring defines a closed immersion
`S ⟶ U`: the projection is a surjective ring homomorphism.
declarations.statement: instance isClosedImmersion_coordinate (n : ℕ) : IsClosedImmersion (coordinate k n)
declarations.comment: the coordinate morphisms are closed immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isEmpty_of_coordinate_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** Distinct coordinate morphisms are disjoint: a scheme mapping to `S` in
two ways whose composites with `f_n` and with `f_m` agree is empty when `n ≠ m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_of_coordinate_eq {T : Scheme.{u}} {n m : ℕ} (hnm : n ≠ m) (a b : T ⟶ base k)
    (h : a ≫ coordinate k n = b ≫ coordinate k m) : IsEmpty T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.etale_relationTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The target projection of the relation is étale: it is the identity on
one summand and an open immersion on each of the others.
declarations.statement: theorem etale_relationTarget : Etale (relationTarget k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.etale_relationSource
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The source projection of the relation is étale: it is the identity on
one summand and an open immersion on each of the others.
declarations.statement: theorem etale_relationSource : Etale (relationSource k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isEquivalenceRelation_relation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The two projections of `R` are an internal equivalence relation on `U`
in the category of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceRelation_relation :
    IsEquivalenceRelation (relationTarget k) (relationSource k)
declarations.comment: the relation is an equivalence relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InfiniteProduct.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_preRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02Z8.** The pre-relation of the example is an étale equivalence relation over
`S`: this is the hypothesis under which Stacks 02WW produces the algebraic space `X = U/R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_preRelation :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (preRelation k)
declarations.comment: the pre-relation is an étale equivalence relation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.strictMorPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The presheaf `Mor(x, y)` of a split fibred category**, Stacks 02ZA. For an honest functor
`F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat` and objects `x`, `y` of `F(U)`, the presheaf on `𝒞/U` whose sections over
`f : V ⟶ U` are the morphisms `F(f) x ⟶ F(f) y` of `F(V)`, and whose restriction maps are the
functors `F(h)`. Because `F(h) ∘ F(f) = F(f ∘ h)` holds on the nose, the presheaf axioms are the
functoriality of `F` and no comparison isomorphisms `α_{g, f}` are needed.
declarations.statement: def strictMorPresheaf (x y : F.obj (op U)) : (Over U)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₃
declarations.comment: for the fibred category of a functor F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat, where g^* ∘ f^* = (f ∘ g)^* on the nose, Lemma 026A with no maps α_{g, f}: the presheaf axioms of Mor(x, y) are F.map_id and F.map_comp

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredEquivalenceOver.isIso_morPresheafMap
declarations.doc:
**`Mor(x, y)` is unchanged along an equivalence of fibred categories** (Stacks 02ZA, from
Stacks 042V). If `G : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` is an equivalence in the 2-category of fibred categories over `𝒞`,
then the map of presheaves `Mor(x, y) ⟶ Mor(G x, G y)` of Stacks 042V is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_morPresheafMap (hG : IsFibredEquivalenceOver p q G) {U : 𝒞} (a b : p.Fiber U) :
    IsIso (hG.isFibredOneMorphism.morPresheafMap a b)
declarations.comment: Mor(x, y) is unchanged when passing to an equivalent fibred category: the map of 042V along an equivalence of fibred categories is an isomorphism of presheaves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.morPresheafIsoStrictMorPresheafGrpd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZA.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` be fibred in groupoids, and let `x`, `y` be objects of the
fibre over `U`. By Stacks 02XY (the groupoid case of Stacks 004A) `p` is equivalent to the fibred
category of the functor `F = splitPresheafGrpd p hp : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grpd`, and the presheaf `Mor(x, y)`
of `p` is isomorphic to the presheaf `Mor((x, id), (y, id))` of that split model, whose
restriction maps are the functors `F(h)` and need no comparison isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morPresheafIsoStrictMorPresheafGrpd (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (x y : p.Fiber U) :
    morPresheaf p x y ≅
      strictMorPresheaf (splitPresheafGrpd p hp ⋙ Grpd.forgetToCat)
        (SplitFiber.ofFiber p x) (SplitFiber.ofFiber p y)
declarations.comment: Mor(x, y) of a category fibred in groupoids is the strict Mor presheaf of the split model F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grpd of 004A, whose restriction maps are the functors F(h) with g^* ∘ f^* = (f ∘ g)^* on the nose

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.LocallyDiscreteOpToCat.pullHom
registrations.comment:
Remark 8.2.4 observes that a category fibred in groupoids is
  equivalent to the fibred category of a contravariant functor into groupoids, and that
  for the latter the restriction maps of the presheaf Mor(x, y) of Definition 8.2.2 need
  no coherence isomorphisms. Mathlib works in exactly that model: for a pseudofunctor
  from the locally discrete bicategory on the opposite of the base into Cat, this is the
  restriction map from a morphism of the fibre over Y to a morphism of the fibre over
  Y', with the coherence isomorphisms carried by mapComp'.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.LocallyDiscreteOpToCat.pullHom_id
registrations.comment:
Restriction along an identity is the identity, the first half of the
  functoriality that Remark 8.2.4 says is trivial in this model.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.LocallyDiscreteOpToCat.pullHom_pullHom
registrations.comment:
Restriction respects composition, the second half of that
  functoriality.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.presheafHom
registrations.comment:
The presheaf Mor(x, y) itself: the presheaf on Over S whose sections
  over a morphism p : X ⟶ S are the morphisms from the pullback of M along p to the
  pullback of N along p. Assembling it is Lemma 8.2.1, which Remark 8.2.4 is a remark
  about; the further ingredient the remark cites, invariance of Mor(x, y) under an
  equivalence of fibred categories (Lemma 042V), is not covered here.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.morPresheaf
declarations.doc:
The presheaf `Mor(x, y)` on `𝒮/U` of a fibred category `p`: its sections over `f : V ⟶ U` are
the morphisms `f^* x ⟶ f^* y` of the fibre over `V`, and its restriction maps are
`CategoryTheory.Functor.morRestrict`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def morPresheaf (x y : p.Fiber U) : (Over U)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isomSubpresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZB**, the subpresheaf `Isom(x, y)` of `Mor(x, y)`: over `f : V ⟶ U` its sections are
the morphisms `f^* x ⟶ f^* y` of the fibre over `V` that are isomorphisms. This is a subpresheaf
because restriction preserves isomorphisms, `CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_morRestrict`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def isomSubpresheaf (x y : p.Fiber U) : Subfunctor (morPresheaf p x y)
declarations.comment:
The subpresheaf `Isom(x, y)` of `Mor(x, y)`; the presheaf `Mor(x, y)` itself is
  `CategoryTheory.Functor.morPresheaf`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FamilyDescentDatum.pull
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZD (1).**
The descent datum relative to `𝒰 = {U i ⟶ U}` obtained from a descent datum `(Y j, φ j j')`
relative to `𝒱 = {V j ⟶ V}` by pulling back along a morphism of families `Φ = (α, h, g)`: its
object over `U i` is the chosen pullback `g i ^* Y (α i)`, and its gluing morphisms are those of
`(Y j, φ j j')` pulled back along the `g i`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pull (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h) (D : FamilyDescentDatum p 𝒱) :
    FamilyDescentDatum p 𝒰
declarations.comment: (1) the descent datum `(g i ^* Y (α i), (g i × g i') ^* φ (α i) (α i'))`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FamilyDescentDatum.pullFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZD (2).**
Pulling back descent data along a morphism of families `Φ = (α, h, g)` from `𝒰` to `𝒱` is a
functor from the category of descent data relative to `𝒱` to the category of descent data
relative to `𝒰`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullFunctor (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h) :
    FamilyDescentDatum p 𝒱 ⥤ FamilyDescentDatum p 𝒰
declarations.comment: (2) the functor from descent data relative to `𝒱` to descent data relative to `𝒰`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FamilyDescentDatum.pullFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZD (3).**
Two morphisms of families `Φ = (α, h, g)` and `Φ' = (α', h, g')` from `𝒰` to `𝒱` lying over one
and the same morphism `h : U ⟶ V` of the targets induce canonically isomorphic functors on
descent data. The component of the isomorphism at a descent datum `(Y j, φ j j')` and an index
`i` is the gluing isomorphism of that datum between `g i ^* Y (α i)` and `g' i ^* Y (α' i)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pullFunctorIso (Φ Φ' : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h) : pullFunctor p Φ ≅ pullFunctor p Φ'
declarations.comment: (3) for two morphisms of families over one and the same `h : U ⟶ V`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FamilyDescentDatum.pullFunctorIsoOfEq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZD (3)**, with the hypothesis `h = h'` on the two morphisms of targets stated as
such: morphisms of families `Φ` over `h` and `Φ'` over `h'` with `h' = h` induce canonically
isomorphic functors on descent data.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullFunctorIsoOfEq {h' : U ⟶ V} (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h) (Φ' : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h')
    (hh : h' = h) : pullFunctor p Φ ≅ pullFunctor p Φ'
declarations.comment: (3) for morphisms of families over `h` and over `h'` with `h' = h`, as in Stacks

registrations.name: Pseudofunctor.DescentData.pullFunctorIso
registrations.comment: (3), with `h = h'` built in by sharing `p`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FamilyDescentDatum.pullFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZD (2).**
Pulling back descent data along a morphism of families `Φ = (α, h, g)` from `𝒰` to `𝒱` is a
functor from the category of descent data relative to `𝒱` to the category of descent data
relative to `𝒰`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullFunctor (Φ : 𝒰.HomOver 𝒱 h) :
    FamilyDescentDatum p 𝒱 ⥤ FamilyDescentDatum p 𝒰

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStack_iff_isEquivalence_toDescentData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZF.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` be a fibred category over a site `(𝒮, J)`. Then `p` is a stack
if and only if, for every covering `𝒰 = {f i : U i ⟶ U}` of the site, the functor `𝒳_U ⥤ DD(𝒰)`
sending an object of the fibre over `U` to its canonical descent datum relative to `𝒰` is an
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_iff_isEquivalence_toDescentData (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒮) :
    p.IsStack J ↔ ∀ ⦃U : 𝒮⦄ (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{max u₁ v₁} U), 𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J U →
      ((pullbackPseudofunctor p).toDescentData 𝒰.f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZG (1)**.
An object of the 2-category of stacks over the site `(𝒞, J)`: a category over `𝒞` whose structure
functor is a stack.
declarations.statement: structure BasedStack (𝒞 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒞] (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedStack.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZG (2)**.
A 1-morphism of stacks over `𝒞`: a functor `G` between the underlying categories with
`p' ∘ G = p`, which carries strongly cartesian morphisms to strongly cartesian morphisms. The
first condition is the field `w` of a `BasedFunctor` and is repeated as `comp_eq` inside
`Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (𝒳 𝒴 : BasedStack.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞 J)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedStack.homCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZG (3)**.
The 2-morphisms between two 1-morphisms of stacks: the morphisms of functors `t` with
`p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every object `x`, that is the `BasedNatTrans` between the underlying
functors over `𝒞`. Nothing is imposed on a 2-morphism beyond that, so this category of
1-morphisms is the one of the ambient 2-category `BasedCategory 𝒞`.
declarations.statement: instance homCategory (𝒳 𝒴 : BasedStack.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞 J) : Category (𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedStack.bicategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZG**.
The 2-category of stacks over the site `(𝒞, J)`: the sub-2-category of the 2-category of fibred
categories over `𝒞` (Stacks 02XP) whose objects are the stacks over `𝒞`, whose 1-morphisms are the
functors over `𝒞` preserving strongly cartesian morphisms, and whose 2-morphisms are the morphisms
of functors whose components lie over identities.
declarations.statement: instance bicategory : Bicategory (BasedStack.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞 J)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStackInGroupoidsBySieves
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZI.** A category `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` over the site `(𝒞, J)` is a *stack in groupoids* if
1. `p` is fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`;
2. for all `U` of `𝒞` and all `x`, `y` of the fibre `𝒮_U`, the presheaf `Isom(x, y)` of
   Stacks 02ZB (`CategoryTheory.Functor.isomPresheaf`) is a sheaf on the site `𝒞/U`;
3. every descent datum relative to a covering of `U` is effective
   (`CategoryTheory.Functor.HasEffectiveDescent`).

Conditions (2) and (3) are stated with the chosen pullbacks of the fibred structure that
condition (1) provides.
declarations.statement: def IsStackInGroupoidsBySieves (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.stackInGroupoids_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZJ.** Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` be a category over `𝒞`. The
following are equivalent:
(1) `p` is a stack in groupoids over `𝒞`, that is `p` is fibred in groupoids, the presheaves
    `Isom(x, y)` on `𝒞/U` are sheaves, and every descent datum relative to a covering is
    effective (Stacks 02ZI);
(2) `p` is a stack over `𝒞` and all its fibre categories are groupoids;
(3) `p` is fibred in groupoids over `𝒞` and is a stack over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stackInGroupoids_tfae (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∃ h : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids,
          haveI : p.IsFibered := h.isFibered
          (∀ (U : 𝒞) (x y : p.Fiber U),
              Presheaf.IsSheaf (J.over U) (p.isomPresheaf x y)) ∧ p.HasEffectiveDescent J,
        p.IsStack J ∧ ∀ U : 𝒞, IsGroupoid (p.Fiber U),
        p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ p.IsStack J ]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZK (1)**.
An object of the 2-category of stacks in groupoids over the site `(𝒞, J)`: a category over `𝒞`
whose structure functor is a stack in groupoids.
declarations.statement: structure StackInGroupoids (𝒞 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒞] (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StackInGroupoids.bicategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZK**.
The 2-category of stacks in groupoids over the site `(𝒞, J)`: the sub-2-category of the
2-category of stacks over `𝒞` (Stacks 02ZG) whose objects are the stacks in groupoids. Since
every morphism of a category fibred in groupoids is strongly cartesian, no condition is imposed
on a 1-morphism beyond being a functor over `𝒞` — see
`CategoryTheory.StackInGroupoids.isFibredOneMorphism` — so this is the full sub-2-category of the
2-category `BasedCategory 𝒞` of categories over `𝒞` spanned by the stacks in groupoids.
declarations.statement:
instance StackInGroupoids.bicategory :
    Bicategory (StackInGroupoids.{w, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞 J)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StackInGroupoids.homEquivBasedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZK (2)**.
The 1-morphisms of the 2-category of stacks in groupoids are the functors over `𝒞`: a
1-morphism `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is the same thing as a `BasedFunctor`, that is a functor `G` with
`p' ∘ G = p`.
declarations.statement: def homEquivBasedFunctor : (𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) ≃ (𝒳.toBasedCategory ⥤ᵇ 𝒴.toBasedCategory)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StackInGroupoids.twoHomEquivBasedNatTrans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZK (3)**.
The 2-morphisms of the 2-category of stacks in groupoids are the morphisms of functors whose
components lie over identities: a 2-morphism `F ⟶ G` is the same thing as a `BasedNatTrans`,
that is a morphism of functors `t` with `p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every object `x`.
declarations.statement:
def twoHomEquivBasedNatTrans {𝒳 𝒴 : StackInGroupoids.{w, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞 J} (F G : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    (F ⟶ G) ≃ BasedNatTrans F.hom G.hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isStack_isFiberedInGroupoids_structureFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZL.** The 2-fibre product of stacks in groupoids over a site `(𝒞, J)` is a stack in
groupoids: the construction of Stacks 0040 does not leave the 2-category of stacks in groupoids.

"Stack in groupoids" is spelled out as its two conditions, being a stack over `(𝒞, J)` and being
fibred in groupoids, because the library's `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStackInGroupoids` is a second,
unrelated rendering of the notion (see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.CategoryTheory.Sites.Stack.Setoid`).
The first condition is Stacks 026G and the second
is Stacks 0041; the hypotheses on `F` and `G` are only that they are strictly over `𝒞`, since a
functor over `𝒞` into a category fibred in groupoids automatically preserves strongly cartesian
morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_isFiberedInGroupoids_structureFunctor {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞}
    (h𝒳 : Functor.IsStack p𝒳 J) (h𝒴 : Functor.IsStack p𝒴 J) (h𝒮 : Functor.IsStack p𝒮 J)
    (g𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (g𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (g𝒮 : p𝒮.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hF : F ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒳) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒴) :
    Functor.IsStack (structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) J ∧
      (structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isStackification_and_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZN.** Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞` be a fibred category. There exist
a stack `q' : 𝒴' ⥤ 𝒞` over `(𝒞, J)` and a 1-morphism `G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒴'` of fibred categories over `𝒞`
such that

1. for every `U` and all `x`, `y` in the fibre `𝒴_U` the map `Mor(x, y) ⟶ Mor(G x, G y)` of
   presheaves on `𝒞/U` exhibits its target as the sheafification of its source (it is locally
   injective and locally surjective), and
2. every object of a fibre of `𝒴'` is, along a covering sieve of the base, in the essential image
   of the functor induced by `G` on fibres.

Moreover `𝒴'` is determined up to unique 2-isomorphism by these conditions: for every stack
`r : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` and 1-morphism `F : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒳` of fibred categories over `𝒞` satisfying (1) and (2) there
are a 1-morphism `H : 𝒴' ⥤ 𝒳` which is an equivalence of `q'` with `r` over `𝒞` and a
2-isomorphism `α : G ⋙ H ≅ F`, and every other such pair `(H', α')` is related to `(H, α)` by
exactly one 2-isomorphism `β : H ≅ H'` with `(G ◁ β) ≫ α' = α`.

The objects and morphisms of `𝒴'` live in `Type (max t₁ t₂ w vb)`, the morphism universe of `𝒴`;
the competing stack `𝒳` may live in any universe and has the same morphism universe as `𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStackification_and_unique :
    ∃ (𝒴' : Type (max t₁ t₂ w vb)) (inst : Category.{max t₁ t₂ w vb} 𝒴'),
      letI := inst
      ∃ (q' : 𝒴' ⥤ 𝒞) (instq : q'.IsFibered),
        letI := instq
        ∃ (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒴') (hG : q.IsFibredOneMorphism q' G),
          q'.IsStack J ∧
            (∀ (U : 𝒞) (x y : q.Fiber U),
                Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (J.over U) (hG.morPresheafMap x y) ∧
                  Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (J.over U) (hG.morPresheafMap x y)) ∧
              (∀ (U : 𝒞) (x' : q'.Fiber U), ∃ R ∈ J U, ∀ ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ ⦃f : V ⟶ U⦄, R.arrows f →
                (fiberFunctorOfCompEq hG.comp_eq V).essImage (pullbackFiber q' x' f)) ∧
              ∀ (𝒳 : Type u) [Category.{max t₁ t₂ w vb} 𝒳] (r : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) [r.IsFibered]
                (F : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒳) (hF : q.IsFibredOneMorphism r F), r.IsStack J →
                (∀ (U : 𝒞) (x y : q.Fiber U),
                  Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (J.over U) (hF.morPresheafMap x y) ∧
                    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (J.over U) (hF.morPresheafMap x y)) →
                (∀ (U : 𝒞) (x : r.Fiber U), ∃ R ∈ J U, ∀ ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ ⦃f : V ⟶ U⦄, R.arrows f →
                  (fiberFunctorOfCompEq hF.comp_eq V).essImage (pullbackFiber r x f)) →
                ∃ H : FibredMor q' r, Nonempty (IsEquivalenceOver q' r H.functor) ∧
                  ∃ α : (restrictMor hG).obj H ≅ ⟨F, hF⟩,
                    ∀ (H' : FibredMor q' r) (α' : (restrictMor hG).obj H' ≅ ⟨F, hF⟩),
                      ∃! β : H ≅ H', (restrictMor hG).mapIso β ≪≫ α' = α
declarations.comment: Mor(x, y) → Mor(G x, G y) identifying the target with the sheafification of the source is read as local injectivity and local surjectivity of the map of presheaves on 𝒞/U, a covering {U_i → U} as a covering sieve, and 'unique up to unique 2-isomorphism' as: a comparison 1-morphism with a 2-isomorphism G ⋙ H ≅ F exists, is an equivalence over 𝒞, and is unique up to exactly one compatible 2-isomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isFiberedInGroupoids_of_isStackification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZP.** Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` be a category fibred in groupoids and
let `G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'` exhibit the stack `p' : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒞` as the stackification of the fibred category
underlying `𝒮` — that is, let `G` be a 1-morphism of fibred categories over `𝒞` satisfying the two
clauses of Stacks 02ZN. Then `p'` is fibred in groupoids.

This is the whole content of Stacks 02ZP over Stacks 02ZN: the source runs the same construction
and observes that it lands in groupoid fibres. The statement is conditional on being given the
stackification, the construction of Stacks 02ZN not being assembled in the tree yet; once it is,
it supplies `hsp'`, `hG`, `hmor` and `hobj`.

By Stacks 003V it suffices that every fibre of `𝒮'` be a groupoid, which is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isGroupoid_fiber`.
declarations.statement: theorem isFiberedInGroupoids_of_isStackification : p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isStackInGroupoids_of_isStackification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZP, as the source states it: `𝒮'` is a stack in groupoids.** The `IsStack` half is
the hypothesis `hsp'` and the `IsFiberedInGroupoids` half is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isFiberedInGroupoids_of_isStackification`; together with
`hmor` and `hobj`, which are the two clauses of the source's statement carried unchanged from
hypothesis to conclusion, this says that the given `G` exhibits `𝒮'` as the stackification of `𝒮`
*in groupoids*.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInGroupoids_of_isStackification :
    p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ p'.IsStack J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_of_locally_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**The determinacy clause of Stacks 02ZN and 02ZP, in the form a consumer uses.** Let
`G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` exhibit the stack `p'` as the stackification of the fibred category `p` — that is, let
it satisfy the two clauses `hGmor` and `hGobj` — and let `H : ℬ ⥤ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of fibred
categories into a stack `q`. If the composite `G ⋙ H` satisfies the same two clauses, then `H` is
an equivalence of `p'` with `q` over `𝒞`.

So two stackifications of one fibred category have equivalent targets, and the comparison realising
the equivalence is any 1-morphism between them compatible with the two presentations. The two
clauses, which for a given stackification are hypotheses carried to the conclusion by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isStackInGroupoids_of_isStackification`, thereby become a
*criterion* on `G ⋙ H`.

`H` is fully faithful by `CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.full_of_extension` and
`.faithful_of_extension`, Stacks 04WQ for a 1-morphism out of a stackification, whose hypotheses
are precisely the clauses on `G` and on the composite. It is locally essentially surjective on
fibres because `G ⋙ H` is, a local preimage under the composite being one under `H`. Stacks 046N,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isEquivalenceOver_iff_locallyEssSurjOnFibers`, then concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_of_locally_fullyFaithful :
    Nonempty (IsEquivalenceOver p' q H)
declarations.comment: the determinacy half of the statement — `𝒮'` is determined up to 2-isomorphism by clauses (1) and (2) — read as: a 1-morphism from a stackification into a stack whose composite with the stackification again satisfies the two clauses is an equivalence over the site. The existence half is the construction of Stacks 02ZN, not assembled in the tree; the uniqueness of the 2-isomorphism is Stacks 04W9, `CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.restrict_isEquivalence`; and the groupoid half of 02ZP is `CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isStackInGroupoids_of_isStackification`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_extend
declarations.doc:
**A stackification is determined up to 2-isomorphism: the "moreover" of Stacks 02ZN, repeated
by Stacks 02ZP.** Let `G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` exhibit the stack `p'` as the stackification of the fibred
category `p`, and let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism into a stack `q` satisfying the same two
clauses — `hFmor`, that the induced maps of morphism presheaves are locally bijective, and
`hFobj`, that every object of a fibre of `q` is locally in the essential image of `F` on fibres.
Then the extension of `F` along `G` supplied by the universal property, Stacks 0435, is an
equivalence of `p'` with `q` over `𝒞`.

So a 1-morphism satisfying the two clauses does not merely land in *a* stack: it exhibits its
target as *the* stackification. The extension is compatible with the two presentations by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.unit`, which is the 2-isomorphism `G ⋙ H ≅ F`, so the
equivalence identifies the two presentations and not just the two targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_extend :
    Nonempty (IsEquivalenceOver p' q
      (extend hG hF hGmor hq.isMorSheaf hGobj hq.hasEffectiveDescent))
declarations.comment: the determinacy half of the statement — `𝒮'` is determined up to 2-isomorphism by clauses (1) and (2) — for the canonical extension: a 1-morphism into a stack satisfying the two clauses exhibits that stack as the stackification, so the extension of Stacks 0435 is an equivalence over the site. The existence half is the construction of Stacks 02ZN, not assembled in the tree; the uniqueness of the 2-isomorphism is Stacks 04W9, `CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.restrict_isEquivalence`; and the groupoid half of 02ZP is `CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isStackInGroupoids_of_isStackification`

declarations.name: Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.isRepresentableMorphism_overMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZR.** A morphism in a category with pullbacks induces a
representable 1-morphism of the categories fibred in groupoids of objects over
its source and target.

declarations.name: Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.isRepresentableMorphism_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZS.** A composite of representable 1-morphisms of categories fibred in
groupoids over a base category is representable.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isRepresentableMorphism_comp
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (r : 𝒵 ⥤ 𝒞)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hr : r.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒵)
    (hF : F ⋙ q = p) (hG : G ⋙ r = q)
    (hrepF : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p q F)
    (hrepG : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism q r G) :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p r (F ⋙ G)

declarations.name: Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.isRepresentableMorphism_product
declarations.doc:
The product of two representable 1-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over a base
category is representable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRepresentableMorphism_product
    (p₁ : 𝒳₁ ⥤ 𝒞) (p₂ : 𝒳₂ ⥤ 𝒞)
    (q₁ : 𝒴₁ ⥤ 𝒞) (q₂ : 𝒴₂ ⥤ 𝒞)
    (hp₁ : p₁.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hp₂ : p₂.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hq₁ : q₁.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq₂ : q₂.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F₁ : 𝒳₁ ⥤ 𝒴₁) (F₂ : 𝒳₂ ⥤ 𝒴₂)
    (hF₁ : F₁ ⋙ q₁ = p₁) (hF₂ : F₂ ⋙ q₂ = p₂)
    (hrep₁ : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p₁ q₁ F₁)
    (hrep₂ : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p₂ q₂ F₂) :

      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor q₁ q₂ (𝟭 𝒞) q₁ q₂)
      (productMorphism p₁ p₂ q₁ q₂ F₁ F₂ hF₁ hF₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZW.** A 1-morphism of categories over the big fppf site of `S` is *representable
by algebraic spaces* if, for every scheme `U` over `S` and every scheme-valued point
`y : (Sch/U)_{fppf} ⟶ 𝒴` of its target, the first projection of the 2-fibre product
`(Sch/U)_{fppf} ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ (Sch/U)_{fppf}` is equivalent, over the big fppf site of `U`, to the
category of elements of the sheaf of points of an algebraic space over `U`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZX.** A category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site
is represented by an algebraic space precisely when its fibres are setoids
and its presheaf of isomorphism classes is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_iff
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳 ↔
      (𝒳.val.p.IsFiberedInSetoids ∧ IsAlgebraicSpaceIsoClassPresheaf B S hS 𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_iff_associatedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZY.** A morphism of categories fibred in groupoids is representable by
algebraic spaces if and only if its functors on fibres are faithful and, for every
object of the target over a scheme, the associated presheaf of pairs is an
algebraic space over that scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_iff_associatedMap
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (c : 𝒴.val.p.ChoiceOfPullbacks) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom ↔
      ((∀ U : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS,
        (Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.inducedFiberFunctor 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f)
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p f) U).Faithful) ∧
        (∀ (U : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : 𝒴.val.p.Fiber U),
          IsAlgebraicSpacePairIsoClassPresheaf B S hS f c U y))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZZ.** A 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of
`S` whose source and target are both representable by algebraic spaces over `S` is representable
by algebraic spaces.

Both source and target are transported to categories of elements, where
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_fibredCategory` applies: the source by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_equivalenceOver_fst_of_equivalence_source`, the target by
Stacks 0457.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒴 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒴) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom
